This is the first Lego title I have played on PS3, and it's proven to be a lot of fun and made me interested in finding other Lego games on PS3 now.You can probably guess already what the game is about, and how it works, so I won't bore you with plot details or anything. The game allows you to start off on campaign mode with Batman and Robin, and the further into the game you get, the more characters you can earn/unlock. Completing story mode will eventually unlock a lot of extra Justice League heroes, but mainly you just wanna get your hands on Superman who has the ability to fly to really get the game going. Unfortunately he doesn't come in until about the 9th level. You can unlock freeplay mode after completing each level. There is where you can use whatever character you want that you have unlocked so far. The rest can be found in freeplay mode where you have to find them by either having enough gold to unlock superheroes, or fight the villains and then buy them.I don't think they have forgotten too many DC super heroes... the only one I don't think is in it that I noticed was Captain Marvel, but still, had it not been for Mortal Kombat vs DC I still wouldn't know who the heck that was anyway?The game took me about 2 weeks to complete, but for people who have more time, it can be done much quicker. The story mode doesn't last that long. It's only 15 levels, however once you have completed it, you can play story mode to get 100% in each story by replaying it, now being able to switch to whatever character you want this time (if you have access to them) and you can explore and break new things which individual characters powers.The only thing that lets the game down is the replay value. Yes, replaying the stories after finishing the game does expand it a bit, however I found it a bit too easy to unlock the necessary characters needed to complete the free mode replays of the 15 levels. You only really need Batman, Robin, Superman, Aqua Man, Lex Luther, The Joker, Killer Crock and Man Bat to get 100% in all the levels. After the 15 levels are completed at 100% each, you have the whole city to explore and find certain items and characters to buy. The thing that puzzles me tho is you need to obtain all 250 gold bricks in order to unlock a few characters, one being Supergirl. Her powers are no different to Superman, so it puzzles me why she is kind of the ultimate, or hardest, or perhaps most patient thing to unlock? You can just create your own superwoman in the create a character area of the Batcave. (with red hair instead of blonde, does a graphics color really matter?)I played through free play around the city collecting various things, I found all the red bricks needed to unlock cheats, I saved all the citizens in peril, and found all of the villains, the only thing I have not done is collected all 250 gold bricks just to unlock about 3 or 4 more characters.... and quite frankly, even with a cheat that allows the map to show you where the bricks are located, I have done about 130 and am just tired of it, and I really have no ambition to finish it just to unlock Supergirl and a few other characters not even needed to complete the main objectives of the game. So what is the point of having to find them all, really? Just so my entire save file says 100% complete or to unlock the 100% platinum trophy that means nothing to most PS3 gamers? The developers really should have either lessened the amount of gold bricks to find, or have a point to why you need to find 250 bricks, one at a time, scattered all over the city, just to unlock Supergirl in the end? What is so special about that? So I don't feel the need to play this game anymore now that I have completed it, and found all the bonus things necessary, and also found the little bonus level.The DLC for the game is just a couple of extra characters. One being Night Wing, another being Batmans son, and a few others I have never heard of. I don't see the point in it that either, as they don't add anything new to the game in abilities, nor do they add extra things to do in levels only their powers can unlock.What the game needed as DLC was more vehicles and costumes. It would have been really cool to be able to dress batman up as all versions of the batman, or at least the Adam West and the current look. And it would also have been nice to have ALL the batmobiles and transports available. As this game does have a big mix of all versions of batman from the movies, to comic books, being able to drive a bunch of different Batmobiles might have been a much better idea than the almost pointless mini kit pieces you find throughout the levels that unlock miniature versions of the larger vehicles in the game. It's just not that much fun after the first test drive of one. By the time I was done with the game I wasn't even using any vehicles,  and just flying around with any character that could do so.Lego should really think about that in future to keep people interested in the game after completion, or finding out that doing a long and tiring task like finding 250 gold bricks is pretty much pointless to unlock characters you just don't need.

Wow! I thought I had played all of the Lego games, but it seems I had missed this one, and my kids discovered that oversight and gave it to me for Christmas. I must admit I was a little apprehensive because last fall I had played Marvel Super Heroes and was very disappointed with that game. But my fears dissipated soon after I started playing and as I progressed farther into the game the more pleased I became.The art work and graphics are incredible and very well done in this game. If your used to playing any of the newer Lego releases, you'll know that they pack a ton of hints and helpful things into the environment. The hub is basically the Bat Cave from which you can launch a level. As with all other Lego games, you are required to play all levels in Story Mode to unlock Free Play. These are brought up in a map in the bat cave by using the central console. Once selected you are taken there in the selected mode. There is a massive open play area Gotham City. This area consists of three connected islands, and are chock full of places to go and things to do, and collect. All of the Citizens in Peril, Gold Bricks, Red Bricks, Vehicles, and Characters that you do not achieve in Story Mode or Free Play of the individual levels can be obtained here. In all there are 250 Gold Bricks. During level play you can get 3 Gold Bricks for each, one for reaching the high score to achieve True Hero status, one for finding the Citizen in Peril, and one for completing the Mini-Kit. All Mini-Kit pieces are only found in each level, none are located elsewhere. Once you have achieved all of the three above there is no longer any reason to play the levels and you can concentrate on clearing the main Gotham City areas.To get to Gotham from the Bat Cave, simply move to any one of the three vehicle platforms, ask Alfred for a vehicle and take off. To obtain one of the Gold Bricks in the river, you will need to use one of the boats at least once and navigate a course of cones. To obtain another one of the Gold Bricks you'll need to use a flying machine and look for the green targets and fly through them in order to obtain the brick. Once your free to roam in Gotham, you can start finding stuff you need. If you start your map and press Y you can momentarily see where objects are located. Yellow dots are Gold Bricks, Red dots are Red Bricks, Vehicles are vehicles, Blue dots are Citizens in Peril, and Gold Arches are Character Portals.Personally, I would start and try to collect the Red Bricks first so you can unlock those Extras and get some help in locating the things your looking for. Many of these are very easy to find and obtain, others you'll need to find Joker and Riddler to get to so also go after characters in the early play. Look for the different colored spotlights. Red spotlights lead you to a Red Brick location, Blue spotlights lead you to a communications port with the Bat Cave and you can either transport to another part of the map, or have Alfred send a vehicle. Some Character Portals will not build because you need to have so many Gold Bricks first, just move on and get as many as you can. Also while your out early on, find the Citizen in Peril and save them. None of them are hard at all. Many are just being beaten by thugs and all you need to do is punch the thug and the Citizen is free. Others its as simple as using Superman to freeze a water spout allowing them to jump off. Once you've collected many Red Bricks, characters, and Citizens in Peril, you can start on the Gold Bricks. You obviously have collected some during your search for the Citizens in Peril and Red Bricks, but there are a lot more to find. Some are easy like knocking down 5 mail boxes, or breaking 4 shrubs, others are more involved and require a lot of climbing, and moves to get to the brick with the proper equipment to get it. The hardest part on some of them is finding where to start. I used Superman to fly up and started by getting the ones on rooftops, and high places. This helps to cut down on the number of gold arrows flashing from your Gold Brick finder extra. Use Superman to fly up to a Gold Brick them use him to fly around and follow the trail to a suit port and thus your start point.There are about 6 water course Gold Brick challenges. You will see the yellow arrow marker in the water and not know how to get the brick. Look along the shore or docks for a boat or a Bat Cave communications platform. If its a platform, call Alfred up and have him send a boat of your choice. Some are easier than others to steer. Sometimes a boat will already be there, buy it if you need to, then jump on and the first set of cones will appear. Run the course to get that Gold Brick. Only the police boat was a weird wobbly contraption that was hard to control, all the others were easy and fun. There are also about 6 flying challenges. Most of these are from aircraft you'll find on top of buildings. I found a glitch here in that the indicator on the map showed a gold dot but no aircraft were found. I restarted the game and then they appeared so be aware that if you cannot find an aircraft on a roof top and there should be one, this may be the problem. As you mount the aircraft a green target will open ahead of you. Take off and make your way from target to target until you get your brick. The only aircraft that was hard to control was the helicopter on the building next to Luthor tower. Flying in general is not super easy and takes a lot of practice to get it working. This includes flying characters such as Superman or Wonder Woman.I did not encounter any of the challenges that were hard. Some were quite involved and one was a little frustrating as you had to make some odd jumps and the character would fall and you would have to get back to a point to try again. Most challenges the grasping function was flawless and the areas designed to be very forgiving if you did happen to fall. Some challenges as mentioned before are hard to find the starting points. Those were mainly the buildings, but there are some confusing cues in the Zoo too. Just look for and ride all 4 animals, the rest are easy.Once you have collected all of the items you should have 2 slots left, one Character and one Gold Brick. You can then play the Bonus Level. You may have passed a pile of gold pieces in the park that were not active or if they were you could not enter the portal. You must have a certain number of Gold Bricks to activate the bricks so you can build them, and you must have Clark Kent character. Then you can enter and play this level. As with all Lego games you need to achieve 1 million studs. Stud multiplier extras are Off so you'll have to work for every stud you can find and get. Break everything, solve the puzzles and work all three areas to reach this goal and earn that last Gold Brick. Then you can go back to Gotham to the building near Luthor tower and get that last character. If you've done everything right, you'll have 100% completion.This game over all was a ton of fun to play. Not as big as Lord of The Rings which was also very good, but big enough to keep you occupied for some time. Art work was awesome, controls were very well done in spite of the learning curve for the flying. challenges were easy to difficult without being frustrating. The individual levels were very challenging but nothing any player should not be able to get through with some persistence. If you really get stuck, there are several excellent guides out on the web from which to get a hint. The timed challenges were few and mercifully fairly easy. There are NO driving challenges. This is a fun, winnable game for those who love the franchise. If I had to complain about anything, it would be the thugs in Gotham City. As your playing in this open world if you stop for more than a few seconds to get your bearings or to do something, your constantly attacked by thugs. They do no harm and you can knock them out with one punch, but they were SO annoying when your trying to find your way or hunt down a clue or save a Citizen in Peril. I avoided being on the ground as much as possible, and used superman almost exclusively to get around. This kept them at bay. You can also jump up onto a wall or a vehicle to get a little break. A nuisance, but not a big enough negative to say the game was bad because of it. Once you complete the game, they all go away and you can stroll around Gotham in peace.There have been mention of the game freezing. I did experience the Level 12 bug, and had to restart the level which was frustrating as it is a big level. I had the game freeze two other times when I was moving fast in Gotham playing in the open world. No biggie, I just restarted the console and moved on.If your into the Lego series, and have not played this title yet, I highly recommend you pick up a copy.

If you've played any of the previous portable Lego games by Traveler's Tales, you'll feel right at home with Lego Batman 2. The only real changes to the formula this time around are the suits that Batman and Robin can change into to solve some of the many little puzzle elements that you'll encounter throughout the levels, not to mention bosses (Really, I've only beaten Lego Pirates on the PSP/DS/3DS so far, and that game contained no boss battles).Unlike many of the Lego games, all of the levels in Lego Batman 2 follow one big, original storyline. This is also the first game in the series to utilize talking characters. While I don't mind this change at all (Besides, I could hardly understand some cutscenes in previous installments), I found Batman's voice to be very monotone. Thanks to the recent Lego Movie, I know they could do better on that aspect. I will say, though, for a DS title, there's plenty of cutscenes, and in a 3D platformer that's GOOD to boot!The tried-and-true gameplay mechanics fare well here. You run around the environment, smash Lego objects, collect studs, and solve puzzles. The puzzles are usually straightforward, but some can actually make you look around for a bit before finding the answer. There's also a good amount of enemies to beat up, and Batman and Robin would sometimes even pull off a flashy finishing blow.Really, the only problem with the game is that it can come off as repetitive. The gameplay never truly evolves, nor is there a lot of variety. Also, for a game with the subtitle, DC Super Heroes, it's disappointing to see that those heroes show up only at the final level of the game, with the exception of Superman.But overall, if you enjoy playing the Lego games, there's no harm in picking this one up. If you don't like the Lego games, then this won't help. If you're new to the series, and enjoy platformers, then feel free to hop in! You just might like it.

This game is exciting to play and breathtaking to watch.  The basic principle follows the old Space Invaders game.  You control a weapon that slides along the bottom of the screen which shoots upwards at various bad things.  But trying to make a direct comparison is like trying to compare Space Invaders to this game is like trying to compare something to something else that is a zillion times better.The graphics are stunning.  It is almost like watching a fireworks display.  The sound effects and music are well designed and compliment those visuals.  As the game progresses so do the weapons and so do the bad things.  The result is a rise to a fever pitch that drew me in... exactly like the description promised.The only "issue" is that with all the stuff being displayed there are a lot of demands on your tablet.  I tried this on a Kindle Fire and a less powerful generic Android tablet.  The performance was definitely smoother and more responsive on the Kindle.  It was still playable on my less powerful device and there were frustrating moments where my weapon stopped responding while the bad guys kept moving.If you are unsure how this will play on your device then today (when it is free) is a great chance to find out.  Like all apps on Amazon, once you buy it and even if it's free when you do, you own it.  That means even if it doesn't work as well as you would like with the device you have now who can say about the one you'll have tomorrow.

As other reviews have mentioned, the graphics on this game are outstanding ... crisp and colorful. Unfortunately that's the most impressed I was by it. The game play is derivative of any of hundreds of "move back and forth and shoot at dropping things" games. I mostly got over that style of game many years ago. I have my own full size Galaxian stand up arcade game in my game room, and even it doesn't see much action anymore. So I'm probably not the best test subject for this app. Compared to other arcade apps of it's type, it looks great and has acceptable play and mechanics.The one thing I definitely don't like about apps like this on tablets is having a button to move left and a button to move right. I know that there must be an accommodation for the limitations of the device, but I've never found that type of virtual control to be an acceptable substitute for a joy stick. It always annoys me quickly, as I personally always "over steer" with the two button system. Possibly it would be a good idea for me to invest in a device like this:MOGA Mobile Gaming System for Android 2.3+To say this game is like Asteroids is a gross misstatement. Other than the fact rocks drop from the top of the screen, it is nothing like Asteroids. Neither is it like either Galaga or Galaxian, as those games start with grids of opponents and you know what you are up against from the start.In this game rocks drop and at random times ships fly across the screen shooting at you with a spray of weapons fire. Your ship fires continuously, automatically, while you use the left and right button to try to dodge weapons fire and rocks, and position yourself to shoot. At times power-ups appear on the screen, You shoot them and pick them up at the bottom of the screen to do things like change your weapon's style of fire.Overall I give this game 5 stars for graphics, 3 stars for originality, and  4 stars for game play ... averaging out at four stars.The game does have a long list of permissions, but for the most part they involve reading the device so that the game knows how to proceed. There aren't any intrusive permissions.I played this on a Kindle Fire HD 8.9 and had no problems with the app's operation.Recommended for arcade game fans.

If you hunger for mindless arcade shoot-em-up frenzy, enter the Twitch Zone with ALPHA WAVE.  This isn't your father's Space Invaders.  I played for almost an hour- good grief, time sure flies when you are saving... something.  Maybe saving the universe, or saving your dog, or just saving up for a plot.  I did say mindless arcade, right?No Network permission for this one, so no IAPs and one unobtrusive dev website link that I originally thought was merely a stylish dev logo.  USB access is the only privacy, the other open permissions being audio control and sleep prevention (well, I should be sleeping, so I guess it works).  The intro music is very atmospheric, and the rest of the action soundtrack and sfx melded nicely with gameplay without being distracting.  The graphics won't blow your socks off, but seamless eye candy in any of the graphics settings, low, medium , or high.  I played with all three settings,  and frankly I only noticed a subtle, crisper difference.  In-game achievments, score ranking, social links in a corner (Google+, FB, and Twitter), three different play environments with their own style of alien baddies (I liked the Blackhole's saucers the most), and when all done, the back-key exits cleanly.Very simple horizontal shooter for kids and adults who want to get their PWN Zen on.  The basic shooting is automatic,  leaving your two thumbs to move back and forth, thumping a bomb or hyper powerup icon to make pretty bang bang.  The loading screen is rather slow, but once you get past that snooze fest, the action is fluid even on the most frantic waves.  ALPHA WAVE uses a health percentage system, which you can add to with red cross drops, and the overall action routine can be monotonous for some, magnificent for others, wave levels increasing without pause until you face the "Bad Daddy" Darkstar for the final win.  There is a pause button in the upper right for "real life" moments.3 different laser weapons although you will quickly realize two of the three are kinda bleah in comparison.  And of course the score multipler that racks up with continuous kills, each series giving you a ranking from OK to Great! to the max OMG.  When finally dead, if you got one of the top 3 scores, you can put your name in so you can brag to yourself how you really topped you... uh, or put your cat's name instead.For a straight-up shooter, for some this will be too delightful, for others too simple.  All depends on how Zen you want your Encounters of the Third Kind to be.

Pros:Excellent gaming engine with the graphical capability to play pretty advanced gamesHigh-quality OLED touchscreenDual analog sticksEasy PSN functionality and download supportBackwards compatible with PSP and PS1 gamesRegion free gamesCons:Lack of good gamesNo internal memory and expensive proprietary memory cardsPortability issuesBackwards compatibility only applies on digital games purchased through the PSNThe PS Vita is an excellent system marred by only a few design flaws. The best part of the hardware for me is the dual analog sticks. These are a major bonus since fpss basically require them nowadays. Not only are there two of them, they are also of excellent quality. One of the things I always disliked about the PSP was the analog stick that was flat to the surface and rather difficult to use. The 3DS has copied this design, although they made it more ergonomically comfortable. The Vita however, has two that stick out from the system, just like on the PS3 remote, allowing much greater control and ease of movement. There are sensitivity issues since the sticks are smaller than their PS3 equivalents, but once you adapt to it the controls are almost as easy to use.The second best thing about the Vita is the OLED touchscreen. This touchscreen is absolutely beautiful and has excellent resolution. I thought the touchscreen aspect was just a gimmick, but some of the games have made excellent use of it allowing them to compensate for not having back bumpers (L2/R2 buttons). Well, technically they do have those in the rear touchpad, but it is so touchy and difficult to use that it might as well not exist. The big plus of this touchscreen is that it is much more sensitive and reliable than the 3DS's. You can type with fair accuracy using only your finger, and responses on one section of the screen rarely result in unexpected reactions from another. It does tend to make the screen oily, but that's the price you pay for all touchscreens.The graphics on the system are amazing, although all that talk of them being almost as good as the PS3 is garbage. They fit comfortably between the PS2 and PS3 level of graphics, with the result probably being a bit closer to the Wii than the PS3. With the smaller screen it is easier to hide bad texture maps and glitches. That doesn't take anything away from the system. On the small screen those graphics look amazing. I'm not sure where these graphics fit when compared to the 3DS, but they are definitely an improvement. It's hard to think of any 3DS games with high graphical requirements since they tend to aim for cartoony and exaggerated worlds, but I can't remember any that even come close to pulling off Uncharted: Golden Abyss. At a guess, I'd say that the 3DS reproduces approximately the same graphics as a PS2 (as can be seen by their virtually unchanged ports of PS2 games) while the Vita is a bit higher (as seen by their improved ports of PS2 games). The difference is more one of style than capability, with Sony focusing on realistic games that show off their graphics engine while Nintendo does what they usually do and try to create fun, cartoony games. The graphics leap between the 3DS and the Vita just isn't that high. Certainly not enough to recommend getting a Vita on that score alone. The biggest advantage they have graphically is that their screen is just better quality, and doesn't waste energy on 3D that nobody uses.I've heard some complaints about battery life but I don't know what all the fuss is about. My Vita plays for about five hours without recharging, which is a good hour or two longer than my 3DS does. I appreciate that the older systems lasted longer but that was because they had less graphics-intensive games. You can still play those games so it isn't a problem. A DS game on the 3DS can last all day, and playing a PSP game on the Vita is likewise. The Vita also has an excellent sleep mode. I found that the system drains far less quickly when asleep than the 3DS does. Besides, it was really only the DS generation of games that worked like that. Previous systems often had terrible battery life (see the two-hour long Game Gear).The layout of the Vita is basically that of a Playstation controller with a big screen in the middle. The two analog sticks are in the proper places and are reasonably sensitive. The PS button has been moved to the left corner and glows when the game is on. The start and select buttons have become a bit crummy since you have to push at quite a difficult angle to get them to go down. The two bumper bars are very responsive, and look quite stylish. The rear touchpad is useless. Comfort-wise the system is very nice, fitting neatly into your hand with some nice pads at the back to support your grip. The system is somewhat heavy, but that's never been a problem for me. The game does suffer dramatically in portability when compared to its competition. Not only is it larger than the 3DS-XL (or the PSP for that matter), it is also bumpier and less protected. With no DS clamshell front to protect it the Vita's screen is dangerously exposed to sharp knocks. I can also assure you that the two analog sticks, despite making gameplay amazing, mean that the Vita will never comfortably fit into anyone's pocket. There are cases for it that will alleviate the protection issue, but the best that you can do is carry it in your jacket. And for some people that just isn't enough. It all depends how you use it.Software-wise the Vita comes preinstalled with some basic programs of varied utility. The main screen is an ugly series of icons accessed by the touchscreen. Sony is trying to make their system into a phone and I don't understand why. Still, it functions well enough. The browser still sucks and the maps app isn't particularly helpful. Due to the presence of a touchscreen the messages app has become functional. The PSN is extremely useful. In terms of new software the main addition is Near. It's trying to do what Streetpass does, but it does it badly. All you can do with it is see what people in your city are playing. It connects through 3G so it bases its records of local Vita users on the last location they signed in on. No, it doesn't continue to sync with other devices when you put it on sleep mode. That'd just be silly. It isn't like the 3DS which communicates with other consoles via wifi.Hardware-wise the only major problem is the proprietary memory cards, which are so obviously money-grabbing as to be insulting. Especially given the Vita's emphasis on downloadable content this is just a kick in the teeth for gamers. After all, some of their games aren't even available in physical copies. And if you want to download any PS1 or PSP games (which look amazing on the new screen btw) then you're equally screwed. Worst of all, since there is no internal memory you need to buy one of these cards to play any game, whether or not you intend to download games. And a good card can cost half as much as the system itself. It's disgraceful.Another silly feature is the 3G option. There's no point to having this since there aren't many online games for the Vita, and most of the other internet functions will require you to connect to a more reliable wifi hub anyway. 3G is expensive and difficult to arrange with your local provider. Maybe this isn't the case in Japan, but it is in the US. And of course, even if you get service it isn't going to be as good as wifi anyway. Besides, what's the point of playing online games outside anyway? When you're in public you can't exactly shout into your mic to inform your teammates that they're being morons. Not that you could do that anyway since the Vita only supports 3G for turn-based combat and Near. Any first-person shooters will have to find some wifi. 3G also drains your battery in a heartbeat. Unless you live in an area that has no broadband internet connection but still gets 3G I can't see the point of it.To be perfectly honest, even this isn't enough to prevent people from buying the system. What might serve as more of a deterrent is the games catalog. The Vita has been out for two years but is still suffering from a lack of truly great games. The best new games to come out thus far areUncharted: Golden AbyssandAssassin's Creed III: Liberation. They also gave Persona 4 an awesome port calledPersona 4: Golden. All of these games came out in the first year, when enthusiasm for the new system was still fresh. There has been little since. The 3DS was suffering from this too until fairly recently, with the most popular games being ports from older systems likeThe Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time,Tales of the Abyss, andStar Fox 64. Now the 3DS is picking up steam withFire Emblem: Awakening,Pokémon X and Y,The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds, andShin Megami Tensei IV, but the Vita seems stalled.One of the major pluses of the system though is its easy access to the PSN. A gigantic library of PS1 and PSP games are available for download. Yes, these were available before, but only for the PSP. Now you can access them on the Vita's high def screen and use dual analog sticks for control. This can be really helpful even on PSP games that have replaced the right analog stick with the top bumpers. There are also demos and free content that adds greatly to the experience. Much better than Nintendo's eShop. Or maybe that's just the opinion of someone used to the PSN. Like the PS3 games are region-free, though DLC is region locked. You can also have only one account connected to your Vita which means no more copying games from different accounts. You have to reformat the card every time you change.To sum up: I really like the Vita. On a strictly hardware level the Vita is clearly superior to its closest competitor (the 3DS), even if that system has advantages when it comes to portability and convenience. Its biggest problem is the lack of good games, and that's hardly the fault of the hardware. Like the 3DS it's had a slow start, but hopefully it will pick up now that the price has gone down and a new and cheaper model has been released. PS4 functionality should also help them. If you're willing to bet on future successes then this system is well worth it and the backlog of PS1/PSP games should keep you occupied for quite a while. If you're waiting for that one brilliant game that makes the system worth buying... it hasn't come yet. But hopefully it will soon. If you are planning on buying this system though go for the wifi only version unless you can find this one cheaper. 3G support offers nothing.

Okay I picked up a Vita as my PS4 Companion, I have been talking about getting one for years but with the Gamestop 50% more trade in credit this week I just pawned off a ton of my PS3 games and decided to pick one up.First OffThis is a very impressive hand held system, completely blows away any other hand held in the market. the graphics are insanely good and the controls are amazing. Mix that with Netflix and Hulu on board and I am in heaven. except a couple things that make me wonder what the hell Sony was thinking.You can not deny it when you first turn it on and load up your first game ( KillZone mercenary ) And it looks just as good as your PS3 and handles just as well also. This is a solid system that has been over shadowed by less worthy hand held systems. Then you head over and link it up to your PS4 as a second screen to get some game time (Second Son ) in your front room while the PS4 is in the bedroom. heavy solid built and worth every penny.Buy my problem is that we have 2 people who use the PSN account in my house ( guessing some people have more ) and you find out that in order to let two people use a PSV ( each on their own account ) you have to have 2 memory cards. each memory card is tied to an account and this is just part of the problem.If you could use a standard SD card like every other device on the market this would be easy. but instead you are locked into a proprietary Sony SD card and the prices are insane for these cards. A 4GB card will only hold at most 2 small games since each game runs in the MB's I mean come on the graphics are AMAZING.I would need at least a 32 GB card and that will cost you around $65-$75+ especially since I am a PS Plus member and look forward to my free monthly games which are digital downloads and will eat up space on the memory card. you can run down to any wall-mart or even Walgreen and pick up a standard 32 GB SD card for about $20-$25 these days. so the markup on the Sony card is just insane !It is simply a defense tactic ( from piracy )  that should have never happened from Sony. I get you want it tied down so people can not copy the games but there are much better ways as far as ( coding the OS ) is concerned to accomplish this without making people regret the purchase.Don't get me wrong I love the PSV so far and am very glad I decided to get one, but I regret not reading more about the memory card issue before I purchased it now.On top of this why make it so insanely difficult for your core customers ? The PSN account is a monthly & annual revenue stream if people decided to purchase a subscription from you they are dedicated to your system. Sony is pretty much making it hard for the people who actually support them. This is one of the most asinine decisions I have seen and seems more like a Microsoft or Apple move and I just can not figure out why they would do it without realizing the consequences of it actually pushing more customers away than anything else.User experience is just as important as anything else in a gaming market. and if people feel they are locked out or not able to use a system the way it was intended then that is a problem and seems more like a ( Ouya ) move.

Do NOT fall prey to crap people who have never had/seen a Vita say. Everything about the system is perfect. It seems to be about as powerful as a Ps3. When I first put in Killzone: Mercenary I was in utter disbelief that a hand-held could ever look THAT good. It doesn't just look good either, the controls are fantastic and smooth. It is really like a mini dualshock controller. It's surprisingly comfortable, and the two joysticks really define the experience and put it on that next level far beyond the PSP. The screen is absolutely beautiful. I've never been a fan of touchscreens, but this one has changed my mind. The screen is large, bright, vibrant, and unbelievably clear. It looks better than my TV. It is insanely responsive too, I can hover my finger over it and it will sense it. The touch controls are really implemented well in the menus and games. You close applications by "tearing" them off the screen, which never gets old. Even the speakers aren't terrible, although I would highly recommend you use headphones to truly immerse yourself.The only way I can figure why the sales are less than desirable is because most people simply do not know how fantastic the Vita is. The Vita is a godsend to people who love playing classics and retro games. Many fantastic PsOne games are available in the store, such as Final Fantasy VII and VIII, Resident Evil 1, 2, and 3, and so forth. Most of them are between $8-10 which is a bargain because you can download it on the Ps3 AND Vita, so you can play them at home or on the go. That's not even the coolest part. You can send your save data to and from the Ps3 to your Vita, so you can continue the same play-through anywhere. Other newer games are available with a "cross-buy" option where you pay for the Ps3 version of a game, and you get the Vita version free. There is also a "cross-play" section. Those work similarly to the PsOne games and allow you to transfer your saves as well. The Vita's emulator is awesome too, as it lets you smooth graphics of older games or assign buttons or the rear touch pad how you'd like. You can also buy PSP games from PSN to play on the Vita, which is great since I missed out on plenty of great PSP games. Being able to play Metal Gear Solid: Peacewalker with a second joystick is awesome. Vita exclusives are the only lacking area; however, the quality is much higher than you would expect since most would be considered spin-offs. Killzone, Assassin's Creed, Resistance, Uncharted, Batman, and more have all graced the Vita, and are surprisingly good. There are plenty of games to play while waiting on more Vita exclusives. Pretty much everyone that says "The Vita has no games" has never had one. There are over one thousand available on PSN, alongside the hard-copy games.Another common criticism is price. It may seem high, but you get what you pay for, and more. Take a chance and get a Vita. You won't be disappointed. Sales will pick up as the price falls, and more games will be available. It's just having a slow start, kind of like the Ps3, which many people thought was overpriced. Sony's only mistake with the Vita is the lack of advertising. Most of the best things about the Vita I found out myself after owning one and playing/experimenting with it. Such as the save transferring I mentioned earlier, and being able to turn it off in the middle of ANYTHING and when you fire it back up it is right where you left off, which is the best thing I have ever seen on a handheld. There's no trying to hurry and save or closing applications when you reach your destination. Just turn it off. I think most people aren't willing to shell out the money for the Vita simply because it is a handheld, and the implied limitations that word brings. Those limitations aren't there, though. You aren't just getting a good handheld, you're getting a good console, period.

HardwareAs with the standard PlayStation 3 wireless controllers (Sixaxis, DualShock 3), both the main PlayStation Move motion controller and the PlayStation Move navigation controller use Bluetooth 2.0 wireless radio communication, and an internal lithium-ion battery[6] which is charged via a USB Mini-B port on the controller.[12] On the PlayStation 3, up to four Move controllers can be used at once[13] (four Move motion controllers,[14] or two Move motion controllers and two Move navigation controllers[15]).Motion controller[edit]The primary component of PlayStation Move, the PlayStation Move motion controller (CECH-ZCM1E) is a wand controller which allows the user to interact with the console through motion and position in front of a PlayStation camera.[1]TechnologyThe PlayStation Move motion controller features an orb at the head which can glow in any of a full range of colors using RGB light-emitting diodes (LEDs).[16] Based on the colors in the user environment captured by the camera, the system dynamically selects an orb color that can be distinguished from the rest of the scene. The colored light serves as an active marker, the position of which can be tracked along the image plane by the camera.The uniform spherical shape and known size of the light also allows the system to simply determine the controller's distance from the camera through the light's image size, thus enabling the controller's position to be tracked in three dimensions[18][19] with high precision and accuracy.The simple sphere-based distance calculation allows the controller to operate with minimal processing latency,[22] as opposed to other camera-based control techniques on the PlayStation 3.A pair of inertial sensors inside the controller, a three-axis linear accelerometer and a three-axis angular rate sensor, are used to track rotation as well as overall motion. An internal magnetometer is also used for calibrating the controller's orientation against the Earth's magnetic field to help correct against cumulative error (drift) by the inertial sensors.[24] In addition, an internal temperature sensor is used to adjust the inertial sensor readings against temperature effects.[25] The inertial sensors can be used for dead reckoning in cases which the camera tracking is insufficient, such as when the controller is obscured behind the player's back.[16]The controller face features a large oblong primary button (Move), surrounded by small action buttons (Triangle, Circle, Cross, Square), and with a regular-sized PS button beneath, arranged in a similar configuration as on the Blu-ray Disc Remote Control. On the left and right side of the controller is a Select and Start button, respectively. On the underside is an analog trigger (T). On the tail end of the controller is the wrist strap, USB port, and extension port.The motion controller features vibration-based haptic technology. In addition to providing a tracking reference, the controller's orb light can be used to provide visual feedback, simulating aesthetic effects such as the muzzle flash of a gun, or the paint on a brush.Using different orb colors for each controller, up to four motion controllers can be tracked at once on the PlayStation Demonstrations for the controller have featured activities using a single motion controller, as well as those in which the user wields two motion controllers, with one in each hand. To minimize the cost of entry, Sony stated that all launch titles for PlayStation Move would be playable[dated info] with one motion controller, with enhanced options available for multiple motion controllers.On the PlayStation 3, image processing for PlayStation Move is performed in the console's Cell microprocessor. According to Sony, use of the motion-tracking library entails some Synergistic Processing Unit (SPU) overhead as well an impact on memory, though the company states that the effects will be minimized.[31] According to Move motion controller co-designer Anton Mikhailov, the library uses 1-2 megabytes of system memory.

Having this grip slightly improves my gaming experience with the PS Vita, as my large hands get cramped within 10 minutes of playing any game.  While I was initially worried with the design since the Vita was only being held in place by a millimeter's worth of plastic at the top and bottom, my mind was at ease after a month's worth of use without the Vita falling out, even when I swung it by the handle while walking around.  However, there is one glaring issue for adult hands: The handle is too narrow, with very little to fill your palm while gripping it.  Let me paint you a picture: When you hold an Xbox 360 controller, your fingers naturally curl around each side of the controller, allowing you to rest your fifth and fourth finger on the back of the controller, with the rest of the handles filling your palm.  Now imagine if you took 1/2 of the volume of the plastic out of each handle to make this PS Vita grip and the open grips are too far down and you cannot reach the bumper buttons.  So you have to move your hand up, and now your fingers are pushing against the back touch pad of the Vita.  There's no winning in this situation:  You either have to grip the back of the vita or grip the bottom of the handles and not be able to reach the bumpers.  The only reason this grip adds comfort is that it provides just a bit more plastic to fill in your palms and give you something to hold on to.  On games that don't require the bumper, it feels just a bit better.  To its benefit, I was able to finish a remote play (via PS4) of the entire single player campaign of Call of Duty: Ghosts by playing 1-hour spurts before my hand started cramping.  When playing Pixel Junk Monsters HD, I am able to play for two hours or more since I can use the actual grips (no need to reach for the bumpers).  If you're an adult deciding on a purchase for yourself, find an extension/grip that offers a little more padding and girth.  In the end, this does provide more comfort than using the Vita on its own, so I will give it a 3/5 rating.

Sleeping Dogs is EXACTLY that kind of game. I'm nearing the completion (after letting this game sit for a while) and I feel I've played enough to give my opinion on Likes and Dislikes.Likes: Good story, lots of content and side activities to keep you busy for a while. The Kung-Fu fighting can be pretty fun and rewarding. I know other reviewers have argued this isn't a GTA clone, but lets be honest here IT IS. Unless you consider driving on the left hand side of the road qualifies as being different, then I must be missing something. Look it's not a bad thing, open world games are among the best (in my opinion). Street races are equally bad (if not worse) and I've completed all but a couple of motorcycle races. Just an Epic and embarrassing failure for the game designers here. The blind fore system in combat is also terrible. It would be nice to have some kind of aiming mechanism to go with firing from cover, but there isn't. Just watch for where the bullets are hitting and try to judge. Hopefully you can do this before you run out of bullets.I can't say I would recommend buying this game, but if you can get it for free I would say do so. Sleeping Dogs is one of those games you play and wonder, "Why was this not more popular?" Think of it as GTA set in Asia.SD has a great story. You play an undercover cop who's just returned from the US and infiltrates the Hong Kong triad. However as you progress through the game, your character starts to wonder where his loyalties should really be placed. Add to the excellent story, there're some excellent voice acting by a surprising number of A-list actors.The main missions are well thought out and appropriate to the story. There are also dozens of side missions that increase your cop ranking or fighting skills which gain you abilities. There are also Face missions that grant you other bonuses. The fighting is a great bonus and one that I really enjoyed - you get to fight large groups of enemies and use combinations to take them down Bruce Lee style. Alternatively you can pick up a weapon (cleaver, knife, gun, etc) and start blasting away...your choice. You can also (a la GTA) steal/car jack cars but if you do, the HKPD will be on your trail.Along the way, you collect cars, clothing, and apartments as you gain money, influence, and progress through the main story.CONSProbably the biggest reason why this game didn't do better are the graphics. They're dated.Typical to 99% of XBox games, very sparce documentation. I didn't find out until the end of the game that you could hire a taxi by holding the Y key and be transported immediately to a desired destination. Would have saved me a lot of time driving to/from different locations.All in all, a great game and one that I'm thankful I got to play.

The title says it all. Think GTA-style in a more realistic and brutal environment based in Hong Kong, China without the silly mocking of other media that the GTA series is known for. This is a solid game that doesn't waste time telling jokes.

While it doesn't have the crazy replay ability of other games in it's genre (I'm looking at you, Grand Theft Auto), Sleeping Dogs is an incredible experience (until you finish it, more on that later). No, it's not GTA or Saints Row, nor is it trying to be. Sleeping Dogs has a more theatrical and story driven feeling to it than other open city games. Taking place in Hong Kong, the game follows Detective Way Shen, an undercover officer who is instructed to infiltrate and become a member of the Triads, Hong Kong's most elite gangsters. What follows is Way battling with his internal and external struggles with both the law and the Triads as he moves up the ranks. The story really pulls you in and you start to care for Way as you learn more about him and his past. The cinematics and writing rivals Red Dead Redemption (really good).Gameplay is most similar to the Batman Arkham series; mashing buttons, doing blocks, and performing crazy combos. Sleeping Dogs incorporates both martial arts and standard street brawling that is brutal to watch (snapping peoples limbs and watching them react to it is extremely well done). Also included is minor gunplay and driving, but the star of the show is really brawling with the environment. Special environmental attacks have been scattered all around the city, such as being able to throw foes into garbage cans, slamming them into aquariums, and face first slams into electrical appliances. I really liked these as they help balance the odds. The driving is very arcady, taking from the Need for Speed series, and is far more realistic compared to GTA in that the more reckless you become, the more responsive the police are.However, once you beat the game it offers little to nothing to keep you playing. Sure, you can go find the rest of the collectables scattered around the world, but that's it. I really would've liked something after the main story. Also, there is ZERO multiplayer. Having an open world to fool around with is always better with other people. This was a huge missed opportunity.Despite this, Sleeping Dogs is still a great underrated game that is worthy of your time.

Hands down better fighting than any Rockstar effort to date! Even in GTAV you just shoot stuff and run away. This game has a deep melee combat system that makes sense and is fun to play around with. Elbow strikes, flying side kicks, spin heels and endless environmental effects (like throwing guys into wood chippers) made this game a ton of fun. All of the side missions were legit - good car and motorcycle races, getting your date on (nothing like karaoke and shaggin), helping out friends with random stuff. One minute a cleaver wielding old lady is chopping arms off and the next you are racing a moped down a crowded staircase to help trace water lines for smuggling. Bottom line, it is fun to play and has a great story.

I'll start off by saying that at the time of this review I have played GTA5 before I played Sleeping Dogs. It's not fair to compare them because of budget and Sleeping Dogs was released a year before. I got it as a free download from Xbox Live. After letting it sit on my hard drive for a couple months I thought I'd give it a shot.First off, let's be clear. This is definitely a Hong Kong knock off of GTA, as others have stated. But don't let that deter you from playing this game. I didn't have many expectations when I started playing this game but I have been pleasantly surprised. This game is extremely fun.The big improvement from the GTA series is the combat. I have read that others compare it to the Batman Arkham series, which I have not played. Wherever it's taken from, it is so much fun. It makes me feel like a kung fu master. The combat is primarily hand-to-hang (or foot-to-face!) kung fu based, instead of gun based. It never gets old throwing out a few punches and then finishing off a guy with a Chuck Norris-like roundhouse kick to the face. Simply put, the combat is so much fun that I've decided to buy the Batman Arkham series.The graphics aren't terrible, but they're nothing spectacular. I was actually expecting them to be worse than what they were. It seems like every year the graphics improve 5 years over the previous year's games so after seeing GTA in 2014, I was expecting stick figures in Sleeping Dogs. The good thing about a game like this is that there is so much action that I don't have time to sit and look at the texture on a trash can in a park.The overall gameplay is quite fun. If you like GTA, you will like this. At the time of this review, Sleeping Dogs is available on Amazon for $15. It is definitely worth that! I highly recommend trying this game out!

That's what I'd say about this game. I know that many people enjoyed it and before you accuse me of the average "Oh, you only like generic Call of Duty games", I'd like to say it's the exact opposite. I've played a wide variety of games and usually stick to singleplayer open-world ones, and I can definitely say that this game is just average. Nothing special or as crazy as most people claim it to be. Again, this is just my opinion and not fact, I certainly hope you'll enjoy it more than I did. But here's what I thought (no spoilers).LOCATION:Sleeping Dogs has a unique environment, I'll give you that. Aside from the regular American cities, the location is a remodeled version of Hong Kong, and it's unique to see the markets, sights, lifestyle, I'll say that. But that's about the only thing this game has going to make it stand out.COMBAT:Being in Hong Kong, it would just be wrong to not include focus on hand-to-hand combat. Which it does! I can appreciate that it tries to try something new in open world and focus on combat. While certainly it's there and is more or less solid, and more unique button mashing combos can be unlocked by leveling up and finding jade statues, the combat doesn't.. 'flow'. It doesn't feel to flow in flawlessly like games such as Batman: Arkham City. It's actually basic. Press Y to counter an enemy when he glows red. There are mainly three or four different types of enemies in hand-to-hand. They each seem to awkwardly stand there and take turns attacking you. While it it is fun for a little while, you'll soon realize it's nothing that again, 'flows'.It also has some gun combat but it's just boring and poorly done. The shooting levels are just boring. Too easy even on hard difficulties.MOVEMENT/DRIVING:While freerunning is also good, it's nothing challenging. Just press A when approaching an obstacle to vault over it, miss you trip but still make it over slower. But the driving is just awful. The camera is the most awkward I've seen and doesn't follow. Try to move it while driving, you'll have a hard time. It will fling back to the head and often seems to have a mind of its own. Cars also drive too easy.. Press a single button and you perfectly drift? Where's the challenge in that? People that like challenging racing games with unique controls won't appreciate the driving.STORY/CHARACTERS:Possibly the thing I disagree with most on. Let me sum it up like this: It's nothing special! It's really short for starters, and it's just really predictable. I saw things coming from a mile away. It never tries to take unexpected events. It only gets interesting in the end, and even then it stays predictable. Voice acting is decent, but characters are about as average as the story. While some found it amazing, I've seen enough cop movies and games and whatnot to see things coming from a mile away, and if you're in the same boat me as you will as well.SIDE ACTIVITIES:While there are a few unique ones to match the location like cock fighting, the rest are just your average side activities. Stranger meets, drug busts, etc. And if you're wondering, they're nothing special and not really interesting nor challenging. They're really repetitive and are not really fun to do.I 100% the game, so I can honestly say that this game is average. I play lots of varies games, mainly open world so I think that I can safely say so. I'd give it a 3/5.If you're a parent getting this for your kid, it's really bloody and full of gore, just so you know.

Games like Grand Theft Auto and Saints Row get most of the attention, but this game (which originally was part of the True Crime series, to be named True Crime: Hong Kong, was canceled and the rights picked up by Square Enix, and rebranded Sleeping Dogs) is an incredible amount of fun to play in its own right.The main character, Wei Shen, comes over from the US to help the cops, and it turns into a very twisted, awesome story in which lines are crossed and friends end up being betrayed (or killed).  The ending of the Triad storyline, especially, is incredibly satisfying, which I won't spoil but is great :)The "story" is made up of the aformentioned Triad storylines and as well as the Cop storyline (Triad shows up as Green on your map, Cop ones are blue).  No mission is truly impossible or controller smashing difficult (something that Grand Theft Auto IV definitely can't claim), but some are challenging enough where if you do not obtain the upgrades from the health shrines (increases your max health) or increase your face meter (which bestows buffs/benefits to Wei) that you CAN die if you're reckless.For those "trophy hunters" out there, this is also a VERY easy platinum, the only frustrating part is obtaining the Gold for the "Pure Gold" trophy, as it requires you to win $1M gambling, and only one cockfight will give you the ability to bet enough to do this, and it's COMPLETELY RANDOM.  Meaning, you better save before each attempt.  It took me 2 hours of grinding before I finally achieved enough wins to earn the $1M.  Everything else (relatively speaking) is a piece of cake.I really could not find a reason to drop a star on this game at all.  In over 30 hours of gameplay, it never froze my PS3 once.  I cannot say that, honestly, about any other PS3 game I have played (for comparison, Fallout 3 and New Vegas, Skyrim and Borderlands 2 have all done it more then 5 times each).  The game rarely stutters or slows.  The radio stations are nice and varies.  The combat is fluid and adds a lot of room for improvisation.  Maybe the only gripe (if I had bought this brand new) is the story parts end up being a little short, so if that's all you are playing it for, that might disappoint you a bit.  If you intend to do everything, you will definitely get your money's worth especially at the current price point ($14.99 or less).Finally, the language is DEFINITELY bad in this game (Including words that Grand Theft Auto V didn't use, and I thought THAT game was bad enough).  If that's something that's a turn off, then I'd look elsewhere.  The game definitely lives up to its mature rating on the box.

Sleeping Dogs is an amazing game. While it may not be perfect, I'd consider it a must-have for any gamer.Story: 4.5/5You play as Wei Shen, an undercover cop who's sent to take down one of Hong Kong's triads from within. This game has a gripping story that makes you want to keep playing the next mission to progress. Every mission holds great plot significance; no "filler missions" here. If I had any complaints, it would be that almost every time you meet up with your police force members, it's the same old "we should pull you out" business, making these cutscenes predictable and annoying. The game's ending is somewhat disappointing, considering everything that led up to it.Gameplay: 4.5/5There's quite a bit to do in Sleeping Dogs. Combat starts off simple but grows in complexity as you learn new moves by collecting jade statues and leveling up. You can perform basic combos, execute grab attacks, and use environmental objects for instant finishers. Besides hand-to-hand exchanges, there are also gun fights. The shooting mechanics in this game work, but they aren't the best; for example, accuracy is a small issue since you can't scope in further. The game makes up for this by throwing in a slow-motion system when you vault over cover, always making you feel like a boss. Combat never grows tedious because the developers knew how to space it out appropriately.  I'll go ahead and say that driving in this game is INSANELY fun. The driving controls are very responsive, and Sleeping Dogs even spices up car navigation with some action. You can ram into other vehicles, leap from your current vehicle and hijack one in front of you, and shoot pursuers as you drive. Blowing up the tires of other vehicles never grows old. Lastly, there are chase sequences, which aren't really chases. You'll run after someone trying to escape, vaulting and climbing over obstacles as you go. I say these aren't really chases because the point where you catch your target is predetermined. It's really more like just keeping up with them until you get to the destination, removing the thrill and sense of urgency that chase sequences should elicit. One small complaint I have is that earning points for police upgrades and increasing your Face Level is far too easy, and you'll likely be maxed out on those 75% through the game. Triad points are much more scarce since you can only earn them through the main missions. Some things I would like to have seen that weren't included are stealth sections and more parkour moves (it's basically just vaulting and climbing), but I'm still happy with the gameplay that's present.Side activities: 4/5There's plenty to do in Sleeping Dogs outside of your main missions. Collecting and returning Jade Statues to your dojo unlocks new moves. Praying at health shrines increases your maximum health. By opening lockboxes, you obtain cash. Each collectible serves a real purpose instead of just being for trophies/achievements. Throughout the game, there will also be Favors, which you can complete to increase your Face Level for bonuses. Drug Busts involve beating up a group of thugs, hacking a security camera, and using that camera to apprehend a drug dealer. A few times, you can can go on dates with girls to unlock perks like being able to see collectibles on your map. There are side activities that can be repeated to an extent, like finding and selling marked cars and harassing debtors. Also, unmarked world events crop up if you're in their immediate vicinity. And of course, what good would earning cash be if you had nothing to spend it on? There are plenty of cars to buy and even more clothes. Wearing clothes of a certain set provide bonuses like earning extra XP and dealing more damage. Then there are secret vendors who will sell upgrades to your apartments. Some gripes I had with the side activities are that opening lockboxes becomes very tiresome because of a combination-finding minigame and that side missions simply aren't fun sometimes. There are 20 car deliveries, which grow very old very fast, and Favors are often short but too similar to some you've done before.Setting/atmosphere: 5/5Hong Kong is a joy to explore. There's a very authentic feel. You'll hear Chinese and English dialogue mixed beautifully together, and you'll find Chinese and American songs on the radio as you drive around. Food vendors are all over the place, providing you with stat boosts. You can even sing karaoke! Overall, there's so much detail here that you can't help but feel like you're really in Hong Kong. The voice actor for Wei Shen does an amazing job. I find it odd, though, that he never actually speaks Chinese, but it is what it is.Technical side: 4.5/5For the most part, the game performs excellently. There are some outstanding issues I should point out, however. It's not unusual for the sound to turn off just for a brief moment when you crash violently or when you enter slow motion sometimes. And no, this is not intentional-it's a bug. The cutscenes are a little choppy, but it's not unbearable. Some bad pop-in is noticeable at times.Overall: 4.5/5Sleeping Dogs is an incredible experience that's very deserving of your time. It's not especially long for an open world game, taking a completionist about 30 hours to beat. At any price $20 and below, this game is a steal. Don't miss out!

I purchased this game because of all the rave reviews and found to my disappointment that it was not all that.First, there was a lot of hoopla regarding the graphics. The graphics in this game is a mixed bag. The in-game graphics is okay actually. But it is not exceptional in my opinion. In one professional review it was said that the graphics in this game is one of the best on the Playstation 3. If I were to compare this to other games such as Uncharted, it would not even be on the same level graphics-wise. But then these are two totally different games so I will compare it to Zelda: Twilight Princess. ZTP blows this game away. Then there is the cutscene animations. They are terrible. They look like Saturday morning cartoons. Seriously, I am not joking. Obviously two different groups created the in-game animations and the cutscene animations.The music was highly rated in professional reviews due to a great composer being in involved with this game. I agree it is good. But I don't think that it exceptional. Zelda had better soundtracks than this game. And I can say that even the old Zelda: Windwaker had a better and interesting soundtrack.One thing that Ni No Kuni has though that Zelda does not have is in-game dialogue by the characters. And they are actually well done. But again, nothing exceptional. I played it under the English speech setting so it was an American voice-over. The actor did a decent job. But why did they do away with the speech for most of the game? Most of it involves reading texts with a silly sound effect to go with it.Story-wise, this game did not captivate me. It was too simplistic and rather corny. I guess that it is due to the type of anime this is. I found it to be rather girly and childish. This game is definitely for the kids. But I don't know if the kids would stick with this game due to the simplistic nature of the story and constant text reading. To give you an idea of what these dialogues are about, in one you spend a few minutes just discussing about a wand that you need to replace the twig you are using in its place. And that discussion runs on over how it is so special and that you need to test it in a big place because such a special wand needs a special place to test its special powers. And that goes on and on. And you can't choose what to say or how to respond. At least in games such as Mass Effect, you can choose what you are going to say. Here, it is all just boring repetitive dialogues. What makes it irritating is the canned Scottish accent that the side-kick Drippy uses.The combat is not like what I am used to in that it is not truly real-time combat in that it is a hybrid system in which is more of the usual RPG spell casting and turn-based stick bashing with a little freedom of movement added in. If you like Final Fantasy, you will feel at home with this game.Finally, the game play, the most important aspect to any video game, is not there for me. I found it rather boring and tedious. Given how dragged and artificially stretched out the dialogue texts are, I can see how this game will last you easily 40 hours or more. The story itself could probably fit in a 30 minute show. After a while of playing this, I felt like I was in a kiddie game and had to stop and put in a different game to get me out of that funk. This game is obviously for the anime fans, particularly Ghibli fanboys who raved so much about this game. Nothing wrong with that. To each his own. But this game is just not my cup of tea.As to those who fanboys who say that I should give it at least 3 stars because it is not a terrible game, I say to you, you got the ratings system wrong. 3 stars means that you like it. I did not like this game at all. As I have stated, it is a boring game. Now, maybe a ten year old would probably enjoy it. But not all of them would like it due to the dragging nature of this game. I'm sure that there will be fanboys bashing my review but to all of you who are reading these reviews to decided whether to purchase this game or not, you have been warned. This review is not for the fanboys. It is for those like myself who have been swayed by fanboy reviews and regretted it.

By all appearances, I should love this game. It has an endearing personality, has elements of classic RPGs, and the combat is reminiscent of Pokemon. I really wanted to like this game. I rarely quit games, but after about 17 hours into the game, I cannot go further.I’ll begin with the obvious strength of Ni No Kuni. The overall presentation of the game is phenomenal. The menus are slick, the music is top-notch, and the writing is witty. The game does come off as childish, but I thought it added much to its own personality.However, once the smoke clears and the reality sets in, I started to realize many of the games shortcomings. First, the beginning of the game is excruciatingly boring. The beginning is riddled with cutscenes, hand-holding gameplay, basic combat, etc. It isn’t until about 6 hours in until the game begins to pick up.The game has two glaring flaws, the story and the combat. The story begins as a heartwarming tale of a son trying to save his mother. Aside from that, there isn’t much meat to the story. The characters aside from your trusty sidekick Drippy are extremely bland and one-dimensional. The combat borrows much from that of Pokemon, but lacks any of the fun strategy elements of the Pokemon games. There is a lot of just mashing the attack button during the wild battles. Many of the combat’s problems are more noticeable during boss battles. While it’s nice that not two boss battles are alike, about half of the boss battles are very difficult because the game randomly spikes the difficulty forcing you to level up your characters, which ruins much of the game’s continuity. The combat has too many menus, so you’ll find yourself getting pummeled while trying to find that one attack. Additionally, your party AI is unbelievably bad. They don’t defend. They always waste their MP immediately even after changing Tactics. This can make the battles incredibly frustrating.The game’s fun comes from sidequests. It is fun to explore and their Merit System is one of the best sidequest systems I’ve played. You can use your sidequest successes to purchase helpful aids that will help in the main storyline. While the sidequests are fun, the main story is incredibly shallow. There is a ton of handholding and a lot of unnecessary dialogue.Overall, I found its flaws too much to continue and Ni No Kuni is one of the most disappointing games I’ve played in awhile. I am used to playing RPGs, but I found this game to be very boring.

I like this game, but I don't understand why it gets so much praise. I have to wonder if some of the reviewers actually played it or did they merely look at it and observe the eye candy and listen to its nicely done orchestral score.  The graphics are beautiful, yes.  The story is great, yes.  But the combat system (and therefore, gameplay) is flawed in a couple of very annoying ways.  Mainly, it comes down to the party AI... as in what AI?First, the "Tactics" system... I seriously wonder if it's even properly wired up.  For example, there are three settings... attack leader's target, attack weakest target, attack separate target.  But no matter which setting you choose, it makes NO difference.  It is completely ignored.  Your party members will attack whoever they feel like attacking, regardless of your selection. The only tactic that actually seems to work to some degree is the "use no abilities" setting.  Other than that, it's anyone's guess what the party AI will do in a fight.  They seem to completely ignore any and all tactics settings.  It was so bad that at one point I seriously wondered if I was doing it wrong.  I flipped through the menus and settings looking to see if there was perhaps some setting that I had missed that was thereby causing the tactics to be ignored.Next, Esther burns through MP so fast as to make it almost pointless to have her in the group.  Depending on the familiars you give her, she will blow through a full bar of MP in either one or two fights.  This happens when you are first exploring a new area and are pushing the leveling curve.  You will die a lot simply because Esther has no MP and cannot heal you.  The "strong coffee" item gives you 30MP and costs 800GP each.  Before a round of combat, I gave her two of these.  That's a cost of 1600GP to give her 60MP.  By the end of the next fight she was out of mana again, not to mention having only 1HP of health due to being slain in combat yet again.  Often she will use the most expensive healing spell on Oliver when he's only got the slightest nick of damage.  The AI has no sense of conservation or management of precious MP.  She burns through it until the well is dry, and the she dies... a lot.  It's an exercise in frustration.So, what you end up doing is grinding grinding grinding, letting her die and autorez with one HP, feed her a couple of sandwhiches to get her back on her feet again and grind some more until she levels up and gets a full bar of HP and MP again.  She can then cast spells again for a few rounds of combat until she runs out.  And you start the process all over again.  Eventually after a couple of hours of this, your party will have levelled up enough so that it no longer is a concern and you will ROFLSTOMP the enemies in combat.  But when you are first entering a new area, the AI of this game will make you cuss and swear.  The AI is just terrible.Also I can't count the number of times a miracle glim finally drops and I want to go grab it to do some epic damage with my main familiar that's all loaded up with awesome offensive fire magic, but Esther's familiar gets there first and the thing is wasted on some stupid pointless party-wide buff or some such.  I liked the game better when it was just one on one combat.  I had full control of it then.  But when the party grew to two and then three members, the AI drove me babanas for sure.Another gripe I have with this game... the amount of flippin reading that you have to do, especially when doing side tasks that aren't story related.  For example, I see a guy with a green dot on the map.  I KNOW it's going to be a Take Heart spell.  Don't make me read 10 screens of text just to get this one little sliver of heart off this NPC.  It gets REALLY old after a while.  The main story is fine, and I don't mind reading that stuff.  It is what makes an RPG and RPG.  But seriously there are times when they overdid it and I couldn't click X fast enough to just get through the countless waves of text I had to "read".Anyway, just sayin.  I see a lot of praise for this game, but it does have some serious problems that can be frustrating and downright infuriating at times.
