I enjoyed this game thoroughly. On all fronts this game delivers and won't leave you disappointed. Whether you like JRPG's or not, it's hard to discount the beauty and charm of this game. As always my reviews are split into 3 areas with story usually getting the heavier weight.Story: 9.5/10The story is great and surprisingly deeper than you would expect for one that the main character is a little boy being followed around by a fairy. You are Oliver, a young everyday boy who lives in a small town called Motorville. One day when his mother unexpectedly dies, a doll his mother gave him springs to life and tells him he can bring her back but he needs to save another world. Oliver travels to this "other world" where cats are kings, cows are queens, and monsters are all over. It's a gripping journey where Oliver finds himself and creates friendships that help him on his way.Really the story is very charming. It's straightforward and does a great job capturing the player and keeping the player's interest. It is a little on the kiddy side (but surprisingly the story is more mature than what you might expect). And the story is fairly straightforward. Thus the .5 deduction. I personally prefer a few good story twists and unexpecteds but the story was fairly straightforward. Nonetheless, this is a very minor complaint as the story is unique and charming that everyone should enjoy.Characters 10/10Here is the strength of this game. The characters are so developed and so well written that the player can't help but fall in love with the characters. Oliver is a boy that is mature for his age but is the eternal optimist. You may get a little fatigued with his optimism and positivity but really his character development is so deep that these things are easy to overlook. Esther, a girl that helps Oliver on his quest, is also developed well and really is a strong presence throughout the game. Her banter with Swaine (the third character of your crew) is great and feels really genuine. Swaine is hilarious and developed equally well as Oliver. The best character I feel though is Mr. Drippy. Just simply hilarious and keeps you rolling throughout the game. They knocked it out of the park with him. The secondary characters are really well written and you can really see Studio Ghibli in them. Really just an awesome cast.Gameplay: 9/10The gameplay is one of those areas that have awesome strengths but some glaring weaknesses. First the good.You will never see a more beautiful game. The artwork in this game is just beyond amazing. The world map is a thing of beauty. The animated cutscenes seem like they came right out of Princess Mononoke or Spirited Away. I could go on and on about the visualizations but really I wouldn't do them justice. I for one loved the battles. I thought the way you can switch between three familiars, pick the familiars that you want in the parties for awesome customization, and really control the tactics of your party was beyond outstanding. The whole familiar system was great too. Very similar to pokemon. There are something like 300 different familiars that can be caught. Training them, evolving them, and tricking them out with sweets is just an awesome touch.Now the bad. And it's not really terrible but it is rather distracting. THE AMOUNT OF TEXT IN THIS GAME. Oh wow was it bad. I am a fan of RPG's and i know there is a lot of text but this takes it to another level. Just for a simple sidequst you may scroll through what seems like pages of text. I almost wish they had put more cutscenes in this game just so you weren't reading everything all the time. I know this seems minor but with all the sidequests and story elements you have, you quickly get tired of reading the entire game. The other negative is some of the capture percentages of a lot of the familiars (monsters you use in your party). In short you have to beat them and then you get a random chance to allow them to join your party. Some of the familiars have a ridiculously low capture rate...almost to the point of being ridiculous. Some may have a 4% capture rate. They could easily make this more bearable by increasing the capture rate for a certain type of familiar each time you fail to capture it. Another thing that seems minor but when you have quests to capture specific familiars and the capture rates are absurd, you quickly find that this part of the game can get maddening rather quickly.Overall 9.5/10This game just delivers. I mean it has undeniable charm, wonderful characters, a gripping story, and some of the most beautiful visuals with a completely unique gameplay. It does have a few things that can get on your nerves in a major way and the story might not be the MOST imaginative thing in the world, but all in all every JRPG fan should play it and even if you don't like JRPG's this game is such a revolutionary game that you should give it a shot.

Ni No Kuni is a well-balanced RPG that should be accessible for even casual gamers.  The main story is quite linear, but balanced by a variety of side quests and optional mini-games/tournaments.  The combat is challenging but not frustrating.  The leveling system is well-paced and keeps grinding to a bare minimum.  And the storyline is Japanese-but-still-accessible-for-western-audiences in the best Studio Ghibli tradition.While Pokemon comparisons are inevitable, the combat/gameplay resembles Eternal Sonata or Final Fantasy more than your average Pokemon game.  Collecting, training, and evolving 'familiars' (read: pocket monsters) is fundamental to the game but one of many components.  The plot progresses by sending the player through dungeons on fetch quests which usually culminate in boss battles.  Side quests involve a mixture of fetch quests, battles, and puzzles/mini-games.  Combat is real-time rather than turn-based and increases in complexity as the game progresses.Completing the main questline requires 30+ hours, depending on difficulty and the effort put into side quests and character improvement.  Once the main quest is completed, the player is allowed to start from a 'completed game save' with their stable of familiars intact and a host of additional (and possibly self-replenishing) side quests.  I expect dozens more hours of gameplay growing an army of familiars and exploring the corners of the game world that I neglected the first time around.  A completist's dream.The Studio Ghibli collaboration elevates the game from good to great - the writing and art direction are well above average, even for a top-tier release.  Characters are complex and well-drawn and the (Japanese) voice-acting is outstanding.Incredible game overall and a steal at the Greatest Hits price.

I found myself tired of fighters like SSFIV. It seemed like they weren't fun anymore. I had always heard of this game and blazblue continuum shift was pretty good so I decided to put my $15s worth of psn funds (thank you "back to 2013" sale! Can't beat 50% OFF!) in the hands of Arc system works.  In return I got what is now one of my top 5 favorite 2d fighters of all time!Story(4/5) Ok.... I've never played a persona Rpg game. From what I can tell this game takes place some time after the events of the case in persona 4. The "midnight channel" which was used by a murder to catch victims by sucking them into a world inside Tvs from persona 4 is back. On there a commercial for the P1 fighting grand prix is displayed. The main characters of persona 4 who were all on an "investigation team" (seeing as how they are high school students it's unofficial) venture into the Tv world to see what's up. It turns out  a few of their members are missing around the same time.anyways... the team falls into a trap by a person/thing claiming to be their friend Teddie and are forced to fight eachother and anyone else who wanders into the TV world.While I don't want to spoil anything else I must say the story is entertaining. I really enjoy the main characters.The "story mode" of the game lets you experience the story through a visual novel perspective before and after fights. The only problem is that like blazblue you play through each characters story mode one at a time so you reach the same conclusion almost every time! Plus the "cliffhanger" that you get which has to be cleared by playing other stories is annoying!Gameplay(4.5/5): a slightly simplified version of BlazBlue. But don't worry, it still has alot of complexity!It's fast and fun. 2 buttons are for basic attacks and 2 buttons for persona/assist attacks. The persona system adds some variety and strategy. There's also an auto combo that lets you do a long string of hits and a Super move by mashing square. This adds a layer of accessibility not seen in other games like street fighter.It's not too overpowered and does cost health so serious players can still dominate online no matter who they're playing against.Presentation(5/5):Much like blazblue this game uses Anime style sprites.They're fully detailed and animate very well. the backgrounds are 2-dimensional. it's good that the backgrounds are 2D because lets face it, sprite based fighters don't look as good with 3D backgrounds(MVC2 and CVS2, I'm looking at you!). in a nutshell, when you're playing everything is "super duper purdy". Where the style really shines though is in the menus,story mode, and even the pre-fight scene where the announcer introduces the 2 characters in each fight. Everything has alot of yellow. I mean ALOT of the color yellow.Sound(5/5): EVERY FREAKING SONG IN THIS GAME IS GREAT! The menu alone has more than 3 tracks! Each character has a well-composed theme that you hear when fighting against them. Sure there's a J-pop song here and there but trust me, this soundtrack has everything. Hard rock mixed with jazz? YOU GOT IT! everyone can find a theme they like. The music is so great infact that it's almost as good as street fighter II,Halo, and even the smash bros series. What about voices you say? English dub and Japanese Dub are available but I suggest going with dub. The cast features anime veterans such as patrick seitz(franky from one piece, kenpachi zaraki from bleach), johhny young Bosch(ichigo kurosaki from bleach and a million other characters from various anime), and laura Bailey who plays Chun-li in all the newest street fighter games.Replay value(4/5): Story mode requires multiple playthroughs for multiple characters so that's a plus. 13 characters is a little lacking and only 5 are male, plus 1 character is almost just a clone. By the time you finish story mode, beat arcade mode with all the characters, clear the insanely frustrating score attack, clear the 200+ plus combo challenges for each character,and dominate the competition alone you will walk away satisfied!Overall(25/5): P4A is a great fighting game that is fun for fighting game fans like me and a newcomer who likes persona. With some of the best presentation in a game ever, an entertaining story for persona fans and non-fans, and amazingly accessible but in-depth combat this is truly an awesome game.

I've had an itch for a new Mario Tennis game for a few years and now that l own a 3DS l decided to give Mario Tennis Open a try. Open is the first new original Mario Tennis game since Power Tennis for the Gamecube. The Wii was basically just a port of The Gamecube game with the novelty of playing with Wii controls, which made it fun but it wasn't a new Mario Tennis game. Now comes a new Tennis game with original content with Mario and co, only this time on the go.Graphically, it looks very nice with that trademark bright and crisp graphic you would expect from a Mario and Nintendo game. The courts and environments looks stunning and inviting. It's easy to just pop it in play and feel comfortable with the controls right away. There are singles and doubles tournament. There are eight tournaments total. The extra mini-games are also fun, playing the original Super Mario Bros controlling with the balls you hit against the screen is pretty neat l must say. Galaxy rally is different and fun also. There's ring shots and paints as well which will all seem familiar if you've played the special games the N64 and GC.As far as the gameplay goes movement is very nice thanks to the joystick. The rest is fairly straightforward in that you hit A,B,X,Y to do different types of hits. There are 3 different menus on the touch screen to select different ball hits which is nice but personally lprefer using the buttons. One goo thing about the menus is it'll flash to indicate which shot would be the best in any case. The 3D is very nice, in some stages like bowser's castle the subtle flames flying in the background provide a great effect. There are two views options. The first is the traditional 3rd person point of view where you see your character. The second is a first person view that l'm not particularly fond of as l tend to miss the ball often with it.There are no items or special moves in Open, it's more of a throwback to the more tennis based game that earlier titles used to be on the Gameboy Colour and Nintendo 64. There are landing spaces called chance shots if there is a bad rebound. If you hit the ball it'll have effects such as having a banana curve, or the fireball space where the ball becomes basically unstoppable or a fast shot on a star sign. They are certainly helpful in a match but even these can be stopped so it's not as unfair as the special moves were in Power Tennis. I think the items added for unpredictability in that game though and were fun and would have been right at home on the 3DS.As for replayability, you'll want to beat tournaments with multiple characters so you can unlock the items in the store. I'll say this, the game has a LOT of unlockables for a Mario Tennis game. Not just characters but shirts, shorts, shoes, wristbands and tennis rackets and there's plenty of each. It's cool because you can equip these on your mii (yes mii is playable!) which gives the game a bit of a unique feel. Of course the more you play the more you will unlock for purchase.It would have been cool to have the tennis academy like there used to be on the Gameboy but that's only a personal wish list. Stats would have been another great addition but then again these games are more about mindless fun than controlled and serious tactical games. That's not to say the game doesn't use strategy on the contrary.All in all, if you've been craving for a new all original Mario Tennis game, this 3DS title is a worthy title. With the tournaments and other modes and unlockables is a very entertaining game. Wether you like Tennis or Mario games or both, you can't go wrong with Mario Tennis  Open. It's not a really long game but then again none of the Mario Tennis games really were. It's a just a fun game that you can pick up and play a few tournaments or exhibitions and enjoy freely wether you're a seasoned fan or a newcomer. A good return to portable console and a fine addition to the Mario Tennis franchise. 4/5 stars.

This game is Assassin's Creed Jr. for the Vita. It has most of the features of its big brothers, but on a smaller screen. The big question is how an Assassin's Creed game can hold up on a handheld system. The answer, surprisingly is pretty well. Assassin's Creed has had to make a few compromises to adapt itself to the Vita's less powerful hardware and smaller screen. Texture maps are far more limited and incapable of standing up to close scrutiny. The look of hair and grass/leaves is particularly false looking. Grass is just a series of 2D images lined up perpendicular to each other while hair just looks like oddly-colored lumps. This is particularly obvious in the case of Aveline's stepmother, whose beehive hairstyle is often seen in closeup and looks atrocious. Also taking away slightly from the feel of the game is the fact that you can watch the populace appear from nothing as you get closer.Given these limitations it is impressive what the game CAN manage to achieve. The city of New Orleans itself is rendered entirely, and looks as good as anything from the other games (apart from the problems already noted). The running and climbing animations are perfect as well, and the character design is well done since the city is populated by a whole series of different looking characters. In fact, in almost every detail this feels exactly like the portable Assassin's Creed game you hoped for but didn't really expect.Some of the other compromises made for the portable market are a bit more annoying. Instead of the long cutscenes using in-game graphics, Liberation relies on shorter scenes that don't go into as much detail. I actually didn't mind this at first because I got sick of the overdrawn cutscenes in the main games, but after a while I noticed that this meant it was giving out much less plot as well. Throughout the entire game you are told to do things with no explanation given as to why, except occasionally for those times when they explain a lot very fast talking at you as if you know why you're there. Let's give an example:  at one point you show up in the bayou with no explanation given and then you follow the arrows to get to somebody who tells you you have to kill somebody. Apparently that is because the target is a bad guy or something? They talk about this as if you already know why you're here and what this guy did. There's some guy there you apparently know, don't ask how because they won't tell you. Then it turns out that your mentor, or perhaps friend, or perhaps temporary partner (without having introduced him the game is unclear) has betrayed you? Somehow. The bad guy says something that is apparently contrary to what that guy claimed. Or something. Oh, and apparently there's someone hacking the game to show you what's really happening. Because there's nothing that makes a game better than having to do bonus quests to have the plot explained to you. Then it's back in New Orleans. Oh, and it's under Spanish rule now. Apparently that's why you were there. Is this important?I understand why they're doing this. People playing a portable system often have less time to devote to it, meaning that missions have to be shorter and simpler and exposition less in depth. Instead of making shorter exposition however (and it tended to the longwinded already) they've written it at normal length and simply cut random chunks out. I don't know what's going on, except that I have to obey the computer in my head and follow the little markers. The compromises made for the portable market are extremely bad for the game.On the other hand, from a strictly gameplay focus this works fine. If you're playing the game on the bus on the way to work or during lunch or whatever, this is probably exactly what you want. The miniquests are fun, and the loss of a complex overarching story is less noticeable. The gameplay is exactly like that of AC3, with the exception that some things that were done by the back bumpers are now done by the rear touchpads, and the L3 and R3 buttons have now been moved. The touchscreen, which I always thought of as gimmicky, is now vitally important in providing the extra control inputs that there is no room for on the Vita. The controls are pretty easy and the entire thing flows naturally, even if the analog sticks aren't as responsive as a PS3's. The only complaint I have is that the combat difficulty has been drastically lowered, making it far too simple to kill people.A nice new mechanic has been added allowing Aveline to switch between three different personas: her assassin guise, her slave guise, and her noblewoman guise. Being notorious in one guise won't affect the others, but you can go around in any guise reducing your overall notoriety. This adds a new level to the game as each guise is treated differently by the populace. As a noblewoman you can go pretty much everywhere you want without anyone stopping you, and can even seduce guards into following you. On the other hand you can't run, jump, or swim, so if you can't charm your way in there there isn't much you can fall back on. The slave guise means that people usually ignore you, which makes it easier to investigate or climb things. The assassin's outfit is basically like the slave's, only all your skills work better. The game takes advantage of this new system quite a lot, and for the first time in a while I actually did feel really stealthy while playing.As I mentioned before the story is nothing special. Admittedly, I don't really like the story in most Assassin's Creed games (the contemporary stuff is boring while the historical stuff is often cheesy or forced) so I shouldn't be complaining about it now. However, I really do need a bit more motivation than 'here is your assignment, do it.' It's nice that they toned down the present day material, but in adapting it to the short timescale of a portable system they have removed the motivations. And that is a real problem.The big draw here is Aveline, Assassin's Creed's first female protagonist. And she works pretty well. She's not go much personality because of the limited plot, but what little she displays is charming and entertaining. She's a vast improvement over bland-as-muck Conner, who also shows up here in an unnecessary cameo. Other characters are rather limited. I enjoyed her father and respected her somewhat complicated stepmother, but generally speaking they don't go in much for characterizations. I guess something had to be cut. Too bad it was that.This game is clearly running at the limits of the Vita's capabilities. The game runs well most of the time with only very brief loading times, but I've never had a game more prone to freezing than this one. It's a good thing the game autosaves constantly because otherwise I'd have been screwed. Particularly glitchy are the popup screens telling you how to use the next new function. For some reason if you don't hit X fast enough the game can freeze forcing you to exit to the Vita menu and close the app. It can be very irritating because these are exactly the moments when you want to spend time reading carefully. None of this is bad enough to make the game unplayable, but it is definitely present in a big way.Assassin's Creed is one of those franchises that probably has no business on a portable system. On the other hand, this is about as good an attempt as can be made to do so. I realize that this is an ambivalent review, and that reflects my feelings pretty accurately. It does have a lot of good game mechanics, but it also has some limitations that are detrimental to the game. The addition of a female protagonist is interesting and adds a lot to the story, but there is precious little story to provide support. The plot is complicated and impossible to follow since they cut large chunks out. The costume-switching aspect is clever, and allows for a more varied way of making assassinations. I did enjoy this game, but at the same time I wished for more. It is as good as a portable Assassin's Creed can get, and I did enjoy it more than 3, so if you're a fan of the games and own a Vita give this a try.As for other Assassin's Creed games,Assassin's Creedis the first and is set during the Third Crusade. I liked it a lot (not least for its little-seen locations including Jerusalem, Damascus, and Acre), but it wasn't as good asAssassin's Creed II, which made a number of gameplay improvements making the combat system far less broken and introducing the best character in the series: Ezio Auditore di Firenze. This game is set in Renaissance Italy and takes you to Florence, Forli, and Venice.Assassin's Creed: Brotherhoodis a direct sequel to the second one and features the return of Ezio. This one takes place entirely in Rome, but the map is so big it doesn't matter. It was probably the best of the games. Certainly it was better thanAssassin's Creed: Revelations, which was set in Istanbul but never had as much of a personal touch.Assassin's Creed IIItakes place in the American Revolution. I'm not a big fan, despite the impressive wilderness locations. I just think that the 1700s are too late to set a game like this in, although Liberation did a fairly good job with it.Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flagis set slightly before the third game and tells the tale of a pirate captain, emphasizing and improving upon the ship-to-ship combat that was so fun in number three. There was also a PSP game calledAssassin's Creed: Bloodlines, which is far inferior to any of the other games. The Vita is the first portable system capable of providing an entertaining Assassin experience, and the compromises the PSP game had to make just meant it wasn't worth anyone's time.

In this game your path is constantly cut offbehind you with fire,falling objects ect. thus forcing you forward . I like to creep andsurvey the terrain before barreling in and like to toss  a few explosives into the unknownarea to see if I can shake anything loose. That doesnt work here as the enemies dontmaterialize until you reach a certain piece of geography on the level , a piece that isoften enclosed with little manuvering room at that. H.R. isnt the first game to do this so Idont fault them but it deflates some of the fun when all you can do is move forward and waitto be attacked.Speaking of which:The enemies in this game are all robotic and of similar designs and similar albeit  limitedattack methods. They're fast , direct and like to slam into you while  some fire mortars androckets , They're also faster than you and battles quickly get reduced to wildly firing intosmoke ,fire,electrical discharges and the like, all very chaotic and frenetic.The music sets the tempo dutifully enough and has a good pulse but has little futureoutside of this game environment, (its getting so that games are becoming worthy of theirown soundtrack releases....except this one), and the SFX are suitable but not reallyoutstanding. The assault rifle ,however,makes a veeerry satisfying sound  and rippingthrough all your ammo while strolling around the level blasting the crap out of it adds tothe experience favorably.The weapons:This game gives you two guns at the beginning, an assault rifle that fires a bullet styleprojectiles and an energy rifle that fires anergy bolts , both weapons use a regeneratingammo as well as findable ammo packs . If you are looking for information about the single player campaign and how Friggin' AWESOME it is then check out 'PRIVATE QUENTIN TARANTINO's' review.  It's one of the highest rated reviews and written beautifully.Regarding TLOU Multiplayer, in my opinion it is the best Multiplayer Experience I have ever had with any game on the PS3.  Bold statement, yes indeed.  However, many would back me up as this game's multiplayer had (still HAS) a huge following.  It's truly a hidden gem and breaks from the norm that one would expect from a popular experience such as Battlefield or Call of Duty, or Halo.  The Last of Us brings forth the survival feel in its MP game modes by starting players with limited ammo and a class system where players choose which strengths and weaknesses their players start with.  Like any other MP game you can edit and save each one of these loadouts but it truly depends on a player preference and experience as to what suits you best.Possibly the most fun part of MP is the in-game crafting of melee weapons or explosives & traps.  There is no pause to create feature it's live, you can be crafting a smoke bomb or a Spiked 2 x 4 as the opposition sneaks up behind you and 'Shivs' you at the same time.The main game modes are 4 vs.4 which is fine for the size of the maps, most of which are not too big.  they feel just right in size.The Stealth is this game is just as important to utilize as is communication & interaction with teammates.  Never before have I experienced such a brilliant combination of teamwork tactics in an online game.  A headset is not entirely necessary but it helps a lot, and it's generally a good idea to always stay close by your teammates.The duck n' cover system is used as the main form of gameplay, alot like the single player version.  it feels perfect with hiding behind or around something, then quickly taking aim or performing a melee tactic if the opposition sneaks past you without detection.FYI- There is no camping in this game and there are never any accusations about performing this style of 'COD' type gameplay. If you camp in one spot too long your team WILL SUFFER and lose.  and you will likely die a gruesome Melee death while doing so.Along with this it's generally a great idea to keep 'on the move' as there are supply toolboxes situated in only 3 or 4 sections of the maps.  these toolboxes don't carry a lot of supplies but they are imperative for giving players any advantage.  And if players can keep moving around the board together in stealth-like fashion, while staying alive the advantage leans their direction.I've witnessed so many Loaners try to run n' gun like this is Halo or COD, only to get quickly cut down by just about any kind of weapon(s).  Noise and Speed are not a good combo!  stealth and silence is the key.  Suppressed weapons are also imperative for success.  don't get me wrong, everyone makes noise in this game, it's impossible not too at some point!  the less the betterHealing is also a big part of the in-game experience, you can pick up bandage kits in several areas of each map and then choose to heal yourself, or you can actually heal a teammate.TLOU MP also has some of the most brutal deaths i've ever encountered in any video game.  Spiked 2 x 4's impaling into necks and skulls followed by a face-bash by the opposite end of the lumber piece to finish the job...is just 1 example of the brutality.  Just look up TLOU Multiplayer finishing moves on YouTube and you'll get the idea.  Or go ahead in and do it yourself!  enjoy.my personal favorite part of this game is the ranking system using the 12 week survival format.  You basically need to keep at least 1 or more survivors alive for this amount of time.  You can add more by accomplishing challenges such as healing teammates or marking enemies during matches.  You can also lose survivors by NOT accomplishing these challenges.  The nice part of this systems is being able to choose which challenge you want to participate in out of about 20 (roughly).  You can participate in a certain challenge more than once, but the requirements get more difficult if you do this (ex:  Down enemies.  starts with 3, next time around you must down 5) you get the idea.I honestly have had so much fun with this multiplayer and I felt almost addicted to playing it because of how fun it was.  Like I mentioned before, it's a great combination of stealth, survival, crafting, patience, silence, and teamwork in order to achieve success.I am not writing this review to take anything away from the single player game, that is the award winner.  I look at the MP as the cherry on top.  it's just unfortunate nobody sees the cherry!Enjoy!!Scottie

I'm not a hardcore gamer and heavily depend on the more experienced ones who post their gaming experience on Youtube for guidance. But this game is more about just playing its main characters. The storyline is so amazing that my wife, who doesn't like scary movies, enjoyed watching me play, captivated by Ellie, the young girl protagonist who follow Joel in their journey. Naughty Dog, the in-house Sony Computer Entertainment developer, did a really good job with this release, from cut scenes and the nice scenery in this game to the music that accompany it (a companion soundtrack album was also released). I thought Grand Theft Auto V was good. Don't get me wrong, it was. But little did I know that The Last of Us was as good. In my opinion, this game was the best one I've ever played on a PS3 console. According to the stats, i spent about 21 hours playing it, so it is a very long game. Many far better experienced gamers spent about 16 hours playing it before beating it. The Last of Us is a game that requires thinking and the art of mastering survival. It's not always about killing the infected. In fact, you will quickly learn that sometimes you can't kill them all. It's about a brave girl whose immune status to the disease is suddenly the hope of a post-apocalyptic America where civilization appears to  be ending. That said, some people (myself included) have scratched their heads about the way the ending played out. But I can forgive Naughty Dog only if there will be a sequel to the game. I know Sony Computer Entertainment is about to release a prequel next month. I sure hope there is a follow up, just like Tell Tale's Walking Dead that now has a second season. That's the one I'm playing next.Disclaimer: I own shares in Sony Corporation and find it necessary to state that every time I review a Sony-related product.

The Good: Fantastic visuals, gripping story, Joel and Ellie are memorable characters, lots of fun guns to use, crafting on the fly, Clickers are down right scaryThe Bad: Poor sense of direction, combat is down right hard at times, combat sequences are all the same, feels repetitive towards the end, some glitches and AI issuesPost-apocalyptic games always try to focus on a mass group of people or the devastation itself. The Last of Us focuses on two people, Joel and Ellie as they travel across the US to find a cure for the biological outbreak that’s destroyed the planet. The journey is a decent length and you really get to love Joel and Ellie and they become amazing characters that you don’t want to separate from.The Last of Us is full of emotion and amazing production values. It’s the best looking game to grace the PS3 and is a great entry for the final lap of the console’s life cycle. The combat is a mix of action and stealth. You can sneak around enemies and grab them from behind and either shiv them or strangle them. Shivs aren’t easy to come by, you must craft them and they can break. Strangling takes about 10 seconds to do and is a slow way to kill someone, make sure no one else is around or you will spotted. You don’t just fight humans in this game, Clickers are some of the scariest monsters since Dead Space’s Necromorphs. The sounds that were used are incredibly scary and original. These creepy creatures can hear you even if you crouch. You must slowly crouch around them and you can only kill them with shivs. Hunters and Runners are also hard to fight but Runners can’t be snuck up on, you must fight them. Bloaters are like Tanks from Left 4 Dead; huge enemies that are hard to take down. These enemies are interesting to fight, but they are the only ones in the game so it can get repetitive after a while.Repetition sets in in other things like each encounter feeling the exact same way. It’s just room after room of zombies or humans to fight. I wanted more cinematic events which were kind of sparse. Crafting and collecting parts helps make the game a bit more interesting. You can craft melee weapons, molotovs, shivs, medkits, and smoke bombs. You can craft in the middle of combat which is nice, but weapon upgrade stations are rare. There are only about a dozen in the whole game and you need to save up a lot of your parts to upgrade weapons. You can add gun slots and even increase clip capacity on one shot weapons which is nice. There’s actually a good variety of weapons and they all feel useful in different situations. I found myself using all of them one way or another often.The game is very linear but feels like an adventure. You go through various areas in the US from Boston to Utah and the game just oozes stylized atmosphere. You really feel like you’re being pulled into this destroyed world and it just feels so compelling. Despite combat though there isn’t much to the game, there’s no puzzles or anything else that’s very challenging. Just pushing Ellie across pallets in water, moving ladders etc. The combat is down right frustrating since Clickers can kill you in one hit and the stealth is a bit iffy. Some times it felt the AI was flawed and got me killed. I also ran into a few glitches.The story itself is the best part about the game. Bringing Ellie across the country and the hardships these two go through is just something else. I don’t want to spoil anything, but you get to play as both characters and Ellie is just a strong character. A little girl who curses, kills people, and wipes out an entire gang on her own? It’s nothing like I have ever seen and shows Naughty Dog has guts to do this.The game itself looks amazing. The textures are at such a high-resolution, the animations and models look great, and the lighting is fantastic. It really shows just how much more powerful the PS3 is over the Xbox 360. 360 exclusives like Gears of War 3 and Halo 4 have some pretty ugly textures and the lighting doesn’t look too hot. The Last of Us looks like a PC game and is blew my mind which is rare for current generation consoles these days. There are a few eyes sores but you really have to hunt for them, if only every developer put this much effort into their games.Overall, The Last of Us is one of the best games of this generation and the best PS3 game this year. Joel and Ellie are highly memorable characters and their journey is frightening and enlightening. The combat can feel repetitive towards the end and can be down right difficult and frustrating, not to mention constantly being lost due to a lack of direction. Despite these flaws this is one fantastic journey that every PS3 gamer should endure.

This is a very well done game. The story is amazing and the game play is top notch. I think what really makes this game standout though is the story and character interactions. It really does make you think and it can be quite dramatic at times. Controls are excellent and the AI is very intelligent. Graphics are also very good. I would love to see what they could have done using the PS4 in this regard. I am sure they would have been even more realistic.  On to the game itself.I started off on the NORMAL difficulty level. The game was very hard at some parts and easy at others. There are quite a few occasions where you will probably be stuck and have to try the part over a few times. The normal mode has a feature called "Hearing" that lets you see where enemies are through walls. This makes it easy to to take down enemies or to sneak by them. The game also gives you enough supplies in this mode that you are never lacking in anything. Now let me talk about the Survivor mode that I played.Survivor mode is the hardest difficulty level. Let me just say that it makes the game SO MUCH More Fun. It is not so hard that you can never get through it. I actually completed the game in the same amount of time or shorter in this mode. You will have trouble at the same spots that get you in the other modes. There is a big difference between Normal and Survivor. In Survivor the "Hearing" ability is gone. You can not see through walls which forces you to take it slow and to peak around corners. The only thing that gives you an indicator that someone can see you is a sound effect. You will have to rely on shadows and lighting to see where enemies are. This alone add realism to the game. On top of this, supplies are very limited. 90 percent of the time when you open items to check for supplies you won't find anything. You will need to conserve your ammo for times when it is needed most and rely on stealth most of the time. You also do not want to be getting into large gunfights because you take a lot more damage in this mode.What I found that adds a more immerse experience and also startled me a few times is to go into your sound settings and turn the music completely off, so that all you hear are the sound effects. Using headphones will make this even better. Now you hear every little footstep and sound in the game.I have not played the multiplayer yet so I can not review that.One word of caution. While I feel most people will like this game if they are into Survival Horror, there might be some that will not. If you are the type that wants to be killing something at every turn of the game then this is not for you. There is still PLENTY of action, but it is not in your face every second of the game. So if you are the impatient type that needs to be blowing stuff up all the time then pass on this.  If you are looking for an excellent story, with awesome, psychological and emotional scenes mixed with intense action then I believe you will really enjoy this game.Also after you have played the game, do yourself a favor and look up the alternate ending of Last of Us. It is a pretty good laugh. There is also a great video on YouTube that does a 20 min long analysis of the Last of Us story that really does make you appreciate the story even more. I would definitely take a look.

This is easily one of the top 2 or 3 best game-stories of all time and is worth purchasing just for that reason.  I cannot overstate this enough.  It's a heart-gripping story in which you will openly cheer and care about what happens to the protagonists while playing.The game-play itself is simplistic; there really are no puzzles to sweat  Find a ladder or plank of wood and move it to spot 'A' is about as difficult as it will get.  Trying to figure out how one approaches dealing with an area full of human baddies or infected monsters is fun.  Sometimes it's best to try to use stealth and pick them off one-by-one.  Sometimes, if you're really stealthy, you can sneak past the whole group of them.  And sometimes, it's fun to break out the big guns/weapons and lay siege.  There are times where you will have to repeat areas with a trial-and-error approach and that gets a little annoying, but thankfully they are few and far between.  The difficulty on normal mode is a breeze and even the most casual gamer should have no trouble romping through the game.  Even if you're having difficulty in an area, the game recognizes this and tries to help on your subsequent attempts.  However, the combat does get repetitive after a while.  This is especially true if you prefer to stealth your way through the game as opposed to running around like you're playing Call of Duty or Battlefield.Here's the one big negative about this game:  The AI is poor.  The developer couldn't figure it out properly and instead of taking the time/effort to do it right, they just made your allies "invisible" to the enemy until your own cover was blown.  This leads to immersion-breaking moments where you'll be huddled behind cover trying to hide from a horde of monsters while your teenage companion will sprint all over, around, and in most cases, in PLAIN SIGHT of them for no apparent reason.  No fear, though, as the infected will be completely oblivious to her mindless jaunt, but swarm you the moment accidentally bump a small glass bottle lying on the ground.  It's not a deal-breaker, but I do laugh out loud when Ellie bolts by a half-dozen monsters while Joel, a grizzled and powerful man, is cowering in a pool of his own fear in a dark corner.Oh, and there's a ton of vulgarity.  I guess it stands to reason in the post-apocalyptic world that the f-bomb and g-d are generously used.  I don't mind it too much, but most of the time the cussing is used just to use it and is obviously forced in there for shock's sake.  The language from the teen protagonist is laughably over-the-top on occasion.Bottom line, though, is this game is still very entertaining and has a surprisingly high replay value.  I found myself replaying the game over and over to beat higher-levels of difficulty, collect all the "artifacts", unlock bonus material, and collect all the trophies.  Plus, I still watch the cut-scenes because the story is so phenomenal.  I recommend this if you're a casual gamer who isn't concerned about rather easy difficultly and bad AI, is truly searching for a great story, and doesn't mind a never-ending sea of profanity.Story: 5/5Game-Play:  3/5AI: 1/5Replay Value:  4/5

The Last of Us (TLoU) is one of those games that comes along every once in a while and reaffirms that gaming is a legitimate art form that deserves a place alongside more accepted formats such as movies and books. The primary aspect that sets TLoU apart from the pack is the storytelling and character development which unfold throughout the approximate year-long saga that makes up the game. Many games try to endear the audience to the onscreen character but few will ever succeed like Naughty Dog, the development studio, has with TLoU.----------------------STORY:The story unfolds in modern day America during the beginning of a fungal pandemic that quickly sweeps across the nation. The beginning moments of the story are an intense blur of panic as Joel, his daughter Sarah, and his brother Tommy attempt to flee from their home as chaos engulfs the world around them. The fungal infection known only as Cordyceps that is spreading across the world effectively turns people into mindless zombie-like creatures.After the prologue the game moves forward in time twenty years to what’s left of the United States. In fact you don’t actually know if the U.S. really even exists. Citizens live in quarantine zones and eek out a meager existence living in constant fear of the outside world around them. Supplies are scarce and the military regime that rules the quarantine zones is waging a two fronted battle – one against the infected human shells that prowl the fringes of the QZ’s; the other against very citizens they’re trying to protect. Many citizens in desperation to survive have taken to viewing their military protectors as oppressors and actively battle against them. Several factional groups have formed including one large group known as the Firefly’s who fight to restore humanity and the former U.S.Joel’s main partner is a female character named Tess. Together they engage in trading ration stamps for goods and services including illicit weapons and ammunition. At the onset of the story Joel and Tess set out to retrieve some merchandise that was stolen from them by a business partner. After meeting up with a contact from the Firefly’s named Marlene, Joel and Tess are asked to escort a girl named Ellie to the ruined capital building that lies outside the quarantine zone. This is really the moment where the meat of the game begins and you’re introduced to the Cordyceps-ravaged humans who are now known as Clickers, Runners, and Bloaters.Over the course of the next nine months or so you’ll visit a variety of locations across the U.S. from Boston to Pittsburgh, all the way to Colorado, Wyoming and Utah. Each area has its own distinct feel and appropriate climate to match the time period. For example part of the game takes place in the summer, fall and then winter.----------------------GAMEPLAY:Gameplay is similar to other third-person adventure games from Naughty Dog, most notably, Uncharted: Drake’s Fortune. The major element in TLoU that differs is the extreme emphasis on stealth and resource management. This is not a shooter and at any difficulty past ‘Normal’ there is a severe penalty for using “run and gun” tactics. I would classify this game as Uncharted meets Resident Evil (the older survival horror oriented RE games).As you explore the varied areas it will be critical to carefully assess your surroundings. Do your risk killing the two enemies you can see in order to search the area freely and hope you find precious resources or would you be better off sneaking past the enemies and just moving on? That is an example of a typical encounter with enemies in TLoU. Enemies will come in both human and corrupted-human form. Although the variety of corrupted humans is limited you’ll find that each presents a unique challenge to overcome. Runners for example are the recently exposed form of humans. They look like humans, are quite fast and retain their vision. Clickers are a more advanced stage of humans who’ve been turned for a longer period of time. They don’t have eyesight but acoustic hearing similar to bats and make a clicking sound as they walk. They are, however, much stronger than a human and Runner. Bloaters are huge, hulking masses that retain little likeness to their once human form. They’re rare and quite difficult to kill.As you scavenge the landscape you’ll pick up a variety of weapons from a simple “shiv” to bow-and-arrow, handguns, a hunting rifle, shotgun and more. Each can be upgraded using components and tools that you find at specific upgrade benches. Joel too can get enhancements to his abilities using supplements that you find.One major advantage that Joel has is the ability to use his hearing to pinpoint enemy locations. Not all enemies show up mind you but most. This greatly helps your sneaking and attack planning.I would recommend after finishing the game another run through on ‘Survivor’ difficulty. This is really how TLoU should be played. Resources are stretched to the absolute minimum and literally every bullet or band-aid makes the difference. Additionally, Joel’s hearing ability is disabled.----------------------ONLINE:The game features an online component; however, I’ve not tried it so I will not say anything more about that.----------------------GRAPHICS:Graphics are gritty and often used to lend moodiness to the environment. I wouldn’t call the graphics beautiful although there are moments where the game is quite pretty. But the graphics perfectly suit TLoU. There are a lot of earthtones, gray’s and other colors that constantly remind you that the world is not right. TLoU maintains the high quality visuals and animations that you would expect from a Naughty Dog game.----------------------CRITICISMS:I often wonder how someone could not like this game but the truth is that this isn’t a game for everyone. Certainly this is a slower paced survival game. Not a shooter. The brutal realities of the story can be quite disturbing in moments. The colors and world can be quite bleak. The lack of resources can be frustrating particularly at higher difficulty levels. So it’s up to the individual to decide. Certainly there is an incredible story here that I think every gamer should experience.----------------------CONCLUSION:Naughty Dog delivers another incredible experience that should not be missed by most. The lines between game and movie or book are again blurred. If you’re a fan of post-apocalyptic stories like The Road or I Am Legend then this is a game for you!

The Last of Us is a post-apocalyptic horror game made by Naughty Dog (the creators of the Uncharted Series/Jak & Daxter/Crash Bandicoot) which follows the story of two individuals, Joel and Ellie. Joel's purpose in the game is to escort Ellie across the infected continental United States, to a group called the 'Fireflies' in order to study and create a vaccine for humanity using Ellie as a catalyst to help understand what exactly sprouted the infection in the first place. Throughout the game, Joel and Ellie develop a relationship that takes 1 year (4 seasons) to tell, and to show how much they grow throughout their experiences together. Although a basic story, the game is told throughout a very cohesive narrative using beautiful cutscenes with realistic facial motion capture, incredible writing and voice acting, and tense easy to control gameplay.Pros:- Story - the story isn't anything new to be perfectly honest, but its the expert writing and character interactions that really grasp you into the story that is being told. The game took me about 16 hours to beat, and from start to finish I was completely engaged.- Graphics - This game is GORGEOUS, in every sense of the word. The environments and lighting effects really create an amazingly believable atmosphere, whether it be a jaw-dropping hallmark card scene in the woods, from the claustrophobic and dark spaces of abandoned buildings, this game is incredible to look at. The in-game cut scenes flow seamlessly from cut scene to gameplay (vice-versa). The facial motion capture are beautifully rendered, and are very realistic. Its really amazing how much video games have evolved over the past 10 years and it really shows the true power of the Playstation 3- Gameplay - This game is a survival action horror game, and a damned good one at that. Gun fights are simple, with a responsive cover system that works like a dream (better than Gears of War in my opinion) , constantly finding items in order to craft weapons is actually fun and easy (complicated upgrading systems and crafting options in games usually are a hassle, but not in this game). The zombie and human AI's can be challenging at times which is great, and Ellie isn't just a useless escort you have to hoard around during the entire game; she actually helps you!- Voice Acting - The rising star that is Troy Baker and the cunning Ashley Johnson simply MAKE this game. Their voice acting abilities can really move the players into a sense of believability and evoke real emotions. By the time you finish the campaign, I guarantee you will develop some sort of attachment to these characters.-  Sound - the soundtrack is minimalistic but perfect for the game. From the horrific sounds of nearby enemies finding your position, to the disturbing/beautiful music playing in the background, playing this game with the sound off would be a crime.- Online - this is truly one of my favorite online games of the year. They have 3 main modes, simple team deathmatch style matches, a "Survivors" mode where there is a no respawns, and an "Interrogations" mode in which players have to interrogate enemy players in order to find a location of a safe where the team is fighting to unlock. Online mode also keeps things interesting by adding a back story and an inventory clan which you have to maintain by winning matches and helping other teammates. So unlike pointless Call of Duty style online gameplay, TEAMWORK is IMPORTANT and there can be repercussions to losing matches. There is also a nice customization option in creating your character.Cons:- The ending of the game could've been done differently, but still good.- Online matches can be uneven and laggy at times.The Last of Us is a triumphant piece of video game entertainment that I'm sure gamers will remember in years to come. It is an astonishing piece of art, and just a great experience that all true gamers and maybe even non-gamers can appreciate. With the recent release of the PS4, it is nice to leave the PS3 era with a game of this magnitude. A true masterpiece in my opinion.

This game is phenomenal, and I can recommend it to anyone. My only reservation is that combat is quite hard. This game is not a run and gun or button masher. They have a terrific game enemy AI that is really smart; the enemies don't just hide and wait for you to kill them. They are constantly flanking you and getting on your six, then grabbing you. They also cooperate, attack in groups, and they exploit your weaknesses (run out of ammo and they will all attack while you reload). Once you learn the right combat skills though, it isn't so bad. You particularly need to get good at sneak attacking, using explosives, melee, and the use of the bricks and bottles that litter any battle area.There is an auto-aim that is disabled by default called aim lock. It really helps save ammo,and makes the game much easier. I didn't turn it on until late in the game and I died 144 times on my first play through. (I don't usually die much.). I used auto-aim on my second play through and it made it much easier. I was also much better at combat by then and breezed through parts where I got stuck before. The game saves very often, and there is no penalty for dying. You are often saved after you have made some progress in an encounter, so you can pick yourself up and try to move further, no need to restart a whole battle from the beginning.Gameplay has one quirk, the save game function saves back to the last checkpoint, not where you are at the present, unless you are at a checkpoint. So if you finish a battle, then loot the area and save, your loot won't be there when you load. You have to move to the next checkpoint, which is usually identified by a cut scene, then save, or just let the game auto-save. I found the game saves so often that manual saves weren't really needed except as a backup in case of a loading mishap, which never happened.To those who comment that it is too slow at the beginning, I say it is that way by design so you can get a feel for the hostile and barren environment, and also learn the fundamentals of interacting with your environment and combat. If the game was a movie, you certainly wouldn't call the beginning slow. There are many movie quality cut scenes, in fact this game could be a movie, the acting and plot is that good, far beyond any other game. You will be moved by scenes in this game, really moved. By the end you will be appreciating the cut scenes as a break from intense combat.I don't know how they pulled off the visuals on a PS3. They are simply stunning. It is without a doubt one of the best looking PS3 games.I bought this on the advice of a friend who has played almost every FPS and RPG game that there is, on all platforms. He said it is a 20/10 and I agree! Do yourself a favor and buy this game, you won't be sorry.

The Last of Us is one of those games that I took a chance on. It's not normally in my wheelhouse of games I typically enjoy so it kind of went in with a strike already against it. Nonetheless, this game is unlike any game I have ever played. It grabs you from the start and simply refuses to let go. As always, this review will be split into three categories: Story, characters, and gameplay with story getting the most weight.Story: 10/10Simply, this story is just amazing. It's a story of a wounded man taking a young 14 year old girl across the country as a favor to a friend in a post-apocalyptic world that has been taken over by zombies. The man has some serious baggage and is simply not the best or easiest person to be around. But the girl endures and slowly their characters grow and change as they journey together.This story is extremely well written. It plays like a big budget film almost. And that's not a bad thing. The writing in this story and the details are just superb. The prologue is one of the better beginnings of a game that I have ever experienced. Simply it's well written. You are in a post apocalyptic world that has been ravaged by a fungus that changes people into zombies. You play as and interact with characters that have lost everything. The game continually reminds you, this is not a pleasant place anymore. It sprinkles in light hearted moments where for a few minutes you start to laugh or start thinking everything is going to be ok then it harshly reminds you, NO this is a world that has fallen apart...and there is no happy ending. The ending ends well and really provokes feelings to the player that few video games can do.Characters: 10/10As well as the story is written, the characters are equally well done. Joel is a deeply damaged man that has had his entire world ripped from him. He has lived a life of surviving and has paid the toll since the outbreak. Ellie is a typical young 14 year old girl but instead has been raised in a society that is in chaos. Whether you are defending yourself from infected zombies or humans that have turned on other humans to survive, these characters live in a unique world. The writers did a great job of letting you get attached to these characters but then harshly reminding you that they are damaged and they have their flaws. As the journey proceeds, you watch as Joel grows from a harsh, deeply damaged man with a ton of baggage to a man who accepts his past as his past and tries to move on and do the right thing. Ellie goes from the typical 14 year old naive little girl to an adult in a 14 year old's body.  The weaknesses of each character play off each other wonderfully. I simply have not seen character development or dialogue like this in any video game ever.Gameplay: 8/10If there is a weakness for me to this game it's the gameplay. But nonetheless, it is still a great gameplay. First the good. The detail in this gameplay is beyond spectacular. From upgrading your character with more health, or with less weapon sway, to collecting parts and upgrading your weapons. I thought overall the upgrading your character and weapons part of the game could have been better but just the fact that they included those elements really enriched the game. Probably the best part of the gameplay though was finding materials and crafting supplies like first aide kits and molotov cocktails. This really enriched the feeling that you are in a ravaged world and scraps of fabric can be the difference between life and death. The combat was also stellar. I loved the stealth feature that the game almost forced you to take in some areas. Sneaking around and shivving zombies in the neck and being able to take out an entire room full without being seen was awesome.Now, I'm probably a little more critical of the gameplay for this type of game (combat/shooter/adventure) than I normally would be as this is really not the type of games I normally enjoy. So keep that in mind. There really wasn't anything HUGE about the gameplay that detracted but there were several little things. For instance like the upgrading you character's abilities and your weapons. Those features were great but I felt there should have been more to them. Learning new combat moves, being able to make attachments for your weapons are just some examples that could have really enriched this part of the game. The load times when booting this game up were horrendous. HORRENDOUS. I also thought it would have been a nice touch if they could have added a few choices into the gameplay and story. I know that they had a story to tell and I wouldn't want it to have alternate endings or anything, but I really thought it would have been a good idea to give Joel options from time to time in what to say to help the player make Joel a little more or less personable depending on how the player wanted him to be. And I guess my biggest complaint about the gameplay were the collectibles. They were a nice touch but really served little purpose. Some of the notes were interesting and even sparked some dialogue between Joel and Ellie which was a nice touch. But really, other than trophy completion, the collectibles served little purpose.Overall 9.5/10Overall, this game is just fantastic. The story and the characters are some of the best written in all of video games. The characters were human in the most basic sense of the term and the story was a stark reminder of what humanity can be in it's darkest hour. The gameplay could have been sharpened a bit but it's hardly enough to detract from the utter brilliance of this game. If you enjoy a good story, and good characters, then really there is no reason to not play this game.

Most of the 1 star reviews aren't even reviews, they are just ramblings and make no sense. So it's sad such a great game is marred by having over 40 1 star reviews. This game is truly amazing and definitely has replay value. I feel like a lot of these comments are from 'fanboys' who are going to compare everything to Metal Gear Solid. This game is more story based, and there are MANY cut scenes that make it more into a movie than a game. It's incredibly intense and emotional with two lead characters you do care about and want to survive. What Joel and Ellie have to endure is heartbreaking and powerful in their search for a cure.While you do meet other players along the way, it centers on these two who travel across states, mostly on foot, through basically a post pandemic world where most of the population is infected by a fungal spore infection that covers your brain. Any human survivors left are doing just that--surviving. By any means necessary which makes for a scary world. Joel ends up being tasked with taking Ellie, who is very special, to a quarantine zone where people are waiting to receive her, thus beings their travels.Game play is VERY slow and paced in the beginning, and mostly consists of walking and climbing and picking up items. Good time to learn game mechanics, inventory, build stealth skills, character development and enjoy scenery, I suppose, but that's fine. Voice acting is excellent and does help keep you immersed. While people are complaining about the boring stealth play, be reminded you can play however you want. If you want to run into a room of 'clickers' with guns blazing, go ahead. The game is designed to be stealthy because infected are trying to kill you. It's not that kind of run and gun game. Being stealthy takes skill.There are many intense moments of being in the dark, being alone, being cornered, etc. that is pretty scary. Scenery, game design and art direction are fantastic, for those who care and appreciate it. There are little touches to the game that make it more intense and emotional and heartbreaking. What comes to mind are Joel and Ellie in the sewer, you can go into one of the sewer workers rooms, where people had obviously been hiding, there are dead bodies there, and also toys and children's drawings, as a sad realization that they were trying to have some normalcy for them amid all the chaos. Scrawled on the floor is "They Didn't Suffer" which was so heartbreaking to read. A nice (morbid) touch and very real. It just made me think of how horrific their situation was.Some gamers will love that kind of stuff, which is throughout this entire game. Ellie will tell you jokes, point out things, and be her own person. You even get to pet a Giraffe. It's an extremely emotionally riveting game that deals with hope, loyalty, trust, love and sacrifice.It is not without faults, as I think the levels are probably to easy on easy and to hard on everything else. Also, it takes forever to build up your weapons, and some important items are not easy to find. There are a few times that shootouts were tedious and annoying and the bad guys were too intense. Stealth works, but it  takes patience and time and that can get boring. I can think of a couple levels I would rather not do over when I replay.That said, this game is still 5 stars for everything else, and since you can keep all your weapons, upgrades, etc. When you replay that should make killing a heck of a lot better  and easier. Again, this game is not for everyone. If you like to enjoy the atmosphere in games, appreciate scenery and landscape that you're playing in, like secondary characters that interact with you, and that you care about, and is also fun and creepy to play, give this a shot.  It is very long, I will admit to that and the ending upset a lot of people, and on some levels doesn't makes sense, and on other levels makes perfect sense. It's up to your own interpretation.I loved it and will play it again. Watch some game play online, there are plenty on YouTube and see if it's something you might want to play yourself.
