This game was an excellent buy.  It's not my favorite game of all time, but now that it is a couple of years old you can have it for a song and it was quite fun to play.  I'm not quite done with it but I'm near the end of the main quest.Much of the game you spend swinging from one place to another on the grappling hook.  It's much faster than walking and utterly necessary in many cases, especially for combat.  It's very much a stealth game because a couple of shots will take you down.  Not that you sneak around on ground level a lot, typically, but you are always looking get on elevated ground or the rafters and jump down on people.  It almost feels like I would imagine a spiderman game would be.The combat took a bit to get used to.  You can tell this game was made for consoles because the computer does all of the work.  You just basically point in the right direction and click and it fills in all sorts of ninja moves.  That's probably the worst thing about the game: it was designed for the very limited amount of control the various consoles give you, so on a PC you end up just hitting space bar over and over for lots of different types of actions (opening doors, jumping, climbing, etc.  All space bar).  On a PC you have much more ability to control and way more buttons at your disposal.  I guess if they had made a different button for everything, it would be too easy on a PC and they would have to rework the whole game.  This is why consoles are a bad thing...they make the games bad for everyone.The atmosphere of the game is fun.  Very batman-like.  I think they did a good job of engaging you in the story and making you feel like you really are batman.  It's consistent with the Christian Bale batman movie feel.  Good stuff.Graphics are pretty decent.  Like I said, It's clearly an adaptation of a console game, but it's a good one.  It doesn't seem to be a particularly large game.  The main quest isn't all that long.  It's not like something like, say, Skyrim, where you spend hours just learning a blacksmith skill.  Here you just play through the various quests.  There are little trophies you can get, but they don't mean much.  You don't really have to earn gear or skills to speak of.The story is pretty reasonable.  The game feels quite scripted, though.  In every situation there seems to be exactly one way to get through.  Sometimes it's a puzzle to figure it out, but there's always just one solution.  Not a lot of freedom on your part.  I guess that makes it easier to tell a coherent story.  I guess I'm comparing it to something like Deus Ex Human Revolution, which is also stealth and has a scripted main story.  But the latter has far better controls and much more freedom.  When you compare it to that, Arkham city is pretty poor.  But that's a high bar.  In my opinion Deux EX HR was a pretty dang good game.

I avoided this game for a lot of years. I'll keep it short since many people don't care, but a lot of people do care about what type of DRM is present. Warner Bros. entertainment has gone back into the game and altered it to now use  Steamworks so a lot of complaints that some reviewers have made are probably gone now. I personally don't like any kind of DRM, but thus far in my experience Steam is probably the most benign.If you grew up with the 16-bit consoles, you know that there were many Batman games and very few that were any good. That changed with the Arkham games. The series has made Batman come alive. There are a few problems, but it's hard to overstate how much fun and what a good job they've done. The game appears to be using the same engine as Bioshock because the backgrounds are textured and have much debris. Everything looks simply great. I played through the entire game on a Nvidia GT 240 and while I had more problems with slow down than I did in Arkham Asylum, it was quite playable. I also didn't turn down any of the graphics settings, so I might've been able to improve them there, but it wasn't irritating enough to need that.The basic premise of the game is that you've been thrown into Arkham city, a big prison city that's been walled off in the center of Gotham, and you get to stop the overall bad guy from implementing his protocol 10 plan. More or less it's just an excuse to go around and beat up bad guys and complete certain tasks. There certain points in the plot that make very little sense, but overall it works and the game is just fun to play anyway. You can do things like beat up thugs, hide above them and drop down on them, sneak up behind them and do a silent takedown, or any other variety of tricks you can use.  One of the coolest is Detective mode, where you can see who has a gun and who has a regular weapon or is unarmed as well as seeing them through walls; think X-ray specs.  You spend this game primarily fighting with Penguin and Joker, with Two Face and Mr. Freeze fights, also Ra sha goul (spelling?).You do not just control Batman in this game. You also get to control Catwoman. This sounds a bit better than it is, because Catwoman is sort of a lesser Batman in many ways. She can do some unique things like crawling upside down on certain walkways, but she's weaker and doesn't have as wide a variety of tricks. Her version of detective mode was very irritating to me for some reason I can't quite place, the colors just off or a bit blurry to my eyes maybe, though on the up side she looked a whole lot better doing the silent takedowns! Don't get your hopes up too much though, she's in the game very little.  The levels she appears in are quite fun, but amazingly short.  Just when you start getting the hang of her moves, the level ends and you don't play another one for a LONG time.  You do get to play her after you've beaten the game, but it's still much more limited to what Batman has and you can't complete his tasks or anything.  Mostly it just seems to be so you can beat up guys or find Riddler trophies specific to her.  Slightly disappointing, but not awful.  I also got a copy of an after the game level bit where Batman is captured and Robin has to go in and rescue him, but again playing as Robin feels a bit like a scaled back Batman.If I have anything complaints, it's that the game is pretty short.  It's longer than Asylum was and you can play after the fact by going around the city, but there aren't a lot of custom tasks to complete after that, it's mostly just to find Riddler trophies, then track down hostages he took.  I just got bored with finding them and quit playing, though if you're a die hard you may like it.  Still, just simply a great game in my opinion.

If you are like me you’re probably approaching Euro Truck Simulator 2 (ETS 2) wondering why you have a strange fascination with a game that simulates a job. And not a particularly grandiose job either. Sure you have your surgeon simulator, even your farm simulators, and the perennial god-like mayoral simulators in games like SimCity and Cities XL. But a game about driving a truck across vast expanses? That’s just silly… or is it? I purchased this game during the Steam Winter Sale ’13 and I’m completely hooked. If you’re a simulator junkie, enjoy building up your little empire from meager beginnings, and the thought of the open road in massive, lumbering multi-axel vehicles is appealing then this is your game!--------------------GAMEPLAY:You’ll start by creating a user profile (registration with the developer is optional), picking a name for in-game persona, selecting an avatar, choosing a title for your company, and selecting a starting point from slew of cities in Western Europe. Your garage is a small sort of dumpy one-stall that will serve as the base for your trucking empire. At the onset you have no choice but to take contract jobs from other established trucking companies hauling freight on a one-off basis for cash.Eventually you can either save enough cash or borrow from the bank and purchase your own truck. Owning your own rig is really the meat of ETS 2. Once you own your own truck you can take better jobs for better pay.The games interface is a clean and easy to navigate menu of icons. You’ll select your next job from a menu that features the trailer you’re hauling, the cargo contents, distance, recommended GPS route and most importantly the pay. You can filter each job by various criteria including, total pay, pay per kilometer, origin, destination.Eventually you’ll be able to buy more trucks and hire more drivers and build your company into a real freight-hauling powerhouse. Truck manufacturers, recruitment centers all have to be discovered in each city. So the game encourages you to explore a bit. The in-game map is very extensive and covers the location of each area in fantastic detail. My understanding of the game is that the routes mirror their real-world counterparts quite well.Your drivers also feature a leveling system. Each driver can invest skill points into a number of areas from being able to haul longer distances, to ADR certifications for hauling dangerous cargos, fragile or time sensitive freight and more. As you level better paying jobs will open up. Your hired drivers will also level and you can set their training priorities.Trucks feature customizable parts from engines and transmissions to aesthetic components like side-skirts, wheels, lights and much more.The game does support keyboard + mouse configurations, controllers and best of all wheels. I’m using a Logitech Driving Force GT and the experience is fantastic. Lots of options to customize controls and tweak the feel of the trucks are present in the menu.--------------------GRAPHICS:In short the graphics are pretty great. This game doesn’t feature any type of crazy effects but the environments are rendered very nicely. Weather effects like rain and fog are perhaps the most impressive aspect to the engine. The draw of the open road and the occasional vista be it seeing the ocean in Calais or the forested expanse of Germany is very nice.--------------------WHAT I LIKE ABOUT ETS 2:• The game doesn’t really have an objective other than growing your business and acquiring more trucks and drivers but it is strangely addictive and relaxing. Driving a haul from point to point and seeing more of Europe is really just a cool experience.• Lots of trucks from a lot of vendors including: Scania, Volvo, Iveco, Majestic (Mercedes), MAN, Renault, and DAF. All feature fully rendered interiors with working gauges.• The map is absolutely huge and features large chunks from major Euro nations including Germany, Northern Italy, Eastern France, Netherlands, Great Britain, Belgium, Luxembourg, Poland, and more.• The menus and in-game aids like GPS routing are intuitive and easy to use. Mapping controls to my wheel is also very easy.• Fantastic user community with a lot of folks making some excellent mods. Mods do everything from changing paint schemes to interior truck makeovers. Larger mods change the made-up in-game companies to real-world companies. Other mods add to the map such as adding all of Hungary or more cities to Italy. The developer has really made their game accessible to modders and the game features a menu to manage mods.• Streaming live radio broadcasts from Europe through the game into the cab of your truck. Seriously, as an American I have grown to love Euro radio.--------------------WHAT I DON’T LIKE ABOUT ETS 2:• The in-game truck customization from the developer are a bit limited. The modding community has done admirably to pick up the slack.• European cities are well represented but are extremely small in-game. Like a few blocks small. After a time you realize that instead of driving through the streets of Munich or Paris exploring your surroundings in a huge rig you’ll just quickly drive the few square blocks in each to discover the local truck vendor and recruitment agency and move on.--------------------OTHER NOTESOne of my biggest questions was about how long a typical haul between cities takes. The answer is that no, the game doesn’t simulate the actual time to drive between cities, that would be insane, however expect hauls to take a chunk of time. For instance and in-game haul of approximately 3hrs might take 20 minutes of real world time.

It isn't often that I get the chance to review a game so close to release, let alone before release.  I stumbled across a retailer that accidentally sold me a copy several days ago.  I can't say I minded too much.Dark Souls 2, for those who haven't heard of it, is the latest release by From Software the brilliant masterminds behind Demon's Souls, Dark Souls and the lesser known King's Field Series.  The Souls series has become well known for being challenging, brutal and quite possibly the most unique set of games of this console generation.  If you haven't played the other games yet, don't worry.  There isn't much of a story needed to jump right in here.The first thing you notice in Dark Souls 2 is a daunting selection of characters to start with and a myriad of stats to worry about.  Don't worry too much here.  These are just your starting basics in the game and there is nothing that will hold back a character if you chose to go another route later on.  A warrior could cast spells and a cleric could live happily as an armored tank given the proper spending of stats.  Think more about what kind of weapons or spells you are interested in and build around that.  Experimentation is the fun part here.  In a few days I have already gone through as many characters and builds.  I found that the swordsman seems to start off with better weapons than most of the classes, but that is rather subjective.Combat is smoother than the previous games.  I could be wrong, but it seems like the tap dodge actually functions now at getting your character to jump back out of range.  It is also possible to turn around and run away while locked on a target.  Very useful to create some distance as needed.  Special attention has been given to two weapon fighting in this release.  While I didn't get into it beyond a few fights, it was nice to be able to string combinations of strong and weak attacks with both hands.  Sadly, this means that the ability to parry has taken a hit for most builds, especially in two weapon fighting.  Enemies are also a bit brighter about not turning their back to you.  This combined with what seems to be a smaller hit box makes backstabs very tough to pull off.Death and failure is a pretty constant companion in this game.  From has decided to go back to Demon's Souls on how it gets treated.  Death will cost you your "Body" form (more on that later) and become hollow.  In this form you will look rather ugly and suffer a loss in total life.  You will be stuck in this state until you use an item to restore you body.  Each subsequent death in hollow form will continue to remove more of your maximum life until you end up at about 1/2 your total.  Can't say I have ever seen a game that makes things harder as you continue to fail.  This sounds tough, but it didn't hit me too hard in my explorations so far.Unlike most RPG's which have separate concepts of experience and money, DS2 groups both together in the form of souls.  You spend souls to buy items, to repair broken equipment, upgrade equipment and to strengthen the stats of your character.  This means that you will end up making tough decisions on what you buy as you work hard to build your pile of souls.Stats got a bit of rework in this game in comparison to the others.  Armor now has requirements to wear, so no more piling up the armor and tanking through the game.  Yout resistance no longer increases with each level, you now have to put points into specific stats to raise it.  No more dumping all your points into spellcasting and ignoring the other stats.  This again sounds tough, but it seems that enemies have been scaled to take this into account.  I haven't bumped resistance much and I still haven't come across many if anything that can wipe you out in one shot.Gameplay aside, this is a nice looking game as well.  I may have been spoiled with the PC release of Dark Souls which had large numbers of mods and enhancements to graphics, but this game looks at least slightly better than Dark Souls 1.  Lighting plays a larger role in this game and it shows nicely.  When you carry torches, light shines and shadows move in a very realistic manner.  Clothing was the largest improvement that I noticed.  It hangs realistically and seems to blow with the environment.More importantly, this game runs very smooth.  I haven't bothered doing an install yet, but I still get tolerable load times (the few that you need) and I don't get the chugging frame rates which plagued the previous games.  Sadly (for me at least) the rag-doll physics of fallen enemies is gone.  No longer will that dead soldier stick to you and flop around like a deflated balloon when you run by.I haven't tried out the multiplayer yet.  It is still a bit early for the community and my 360 isn't setup in a spot where I actually have internet.  If I try it out I'll come back and give this review an update.I still plan to get the PC version when it comes out, but I still don't regret this impulse purchase.  I plan to get many hours of enjoyment out of this.

Horribly annoying (Insert curse words here) at best.So instead of a enemy character in game, going through a full range of emotions, giving you time to react. Now when this is on a little small ledge and you can't do that, well your pooper is going to get banged by the enemy. So its frustrating. On the other hand, your player tracking...works at best, and at its worst, will either pull you to your death if an enemy gets knocked off a cliff edge, or even when the automatic targeting is turned off in game. The game is fundamentally broken. This was one of the hugest most tragic mistakes by FromSoftware in my perspective, because its trying to combine two completely different elements of gameplay and make it work...I can't comment on PC games. But on console games, as far as I know, most game developers have always had Story, and PvP separate, for good reason. It's like trying to combine oil and water, it can be done, but it doesn't work. Because when your fighting mini bosses, and that's what a lot of the enemies in the game are, you don't need some douchebag to show up and invade you during this time. It works right now because you can find people to summon.. pretty much all the time, and you can get summoned decently. But so help you if you are trying to make your way back through the game and get your souls, and some BS magic user is the one who's invaded you. Which will most likely be the case. There is now a backwards invasion system, sort of. You get summoned forcefully to the world of another user when you enter a particular area of the game. The 'Rat Covenant' and your goal as far as I can tell, you know besides being pulled into PvP you don't want to participate in, is to either defeat the user... or make it to the end of the area.So then if the gameplay mechanics, and underlying structure of the game is basically broken? What's good about Dark Souls 2?Well, Dark Souls 2, has a TON of great armor, at least aesthetically that you can get. Has a lot of very very cool weapons you can get as well. Now even when you upgrade them to max. Their still not going to be as potent for you, as they are for any enemy character using the same weapon. It has a pretty cool world, nice fantasy setting. The enemy designs are nice looking. Some are even sexy looking.They actually fixed the crossbow gun, you can now manually aim it. Which is wonderful. Quite frankly the only thing they've ever gotten right is the fact that you can be invaded.. but as far as balance goes.. I don't think its something that will ever work out. Just because of all the elements involved.So to sum it all up in a nice little neat package. The world seems better, seems bigger, but its really just as small as the first game. Levels are just a bit more open, but it isn't an open world at all. Travel is improved. Weapon moveset's have improved. Cool enemies, some cool characters you get to talk to. A lot of cool armor sets, if you can find them or get the drops. Drop rate's have not improved by much. Fundamental gameplay and mechanics of the game are broken because they are trying to combine PvP(Player verses player) and PvE (Player verses enemies in game). You'd think they would have learned more from Dark Souls and other RPG's. You'd think armor would actually do its job but it really doesn't. The difficulty curve of the game goes at a steady climb and then just spikes through the roof toward the end of the game (Maybe I should say "ends"). So you will probably start running into a lot of brick walls in the game. The game is designed with a lot of traps. So its not like they say "learning from your mistakes" its "Learning to spot FromSoftware's traps" would be much more appropriate. They think this is making the game hard.. but anyone can put a person in a box an then beat the fire out of them, and call it "Were making this challenging" but that's not really making the game harder, so much as making the game abusive to the player.A lot of awesome elements in the game. And it really could be such a fun experience and really bring friends together. But being as co-op is sporadic at best. Before my review I would like to address some complaints people have and inform you how to avoid these situations and potential angry moments towards the game. The complaints I'll briefly address will be 'the game is too hard', leveling and improving your estus flask.So, while hollow, when you die your health bar progressively gets smaller and smaller until you are at 50% health. To avoid this you can use a human effigy to restore your humanity and then wear a Ring of Life Protection. Like Dark Souls 1 this ring will break when you die but you won't lose any of your souls or humanity and you'll be returned to the last bonfire without having to risk returning to where you died. But here's how it's different from Dark Souls 1 in this game you can repair your broken Ring of Life Protection in Majula for 3,000 souls at the blacksmith. Which takes out essientially any risk factor in the game, making the game easier than Dark Souls 1 not harder. And I've come across three of these rings.People also seem to have trouble with understanding how to level up or how to level up their estus flask. You don't level up at bonfires anymore, you level up from the lady in green by the bonfire in Majula and only her. Leveling up your estus flask is not done by increasing the intensity of bonfires doing that in this game by using a bonfire ascetic makes that specific area NG+ difficulty and respawns the enemies including bosses. So you give the lady in green estus flask shards to increase your total count of estus flasks and to increase their healing ability you have to burn sublime bone dust at the bonfire. These items are found throughout the game as you progress.MY REVIEW:-Overall I feel like the story is easier to understand than the first game. And that it's overall more fun.-Graphics are improved from Dark Souls 1.-Movement, jumping, rolling and combat are improved.-Summoning is now easier especially with friends by using the name engraved ring.-All new enemies, covenants, weapons and areas for the most part.-Very in depth game where you get to choose your path fighting numerous bosses along the way. Depending on which initial routes you take you will fight them in a different order than someone else and a lot are missable.-The sense of reward and accomplishment is still there like with the first game.-I would rate this a high 9 out of 10.-Overall I like the improvements and how they simplified things. For example in Dark Souls 1 if you had 3 specific souls you wanted to use you had to use them individually. Now you can select the amount and use them all at once. Little improvements like that are nice but all in all the game is greatly improved over the first one.NOTABLE CHANGES:-Humanity. The counter is gone from the top left corner. Now human effigies are used to become human.-Leveling up your character and estus flask.-Leveling up only can be done in Majula, which is Firelink Shrine of DS2.-Increasing bonfire intensity makes the game more difficult for that specific area.-Additional useable items, right/left hand slots, and two more ring slots.-Each armor piece has its own section now so it isn't all clumped into one location.-Decreasing health bar while hollow (having the dark pyromancy glove scales with your 'hollowness').-The Dark Souls 1 DLC that added 'dark magic' is now more prominent in this game they're called hexes.-New 'cross region' feature added in the in game menu which allows you to restrict it for better connection during co-op and PvP which I find does work. I've had very few laggy moments.-You are now matched with people based on your soul level AND overall total soul count. Meaning staying low level to match low levels will no longer work for PvP.-Name engraved ring which allows for you to connect with friends easier while wearing it.-Along with the cross region being set to restricted by default so is in game voice chat.-Soul Vessels acquired throughout the game allow you to reallocate your skill points.-Fairly in depth tutorial at the beginning for new players.-You can no longer farm enemies in this game they will stop respawing after you kill them around 10 times.-Only one ember required for all weapon infusions.This game is loads of fun which you will undoubtedly spend at least 60+ hours per playthrough. The sense of reward and accomplishment is still there like the first game when you defeat a tough boss that has killed you multiple times. I would recommend this to anyone looking for a fun challenge. And I hope this review / mini guide helps out.

First, don't listen to the crazy nitpickers who are dropping this game to 1-2 stars because it's not exactly the same as the original. They probably only put a few hours into the game and didn't get to realize its full potential because they ended up running away. I've put over 60 hours into this game and have scratched more than just the surface. Even though some of these nitpicks are warranted, this game is still far better than most others out there and thus doesn't deserve a 1-2 star review. That being said,The Dark Souls games have me hook, line, sinker, pole and fisherman. For once I feel like I'm playing a true RPG. I'm tired of all the hand-holding more modern games tend to employ. In Dark Souls (both 1 and 2) you have a vague idea of what you need to do, but the direction you choose is all your own. Finding awesome loot and destroying seemingly impossible bosses feels SO REWARDING! No maps, no cursors, no piles upon piles of loot ala games like Diablo 2 and 3.The original Dark Souls (DaS) completely blew me away with the raw challenge, the few cheap deaths (it happens, but it's rare) and the environment. It sort of reminded me of Ico, but in hell.Dark Souls 2 changes things up a bit, mostly for the better, but some aspects don't quite live up to the original.The biggest improvement in my opinion is the combat and enemy AI. Two-handing weapons are a real viable option here. Also, being able to move while aiming with a crossbow, the ability to cancel spells, strong attack combos and grealy improved animations really keep the combat feeling fresh. Each weapon feels very unique. Also, foes are much more challenging this time around, no more backstab-fests like DaS1.The online components for DaS games are great. It feels and plays mostly like a single player game, but on the ground are littered helpful (or humorous, or misleading) messages, bloodstains which allow you to watch the final seconds of a fellow player's demise and if you're human (as opposed to hollow, which I'll touch on) then you'll see summon signs which will allow you to summon other players so you can co-op against a tough boss or a difficult stretch. Red summon signs allow you to PVP with other players. Also, you can invade other people's game or have your game invaded. One difference between Das2 and the original is that you can still be invaded while hollow. The way player worlds bleed into each other is genius.The way humanity is handled in DaS2 is significantly different. Now to become human you have to consume a (fairly rare) consumable called an effigy. Death will make you hollow and cut a small percentage of your maximum health. Each subsequent death continues to chip away at your max health until it reaches 50% In order to get your max health back to 100% you need to consume an effigy.I'm really not sure how I feel about my health meter being chipped away with each death. On one hand it adds a new dimension to the game and it really plays into the idea that you are becoming more hollow, but on the other hand it makes an already difficult game much more difficult. The more you stink at the game the harder it becomes. I can see this putting off new players. There are ways to mitigate this, but for the sake of keeping this review spoiler-free I'll avoid diving into that.One other big change is that in DaS2 enemies will quit re-spawning after you kill them a number of times (I believe it's 10 or 15). This makes farming for goodies much more limited, which I happen to like but other people may disagree. One benefit is that if you are having a tough time in an area then sheer persistence will eventually pay off because enemies you do kill will eventually fade away, making level progression easier.Healing items are handled a bit differently as well. Estus flasks are the healing item of choice in DaS games and in DaS2 you start with zero. Instead you'll start with a few lifegems which regenerate your life significantly slower than estus, but you are able to consume on the move and they are a consumable item which you can purchase from a merchant. Soon after the tutorial level you'll get your first estus flask, but only one. You'll need to find estus shards to get more than one swig off that sweet nectar!Here are some of the negatives:The biggest disappointment for me is that the world doesn't feel as nearly cohesive as the first. The world design in the first game is absolutely breathtaking, everything flows together so perfectly and the shortcuts that you unlock are just brilliant. DaS2 has some of this but it just doesn't feel quite as "organic". DaS1 reminds me of Ico in the way that exploration works, Das2 is more conventional. However, the world in DaS2 seems to be far bigger and more varied, so there is a plus to this.Textures do seem to be a step back from the original, however, the framerate is buttery smooth. 60+ hours in and I still have yet to experience any sort of framerate issue. In my opinion this tradeoff is worth it, but this may be considered a negative for some.One other flaw in my opinion is that instead of leveling up a bonfires, you have to travel back to the main hub town (Majula) and talk to somebody. This is annoying because it requires two (fairly long) loading screens as well has having to click through the same 4 lines of dialog. This doesn't seem like a big deal at first, but after a while it becomes a bit grating.There are a few other nitpicks I have but they are mostly minor compared to the above. DaS2 does have its share of flaws, but they are greatly overshadowed by how awesome everything else is.As verbose as this review is, I still haven't touched on so many of the awesome features of this game. I'll leave that for you to discover. I will end with this though:I have no idea why some people (especially published reviewers) are saying DaS2 eases new players better than DaS1. DaS2 is SIGNIFICANTLY harder even right at the beginning. Death means lower max health, only one estus flask to start early game as opposed to five, way more enemy mobs than the first, enemies hit harder, are smarter and chase you down with a vengeance should you try to run away! Also, rolling through attacks and parrying is significantly harder. Furthermore it's harder to farm, fall deaths are much more frequent, and more. I think new players should start with the original Dark Souls, I find it to be much more forgiving, besides it's a masterpiece! The extreme difficulty is certainly not a bad thing, I was worried that this game might be too easy after having played so many hours of the original.If you're a new player then just be prepared to die. Over and over and over again, but also be prepared for some of the most rewarding gaming experiences possible. I've played many great RPGs, including Chrono Trigger, many Final Fantasy games, Baldur's Gate (both console and PC), Planescape and much more. The Dark Souls games are now my favorite RPGs of all-time. They're that good.

Let me start by saying that DSII is awesome but very hard, most likely only hardcore or masochistic people will enjoy this game. You must learn from your mistakes, and you -WILL- die, a lot. If you disliked Dark Souls you most likely won't enjoy Dark Souls II since they are so similar, but if you did enjoy Dark Souls then you know what you're in for. DSII is familiar in a way DS vets will understand (controls, mechanics, UI mostly the same), with enough new material and variation to keep things fresh.A few great changes: you can warp from any bonfire to any other bonfire you've already discovered, basic fast-travel is fine and unlocked at the beginning of the game; secondly, DSII holds a solid 30fps at all times even when there are a dozen things happening on screen at once (remember how awful Blighttown was in Dark Souls?); thirdly, DSII has an updated game engine and visually it's an obvious step above DS, the lighting is especially enhanced and really makes for some fun exploring - especially when monsters come sneaking out of the shadows! You're also able to light torches at bonfires now which helps you explore extra dark areas, it's a very cool feature.Souls `vets will find just as much difficulty as DS offered and new players may find the game a bit strenuous. Players who explore, persist, and learn from their deaths will find great reward in the new challenges DSII offers - especially those players who explore each nook and cranny in the world. The stakes have never been higher in DS, with each death your total life will be reduced, and while a rare human effigy will restore this, it makes each venture into the unknown a tad overwhelming (which is kinda the point, amirite?).Multiplayer is monstrously improved this time, connections are smoother, and joining another player is much easier - the best part, if you summon another player you get an immediate response whether or not it was a success, thank goodness! It wasn't as hard for me to buddy up with a phantom in the first few hours and we had a jolly good time breaking faces. There are new covenants this time around, each offers a different take on multiplayer, but I won't spoil those here.New-Game+ is here as always but now you can choose when to begin, very nice if you're holding off for late game PvP. Over all it's a really dang fun and a worthy successor to Dark Souls, definitely a must buy for me.One thing is for certain though, DSII is not watered down.Prepare to die, over and over and over again.

But no amount of pretty visuals or decent voice-acting can make up for such pointless moments in the story, if there is a story. There's just no real good reason to care about what's happening or about the characters, despite the variety. Enemies also have no meat on their bones, and are simply just there for one thing; to be the bad guys. While some of you are okay with this, it just doesn't cut it in this day and age anymore. They are there, just to be defeated.Plot holes are also another issue. A lot of the stuff that happens in the game are never explained... they just happen just because. There's just no history or sense of consistency within the events that happen. I suppose in medieval times it certainly felt that way, but if there is going to be a story worth telling.... there should be reason behind everything that happens, not just "Hey, I'm a hero. let's a kill a baddie, and do it again tomorrow. Oh look, a transexual just teleported in front of me, and killed two more foes I could have easily dealt with... and now he/she's gone. Hmm. Oh well."That is a big no-no. You don't do that, ever. Oh yes, speaking of "no-no's", there's a character named Nowi whose name is Nono in Japanese. She looks and acts like a child (an adolescent child), and yet... she's supposed to be 1000 years old. Yep, that's right... a 1000 year old barely-teens girl. This feels like an excuse to fanservice her for those creepy pervs who are into minors between the ages of 12 and 15 in real life. How could you possibly see a girl who looks old enough to be your little sister in middle school to be 1000 years old, especially if she acts like a middle schooler? Living for 1000 years doesn't serve a purpose to her character at all, other than for a man's fantasy.Overall, the story is not immersive, it's cliche, with creepy fanservice. Most of you may disagree, but you obviously have not either played all the Fire Emblem games, nor have played enough games with better stories (*cough*, Chrono Trigger, Bioshock and Silent Hill 2, ahem... The Last of Us too...) that know how to make you care without needing to be overly complicated or stereotype anything. But I suppose given the genre is mostly Strategy, it's hardly surprising. It's just disappointing. Command & Conquer Red Alert series kinda does the same thing.Gameplay (7.9/10)It is without a doubt, one of the best in a Fire Emblem game. What's new is the Pair-Up system (no, the marriage system is not new, it's actually in Fire Emblem 4. It' just that the Western audience never got to play it), which allows you to combine two units into one, giving the leader of the pair-up benefits like stat boosts or better chance of criticals as examples. But whether you pair up or not, if two characters of the opposite gender battle next to each other enough, they can eventually get married and have children, which are basically new units with mixed traits from both parents.Reclassing allows a character to... change their class. If a character is a Tactician, you can choose to make him/her anything else (most of the time). Some characters have limited options, though, but at least the good thing is, this feature is not forced... meaning you most likely will never actually need it to progress through the "story" or challenging areas of the game.Casual mode removes the grief that plagued other Fire Emblem games; losing characters permanently upon defeat.  You can choose to go Casual regardless of the difficulty too. I don't see why most people hate that feature being on there... you are not being forced to dumb down. And besides, it allows you to enjoy the game with relaxation if you really want to.However, I find the difficulty balance and map challenge to be a bit broken. Normal Difficulty, you are strolling about defeating enemies you excel against like you should. Lunatic and higher, you basically have to grind and use exploits to win. There's just no way to progress without being cheap yourself, and even that's hard to do. The maps are not as tactical as other FE games, simply put.They just aren't. In fact, I find myself hardly finding a way to outsmart my foes (whether it's the lack of need to make an effort, or regardless of the effort, it's nearly impossible to do so). If you ask me, you should just stick to Normal, because at least it won't be unfair (or boring for some people).Also... the DLC is nothing special, and they mostly feel like cash-ins. And what's the deal with not being able to create a custom character that's not white? There are black NPC's in the game!Graphics (8/10)For the most part, it's charming, It's certainly an improvement from other FE games, and you will mostly notice it during battle between units and during cinematic cutscenes. Other than that, it's pretty much the same 2D sprite when playing in general.The 3D is rather impressive, though. I figured it would be tacked on, but it's not. In the gameplay, in the cinematics... everything, looks pretty awesome in 3D. There's not much to complain about the looks of the game, other than that the transition between dialogue or cinematics and gameplay... it feels out of place. Oh yes, speaking of dialogue...Voiceover (6/10)While it's decent for the most part... it's just cliche as well, besides the story. Unnecessary grunting and screaming, and overly dramatic at some points. Melodrama would be an understatement, especially in situations that just don't call for it. Here's an example: Someone walks into a door and actually breaks their nose, and soon pass out. Commencing funeral and overwhelming tears.Oh, here's another thing... the voiceover for the dialogue in-game is something like this:Avatar (Dialogue): Y-yes... Thank you, Chrom.Avatar (Actual Voiceover): Thank you, Chrom.Chrom (Dialogue): Ah, then you know who I am?Chrom (Actual Voiceover): Hm?Avatar (Dialogue): No, actually, I... It's strange... Your name, it just... came to me...Avatar (Actual Voiceover): Huh?Chrom: (Dialogue): ...hmm, how curious.Chrom (Actual Voiceover): Hmm.Seriously?! 80% of the dialogue in-game is just a bunch of grunts, questioning sighs, and screaming that fill in for conversations! That's terrible. If they can bother putting in noises for dialogue, they could have actually put in some voiceover like they did for some parts of the game! I'm disappointed by this...Sound (8.2/10)Every sword clash, every enemy attack, every magical property... everything fits, simply put. There's not much to say here, other than that there's always room for improvement. The music is charming and fits the setting of the game too, and I don't need to explain why.Replay Value (7.5/10)If you like to explore other marriage options, then that may get you to replay the game's story. Other than that, there's not much reason to go back other than to test yourself on how you can deal with the absurd difficulty levels or how fast you can beat the game with no mistakes.Overall (6.8/10)This game is something a lot of Strategy genre fans will like, as well as anime fans. The Casual mode allows everyone else to not be scared away. Everyone else... you should approach this game with caution. Find a rental first, or borrow a bought copy from someone else. It's not as great as most people claim it to be. No game really is, but this one is just too obviously bogged down. You'd be a fool (or insane) to think this is the best Fire Emblem game, or best game in general, to date.

this is the thirteenth installment of the 'fire emblem' saga. those of us in north american having been privy to only about half of the series. nevertheless, the franchise has spanned every console from NES to 3DS. the game mixes sleek suikoden III style storyline graphics with a battle system reminiscent of 'advanced wars: dual strike', one of my favorite titles for the DS.this is my first foray into the fire emblem world so i chose the normal difficulty and casual play (indicating that if a character dies in battle they do not die permanently for the entire game). i am breezing through it easily enough and may re-play on a harder difficulty or non-casual play, my characters seem to rarely die anyway.things i like about this game: you level up fairly quicky and easily; some of the negative reviews for this game indicate it's hard to level or they are having difficulty progressing after a certain part because the enemies are too strong. however, the game offers paralogues (side-quests) aside from the main story to help you level up a bit more. there are also opponents that randomly pop up on the world map after completing a chapter. i've also read on reviews that you can level up by challenging other players online, but i have not tried any of the wireless features yet.i like aspects of the battle system: having an ally adjacent to you powers you up and make trigger a double attack. there is a clear delineation of which weapon trumps which: sword beats ax, lance beats sword. however, i stopped utilizing the 'pair up' feature as i fail to fully understand it's usefulness. there are probably other aspects of the battle system that i fail to understand or use to their full advantage. i never 'trade' and rarely go for opening treasures in the battles.one thing i DO NOT like about this game is the inventory system. why does each character have to have their own little mini-inventory of items that then need to swapped between a continuously ballooning cast of playable characters? i wish all weapons and items would be in one big inventory that all characters could access. this would make buying/equipping weapons a lot easier.another thing i do not like is that this game does not allow you to compare two weapons' stats side-by-side, so you can instantly see which is better. instead you have to toggle between to the two weapons you're comparing and hope you can remember that four stats each weapon has.my last gripe, most weapons are consumable! they only last a certain number of attacks that tick down with each attack. however, you are constantly finding new weapons and there are a plethora shops about so it's not much of a pain, but if you refer to my first gripe about the inventory system and such. this gripe relates to the other.so those are the only three drawbacks i see to this game. the game also keeps kind of a 'story, fight; story, fight;' rhythm that can leave you wanting to skip through the story to the actual playable parts of the game (the story's not that grand, but since i've never played any other 'fire emblem' games i'm sure i'm missing some references or something).all in all a good game, i can see how it got an honorable mention for 'top 10 games of 2013' by amazon and it certainly utilizes the 3D well. also, one last note. if you check most of the previous 'fire emblem' games fetch a nice price once they're out of print (the wii and gamecube games go for +$100) so this game is also likely to retain its value and likely to become valuable in a few years as well. another reason to get this game!

Im mainly an online RPG gamer and was interested in this game due to the RPG elements such as equipment upgrade and 4 distinct classes. Theres so much this game does right but it also has several flaws. Ill start off by talking about the game itself and then the pros and cons as  I see them.In this game you choose one of four classes and kill bugs. Thats the entire game. There arent hundereds of different types of bugs, but the variety is enough to engage the player. Instead of being one long fluid game with check-points, its mission based meaning after each mission you get to upgrade your character and continue the game. You can also repeat the mission or do previous missions. Given that there are a grand total of 85 missions and 4 characters, your looking at 340 missions worth of gameplay. Add in the 5 difficulties and your at 1700 missions; though to be fair, you most likely wont be playing through every difficulty. This brings up another positive aspect of the game - you can switch to any difficulty at any time. Want to start the game on the hardest? Go for it, you wont beat the first mission, but the options available letting the player decide how steep they want to grade the difficulty. Armor and weapon upgrades are found by killing enemies and picking them up - the same weapons are found on the same levels. The only downside is once all the enemies are dead, the mission ends even if there are weapons lying around so you better be picking up upgrades as your playing.The classes are also balanced and equally fun to play, though its smart to stick with one class and complete at least half the missions to get a feel before trying out another. This is especially true with the games lack of instructions, its clear the port to the US had little investment from major publishers.There are several aspects about online gameplay in EDF20205 which are lacking from modern online games. For one, players create a room and get to name the room (eg Farming, progressing in story, need help, etc.) For some reason, over the past decade, creating a room and naming it has died off. I find several modern games irritating when you join and the players either have different goals than you or sometimes kick you out for no reason. Also, its not an MMO, so your success is based upon the co-operation and the support of your teamates. providing the option for players to join at anytime is nice versus having to be in some kind of elite guild to gain support.Online play is a blast, you can have characters of any class and strength combination. Sometimes its nice when someone joins on a hard level and they have way better equipment and just help me blast through problem areas while helping my character get stronger. Or even playing on harder difficulties and dying repeatedly, changing your team strategy to see what can be done differently to conquer the level. Unfortunately, levels can be long.... real long.... and a character cant join mid-game. Instead you have to either finish the mission or retreat which makes you lose all the equipment worked so hard to gain. Its also important to note that you can kill your teamates rather easily, if your blasting the hell out of insects, make sure no one else is there. The game also supports voice chat and has hundreds of pre-rendered messages you can send out to other players. For instance, if someones waiting to join, you can send them a message "hang in there!" Or if you have 4 people playing together you can send a message "Ill collect weapons" or ""We need to get items."Now for more of the cons. For some reason, if you complete a mission offline, its not completed online and vice-versa. This makes no sense, especially considering you get to keep the equipment you earn and switch between the two. One of my biggest compaints is the black scren of death.... the game freezes while loading. It seems rare but can be very frustrating and make you use certain words when the game freezes after a particularly difficult mission is completed. Another huge flaw is that the game provides no instructions. The game is actually rather complex - way more than what "professional" reviews give it credit for. I couldnt even figure out how to navigate menus completele for a couple hours until I realized *BOTH* the D-Pad and left analogue do different things. Also, certain weapons may have a secondary function such as a booster but others may not. You can read the weapons description and make a guess but trial and error is equally prudent.There have been some complaints about the graphics and I have to say their a little misguided. There is absolutely no way this game is comparable to a PS2 or XBOX game, the engines wouldnt be able to handle the graphics. On that note, dont expect a world brimming with color and complexity. The characters and bugs have a solid design with the surroundings decent enough given that you can blow up anything in the game. Also there have been complaints about lag, I have had very minimal lag during my gameplay and never enough to interfere with the mission objective.In summary, if your patient and like to kill bugs for absolutely no reason in a giant bloodbath while strengthening your character, this games for you. Its fun for both casual and veteran gamers given 5 difficulties and theres a 2 player co-op mode. I would recommend giving this game a try if you have any interest in 3rd person shooters at all!

Earth Defense Force 2025 continues the series on the PS3 by offering new weapons, characters and abilities against familiar foes, including giant Ants, Spiders, UFO Ships, Giant Robots, Monsters and more. What separates this series from the competition is the epic, intense and overwhelming scale of battle, where if you're not constantly moving, strafing and blasting away at the enemy, your character is probably deceased. Picture exploring an open city, landscape or village, and in the distance, hundreds of Giant Ants appear, heading right towards your direction. Load up your high Tech Machine Gun and Rocket Launcher, and prepare for battle through each intense stage.+Some of the most epic and intense "One vs All" battles in a video game.+Pick from Four Characters, change their costume color, weapons.+The Jet Pack character (Female human) has the best flight in the series allowing for longer and higher flight like never before. Right from the start.+Open Maps in each level. Though there are invisible walls (no more red walls as in EDF:IA), the open world maps are much, much larger and filled with detailed buildings, cars, streets, trees, stores, skyscrapers to ascend, mountains, rivers, oceans and more.+You can swim freely.+Great controls, though the new layout takes some getting used to with the button layouts. Adjustable? Yes.+Massive amounts of enemies fill the screen. You against an army.+If you loved the prior games, this delivers more of the same with some improvements.+Massive explosions when the enemy ships or robots are defeated.+Easy, Normal, Hard, Inferno difficulties offer different rewards and new weapons.+A fun, thrilling experience that doesn't take itself seriously.+Comical dialog of the EDF soldiers and screaming pedestrians.+Seriously awe inspiring giant scaled Monsters.+Reach the tallest skyscraper with the jet pack character.+Freely avoid combat and explore the city if you want on many levels. Until they catch up to you eventually.+New vehicles.+Many more levels, cities, towns, seaports, factories, malls, underground, landscapes to explore and conquer.+If you see steps on a building, you can climb them all the way up if you want. Many games don't offer that level of detail.+Fully destructible world. Everything but the ground can be leveled and destroyed.+There's an indoor mall to run through. That hasn't been done before in an EDF game.Earth Defense Force 2025 is a welcome return from Sandlot to the PS3 after the fun EDF Insect Armageddon from Vicious Cycle, but the concept of fighting the same enemy each game is beginning to lack originality despite a few new enemies here and there.-Ants, Giant Robots, Spiders and Monsters are fun to battle, but I'd like to see some new enemies in the planned PS4 upcoming EDF game. How about more new enemies next time?-The Graphics, though never what the series has been known for, take a big step backwards. Usually at the end of a Consoles cycle, developers learn more. Here, though there is plenty of detail, the game looks washed out in brightness, and the textures are PS2 quality on a PS3 machine. I wouldn't bring this up, but EDF 2017 had much sharper, more refined and better graphics. Here, expect mostly muddy textures and the trees far away look like green flat pixels blocks.-As is normal for the game, once the enemies are defeated, "Mission Completed" appears even before you collected all of the loot. So before you kill the last enemy, collect the upgrades first or miss out.-Slowdown sometimes gets to a crawl on certain levels. Other levels are fine.-As good as the game is, it feels much like you're playing EDF 2017. Again. Lacking originality.(I haven't tried the Online portion).In the end, EDF 2025 is a one of a kind, epic battle game where you face off against overwhelming but manageable enemies and situations. Few games offer this kind of experience. Picture the madness of the old arcade game Gauntlet, fighting of hordes of hundreds of enemies alone. If you'd like the concept of one man against an entire army, don't pass up EDF 2025, despite Sandbox's reliance of retreading the same formula each EDF game.If D3 and Sandlot want me to buy a new EDF on PS4, new enemies and some new concepts will need to be added to the EDF concept to keep things fresh. I hope the PS4's abilities are taken advantage of with better graphics and framerates also.-Fun Factor: 9/10-Gameplay: 8/10-Controls: 8/10-Options: 9/10. Plenty of options to adjust thankfully.-Replay Value: 10/10. Easy or as difficult as you can imagine with lots to see and explore.-Graphics: 6/10. Very detailed with nice store fronts, but muddy and flat textures. Not as good as EDF 2017's (Sandlot) graphics, or EDF Insect Armageddon (VC). A step backwards.-Frame Rate: 7/10. Things slowdown badly now and then, affecting the control of your character.-Genre: Action, Epic Battle Game set in an open series of Landscapes and cities.If you don't have EDF 2017, this is worth a buy. EDF 2017 is a better game overall despite some new improvements with weaponry and the Jet Flight in EDF 2025.TIP: Biggest advantage goes to the Jet Pack character. Equip her with the Mirage (homing missiles) and Rocket Launcher for a very powerful character. Fastest and able to fly anywhere.

Earth Defense Force 2025 is the fourth game in the EDF series (although the third released statside) and the concept is the same as it has been for the past three titles. Aliens are using giant bugs, robots, flying saucers, and transformers to obliterate the Earth's human population. Enter the EDF a squad of bug smashing soldier sporting massive squishing boots in the form of insane, explody weapons.There is a whole lot of game here with 95 missions right out the gate, five levels of difficulty, and a stuipifying sense of destructive power with the weapons you use, not to mention four classes that all handle drastically differently.The game has a metric ton of flaws though. It crashes during loading screens (which are way longer than they should be) during online gameplay far too frequently to be forgiven, sometime enemies will spawn inside walls and since the goal every mission is to kill all the enemies it makes completing the mission impossible, loot drops are random to the point of being downright evil on the higher difficulty settings (netting level 1 gear during a time when gear should be dropping in the high 90's), the framerate bogs down to impossible to play levels when there are multiple buildings being destroyed and over 100 bugs being blasted into the strasphere with a well placed high impact grenade, and, on the rare occassion, you will be listed as dead when you are alive and well and killing bugs left and right causing the game to count the mission as a loss. This isn't even addressing the wildly inaccurate hitboxes and bugs being able to shoot through walls and other obstacles that randomly pops up.The graphics are right at home on the PS2, such a shame this is a PS3 game. The music is bland, the voice acting is terrible, and the overall polish is just lackluster as all hades.But the game does have one strong point going for it. IT IS FUN!No matter what else I have said about all the flaws, to me and to those that have played it, the game is still golden because of the sheer fun factor that comes with sending a jumping spider the size of Hummer blasting off into the air team rocket style with a high powered shot gun blast. The framerate drop from buildings being destroyed is annoying, but you will still be tossing grenades with an arm that will make a quarterback jealous to call in massive airstrikes. Four players will relish jumping in a massive mech-suit and blasting hordes of red ants off the face of the Earth while chanting "E-D-F!" at the top of their lungs. Zipping around the map as a female soldier in a jet pack and firing off pink globs of exploding energy into the face of a robot the size of a skycraper never gets old, nor does the feeling of satisfaction of using a strength-boosting powersuit to bring down a hammer with enough force to send out a massive shockwave to destroy annoying ants in your path, speed bursting through the freshly made break in the defense of the creatures, and then brandinshing a epic minigun to mow down the mob from the inside out with the bodies piling up around you.While this may seem really violent, it is highly stylized fair and I don't really see any problem with making this a game that anyone over the age of 8 could enjoy.Don't buy EDF2025 to enjoy the story, to marvel at the technical grapical achievement, or to experience a new dynamic in video games Today. No, EDF doesn't offer of that stuff. It is all about having fun with a few other people while kicking those terrible alien invaders off the Earth with mighty explosions and simple gameplay mechanics. While it isn't the prettiest game in my collection, I will be playing with this game for a long while.

**UPDATE (Day Six)**I've decided to put this update at the top since I'm at the point where I'm cautiously bumping my rating up to three stars. The online portion is feeling a bit more stable lately. We still get the occasional dropped game or dropped player, but it has gotten to the point where we can actually play for an hour without issue.The graphical lag is still very much a part of EDF. When the game spews a giant nest's worth of ants at you, or fills the sky with fliers, the PS3 drops the framerate like a rock. It's not quite as bad (yet) as I remember in Insect Armageddon on the 360 (where the heavy's black-contrail'd rocket launchers would nearly lock up the screen - 3 seconds per frame, instead of the other way around), but I don't think I've gotten the most ridiculous weapons yet, or made it to inferno (currently farming hard for weapons/armor). Tip: Turn off screen shake in the options. It makes the game a lot more playable. This game is screaming for a PC port, the consoles simply can't handle the amount of data EDF is trying to throw at it. Unfortunately there doesn't seem to be any plans in place to make this happen (at least not yet).As the game stands, the multiplayer is getting much more stable. We still have the random game where a group member doesn't load and we have to retreat/reload, or the game locks up during load/saves, but they're becoming much more rare. I'd say it's affecting maybe 1 mission in 15, where before it was 1 in 3. If the stability keeps getting better, I'd be more than willing to give this game four stars.**Original review below**I've been looking forward to EDF2025 for almost a year now, waiting with bated breath while the release date got pushed further and further back. It finally hit my doorstep this afternoon and my friends and I couldn't wait to kill some bugs.if you've played any of the EDF series in the past, you know exactly what to expect. Mindless bug killing, wave after wave - a loose "save humanity" plot tying things together. Four very unique classes and boatloads of weapons. Best played with a group of friends who want to join in the mindless fun with you, hording weapons and leveling their characters.Maybe, just maybe, this is release day jitters - and if so, I'll update my review accordingly. However as of release day the game is nearly unplayable in multiplayer.I don't think it's a server load issue - when you load the server list, there's tons of servers listed and barely any games being played on any of them.So what happens?You connect to the game lobby with your friends, chose your load out and go into the mission. 1 out of 3 attempts, the game will crash. Hard crash or soft crash, it seemed to be different each time. The PS3 would get to the point where the PS button wouldn't work and you had to force power-off the console and reboot. Other times, it would only be the game that crashes, and you can Quit Game and return to PS Home. When I say that this happened every one out of three missions, it's not an exaggeration. We'd honestly play fine for one or two missions, and then fail to load / crash on the next. I think the longest we went without a problem was three consecutive missions.We've even had a couple of games where the sync at the end of the mission would fail and the game would lock up - all weapons and armor accumulated lost, because the game didn't save the data.TL;DR - If you're buying EDF2025 to play with friends on the PS3, cross your fingers and hope for a patch/fix. The game crashes way to often to be enjoyable right now. Maybe it's different on the XBox version, but avoid the PS3. I'll update this review if it gets better in the next few days.**UPDATE (Day three)**The game feels a little more stable, it's not crashing every other mission, now it's consistently on the third consecutive mission (which is sadly, an improvement).

I bought this off Live almost as soon as it became available.  I didn't really get into Insect Armageddon, this feels more like a true sequel.  Destroying buildings is more fun, killing the bugs is more fun and the Air Tortoise...is a hair faster and just as useless as before.EDIT 7/11/14Just wanted to update this to go into a little more detail now that I have 260hrs into it.This game has 85 single/split player levels.  I've beat every level at every difficulty except for level 85 on Inferno with the Ranger.  I haven't figured out how to beat it yet even with 12,000 health.  There are three DLC's that add a total of 45 more levels.I've found that while the Ranger is the easiest character to play with for newcomers, the Wing Diver is much more fun and mobile.The Air Raider has some pretty great support he can call in such as the Gigantic Artillery, various bombers, the Vegalta Busterlord (artillery mech) and some of the higher level Bazelarts (helicopter).  The Proteus is a huge mech and can wreak havoc if you get 4 people in it.  I have no idea who was in charge of the motorcycles.  If you ever drove the SDL on EDF-2017, this one handles even worse.  It does have a side car though.  Also the Air Raider can call in no more than two vehicles during a match. I have been playing SL for about 8 years as of this review. I have spent most of my time RPing (Role Playing, will detail later) and designing virtual items for an in world shop that I run. My review focuses mostly on those aspects but in no way are you limited to doing just those things.What is SL? It's not really a "game" but a virtual world, or a 3D chat room. There is no main quest, no damage system, storyline, or anything typical of a game. Instead, everything centers around interacting with other residents and creating items for the world. That is one of the real beauties of SL, you and other residents build the world around you! It's the ultimate sandbox "game". You begin in the world with your newly created Avatar equipped with one of the default looks available at start up. This is only the beginning. You can completely customize your avatar, and they don't even have to look human. However, everything you will need to create your avatar is made by other residents, many of whom run businesses in SL creating items for other users to purchase. You do this through what is called Lindens, the SL currency. Lindens are purchased with real money (or earned in game, or if you have a Premium account you get an allowance) and used to buy in world items. In addition to pimping out your avatar you can also buy homes, vehicles, furniture, pets, just about anything you can think of. And if you're handy with building and graphics you can become a designer too. Some people may not like the idea of paying real money for these items, but I personally enjoy knowing that I am supporting some fantastic designers. As a designer myself, and someone who appreciates the work that goes in to making quality items, I don't mind paying for things. There are free things available if you know where to look, but most of the quality items will not be free.Another major pass time is Role Playing. This is where you find a world you like (Medieval Fantasy, Steampunk, Victorian, etc.) and create a character. You then write as if you are that character, interacting with other players as your character would. This is a lot of fun if you enjoy writing and character development. I have had some great times and made many friends in RP sims. However, it can be high drama if you're not careful how you interact and if you get too involved with people who have difficulty not taking RP personally, so approach with caution.Other things to do include going to dance clubs and chatting while listening to live Djs, playing games like Slingo or Greedy, exploring the hundreds of worlds, photography, attending classes, hanging out with friends and meeting new people, and more. Because players come from all over the world, you can meet all kinds of interesting people.But as with anything on the internet, be cautious. Some people are not what they seem, or may only be interested in adult activities you may not be looking for. That is also why SL really isn't for kids. Despite the rating system that was put in place, there is still a lot of adult activity even in the lower rated areas simply because there are a lot of people playing SL who are looking for that. It's easy for an underage person to pretend to be of age simply by getting certain information from someone of age and using it as their own, so it's also dangerous for adults who don't know how to take precautions about who they "play" with. There has been a lot of controversy about SL's more adult issues, but that's just the way the internet is. If you aren't interested in those things, just avoid them. There is plenty of other stuff to do and the really seedy stuff is sectioned off in adult areas so you don't have to worry about running into them by accident. Just pay attention to location ratings, of you can even change your settings to not show Adult locations. Also, bear in mind that in order to access Adult areas you will need to go through an age verification process which requires you to submit some information to prove you are 18 or older.In terms of the quality of the "game" like the graphics, there are some major pluses and minuses. On the plus side, the world is updated without the need of an "expansion pack" or anything of that nature. It's free to play (besides any in world purchases) and you don't need to worry about upgrading. However, you do need to regularly update your viewer, the program used to play the game. This is fairly easy and pain free, but it can be frustrating when an update goes poorly. There are also different types of viewers besides the default one which Linden Labs (the game makers) created, which can be great for advanced users. I myself prefer Firestorm, but there are others out there for different needs. If you have a good PC, the graphics can be really great. Even if you just have an average PC you can usually tweak things to look pretty good for everyday play. However, the game can be a big system hog so some PCs won't be able to handle it well or you may not be able to have other programs open at the same time. Sadly... bugs, lag, glitches, errors and other issues are common in SL. Some are due to other players not being courteous about their builds or avatars and causing those around them to be bogged down or griefed. Some issues are due to the general lack of that stability SL which residents have dealt with for years. Rarely are the problems game breaking, but it's not uncommon to be unable to teleport, build, or chat in groups. Some people find they crash a lot, others like myself are lucky enough to have very few crashes. Sometimes issues can be fixed by tweaking your settings, sometimes they are due to something with your hardware interacting poorly with the game. It's just the way things are in SL.There is also a BIG learning curve when it comes to your first time playing. It uses standard movement controls (WASD and mouselook) but when you add in flying, chatting, camera view, inventory, messages, groups, etc. it's a lot to learn your way around. If you're used to PC gaming this may not be such a big curve for you, but a lot of people complain that the game is too difficult to learn to play. If you have a hard time with navigating even simple games, this may not be for you.I have been playing for years now and think that overall SL is a wonderful place to socialize and be creative, even with all its problems. My biggest negative is the glitches and lag, but I still play so obviously they are not bad enough to scare me off. SL is so open that it has a lot to offer. It's worth checking out for anyone who is interested in socializing online or being creative with graphics.

The Good: Dozens of fantastic songs, great use of the touchscreen and rear pad, lots of stuff to unlockThe Bad: Not many modes, still no multiplayer, feels a bit too similar to PSP DJ Max gamesDJ Max was the best rhythm franchise on PSP and helps jump start that genre on Vita. Technika is a reboot in a way but still feels familiar. The game uses the touch screen and rear pad exclusively ditching the button interface. This may take a while to get used to for DJ Max PSP vets like myself, but after a while you will see the difference in challenge and pace when playing.One thing I did notice right off the game is the continued lack of mulitplayer and modes. There is Star Mixing (3 songs using the touch screen), Pop Mixing (4 songs using front and rear), and Club Mixing (a choice of genres), and Freestyle. There’s the usual album which shows your wallpapers and unlocked videos but that’s it. Why Pentavision insists on having no multiplayer is a mystery, but I’d like to have it in future installments. Thankfully the game is packed full of songs featuring both licensed and original music from J and K pop to rock. Kara is a huge appearance in the game since they are one of the biggest female KPop groups in Korea. They have 5 songs on here and they are fantastic, I actually listen to them outside of the game now.The songs still feature various DJs and mixing masters from previous games like ND Lee, NieN, and vocals by So Fly and various other Korean singers and rappers. Getting into the gameplay, videos are now played full screen in the background and look gorgeous on the Vita’s screen. Colorful dots are displayed and you must tap them to get Max 100% with the timing of the beat but there are long strands you have to hold down and follow the bar along the screen. The play field is split horizontally into two sections and you will be going back and forth between them. Some notes require quick flicking of the touch screen as well and it all adds up to tense fun. The rear touchpad notes look different with purple and black borders around their notes requiring you to tap and hold. After a few hours you will get used to the system and slowly increase your difficulty.As you level up you will unlock equipment that gives you passive abilities like extra XP gain, HP, and even free breaks. There’s also an option to add a modifier to increase the speed of the notes coming in which is sadistic but it’s there. Even after playing for a good 10 hours I’m still unlocking stuff and increasing my score. The songs are so great and fun to listen to that I can’t get enough of the game. If you loved previous games you must get this, anyone who hasn’t should jump in anyway. Technika Tune is the best rhythm game on Vita right now and hopefully future installments will improve upon the franchise further.

The GX-M1 mouse isn't the top of the line gaming mouse. If you're looking for the best for nothing, you'll not find it here. If you're looking for a mouse that can do more than a normal 2 button mouse, look no further.The design of the GX-M1 is nice. I have average sized hands and it forms well to my palm. Almost too well as the left side buttons tend to get pressed by my resting thumb. The left and right mouse buttons are well formed and place. A small and concave curve to each button allows for your fingers to really settle in while holding the mouse. The amount of effort needed to depress the buttons is small, although not overly sensitive to clicking on accident. You can also click almost half way up the mouse, which I found to help the overall leverage while resting my palm.The laser tracking system is as good as you'd expect. Depending on the surface you play on will have an effect on how well it responds. Solid surfaces like desks and mouse pads work great. Trying to use it on a fabric sofa will obviously net you bad results.The wire connecting the mouse and USB is also unique. It is woven similar to a rope. It gives it yet another unique aesthetic feature that you don't find on many computer mice. It feels neat and almost more secure. It doesn't do anything for compatibility or functionality, but it's still something unique.Another unique touching point is the LED lights. The top and sides glow with color throughout the mouse.
