The PS4 was released late in 2013 and has become one of the quickest selling consoles at launch and within its first few months of all time.  Obviously this means the console had a lot of hype around it, but is the hype worth it?I think its a very great console for being its first year. First years in a new consoles life are usually a little rough and company's typically have a stronger focus on selling the system and getting it out there rather than actually focusing on the games. However within the first few months since its release we have seen plenty of games so far. My only problem is that there have been to many ps3 ports. I really recommend getting infamous second sun as that is the best title on the system that I played since launch and is only available on ps4 and pretty much shows what the system can do. I will probably have a review on that very soon so feel free to check it out. The other games I have on the system are thief, tomb raider definitive addition, killzone shadows fall, trails fusion, and pinball arcade. although the games are limited in number there all really well done even though right now most of these are playable on ps3. Give them some time and there will be plenty more ps4 exclusives though so if your waiting on them your probably better off waiting tell next year before purchasing the system.Now the important question, is this going from a Nintendo to a super Nintendo or is this just barely an upgrade to the previous consoles? Graphically speaking its way to early to tell just yet however I don't think its quite a big of leap as the other console generations have been. The main reason for this console generation is to have a affordable way to keep up with pc gaming. Which graphically is probably just as good as this console if not a little better if  you have a couple grand to spend. You see if the had not released this console company's would have to downgrade all there games for ps3 and 360 and cut out a lot of things unless the kept it pc exclusive. (very few games do these days).Of coarse there is some new features as well that separates it from the ps3 and the other systems like the controller. I think it is a mass improvement over all the previous PlayStation controllers which have pretty much stayed the same since the added the joysticks. Gone is the select button for the first time since the atari joysticks and is replaced with a share button. The share button lets you record gameplay and upload it to Facebook, YouTube and all that good stuff. Which is kinda a big deal considering  it used to be a pain to record off game consoles without owning multiple hundred dollar equipment. The ps4 is also more integrated into Facebook which you can thankfully turn off so you don't spam people with a 1000 different "I played infamous today" posts but it is there for people that want it though. Also whats new with the controller is the *EXTREMELY* bright led light. Its default color is blue however when playing some games its color changes with the situation (blue when enemy's not alerted, red when the are, etc).There are some downsides to upgrading to the ps4 however. If you plan to play online for free you will be disappointed as it forces playstation plus on you which is the main reason I put 4 stars instead of 5. However Playstation plus does get you some free games every now and again so that almost kinda makes up for it. That and if you plan to play mp3s and import cds you will be disappointed  as well as the only way at the time of this review to listen to music is to subscribe to music unlimited. This however is supposed to be changed eventually and hopefully as music unlimited is missing a lot of good songs and it costs $10 a month. With that being said however from the free trail I've used its a real nice service that allows you to play songs while playing games with the ability to adjust the volume on the music without turning down the tv so you can still hear the people talking in a game. Also even though apparently you will be able to stream older playstation games through the playstation now the console is not backwards compatible with any previous playstation systems 1-3, psp, vita.Anyway while the system is missing a lot of great features its still a great console to game on. Which is essentially what its here to do its more streamlined and has a more focused point on gaming  which is what video game consoles where originally made for. Comparing this to the other systems I have not played a Xbox one nor do I plan to any time soon but I also own a Wii u. I would recommend getting both systems as the both have there on strengths and weaknesses if you are able to do so.

The PS4 is amazing.  Truly next-gen.  I'll break my review down into several sections:Hardware-------------Independent tech sites (generally PC and gadget benchmarking sites) have benchmarked the PS4, and suffice it to say, he hardware and design (availability of the hardware for actual game use) is exponentially greater than that of the Xbone.  Devs at the large studios are saying that the PS4, on an unoptimized A to A port of a game, is 50% faster than the Xbone.  50%, unoptimized!  We've seen this; the proof is in the pudding:COD Ghosts - PS4 1080P 60FPS, Xbone 720P ~60fpsAssassins Creed 4 - PS4 1080P, Xbone 720P (framerate varies, but is better on PS4 by all accounts, there is also a physics engine enabled that is only available on the PS4 version).PS4 has a lightweight, BSD-based OS that only uses one core of the 8 CPU cores; Xbone uses 2 cores for its large, 3-layer, bloated OS (Hypervisor, Windows, Kernel-Game).PS4's sharing and social features are superior out of the box.  Xbone, as of this review, is having problems recording and sharing video at all, but MS is promising a "fix".  PS4 always records 15+ minutes in the background, which you can then save, edit, upload, share, do whatever with.  It has a separate co-processor (basically a mini-PS3 in power) which handles these background functions, so gameplay isn't ever affected.  Xbone uses its system-wide resources to do recording, which is why, on top of having a last-gen GPU, last-gen CPU, and much slower RAM (DDR3 vs GDDR5 in the PS4), the Xbone is a much slower, less graphical, poorer overall experience than the PS4.PS4 also has all the voice commands like the Xbone, but you can simply do them through the controller; no need to buy the camera accessory if you don't want to.  Whereas Xbone forces the Kinect on you to be able to use voice commands, but let's face it, actual Kinect GAMES have never been worth playing, and never will be, so the Xbone is seriously overpriced.It's worth noting that the head Xbox Exec at MS left the company prior to the console's launch, because he knew it would be a failure.  While review sites got PS4 consoles early and were able to show reviews (commenting that the graphics were on par with a high-end PC with the graphics set to "high"), MS did not release any to reviewers, and instead only showed their own demos, which were running on a high-end PC.  They knew their console couldn't produce the same quality of graphics and gameplay that the PS4 is capable of.Controller-------------Last generation, I had a 360, PS3, and Wii, and the 360 controller was probably my favorite.  This generation, the PS4 controller definitely takes the win.  It's much sturdier and well-built than the Xbone controller, still features motion controls (which the Xbone doesn't), and adds a new touchpad and speaker on the control.  This is great; in a game like Assassin's Creed 4 you can pinch and zoom around the world map, and it's clickable, too.  In games like Killzone, when you pick up an audio log, the audio comes out of the controller, which is really cool; it increases the feeling of immersion, as if I'm holding the actual audio log in my hands.It's also worth mentioning that DualShock 4 controllers come rechargeable as standard.  Xbone controllers, you have to spend another $30-40 for a charging kit just to get ONE rechargeable battery.  Out of the box, Xbone just gives you two AA batteries, which will go out quickly.Games-----------The generation is young, but there are already some great games out.  All the gaming sites have said the PS4 version of Assassin's Creed 4 is the "definitive" version, with the best graphical fidelity, and the use of the controller touchpad, etc.  Killzone: Shadow Fall is arguably the most truly "next-gen" game that exists as of this review, as it is the only game out that was written specifically for one console, and optimized to use its hardware in a next-gen way.  The graphics and gameplay are outstanding and immersive.  Multiplayer will suck you in for hours upon hours.  Knack is actually a pretty good game despite the mediocre reviews.  Resogun, another PS4 exclusive, is free with your PS+ account, which you'll need to play online (like XB Live), and is graphically stunning, requiring super tight timing and constant focus (don't blink!).  All the other multiplat ports are available, too…  Madden, NBA, COD, etc, and run by far the best on the PS4, given its exponentially more powerful hardware.Sony and PS4 have 20+ exclusives coming out in 2014; Xbone has about 2 (and one is a timed exclusive; it will be released on PS4 slightly later).  So it's pretty simple; with multiplats being lead SKU for PS4, and Sony always being stronger in exclusives, it's the go-to console this generation.Conclusion-------------The PS4 is the way to go if you want to get into the new generation of gaming.  Sony did their homework, and have outsold the Xbone 3 to 1 in North America, and 9999 to 1 internationally (where the xbox doesn't sell at all).  The sales numbers are in, and even the Wii U outsold the Xbone throughout Nov/Dec 2013.  PS4 has won the console war, and it deserves it.  It's a spectacular piece of hardware, and now with multiplats being developed for PS4 firstly in mind, and Sony's strong exclusives lineup, it's a no-brainer.  I have owned nearly every console since Pong, except for the Sega Genesis during the SNES/Genesis years.  It looks like that's going to be the case this generation, too, for the second time, because Xbone just doesn't bring anything to the table; it's seriously underpowered for games, and they relied solely on the Kinect/TV tuner functionality to sell it.  Cable is on its way out for a lot of people (with online streaming apps replacing TV, etc), and those who do have cable already have an interface in place (a DVR, Tivo, Google TV, etc, which aren't compatible with the Xbone, which has to be the primary tuner).PS4 = epic, next gen win!Xbone = epic, last-gen fail!

Despite preferring the Xbox 360 in last generation's lineup of consoles, I opted for Sony's PlayStation 4 after countless missteps taken by Microsoft, and because I enjoy Sony's console exclusives over Microsoft's. And while it might not be worth rushing out and buying a new console right this second because of the lack of games, it is definitely worth upgrading from the previous generation in the near future.Games aside, the PS4 is also a Blu-Ray and DVD player with Netflix, Hulu, and Amazon right out of the box. The internet browser also returns from the PS3, which can be used with the incredibly comfortable Dualshock 4 controller, or with a keyboard and mouse. The menus are familiar but also refined, cross game "party" chat is now available, and the PlayStation Store has ironed out the slow updates and load times of the PS3 and is now much more user friendly. Unlike the XBox One, which only offers 720p screen resolution,  the PS4 supports 1080p. All of these improvements really make the PS4 feel like a professional machine, and not so much a fancy, flashy toy like its predecessors.While you are now required to purchase online play, Sony has improved its reliability, so it feels like a good investment. They also throw in monthly free and discounted content after you buy the online package.Before you buy either the PS4 or the Xbox One, do some research on which exclusives you feel you will be more interested in. While the Xbox One tends to focus on blockbuster multiplayer action (such as Titanfall and Halo), the PS4's lineup leans towards crafting masterpiece single player stories and great gameplay (such as The Last of Us and InFamous).All in all, the PS4 is a great console, and I'm excited for what Sony plans to offer its customers over the course of its lifespan.

It's very rare that anyone will hear me say a product is worth more to me than what I paid for it (it's usually the other way around). I'm not a fanboy by any stretch, so I'm not here to bash the X-Box One, or romanticize about how much better I think the PS4 is than any other console. The only console I'll be comparing it to is the PS3, which makes sense because that's it's predecessor.I'll start by highlighting some of the improvements I've noticed with the PS4, when compared to the PS3.-- The controller looks and feels different. The shoulder buttons, as well as the sticks are different. During heated gameplay, my thumbs would always slip off the sticks while using the PS3 controller. So far, that hasn't been an issue. The 'start' and 'select' buttons are now a thing of the past; they've been replaced with the 'share' and 'options' buttons. The share button allows you to broadcast live gameplay, or save a video / screen-shot to your PS4's hard drive, for future viewing. While playing a game, the options button works similarly to the old start button, but does give you other options while navigating the PS4 home page.-- The console itself has undergone quite a face lift, and looks pretty damn good. Here are a couple of changes that are HUGE for me, but may or may not matter to you. I really, really hated that the PS3 had to be turned on in order to charge my controller. This is no longer an issue because the PS4 can charge the controller while in standby mode! I used to plug in my controller and let it charge before going to bed. I'd wake up the next morning, and touch the back of my PS3 and notice it was hot to the touch, which is a by product of being on for 8 damn hours (I'm aware there's a setting that shuts down the PS3 after 2 hours, but we shouldn't have to do that). If you like to download movies from the PlayStation store, you'll be pleased to know that you can start watching your movie as soon as you start the download! This wasn't the case with the PS3 - If I didn't allow the movie to finish downloading, it would start buffering every other minute, and that's no fun. Oh, one more quick note. There's no longer an on / off button on the back.-- I've only owned my PS4 for about a month, but I've learned a lot of neat things about it. There's an app called 'Live on PlayStation', and you can watch other gamers play their games, in real time! I no longer need to rely on YouTube walkthroughs to help me decide if I want to buy a game or not. For example; I was very curious about Destiny, so I decided to visit Live on PlayStation and watch people play it. I ultimately decided it wasn't for me. I had this console for about a week now, and so far I like it very much.+ Not too expensive, surprisingly! Remember how much the PS3 was?  How can you not?  While the PS4 isn't cheap, it sure isn't $600 dollar expensive either, and I think it's a good price point for the system.  I also think you'll get a little bit more bang for the buck than you do with the consoles the competitors have out, not trying to say anything against them though.+ The console itself! I think Sony skipped a generation.  Console manufacturers usually start off big, literally, and then just make a smaller size system.  Not the PS4! I still have my PS3 Slim, not the Super Slim, and the console is a bit smaller than that.  It is a bit longer, though that's due to the design looking like an eraser.  The looks aren't bad either.+ The controller! The Dualshock 3 the PS3 had wasn't a bad controller, but it was small due to the fact the L2/R2 buttons were convex.  I had to spend money for snap on triggers just to have a confortable controller.  With the Dualshock 4 included with the PS4, everything was fixed.  It doesn't have the form factor everybody knows about, but it does have a better form factor, better thumbsticks, feels a bit stiffer than the Dualshock 3, the trackpad isn't out of reach, allows you to use any headphone with the thing, which you can listen to chat or game audio, and finally, the triggers actually feel like triggers.  It also has a speaker on it, which can catch you off guard sometimes, but it's a nice subtle feature I hope developers take advantage of.  - If there's one problem I have, it's the Light Bar.  Unless if you have the PlayStation Camera, which I don't, it's just there to just look pretty, and it could either distract you or just run down the battery.  It's a subtle feature, like the speaker, and it's used for stuff like health or whatnot, but I don't think anybody will be staring down at the controller while playing a game.+ PS Plus! While it doesn't have free multiplayer, the value the PS Plus service gives you outweighs the cost.  You can get good games for free, examples are Don't Starve, Resogun, and the soon to come out at some point, Drive Club.  You can also find some good discounts as well.+ Remote Play! I tried the Remote Play feature, and it feels like playing the game on the Vita itself.Now, this is a good console, but it's not a perfect system.- The dashboard! It's a preference thing, but I feel like once I start getting games on it, it will take forever to find the game I want.  For disc-based games, it's not a problem since they pop up at the start, but for digital games, it might be a good idea to learn the voice controls.- Not backwards compatible! This is the reason why I'll be keeping my PS3.  I got some PS3 games that would like to play, but can only be played on the PS3.  Ironically, you can play some PS3 discs, but that's if you buy the PS4 upgrade for it.Verdict: If you are thinking about getting a PS4, then get one ASAP.  I was lucky enough that my class schedule ended at 9:15 when they became available at a local store, and I gone straight there immediately, because I know that it was a limited supply, and because of demand, it would likely not last long.  If you can't find one, then be extra careful getting one second hand.  I've seen PS4s go for $500+, sometime not including shipping, and I really recommend you try to find one for $400.  Anything more than it, and it better be bundled with an extra controller and a few games.  Other than that, it's a really good console.

Well for Sony's latest iteration of Playstation, seems they've decided to go back to the PS2 form factor of sleek jet-black and blue LED light. Very sleek looking console all around and not as big as you might imagine. Although a top-shelf PC outclasses it, PS4 is the most powerful gaming console on the market, and as we get closer to realism in our gaming graphics, I think the decision to use PC architecture and not use expensive parts (like PS3) did will pay off for Sony.Controller is much improved, I'm sure you can find in-dept analysis elsewhere, but it really feels great. Nice improvement to triggers, comfort, and most of the analogs. Little larger than DS3, but overall, not a single thing is lacking in comparison. Touchpad is useful as well, although I would have liked a larger surface to swipe along, it does it's job well enough.Now for what matters most--the Games! Infamous, Ground Zeroes, Final Fantasy 14 are my favorite games for the system so far, but be assured, if you aren't a "hardcore" gamer, PS4 is pretty awesome out of the box with PS+ and free titles to try out. Warframe being one of the better examples of the free-to-play model done right, and PS+ is filled with goodies already like Don't Starve, Towerfall Ascension, Resogun, and Mercenary Kings. Knack is also a nice old school title that's got that "cheap" hard factor to it, but brings a certain level of nostalgia that's hard to deny. Overall, it's one of the best launches I've ever been a part of. No stand out classic like N64 launch with Mario 64, but everything early on has been good to great, with Infamous topping the list in just over 5 months of PS4 being available. I really feel good about this one. Sony's marketing and messaging has been spot on with gamers, they are gathering indy guys up to the platform, and really, that's where a lot of amazing experiences is coming from. It really does feel like the Renaissance of gaming and developers going back to basics with old school designs, and fresh perspectives and stories.People get into game! There's stories out there like The Last of Us or Gone Home that are just as good as movies we spend $30 to see just once. Support this medium, check out games, and sit down with one for a few hours. This is no longer a children and "geek" hobby. Games are really beginning to reinvent themselves, with some truly touching stories that you feel more connected to since you are a "player" in that world. It's an entertainment industry unlike anything else, and short mobile games (while tons of fun) just don't give you the full spectrum of gaming. It's my favorite past time, even beating out reading, sports, and running. PS4 is a good well-rounded platform for any new comers looking into gaming.ProsPS+ You pay $50 a year (or cheaper if you can fine deals) and you get free games every month! The best value right now is still on PS3 (Over 150 games now) but it's great on PS4 as well and will get better. One of the best things Sony did this generation of gaming.Controller-Huge improvement and feels nice in handSoftware-Great catalog of games already when new systems usually are pretty sparse on content in the beginning. Infamous/Watchdogs/The Order/Dragon Age are my potential big hitters for this year, but honestly, I'm having a lot of fun with the smaller, more personal titles. It really is going back to basics.Community--PS4 quickly seems to be becoming the goto console for gamers. I think it may end up being this generation's "Live" where all your friends are on PS4, not Xbox, meaning community titles like Street Fighter or Call of Duty/Battlefield with have more active communities on PS4. We'll see, but so far, gamers are choosing PS4 as the machine of choice.Cons-OS (Operating system)  is barebones and not much customization is available-Many of the cool features like Pause/Resume, Controlling your friends game through the network, and PS now and Sony's IPTV which lets you stream games, movies/shows and Live TV are not available yet.-Best studio's titles are still a ways off (Gran Turismo, Uncharted, God of War, Little Big Planet) and Sony's is being very quite on what there in-house guys are doing. Likely won't be updated until E3.

Needless to say he has been added to my ignore list. So I am re-posting with out all the arguing because well it just isn't needed.First, Sony seems to have broke the BlueTooth feature, the former PlayStation remote does not work and the Logitech Harmony Ultimate will not work with the PS4. This is absolutely a PS4 issue as the remote works great for the PS3 and the X-1. This has proven to be very frustrating but I do not use my PS4 for movies so this is not a huge issue, I just thought it worth mentioning.Secondly, any downloaded apps and games are just thrown on to one screen, the PS4 has zero organization capabilities! For most this probably is not a big issue but I am a bit OCD-ish when it comes to organization and the lack of it on the PS4 is a headache (especially once you acquire more than a few games. The PS3 you could place games into different albums and then set it to reorganize by albums and I loved having this option! This for me is the biggest issue, if Sony fixes this in an update then it would definitely improve my rating. There are also no themes, you are stuck with the PS4 UI, which isn't much (themes are fun and nice to change things up but trivial).The battery life on the PS4 controllers is terrible and I have had to get two controls just so I can have one charging at all times. Giving the option to turn off the Lightbar would probably help a bit. I am aware we can now dim it but we still cannot turn it off. The touch-pad may factor in a bit to the battery life as the control seems to drain really quick when the touch-pad is in heavy use but games that do not use the touch-pad do not drain the battery as fast as the ones that do. I beleive that battery consumption from the touch-pad is minimal when it is not being used so I am not 100% why the controls seem to drain so quickly. I suppose it is possible that I have a faulty charge station that is messing up my battery. I would like to hear from others on if you experience this issue or not.The PS4 is Sony's first console that has zero backwards compatibility, which for the most part is not a big deal as I have no interest in playing old PS1 and PS2 titles but I feel that any NextGen Console should at the very least be backwards compatible with the most recent Previous Gen console (PS4 should be backwards compatible with PS3 but that is the extent of it). I just had to purchase a new PS3 because my old one passed away and I would much rather pay a little extra to have my PS4 be able to play PS3 titles instead of having to buy a new ps3 or a new ps4 anytime one dies.If you are wanting a console to use for streaming movies then you should go with the PS3 or X-1. The PS4 is not the media super center that its predecessor was. I use Plex for my Roku and PS3 and I have read that it is supposed to work on the PS4 but I can never seem to get it to work. Again, not a big issue if you stream to another device.You will at this point in time find that some game producers are still doing PS3 only and not PS4 two titles that  instantly come to mind are the South Park game and the Borderlands Prequel. Yes there are more but there is little need to list them all, if you want to know if a new game will be on the PS4 just do a search on it ;) **Please read what I say here and not try to add your own twist to it. The PS4 plays games and it does it well, I am in no way saying that the PS4 does not play games! Although I am not sure if others have this issue or maybe I have a fault somewhere but it seems that for every 24 hours that I play on the PS4 a game will eventually crash and my PS4 gives me a blue screen error.I think that the PS4 has huge potential but it still has some ironing out to do. The consoles hardware is great and like the PS3 Sony makes it easy to swap out hard drives and upgrade your storage which is a pretty awesome feature! However the software still needs some work.So, if you are on the fence about making the purchase do your research and see if the issues are worth it to you. If you are unsure give it a while and we will hope that these issues start getting resolved sooner rather than later. If you are a gamer and want the PS4 just for gaming and nothing else and you do not care about the lack of organizational options then you would probably be quite pleased with your purchase.I would also like to note before starting that this is my review. They are my opinions based on my experience with the PS4 console...it should go without saying but some people don't seem to understand that but my reviews will always be my opinions and experience about the product. If you want specs read Amazon's description, go to the Sony website and read the reviews from others. As I said these are my opinions and the things that bother me may not be a big deal for you. Ever since the Playstation 4 was unveiled at E3 2013, I had been anticipating it to bring about a new era of gaming that promised to display amazing graphics and truly-engrossing games that would be cherished as treasures by the gaming community.  I myself did not really know, though, what to expect when I finally purchased a Playstation 4 in April of this year.  So, for all of you that are undecided, contemplating trading your Playstation 3 for the next-generation system or, jumping from camp xbox to camp sony, I will do my best to give a comprehensive review of the system and everything it offers.The outside of the system is nice to look at but not really a game changer.  It is solid and sturdy, and decent in construction.  A couple of times I have had to unplug and re-plug in my hdmi cord in back due to lack of sound while my system is on - not sure if this is an internal or external issue.  Also, the power-on and eject buttons are recessed and do not always respond when pressed - again, not sure if this is an internal (connection) issue or an external (design) issue.When you power up the system, the background music that plays is ambience (I think) and is peaceful and calming.  However, much to my dismay, it cannot be changed, just turned off.  In fact, there is much you cannot do on your PS4 that you can on your PS3.  For example, you can't change your avatar from the PS4 - you have to do it on your PS3.  Also, you cannot listen to external music or watch movies off an external hard drive on your PS4 (no way that I have discovered yet, anyway), and you cannot change the background/desktop, so to speak, as you could on the PS4.The controller is unique and is, IMO, a better controller than the PS3 controller for size and comfort.  Word of advice though, buy protectors for the joysticks, as several friends of mine have complained about the rubber coming off of the joysticks after heated sessions of Battlefield 4 mp.It also has a slew of apps, from crunchroll for anime fans to netflix, wwe tv (whatever its called), IGN, etc.  They are all easy to download and access.  Also, the setup of the main menu is side-scroll just as before, and is pretty easy to navigate.  Another plus, for those who like independent games, is that there are many of them already released that are quite good, like Dead Nation 2 (whatever the official name for it is) and Resogun, among others.  However, if you're not all that impressed by independent games that, quite honestly, are good for passing half an hour, at most, then you may not care about the plethora of indies offered (and proudly touted) by Playstation on the PS4.  Now for the bad news.With the Sony Playstation 3, third party developers were quite vocal with the plethora of titles available shortly after release for the latest entry in the gaming market.  Uncharted: Drake's Fortune, God of War III, Little Big Planet, Motor Storm, Resistance: Fall of Man, Infamous and Killzone 2 were all big titles that helped the Playstation 3 to survive and to thrive.  The Playstation 4 has not excelled in this department, thus far.  Killzone: Shadow Fall and Infamous: Second Son were both released to much fanfare and were good, but by no means capable of holding people's attention for more than a couple of play-throughs.  Driveclub was delayed almost a year, while The Order:1886 is in development and grows less impressive with time.While the console itself is capable of bringing greatness to this next generation of gaming, the lack of high-quality first-party games is disheartening, to say the least.So, here  are my ratings for a few separate categories:Design: 5 out of 5Functionality: 5 out of 5User Interface and Ease of Use: 4 out of 5 (because of the Avatar and background issues mentioned above)Sound during use and games: 5 out of 5 - clean, crisp, and perfectDisplay during use and games: 5 out of 5 - the best you can get right nowLibrary of games: 4 out of 5 - props for the tons of indies, but the lack of first-party games in troublingSummary: While the Sony Playstation 4 is a technical marvel of modern gaming, its limited library is a reason for pause.  Unless you have played all the great games that your PS3/Xbox 360 have available at this time and need a new system to alleviate your boredom, just hold off until more substantial titles arrive (like next year).

I like my Playstation 4, some of the games are quite good and I've seen no lag or choppiness at all during game play thus far. The console is very compact and is much quieter than my Playstation 3.  I can't say I'm that impressed by the look of the console but the styling isn't bad either, it doesn't really draw much attention to itself at all which is fine by me.  The hard drive can be swapped extremely easily (it requires sliding off one panel and removing 5 screws total) which is great because some of the games install at close to 40 GB on the hard drive (that means about 10-12 could fill up the 500GB drive that comes installed). I personally already swapped out the hard drive for a 1.5 TB drive so that I wouldn't have to worry about filling up the hard drive like I did on my Playstation 3. (Note: if you do swap the drive be sure you read Sony's FAQ on hard drive requirements, some laptop drives will be too thick to fit)That being said it has been a rocky start for me.  The Wi-Fi was driving my crazy at first given that it would go through periods where it was popping a message up on my screen every 10-15 seconds for 15-20 minutes at a time.  Also during these periods of Wi-Fi drop outs my Playstation 4 would lock up while using apps such as Netflix and Amazon Video.  I initially thought this was just a bum unit (there are always going to be some) so I got an RMA from Amazon and traded it in for a different one.  The new unit has the same problem so it was not a hardware issue, which in the long run is probably good as it can be patched. Amazon was great with shipping out the new one (as usual), they allowed me to keep the old unit until the new one arrived so I wasn't without the console during the return process.The other downside to this console is the lack of features.  No music playback at all (other than Sony's service which costs monthly), no streaming movies from your local network, no movies or music from external drives, no DLNA.  I'm sure there is something I'm missing here but those are the big ones I think.  What all of this means is that the console doesn't stack up to the Playstation 3 (yet anyhow) and the games that are out currently are not reason enough to get the console (as of 1/14/2014).Overall I like the console and have great hopes for what it will be in the future (after bugs are fixed and more features are added) but if I had it to do over again I would have waited a year before buying one.  There is nothing terribly wrong with the console (other than those periodic Wi-Fi issues, which in fairness have become much less frequent) but it just isn't a great upgrade yet from the Playstation 3.  The graphics are smoother, the fan is quieter, it runs cooler, and I even like some of the new games, but after owning it since November 15th I can safely say I would have been better off waiting.

I've been a happy Xbox and Xbox 360 owner since the two systems launched in 2001 and 2005, respectively.  However, when Microsoft botched their presentation at E3 last year, all of my hardcore gaming friends said they would be switching to the PS4 for next generation.  I was still on the fence, torn by loyalties, so I pre-ordered both the Xbox One and PS4 right after E3 just to be safe, knowing that I was going to cancel one of them.I ended up cancelling both and picked up a cheap PS3 to see what I thought.  My first impression was that I hated the PS3's main menu / user interface compared to the XB360's (maybe just because I was so accustomed to XB360's after 8 years of use).  My next impression was that PS3 had the much better action-adventure exclusives (Uncharted, The Last of Us, InFamous, God of War) and platform exclusives (Sly Cooper, Ratchet & Clank), while XB360 had the much better first-person shooter (FPS) exclusives (Halo, Gears of War).To be honest, while I enjoy FPS games, I am much more of an action-adventure and platform game fan.  Additionally, being able to play games with my friends online was my # 1 priority.  Therefore, I decided to pick up a PS4 about a month after launch because all of my gaming friends already had one and I was more excited about InFamous (out now) and Uncharted (future release) on PS4 than Titanfall (out now) and Halo (future release) on Xbox One.  For FPS games, I will be more than happy with Call of Duty and Destiny on PS4.I've had the PS4 for about 4 months now, and I am very happy with the purchase.  The main menu / user interface is much better than the PS3's, and the controller has been improved as well (the games so far haven't made much use of the trackpad, but the built-in speaker has been surprisingly cool when used).  The Playstation Plus subscription (required for online play) is much better than the Xbox Live subscription, since it is $10 cheaper per year and so far has given me seven FREE downloadable games (compared to none for Xbox One via Xbox Live).The only disappointment so far has been that the PS4's Blu-Ray player does not currently support 3D Blu-Ray playback (and neither does Xbox One); however, this will probably be added during a future system update patch (my friend has the game Trine 2 on his PS4 and it looked beautiful in 3D, so clearly the PS4 is capable of outputting a 3D signal right now).I strongly recommend the PS4 to anyone who prefers action-adventure and platform games over FPS games, or who enjoys getting at least one FREE downloadable game each month, or who has several good friends who already own one.  If your friends haven't bought a next-gen gaming console yet, then odds are that they will be buying a PS4 since "VGChartz says that total cumulative global PlayStation 4 sales sat at 6,563,350 as of March 22nd, while cumulative Xbox One sales reached 4,021,382 units."

The PS4 is a well-built machine that gives you a lot of horsepower at a relatively low cost, especially when you consider the fact that its predecessor, the PS3, launched at $200 more for the primary SKU. While it doesn't have many exclusive games at the moment, you're buying into the PS4 for its potential. As Sony demonstrated with the PS3, they know how to create great games with characters you care about, not just soulless experiences that are, sadly, flooding the market on mobile devices. If you want high quality gaming experiences with cutting edge visuals, well-realized worlds and characters, Sony's developers have mastered that craft.As for the hardware itself, I've had no issues with it. There have been some complaints about the blue light of death error, disc read error, and some HDMI issues, but these issues seem to be within the acceptable failure rate for a new game console. Sony's competitors have also had issues reported with their consoles on the internet, so no matter which piece of hardware you buy, there's always the possibility that it could be a lemon, though it's not likely. With my experience, however, the PS4 was easy to set up and get going. The hardware does get a bit warm when running a disc, but if you turn it off in standby mode the fans will continue to run until it has cooled down, then the fans will turn off, so that's nice.As for the controller, it fits well in my rather large hands and feels comfortable during long play sessions. With that said, it's not without issues. I have noticed that the analog stick covers are a bit cheaply made and can often start to wear off if you're rough with the controller. It's a bit of a shame that the controller can have some issues because otherwise it's a very nice controller overall.And as for the games, there aren't a ton of exclusives, but there's enough to satisfy you. My game recommendations are as follows:Infamous: Second Son - One of the best looking games out there, if not the best. Absolutely stunning open world environment.Killzone: Shadow Fall - Not my favorite Killzone game, but definitely still worth playing. It also boasts some impressive graphics.Warframe - It's free to play and it's great fun.Thief - Criminally underrated. Not perfect but I love it. Great atmospheric stealth action.There are more games that you may or may not like, but those are some that I've enjoyed the most.Overall, in my opinion, the PS4 is a very nice system that I can recommend to any gamer looking for a new console.

PREAMBLEI have nearly every console ever made and controllers for most of them...even esoteric ONEs such as the Nintendo "Wavebird" and the more professionally made 3rd party controllers such as the Logitech ONEs with IR receivers for PS2 and the original XBOX (which tended to have some degree of noticeable input lag). Prior to the PS4 DS4 controller, I would say the 360 was the most solidly built controller ever. It felt great to hold and I felt like I couldn't break it with my bare hands the way I could with the PS3 controller...I love controllers.MICROSOFT SPENDS MORE TO GET LESSMS reportedly spent $100,000,000 developing the XBOX ONE controller. They spent 100mil to develop a controller inferior and less ergonomic to the 360 controller. My "DAY ONE" XBOX ONE controller has a less solid, more "plastic-y" feel to it (similar to the PS3 controller) and the seams tend to cave in as I grip it. I am forced to grip it much much harder because it's wider (for no apparent reason) and that forces my hands apart. Worse, as professional critics have noted, the shoulder (bumper) buttons no longer depress on the outer portions of the button - can't fathom the stupidity of that. If you're used to being able to push the shoulder buttons in anywhere (as you should) you'll screw this up over and over again and fail to throw a grenade or do whatever action the button is supposed to do. I see no intelligent design reason for this. It's just stupid. The only big noticeable things the ONE controller has over competitors are trigger rumble and a removable battery.XBOX ONE CONTROLLER IMPROVEMENTSThe XBOX ONE controller dead zones are supposed to be better and the D-pad is improved. I bet that will please the folks that play stuff in Major League Gaming, but I never really cared about those things to begin with and 360 controller revisions had already fixed the d-pad with a cool interesting transforming method. I can't tell if latency or lag has improved yet. They made it uncomfortable to hold and nearly no functionality was added. NOTE: my TITANFALL controller (which you'd think would be identical) seems to not have the same caving-in-at-the-seams problem the DAY ONE controller has...So there's that...XBOX ONE CONTROLLER / OS INTERFACE PROBLEMS & REDUNDANT BUTTONSEven the way the controller interfaces with the ONE OS is worse. The ONE OS stupidly didn't launch with a battery indicator (patched later) but the controller itself still has no low battery warning indicator (the 360 controller did). So if you're in the heat of battle and the team is counting on you for the big win, your controller will just die randomly...Thanks Obama.Also, the ONE controller has a menu button (previously start) which mimics current website and mobile standards (which is good), another redundant button (previously back) and I don't even know what the hell you call it (app switcher button?) and yet another to turn on/off (the classic middle X button). The middle X button used to be more functional. Tapping it would take you to a very fast, responsive and convenient text-based shortcut menu on the 360, but this was abandoned in the ONE OS rendering the button less useful and more redundant. Worse, when you receive a game/party invite, you're supposed to HOLD the middle X button (IT TELLS YOU TO DO THIS). Because of buggy OS latency problems here, this never works fast enough and takes you to the "turn off" menu instead. You're supposed to only hold it down for a few seconds, but IT DOES NOT SAY THAT - you'll learn the hard way and maybe accidentally turn of your system (this still has not been patched). If you're coming from PS to XBOX or are new to XBOX, these buttons may not make any intuitive sense to you at all, may be difficult to get used to and game/party invites will confuse you...Because of all this crap, these 3 buttons really should be ONE button the way it is on the PS4...There isn't enough functionality to them thus there isn't a good reason for them to all exist...A LOT OF PS4 CONTROLLER IMPROVEMENTS AND INTELLIGENT BUTTON PLACEMENTThe PS4 controller feels much more solid than the PS3 controller and yet is light and pleasant to hold. It is improved in every way to its predecessor, has better button placement and more functionality than the XBOX ONE controller. I like the 1-button-tap in the middle to take you to the dashboard (or back to your last app if already at the dashboard) or hold-down-to-turn-off. I don't particularly like the PS4 dashboard (XBOX ONE wins here hands down in my opinion) but this review is for the controller not the dashboard...The PS4 controller has new (or moved) buttons near the shoulder buttons that are OUT OF THE WAY and innocuous. Don't use the share button if you don't want to and you probably won't ever hit it by accident.Many people have remarked that they don't like the big interactive light bar but I find it pleasant and informative (bad things happening on screen = red, good things = green and so on). Nevertheless Sony SHOULD LET YOU TURN THE DAMN THING OFF for those that hate it and Sony claims the won't or can't. That's dumb.I like the speaker addition. This was always a cool function with the Wiimote (a thing it had over other controllers at that time) and now Sony has it as well. This gives developers the ability to play 1 thing over the controller and another over other speakers (audio logs in KILLZONE for example). Also has a built in stereo headphone jack. XBOX ONE controller - you have to buy some extra thing for this and it sticks out, adds major girth and is obtrusive...The clickable touchpad is a great addition. As much controller real estate as it consumes, it's still relatively out of the way. I wonder if they could even improve it more and make it a TOUCHSCREEN! Maybe down the road when the added costs wouldn't be prohibitive.The sticks are much improved, less floaty and wobbly.The SIXAXIS gyro thing was the only benefit the PS3 controller had over the 360 in my opinion...and I believe this tech was changed for the PS4. But so far I haven't played anything that uses it, so I can't comment on it...It was always a cool function but most games never used it and a few that tried to implement it in a serious fashion made gamers hate it and wish it was dead (LAIR).One of the dumber things about PS3 was that the trigger buttons were often not used AS TRIGGERS in shooters - the shoulder buttons were instead confoundedly used for this. As someone that is fairly console neutral, I can't tell you how annoying it is to pop in a shooter, proceed to hit THAT BIG THING THAT LOOKS LIKE A FREAKING TRIGGER ON A GUN to shoot an alien or whatever-it-is and instead a grenade or some other dumb thing pops out. The PS3 trigger buttons themselves were horrible anyway. Holding them down would cause the entire controller to move which is NOT what you want in a twitch shooter or intensely hard gaming session. Somebody at Sony apparently got a brain and fixed all this...Note, there are no real PS4 unimprovements, the way there are with the ONE (other than the lightbar annoyance - which doesn't personally annoy me).Other than turning the touchpad into a touchscreen, the only way I could imagine they could improve this thing is to add a microphone...PS4 CONTROLLER FOR THE WIN.

The hand grips are thicker and it fits into my palms perfectly. I just generally feel as though the DS4 is more sturdy and ergonomic than the DS3.--In spite of the peeling rubber I really enjoyed the concave shape the DS4 thumbsticks have as opposed to the convex shape of the DS3. I think the concave shape gives better grips and thus more control in games. So when I bought thumbstick covers (silicone) I made sure to get concave ones to match the DS4's natural concave shape.--They did not stray too far from the much loved DS3, they just improved upon it. Which I think was a smart move on Sony's part.--The touch-pad is a neat feature, I think at this point Im up in the air about it, time will tell how well game developers utilize it. But I definetly dont think its a CON, so I put it under PRO because I see major potential there.--The triggers on the top have a slightly curved shape, almost like a gun trigger. I really like how that feels.--It has a built in speaker in the controller itself, I have only used one game that utilizes it so far (Resogun) but I can see potenatial here just like with the touch-pad. I really hope developers utilize that feature in the future.CON's--Obviously, there is a quality control issue at Sony due to how many people are having the peeling rubber problem like I did. Go ahead and google "DS4 Peeling" and you will find NUMEROUS reports of people with this issue. Again, Im very dissapointed in Sony in regards to this peeling debacle--The battery life is much shorter than the DS3. On a full charge I get about 6-8 hours of play. With the DS3 I could go 2-3 days without having to recharge. So I dont care what anyone says, the battery life on this is DEFINITELY shorter.--The LED light on the top is incredibly bright and cant be turned off. I know it is related to PS Move, but I do not have PS Move, and I wish the light on the controller wasnt so bright that it literally illuminates a dark room on its own. Gee Sony... maybe this why the batteries die so quick, because there is a FLASHLIGHT attached to it that cannot be turned off.--No external batteries (like AA's) can be used. I know some people like this and some people dont. But for me it is a CON. For my Xbox 360 controllers I have a pair of Eneloop rechargable batteries which have worked for years, and I simply swap out a pair when they get low. I have two pairs of Eneloop's I rotate to make sure my 360 controllers always have some charged batteries ready. With the DS4 however I have no choice, and once the battery gets low I have to tether myself to the console with the USB cable. I suppose I couldn invest in a longer USB cable, but I digress.If it wasnt for the short battery life and peeling rubber, I would have given these things 6 stars!But 3 is what they get from me.

Having used both the PS4 and Xbox One controller and their respective predecessor, here is my take on the PS4 controller. Compared to the PS3 controller, the redesigned PS4 controller is better in almost every way possible. Instead of being an evolution of the PS3 controller, this one is a completely revolutionary design. The biggest difference of this controller is the touchpad on it, and while not many games have incorporated the use of the touchpad at launch (Killzone is one the games that does have touchpad support) there is a huge potential for games to incorporate the use of the touchpad. The inclusion of a speaker on the controller is another nice feature with big potential, so far I have only seen it be used in Resogun and Killzone (playing audiolog). There is a light in the front of the controller that has replaced the controller 1, 2, 3, 4 light on the PS3, again another feature that has potential depending on how developers use it. In FIFA, the color of the light represent the color of the user controlled player in the game, Player 1 is red, Player 2 is blue, etc. Now it is up to game developers to include the touchpad functionality and use the controller’s speaker in their game. It will be very interesting to see how those features will be implemented. The controller is also more ergonomical this time around. Since I have fairly large hands, I have found the Xbox controllers to be more comfortable to use compared to the Playstation controller. However, that is a wash this time around as the overall design of the PS4 controller is very comfortable and ergonomic. The triggers are now designed to contour to your fingers similar to the Xbox controller making it so that your trigger fingers sit their nicely and reduce the chance of slippage from previous design, good for those playing with sweaty or greasy fingers and all around a more thoughtful design. The back button is now replaced by a share button for sharing all your glorious moments online for your friends to see while the start button is replaced by the option button. At first locating and hitting the option button can be frustrating due to it’s small size and the fact that it is not raised from the controller’s surface. However after using the controller, you’ll get the hang of it and that will no longer be a big issue. So now for the gripes against this controller. The first issue with it is the durability issue and there are many reviewers saying that the rubber, especially on the left joystick/thumbstick is degrading. I’ve had the controller for two months and the rubber is already coming off. The second issue is the battery life. Compared to the PS3, Xbox One, and Xbox 360, the battery life is the worst on the PS4 controller. Hopefully Sony will release a revision of the controller that addresses these two issues because this controller has great potential. Only time will tell.

Here's what you all need/want to know. The durability problem. I have gone through 3 of these controllers, and I have barely used them at all. The first blatant issue is the material used on the stick. It starts wearing off, down to the plastic of the stick, within the first week of light usage. But that's irrelevant, the controller still operates after this. What happened to my controllers making them unusable is what the problem is.First I want to start out by saying that I am not rough with my controllers in any way. I am paranoid about proper care of them. I don't ever drop them. I never use them without washing my hands first; greasy and sticky controllers are something we can all agree nobody likes. Only I use them, so I know with 100% certainty that they have never been mistreated in any way.My first controller that came boxed with my ps4 lasted the longest. I got it on the release date. Throughout about 6 months, I put about 30 hours on my ps4, 100 hours on my ps3. and another 60 hours on my pc. (added up all my game hours on ps4, and my hours spent on Dark Souls 2 characters on ps3, and the 2 games I bought and played on steam, so the hours are 100% accurate.) My left control stick stopped working. Pushing the stick forward still functioned. But pushing to the left registered as a forward left diagonal. and pushing it to the right registered as a down and right diagonal. Pushing the stick down almost did not work at all. So basically I cannot use it for any game that needs the left stick.My 2nd controller I bought brand new at walmart. I used it about 20 hours within 2 weeks, and the R2 button that you use to shoot with in pretty much every FPS game broke. Looking it up, seems like the hinge broke on it. The trigger is like halfway coming out of the controller on side since it broke, and it sticks too. So its... Well, broken. Can't use this controller either.My last controller I purchased here on amazon, which is from this review. The controller was delivered on June 17, and stopped functioning correctly today, June 25. I only used this one on my pc, and Registered 17 hours on Steam with a game I just got from the summer sale. Something is wrong with the charging port connection on the controller. It loses connection with the slightest of movement. This makes it near impossible to play anything on pc since you need the controller connected via usb. This happens when charging on the ps4 as well. a little wiggle and connection is gone. It's done. I can only use it when its fully charged, with the ps4 now. It should be noted that I DID drop this particular controller one time. While I was using it with my pc. The problem occurred about 3 days later. So I am sure its related, and is my fault. But the other controllers, I did nothing to. If I have to say anything about this, is that a controller should be able to withstand a drop from my fully lowered computer chair to the floor. It couldn't have been more than a 3 foot drop. I had it resting on my leg while tabbed out and typing, and it slipped off. That was it.And that's it. 3 controllers. All of them broke. None of them even lasted a year. As much as I love this controller, I can't recommend it until problems with the hardware are addressed and fixed.And what review would be complete without the good side of things? Well. Honestly it is the BEST controller out there. In terms of how it feels in your hands, the button placements, and all that jazz. Whether you are playing a modern game and using the sticks, or an older game with the dpad. It feels natural. Other controllers like the Xbox controller just don't feel right when playing old games using the dpad. its not really comfortable with the dpad on the lower part of the controller. This is my favorite layout. since the sticks are raised unlike a dpad, no matter what you are playing, its always comfortable and natural feeling. This is the best controller out there. My only complaint is the share/options buttons. which are basically start and select.they are pretty hard to get used to pressing. Thats all.

Full disclosure: I have always hated dualshock controllers. With the exception of the VERY FIRST dualshock every one of them has lagged behind the competition. This one changes that. First of all, the sticks have much much more resistance which is a welcome change, secondly the shape is actually designed to be held by human hands and not by some sort of android with square hands. The touchpad might seem like a gimmick, but game devs have used it pretty well in my opinion. The little speaker that first showed up on the Wii-mote is here on this controller as well, and it actually adds a good bit of immersion to your game. It mainly plays things like audio recordings you find in-game, and the low quality of the speaker makes it seem like you're actually listening to a crackly, muffled recording. Very cool. The best feature by far is the headphone jack. The 360 and PS3 had headset jacks on them, but they only piped chat audio through them. The ps4 controller can channel FULL GAME AUDIO through it. It's FANTASTIC for playing late at night and not bothering anybody, especially since literally any 3.5mm headphones will work with it. I will say, the amp for the jack is hella weak and if you want better audio a dedicated amp like the Fiio E-06 is dirt cheap, tiny, and will help the game audio drastically.Anyway, great controller Sony. Easily on par with the 360 controller which is the greatest controller ever made.

Over the years, Killzone has become one of my favorite video game science fiction franchises. Each of the games has generally fallen short of its true potential, and it never became the "Halo killer" that it was intended to be, but as a whole the series poses an interesting premise and has developed its own identity. The iconic Helghast take obvious visual cues from Nazism, of course, but stripped of the genocidal underpinnings that would ordinarily come from, say, a World War II game. Meanwhile, the ISA generally comes across not as liberating heroes but at best largely incompetent and at worst nearly as bad as the Helghast. The series has also tended to emphasize the ugliness of war rather than celebrate militarism -- the end of Killzone 3, for example, featured the heroes not celebrating the final defeat of their foes but rather horrified at the cataclysmic destruction of the planet.Shadow Fall takes this general formula and tries to apply a new framework, and succeeds for the most part. Rather than an extended World War II analogue, the series has now graduated to the Cold War. With Helghan rendered uninhabitable, the ISA has cordoned off half of the planet Vekta for the establishment of New Helghan, complete with a wall separating the eastern and western halves of the planet. Needless to say, tensions are high between the two neighbors. Players take on the role of Lucas Kellan, a Shadow Marshall with the newly formed Vektan Security Agency (shorted to VSA, in an obvious nod to the most prominent American intelligence agency). Over the course of the game, Kellan uncovers the schemes of Helghast extremists bent on taking full control of Vekta as well as his own superior's plans to expel the Helghast threat for good. Teaming up with a Helghast agent, Kellan must avert a new war between the two factions.First things first, it must be said: the game is truly dazzling. In a next-gen launch filled with ports and a host of underwhelming titles, Shadow Fall stands out as a true next-gen experience. The lighting and textures are brilliant and the level of detail is extraordinary. There is a strong variety of levels, ranging from lush forested environments to gritty science fiction underworlds.The sound is also exceptionally well-done. The voice acting is generally quite good (though Kellan comes across as somewhat flat at times), the guns and explosion have a great pop to them, and the music nicely complements the gameplay. Technically, the game is a marvel and offers an eye-watering glimpse of the future.As compared with past Killzone games, Shadow Fall is a more contemplative shooter that features fewer scenes of non-stop military action. Kellan is, after all, supposed to be an intelligence agent. I initially found this disappointing, having become accustomed to Killzone 2 and 3-style action sequences, but the gameplay style grew on me over time. This was surely in part due to the addition of the OWL, a small robotic ally that will, depending on your orders, provide cover fire, stun enemies, set up a shield, or allow Kellan to quickly traverse the terrain via a zipline function.I also found the story not up to my expectations at first due to some flawed execution. Kellan in particular is not especially well developed, and the decision to present all cutscenes in first person disrupted the flow at points and rushed the pacing. Still, having played through it twice now, I find that I have increased appreciation. Compared to Battlefield 4's truly awful campaign, Shadow Fall's is at least based on good ideas and in keeping with the series' tradition of exploring interesting themes.But what keeps me coming back is the multiplayer suite. In contrast to other shooters, all classes and weapons are available at the outset (though you must unlock attachments and some equipment). Rather than level up, players progress by completing a variety of challenges which require effective use of all weapons, abilities, and equipment. Multiplayer is also highly adaptable. While players can engage in a variety of standard Killzone matches, including Team Deathmatch and Warzone, they can also create their own matches, allowing them to customize which game modes are included and even what classes and weapons others can use. This feature promises to foster the game's continued vitality well into the PlayStation 4's life span.In the end, Shadow Fall is far from a perfect game, and even far from a perfect Killzone game. Nevertheless, it earns its place in any gamer's library and presents a strong opening salvo for the PS4.

Upon my initial playthrough of the single player campaign, KZ Shadow Fall has little going for it to make it a memorable title.  I haven't gotten into the multiplayer yet, so this review is only considering the campaign.  Here's my straight to the point pro/con list, hopefully to be updated as patches are rolled out:Pros:* Beautiful.  This will show off what the PS4 can do, mostly in terms of lighting, lens flares, effects etc.  The environment is never lacking in eye candy to get lost staring at, especially off in the distance.Cons:* Sound levels/mixing.  The audio of the dialog is totally off from the rest of the game.  At best case it's barely audible, so I resort to the subtitles.  The music levels also dips between blaring and nonexistent.  The Sound effects, especially the gunfire, are always pinned to the max and thus make it necessary for me to turn the master volume down to compensate.  There is an in-game audio adjustment allowed, but it doesn't really seems to help.* Lip Sync.  Simply put, when I can hear the audio, it's been noticeably out of sync with the character models by as much as 10 seconds or so.  It really helps kill any feeling of immersion I may start to get.* Save Games: This is really the biggest problem I have with KZ:SF.  I am an adult gamer, which means after getting home from a job all day, getting kiddos for ready for bed, I generally have between 20 and 30 minutes to game in any given evening.  The game says I've reached a checkpoint, but in fact this is stored in RAM, so when I close down the PS4 for the evening and start again the next day, I'm magically whisked back to the start of a early section losing all progress I made the night before.  I'm effectively stuck on the early levels as I cannot sit an play through an entire level in one sitting.  The devs have said they'll be patching this but to me it is a broken single player campaign until that time.* The AI isn't particularly smart, there are just tons of them, and from all directions.  So the game seems artificially difficult because the moment you open fire on one baddie, you just simply get overwhelmed by 12 others looking your way, oh and more dropping in from reinforcement ships.* The story (so far any) is totally forgettable, but I haven't seen it through yet.Overall, Killzone: Shadow Fall LOOKs like a top notch production, but plays like a half finished mess.

I have noticed from playing the new generation games (Dead Rising 3, Killzone SF, Infamous SS, ect) that most of the new "sequels" are, in fact, not necessarily sequels. Each title, for the most part, are rebrands of the original IPs; they accept the events of the previous generation's titles, but they go their own way, with whole new areas, new characters, new stories, and barely bring up the previous title's events (also, each of these have very different mechanics, tones, stories, and so on compared to the original series). Personally, I like that sort of direction for each series; it is a good excuse to change much of the structure of each series for the future due to the new system, and yet still holds on to the original framing.That being said, I liked Killzone SF. Was it amazing? No; if Amazon gave half stars, I would give this a 3.5* of 5 personally. (The * is because the 0.5 I deducted could easily be fixed due to the multiplayer issues, see that section).Gameplay wise, this game actually felt nice and slick; the OWL was fun, used the touchpad in a cool way (and actually, to me, proved the use of the touchpad at a separate action mapping system and not just gimmick scenarios). Gone was the feeling of cumbersome soldiers, for you are not necessarily a soldier, but more of a stealth operative from the ISA (kind of felt like a Shadow Marshall, even from KZ 1, was a badass who was almost like a Bond but in a war setting, who did whatever they wanted for success). They were like CIA agents, and in this game I felt like one. The guns, the OWL, bullet time, ect. = all made me, as a player, feel powerful, and I never felt frustrated on the hardest difficulty for every death (which I had plenty), were my fault and not the game (versus Killzone 2, those AI problems though). Also, the controller being revamped actually benefited this games controls, with triggers actually being triggers.Visuals wise and sound wise, this game is basically was Forza did for the Xbox One - really showed off the graphic abilities, frame rate successes, and sound quality of the new generation of consoles and games. And to be honest, I expected this game to look great, for the previous Killzones looked great too (despite bland color schemes), and they also sounded great too.Story wise is the main reason why I will not give a higher score. I liked the story quite a bit, don't get me wrong; I liked the aspects of going from a CIA agent who followed blindly to being shown the facts of the enemy, and even showed how the "good guys" were the bad guys too. So really, everybody was bad, and all those in power wanted destruction of the other side, with the soldiers and agents only wanting peace and being forced to kill the other side. I liked this alot, but I also felt that there was a missed opportunity,  and this is where my whole 1 star deduction comes from: this was the perfect opportunity to introduce a much more human element to the Helgast, and allow the player to play AS THE HELGAST for once (which was teased at the start of KZ 3). Instead, you played as the ISA the whole period, and it made me wonder why the main character took so long to break away from his boss after all he had seen, and never tried to do some solo work himself. But still, this game could have done so much more in story mode wise, and for a game that is basically a reboot in so many ways but still accepts previous events (despite little recognition beyond the intro scene), it played it safe by doing the same old kind of story in terms of characters, expected "twists", and so on. I personally wanted to be a Helgast for once, and to see that maybe, JUST MAYBE, there is a reason for their being ***hats and killing civilians and always wanting power. Not only that, but this game could have revealed a true political and world reflection of our current state of life now (could have been a nice 1984 by Orwell story lined game), and it touches on such a possible game, and yet never fulfills this. However, the end of the game gives me hope for the series and for a very interesting set-up for future titles. Still, the story could have been better; it wasn't bad, and I enjoyed it for what it was, but it could have been something so much more.Finally, after that little rant, is the multiplayer, and personally I loved it. It was fun, it was addicting, and for me it felt fresh and unique. It felt like the best of the shooters that had released at the time, with mechanics, maps, play-types, servers, and all else that not only rivaled, but beat the competition (at least for a while). I loved it for the time I played it, but the sad fact is that the servers have gone down hill a bit. I recently played the servers again, and while before I rarely ever experienced lag, every match I had was littered with bugs and problems at some point. This is where my final half star comes in, but I put a * around it due to such problems can be fixed easily (usually).Like every review I write, I encourage questions, conversations about the game, and for each gamer reading this to play the game and make up their own mind, for each gamer is different. Enjoy!

Sadly, I knew from the opening sequence that this game wasn't going to be very good.  I had high expectations that were not only not met but actually dashed to bits.  In a nutshell, this game stinks.First is the environment.  Forget the lush visuals of the trailers and promos. at least 80% of the game will be spent in dark rooms, hallways, corridors, outer space, spacecraft, vent shafts and other drab environments.  Second, the navigation stinks.  The navigation and objective markers are very confusing at times. And that's only when the directional objective marker actually feels like appearing (there were several times I tried to invoke it, only to get a text display of my objective and nothing more).  It can be more confusing than helpful at times, especially when it rotates 360 degrees, like when you're in outer space, zero gravity or on a multi-level structure.  And some of the mission objectives are just downright confusing.  You'll get a vague hint like "assist so and so" but it doesn't tell you that this assistance involves several steps that aren't very intuitive.The weapons for the most part are decent but there are major shortcomings.  For instance, the game loves to put you in rooms full of ammunition and weapons like you're in a candy store but you can only carry a ridiculously small supply. You get one primary weapon, one secondary and a max capacity refill of reach. There are two types of grenades but you can only carry one type at a time.  When you're looking at a weapon on the ground, you can see the specs for it but the lame comparison leaves a lot to be desired.  Instead of orange and green bars to indicate more or less power, just do a side by side.  The worst glitch with the weapons is that some of them will simply refuse stop working and refuse to fire.  There is no explanation, no little text message to say "too close to target" an indication that the weapon is empty or anything.  Nope, you just sit there pressing R2 like a maniac while getting riddled by the enemy.  As if ridiculous cheapness were';t enough, the AI enemies even do little victory dances over your body and take cell phone pics of their kill.  So after the game fails on you, it celebrates its failure in tacky fashion.There are adrenaline packs that you can use during battle.  They will restore your health and also give you a temporary slowed down Matrix style "bullet time" boost.  It's helpful when facing a few enemies but pretty much useless when needed most, against scores of enemies as you'll encounter in the latter stages of the game.  Like the weapons, they also seem to disappear without warning when you need them most.  I'll start a new section with a full supply of adrenaline packs but somehow go down and see the message "no adrenaline packs available".The tactical echo and O.W.L. were the only two things that really stood out about the game and even they had their faults.  They are usually excellent tools in your arsenal, especially for helping  deal with the darker environments.  The tactical echo acts almost like a heat sensor, displaying enemy silhouettes through walls, doors or floors.  The O.W.L. is your personal drone that is capable of providing a shield, attacking enemies, disabling enemy shields and hacking computer systems which accomplishes numerous objectives like disabling alarms, opening doors, navigating ships, disabling security systems, etc. Unfortunately, when you use the most useful features like shield and pulse, it quickly drains the O.W.L. and it will end up off in a corner recharging when you really need it.  Also, as far as engagement, although it occasionally kills enemies, (more in the beginning than latter stages), by the last few chapters of the game, it amounts to little more than a distraction and hacking device.  99% of the enemies will need to be dispatched by you.All in all, I played the game only because I paid for it. I can wholeheartedly say if this were offered free as a PS-Plus game of the month or some other deal, I likely would have deleted it by now.  I would not buy the game again if given the chance all over again, but everyone has different tastes.  My advice is to watch a couple play through videos online just to get a grasp of the environment you'll actually be playing in versus the much prettier environments shown in the ads.  Might not hurt to rent it first as well, if you're able to do so.  Otherwise, grab it in a bargain bin as cheap as possible or wait to see if Sony offers it as a free PS plus game (highly likely in the near future) if you simply must have it.However, if frequently getting lost in dark environments with malfunctioning weapons and vague directives while having enemies twerk over your body and take cell phone pics after a ridiculously cheap kill seems like fun, then dive on in.  This is the game for you!

First of all, I'm a PC gamer at heart. I have a pretty beefy setup with an I7 3770K, 16GB DDR3 2400, 512GB SSD, GTX 680 4GB... I can basically run everything maxed out. I'm saying this in order to contextualize my (very) short analysis of Killzone: Shadow Fall, which I'll break down into a few parameters.Pros:I found the game beautiful, rivaling with the most beautiful games currently on PC. The textures, character models and all I could see looked really good and pleased me. The campaign runs at an almost constant 60 FPS which, to me, is the least the new generation could offer. The best part, however, is the artistic component: I found the character and architectural designs top notch and extremely believable. Vekta City looks beautiful and very believable, and the color pallet is great, with its saturated reds and blues.The Multiplayer, however, runs at 30 FPS, and this is sad because it makes the overall experience much, much less enjoyable: the gameplay ends up feeling dragged-on, almost as if the game was running in slow motion, and it frequently drops bellow 30 FPS. It can still be fun, but could have been much better.Cons:The game is buggy and glitchy. There are graphical glitches in a lot of the places, especially the run-down, rubble buildings. But the worst part is the sound. Although I enjoyed the musical score and the gun sounds, I frequently had it cut on me, especially in multiplayer. At first I thought it was an effect, as to simulate deafness from explosions, but that's not it. Also, everything sounds muddled and low, and I found it really hard to understand the story since the music and explosions always muffled the voice.All in all it was a good game and I intend on playing it further as to unlock more Trophies, but I can't shake the feeling of disappointment. It could have been much better and I feel it was rushed as to follow the PS4 release. It does showcases what the next gen of consoles has to offer - and I do think we have reason to be excited for it.
