In the late 90s, one of America's most infamous hackers was arrested and locked away in solitary confinement. At the time it was believed he could launch a nuclear missile by just whistling into a phone. While back then this notion may have seemed quite far-fetched, computer technology has become an integral part of everyday life, and with more devices becoming interconnected there are growing fears about what some people may be able to do if these systems were to fall into the wrong hands. Ubisoft’s latest title, Watch Dogs, takes this idea and puts players in control of a future where digital warfare is a scary place to be caught in the middle of.Set in an alternate version of Chicago, gamers take the role of a computer hacker named Aiden Pearce. Using a tool known as the Profiler, Aiden is able to hack objects within the open world of Chicago and use them to his advantage.  Because the entire city is connected -- as we all know by now because of the Watch Dogs' hype train -- using a central system called ctOS, it also gives Aiden the ability to discover personal information about other people. Furthermore, it displays the questionable access that this system has overall within the streets and homes of the city, unknowing to those living in it.The game sets itself up to play more towards a stealth approach. Throughout the world security cameras play an important role of providing a strategic view of the area and mapping your plan of attack. Because Aiden is not your typical video game bullet sponge you’ll want to avoid running into a mission with an assault rifle just gunning down enemies.Instead, slowly taking out each foe one by one is a more reliable and satisfying task with the environmental hacks you’ll have at hand. Even when driving around you can trigger a number of events to aid in your missions, like manipulating traffic lights to cause chaos at intersections, raise and lower bridges to slow down pursuers or deliver a blackout to the city and shutdown every electronic device in the area. When you successfully pull off one of these events it’s great to see the outcome as the game will normally switch to a cinematic camera to show the damage you’ve caused.There are some small touches that help make the world a little more realistic. You’ll randomly see a car accident and the people involved will jump out of the driver’s seat and engage in an angry conversation. Passers-by on the streets will recognise you from the news and, depending on your notoriety, may contact police officials to notify them of your whereabouts.Apart from the quite lengthy campaign, there is a lot of side content to explore within Chicago. In addition to this you’ll sometimes receive information about events taking place nearby as you are driving around. As you progress and complete tasks the skill system allows you to unlock a vast array of extras for Aiden ranging from new skills to weapons and vehicles.There are however a few things that really stood out as problem areas in Watch Dogs. I found Aiden Pearce to be quite a bland character; there isn’t much of a personality behind him. The story starts off quite slowly and it does not give you much of a backstory relating to who Aiden is and what his motivations for hacking are. At the beginning of the game you are given a brief flashback of Aiden’s past, but this doesn’t start to unfold more until half way through the main campaign, by this time I had lost complete interest in the character and didn’t really care about him at all.One of the most interesting directions Watch Dogs takes is with some of its online multiplayer components, borrowing the popular player invasion system that can be found in Dark Souls and Demon Souls. While roaming around the world you can be invaded by other players who have been tasked with an objective. At the same time you’ll have to try and stop them from completing their mission, which usually involves first profiling your target and eliminating them. What makes this so fun is that the person that initiates the invasion will have their appearance changed to look like an ordinary NPC; they're able to blend into the surrounding environment.The challenge for the invader is to complete their task without being found to be another player; a stealth approach is usually a key factor. This gameplay makes for some really intense situations that you don’t normally find in the course of the main game. Apart from the invasion system there are a few other multiplayer modes including online races and free roaming. This is bound to keep many players engaged after working through the main story.It’s hard not to compare Watch Dogs to Grand Theft Auto V; as the latter was one of the biggest titles of last year and also set in an open world, you can draw parallels straight away. Grand Theft Auto V does a lot of fantastic things that really build the world and the characters within it, which is something I don’t think Watch Dogs does nearly as well. The way Rockstar Games handles its storytelling, characters and missions is what puts them on a completely different level compared to other open world games.The fact that Watch Dogs has come out as second-best against the juggernaut that is the Grand Theft Auto franchise doesn't mean it's a bad game; it's quite the opposite. It’s quite a great achievement for a brand new IP to come out and be as good as it is and to also try to do some new things on such a large scale. Its multiplayer is by far one of Watch Dogs' stand out components and this is where you’ll start to see some great videos floating around online from the community as they invade your game. Watch Dogs has dozens of hours of content and will certainly keep you entertained its world and what's on offer.

Aiden is a hacker who got in too deep resulting in the loss of his family. Now he hacks to find out who ordered the hit on his family. While the game info tells us to expect to hack and control the city, chase down leads and ultimately find the person behind the tragedy the fact is that the game is very, very much like so many other open world games: drive here or there fast enough, lead the cops on a chase, follow the glowing blue lines to hack the box that will enable you to enter a building and expand your hacking powers and such. If this were GTA or Saint's Row you'd be doing a lot of the same things: drive here, kill these guys, expand your influence. It's really similar and what was supposed to make this game distictive really doesn't add much.You can do cool stuff like mess with street lights and hack people's ATM accounts. You can listen in on their fictional conversations. You can hack gates to let you in to neighborhoods. You can set off explosions. Later, you can control even more of the city, but most of the stuff is really to help you get away from cops. Most of it is a shrug.One cool thing you can do is to take control of cameras and then move between them and then hack from a distance. This does bring something new to the table. Consider this CtOS mission: you can inflitrate a building with a bunch of armed guards, collecting a key card, and gaining access to part of the city's network. If this were GTA or Saint's Row or even Assasin's Creed you could go in guns blazing or (in the case of AC) climb over walls and stealthily kill everyone. You could do that here in Watch Dogs but I found I got wasted a lot easier in this game going that route. In this level, for instance, I went another route altogether. I hacked camera to camera and then used set up lures to move guards into position for my expolosions. Then I hacked noisemakers to move them out of the way. Then I hacked lifts and lights and alarms. I hacked guy's explosives that they carried to cause them to detonate. Then when the guard with the key died I hacked the card. Then I hacked a guy who was carrying a camera (why? Who knows but you can then be on a moving camera to get to other places in the building.) I used the camera guy and noises to move him closer to the node where I hacked the system and got access to the network. I did all this from outside the compound, safely on the street, just another dude standing around. It was more rewarding than running in guns blazing.When you do that kind of stuff - when the hacking actually enhances the game play - then this game shines. But too often I'm stuck trying to drive a car all over fictional Chicago within a time limit. I don't want to play a race car game. If I did I would've bought Gran Turismo. I want to play a hacking game in an open world. As such, I've been disappointed and frustrated at times playing this.The game shows potential and likely sequels will be so much better. In the mean time, this is a fun diversion that never really lived up to the hype.Note about the systems: I had both 360 and One. I felt like I lost nothing playing on the 360. The One looks better, of course, but how it played was very similar. If you only have a 360 don't worry about missing out on anything with what comes shipped.

I'm just an average gamer that has a passion for gaming. I like reviewing games because I'm not a fan boy and don't get paid to favor one thing over another. I did not follow Watch Dogs over the years as it was being developed. I actually did not really look into the game until about 2 months ago. I kept hearing about the game but had no idea what it was about. Since I wasn't really playing other console games the past couple of months I decided to pre-order the game since it was an Ubisoft title and always loved Ubisoft games. So I will go over the pros and cons of the game.Cons:- Same feeling as other open world games. This could be good for other people but after playing the GTA games and Assasin's Creed games, you don't get that full excitement of open world like you did with GTA 3 and AC1 and 2.- Repetition. I ended up playing the game most of the night but it's pretty repetitive when you are doing side missions. You hack someone, track them down, then knock them out or kill them.- You can only have one save. So far Ubisoft only allows you to have one save and its tied into your Xbox live account. If you want to start a new game you have to use a different account. I haven't looked at all the achievements but this does not give you a chance to play a good guy and then a bad guy or vice versa.- Online play. They say its optional and it is...but if you want to turn it off you lose all your notoriety (points that rank you against other players).Pros:- Unique story line. People are comparing this game too much to GTA 5. Well you shouldn't because the story line holds up on it's own. Some people say it started off slow but I feel the main story line started off with a bang.-Detail. I'm not talking about the graphics here. I was shocked to see that every single person you run into the street has a story. Basically when you are in scanning mode, every person has their age, profession, income and a sentence explaining what stands out about them. EX. I was running around just wanting to destroy stuff. Just ran into the middle of the street and a car came close to hitting me. I pulled out my gun and aimed it at the driver. I actually felt sorry for him and I couldn't kill him. He was a custodian, didn't make much money, and his brother was murdered. I couldn't bring myself to bring him to his end but I love a game that can make you feel connected to the game like that.-Talents. Like most RPGs this has a point system to upgrade you abilities. For Hacking, Combat, Driving and Crafting. You do have to follow upgrade trees because some of the better abilities don't unlock until later in the game. I find the trees simple and easy to understand. Also adds that extra excitement because the next thing is something that can always help you out.-Chicago. Even though this has the same feeling as other open world games...it's always nice being able to run around a town you never been in before. I already read from people that actually live in Chicago, that a lot of the places are inaccurate besides the landmarks that are really there. But to me, it's different.-Content. There is a lot do and a lot to learn. When something new comes up you get a tutorial window popping up for it. At the same time you have to find your side missions by hacking other people, or sometimes a side quest will pop up and you can accept it. When I first started I felt overwhelmed just because I just wanted to scan people around me to read their profile, lol.-Play the way you want. When doing missions you can approach them guns blazing or using stealth. Either way can be successful and at the same time, it adds enough change to want to try it both guns blazing and using stealth.Final thoughts:You will not be complaining about lack of content since there is so much to do.Too many people seemed to be turned off by Ubisoft for delaying the game and all of a sudden..they have nothing good to say about it. I guess you are entitled to be upset...but the game is out...just enjoy it for what it's worth.(This part was written from playing on the Xbox One)The graphics are good, but at the same time, not a huge upgrade from what you will see on PS3 or 360. To me the graphics were good. Could they be better? Yes they could but that didn't upset me. People don't seem to understand that if you release a title for current and previous gen consoles, you are not going to have a major graphics improvements. That is why I won't judge a game by its graphics until the end of 2014 and 2015 comes around. By that time, there will be titles that have been developed only for the new generation.The game definitely has its ups and downs. There is still a lot to do but at same time you can get bored. After taking a 20 minute break... you are itching to play again. I was doing that all afternoon and all night last night. I think that this will be a good grab for anyone. I found myself not playing many console games recently since nothing good was out that caught my interest. This will keep you busy until the next big thing comes out.Sorry for the Watch Dogs fans that have been following this game and were upset about the the delays, but I really think you should try the game. I was immediately immersed into this game and world. I am not giving this 5 stars because in the end I feel things were copied from GTA and Saints Row. That's not a bad thing because it makes a fun game, but Ubisoft added their own aspect of hacking and I think that hacking makes it great. I was pretty upset about having only one save so I hope to see a change or update for that.Thanks for reading and I will add updates as I finish the game and try more of the online play.***UPDATE 5/29/14***I tried out more of the online functions and it's actually very fun. The online servers are not that stable at this time because I have been disconnected to another player a couple of times. There is only one mode I have tried and it's basically, track down another player...you need to hack them, then install a back door.Installing the back door is when it gets very stressful/exciting because that player knows he is getting hacked and has to reach you before the back door reaches 100%. Every 25% the search area narrows down for the player being hacked. It's more of annoyance getting hacked but when you are hacking, you get a major adrenaline rush seeing the other player running around with a weapon, intending on killing you.***UPDATE 6/12/14***I'm still going through the story because I keep getting distracted by other online players hacking me and getting caught up in the side missions.  The more I play it, the more fun I find in the game.  Escaping the cops in GTA is one thing, but escaping the cops in Watch Dogs is a lot more fun for me.  As you drive around you can hack lights and road blocks as you go.  My favorite is raising a bridge over the river and ramp off of them.  I find myself screaming and laughing out loud throughout the escape scenes because it's a blast.One thing that I don't like as I play more is, how easy it is to get the cops called on you.  If someone witnesses you do anything bad like shooting a weapon or stealing a car they will call the cops on you.  You could neutralize the caller but of course that would lower your reputation points and start turning you into a bad guy.  That's fine if you are playing a bad guy, but I am playing as good right now.Even playing as a good guy, you get those sudden urges of wanting to go on a killing spree or rob a store.  Obviously it's more realistic if someone is calling the cops on you when you do something like that but it doesn't allow you to go on a rampage very long before the cops are on you.

Watch Dogs is an ambitious game. It combines driving elements, stealth, and combat.  This game tries, and for the most part succeeds at taking elements of GTA style 3rd person gaming with Assassins creed style stealth and movement. The learning curve is steep for this game: figuring out how to seamlessly move and hack cameras, cell phones, or spike strips takes a bit of getting used to. But once you get the hang of it, the gameplay is very satisfying: especially when you use focus time to pull of headshots and hacking skills to cause massive explosions for a huge kill combo.Much like GTA the game has a main set of missions and various side missions you can complete. Like an RPG, completing side missions and regular missions unlock skill points which can be used to level up your character using the skill tree. Broadly, your skills can improve in combat, driving, hacking, and crafting skills. Which skills you unlock will depend on your playing style - although the skill tree never collapses or narrows so you can unlock all the skills eventually.While the gameplay is really satisfying and the RPG-type progressions is great, the story and graphics keep this from being a 5-star game. The story requires quite a bit of suspension of disbelief and plot holes abound. The graphics, sadly, are pretty bad. Most of the characters are unrecognizable blurs at even a medium distance on screen and there's not much resolution even closer in. The background "pops" into view when you get close while driving.Complaints aside, I got hours and hours of fun from this game. It's strengths make it easy to overlook its flaws.

I was very excited to get this game.  I had seen the commericals and I'm an Xbox fan, so I was glad to get something a little different than the usual RPGs or Shoot-em-ups I always play.From the very start, this game bothered me; you have to "install" it, meaning, you can't play this on a normal XBox 360 with 4 Gigs of storage.  You need close to 8 gigs to "install" the game before you can play it.  The game is TWO discs; one to "install" it, and the other is the game itself.  I had to take a memory card and hook it up to my 360's USB port, and thankfully, that worked.  It took awhile to "install", but I did get the game working.  I understand the need to do that - but I don't like it.  A game should work on a system despite the system's limitaitons; every Nintendo 64 game worked with the Nintendo 64. You didn't need more memory or storage - that's the rule.  That's the whole reason why we buy consoles; so we don't have to worry whether or not a game will work correctly.Despite my not liking it's intall procedure, the game is OK.  The graphics are really good, the control is rock-solid (although I question some of the buttons usage), and it's very much like a GTA feel, only you're a hacker instead of a madman.  The gameplay is fun - you hack nearby items, cameras, doors, etc.  You distract people and sneak by.  You trail people, try to catch them / hurt them.  But - and here is my main flaw - if you mess up, if you are "caught" or seen, the game will end and you have to wait a good minute or so for it to re-load some prior saved game.  You can only save the game in your hotel room or certain safehouses; very GTA Vice City.  How come I can't save wherever and whenever I want???  The game-over-reload screen killed me and made the game tedious rather than fun.It didn't live up to the hype, which was disappointing.

Watch Dogs. It's been compared to a futuristic Assassins Creed and GTA5. So how does it stack up?The whole hacking concept is awesome in an open world game. There are so many ways to interact with the world and learn about people. Hacking into traffic lights and underground steam pipes, arming enemy grenades, looking though remote cameras…it really helped make the world real. Once the novelty wears off, however, hacking feels like it could've used more depth. It's mostly reduced to a basic button press or hacking mini-game (which got annoying at times).The open world definitely has character. It's amazingly detailed. NPCs aren't just background decorations; they feel alive, aided by the great animations in both the open world and cutscenes. Loads to do: poker, chess, drinking games, racing, space invaders, gang hideouts, crime prevention, and more. Though these quickly become repetitive and grindy.It has great open-world combat with various ways to complete missions. This was probably my favorite aspect of the game. Character progression is also nicely done. The cop chases are super fun, though super easy to escape from via boat.The Xbox 360 version looked decent enough. I don't have a next gen console to compare it against. So, impressive for what it was.I won't delve too much into the story. Our protagonist, Aiden, is a bland and uninteresting vigilante – an everyman with little to no personality. I never developed any real emotional attachment with him or his situation. The side characters were much more interesting. Good voice acting, but the story is weak and filled with cliches. Overall, it's an average story at best. The stakes are never very high, in the end it didn't feel complete. Saving that for the sequel, Ubisoft?What didn't I like? The vehicle control/physics is laughable, and no melee combat? Huge oversight there, given the huge number of ways Aiden can interact with the environment and the crafting system. The radio stations are terrible. Online modes are interesting in concept but sadly easy to exploit (by people disconnecting when their opponent is about to win). And of course, Uplay.Overall score: 3.5/5. Definitely worth renting or picking up on sale, though I've read that the PC port is terrible. Probably want your console version of choice for this one.

Watch Dogs is a game I desperately wanted to like, especially since it's exciting unveiling a few years back.  GTA clone with hacking and a dark revenge storyline, that sounded pretty cool.  It turns out it's a lot more fun to think about than actually play.The introduction is actually one of the best scenes in the game.  A brutal interrogation of the guy who caused the crash that killed the main character's niece.  Followed by a tense escape using your hacking techniques in many different ways.  Setting off a tennis ball machine, a car alarm, blacking out a building etc.  It is great.Once you get to the actual game, it grinds you away.  Aiden our hero is a grouchy dope.  The revenge plotline is ham handed.  Most depressingly, the gameplay is a slog.  Almost every action in Watch Dogs follows this general route.-  Get mission via either hacking a pedestrian or through game story-  Go to mission start-  Wait for some action to take place whilst watching on a video camera.-  Depending on mission type, chase and tackle a criminal, kill everyone, or kill everyone and solve a rudimentary puzzle using a number of different viewpoints with security cameras.That's all it seems to be.  Sometimes your actions will cause the police to chase you and you drive at high speeds while changing the lights or erecting barriers in the road.  If you are successful, you get away, if not, you eventually get chased and killed by a helicopter.  Or you can slowly swim into Lake Michigan until the cops give up and slowly swim back, a scintillating 10 minutes to be sure.Everything about the game is fine.  The cars handle fine, the shooting is fine, even the hacking, which mostly amounts to viewing your targets with security cams and occasionally blowing up a fuse box or lifting your character on a forklift is fine.  Everything is fine and that adds up to everything getting boring in a hurry.It's a clever idea and one that could have been great, but it falls so far short into mediocrity you'll be left wondering what could have been.

Watch Dogs gets a lot more things right than it does wrong.  It may be short on ideas and story lines, but it makes up for that by being just a fun game to sit down and get lost in.  Anyone who has ever played GTA will find a ton of similarities with Watch Dogs, from the look, to the driving, to the movements, to the camera, but at the end of the day, this game is an engrossing time suck that is well worth your time and efforts.The gameplay, while slightly uninspired, is more or less a complete rip-off from GTA, but that's no bad thing.  When you're running and driving through the city it's more or less JUST like GTA.  The movements, the weapon cycling, the chatter, and the cars crashing will leave you thinking a lot about GTA and what a unique game series THAT is.  While it leaves you with an unoriginal distaste for the lack of creativity, Watch Dogs is still pretty fun.  It models itself from the best, and they don't skimp on tight action and explosive gameplay.  One of the obvious attractions of this game is the hacking aspect which is actually pretty fun and easy to get into from the start.  You can zone in on cameras high above enemies, spy on them, and manipulate objects in order to distract and kill.  There are lots of situations where you'll need to sneak into an abandoned warehouse littered by thugs, and you can remotely hack into a camera and peer through it, and further find explosive devices to eliminate anything that may stand in your path at a later time.  If that's not your thing, you can use the radar to try and sneak past.  It makes for tense situations, and the game really does a nice job of giving you options as to progressing in the game.Something else I found fun is the ability to hack bridges, street lights, etc.  When you're evading the cops, it's always fun to fly over a bridge as it's opening on your command, leaving the police trailing your dusty wake.  There are lots of getaway possibilities available to you with a simple hack.  I also find it fun to hack into other players games, or get hacked by other players.  I was wandering around on a random crime mission, and all of a sudden a warning flashed across the screen telling me I had a minute to go find some punk who was hacking into my funds.  It's hilarious trying to catch these random players, and it gives the game another aspect of tension.  I also really enjoy how you can hack into people's bank accounts and profile them as you walk by them in the street.  When you're short on cash, you go to an ATM and take out the profiled characters money.  It's an original touch that works.Another plus are all the random side missions.  You won't get bored easily with this game as it literally has hours of stuff to do.  It's pretty wide open as far as how linear you wish your path to be.  It's not a overly huge world, and you won't feel even a smidgen of freedom you have in games like, say, Skyrim, but it definitely feels on par with GTA in terms of size.With all of these things going for it, it gets bogged down by the incredibly lame story, and stupid dialog and characters.  You play a guy who was betrayed, he's come back to avenge someone's death, blah blah blah.  We've all seen it 1,000 times before.  The main character has a dumb, monotone voice like every other dopey video game out there.  He says things like "let's do this", and "the pain never goes away", and "you're going down".  Really?  Is this the best the writers can do?  You just end up wanting the main character to shut his trap and stop talking so you can enjoy the game.  Also, the chatter from the NPC's is flat out dumb and irritating.  They say stupid, childish things, and it's one of the aspects that makes you miss what the GTA series does so well.  I walked by a character talking about beating up his girlfriend because she was annoying him.  No humor, no reason, he just said it.  Without any context it just ends up sounding like a bunch of immature meatheads got together and wrote the script for the game in two hours.  GTA deals with the same themes, but it does this by engaging characters, and most of all, humor.  It takes you out of the game when people are just wandering aimlessly saying dumb stuff.Watch Dogs has plenty of cool gameplay to keep you occupied for a while.  The hacking aspect is fun, and it's action packed.  The driving is easy and intuitive (I may be in the minority with this opinion), and fighting and missions are plentiful.  If it weren't for the dopey story and abysmal dialog, this would be a really fantastic game.  Amazon doesn't award half stars as I would normally give this game three and half, but I think it warrants a strong recommendation with four stars.  If you're up for some braindead fun and high-tech hacking, this game is for you.

I will start off saying that the concept of the Watch Dogs game is great. It is a third person, open world, action game that follows a vigilante/hacker, Aiden Pearce, as he battles the crime and corruption in Chicago by using the CtOS system (the city's surveillance system) to his advantage. Don't get me wrong this is not a just a hacking game, Aiden uses an arsenal of automatic weapons and explosives along with his various hacking devices to achieve his goals.My main complaint is with a pretty awful glitch in the Xbox One version of the game, even after I downloaded the most recent updates. The voice sound, when in mission and during phone calls, in nonexistent. I checked the settings, deleted the install and reinstalled the game all for nothing. I have seen a number of complaints and that it is not uncommon. I have contacted the Watch Dogs team about the issue, multiple times, and I was ignored. The reason this makes the game so difficult is because you can be in the middle of a car chase or gun fight and be totally lost because you can't read the subtitles, which do work.This is extremely disappointing because Ubisoft is usually great about getting back to you and patching up glitches. I will update this review when the glitch is fixed or if I find a workaround.

I like open-world games. However, I have to wonder how this game won any awards. Granted, I haven't finished it yet, but I'm a good way into the game and I'm not seeing anything here that hasn't already been done better in other games. The hacking component is an interesting addition to the GTA style of play, but it's really not that amazing and actually gets a little boring after a while.Now, I'm not saying the game is bad. Three stars is "average" as far as I'm concerned. I'm just not seeing how it lives up to the hype, and to be honest, I found the characters kind of unlikable. I don't know if it was the voice-over work, or just the general blandness of the characters, but I just didn't like them. They didn't grab me and keep my interest. For example, in Red Dead Redemption, I was ENJOYING being John Marston. Meanwhile, I care so little about Aiden Pearce in Watch Dogs that I had to look up his name after being away from the game for a day.One thing that kills one whole star in my review is the driving control. The cars control very loosely, like they're driving on icy roads. When you're slamming into things all over the place because the driving physics are so wacky, you get frustrated. Being able to change the traffic lights via hacking was pretty cool, I'll admit, but it didn't make up for the driving being the way it is.Hacking individual pedestrians is interesting for the first five minutes, and then you realize it's really not DOING anything but filling in for the "picking up random money lying around" game mechanic of other games. Instead of picking stuff up, you hack people and get their ATM information, and then you steal money from them. Big thrill. Sometimes you find out that they're about to commit a crime, so you have to high-tail it to where the crime is about to happen and carefully sneak up on them so as not to alert them, so you can catch them in the act. The problem with this is that everyone is hyper-aware, and if you walk into a room filled with people while someone's about to commit a crime, they somehow are able to pick you out as the guy who's there to catch them, despite you not looking like a cop or doing anything particularly suspicious. Again, it's frustrating.If the potential criminal runs away before going through with their crime then you can't do anything to them without being penalized. for it. It makes little sense. If the guy was going to kill his girlfriend and just stopped because he saw you out of the corner of his eye, why wouldn't you want to stop him ANYWAY to prevent him from going back later and doing it when you're not there? It's just plain stupid the way they worked out some of the crimes you're meant to prevent, because they don't actually want you to PREVENT them-- They just need you to catch them in the act. But you're a vigilante, not a cop. You really shouldn't care about catching the guy in the act so much as preventing him from acting in the first place. It's a logic breach I can't accept in a somewhat sloppy story.Now, is it fun to play? Yes, mildly so. It's not as fun as I'd hoped, though. I'm not a kid, though, so maybe some of the "cool" factor is lost on me. All I know is that after playing for a while it just feels repetitive and I find myself shutting down to do something else. Most of the time, it just doesn't feel like you're really accomplishing anything in this game. It's like they had an interesting concept-- hacking everything-- and then didn't build up much of a game around it.This is a moderately-good GTA/Saint's Row clone without as much humor or fun as the originals. It lacks sorely in character development and likability, and the driving mechanics make car chases a lot less fun than they were in GTA or Saint's Row games. The combat is decent, and the story is acceptable but not groundbreaking. Everything looks good and the sounds are well-done, but overall it feels like a cardboard world you're running around in, and you just never feel an attachment to what's going on around your character. Personally, I also found it difficult to root for Aiden Pearce, as he's restricted enough to not be crazy fun like a GTA or Saint's Row character (You're penalized for harming civilians, for example),  and he lacks much in the way of a personality. He just feels like a stereotypical hacker vigilante archetype and slapped him on the screen expecting players to make him interesting somehow... And it's not easy.It feels like the "Under The Dome" (TV show) of video games: Great concept slightly soiled by dull or dim-witted characters who you try to like, but just never do, and thus you never really care who live or dies, who wins or loses, and won't be terribly upset if you never see the ending. It's junkfood. It's mildly entertaining, "I'm bored with GTA and Saint's Row so this will do until a new one comes out" off-season filler. It's what you play in the summer while waiting for the better games to come out at Christmas time.Again, it's not a bad game-- It just doesn't really reach for the stars. It's just a lot of the same-old, same-old, but it takes itself too seriously and just never feels amazing. It's just average, which I suppose might be disappointing after the hype from the early trailers, but it's really not so surprising. Perhaps the experience on the newer-generation consoles is more involved, but I doubt that better lighting and shadows could make Aiden Pearce any more interesting, or his sidekick any less annoying, or the civilians any less like manikins in a department store designed to look like Chicago.Slow load times despite being installed on the hard drive add to the unpleasant experience. I assume this is a better situation on the newer consoles. Sometimes I wonder if developers are tasked with making previous-gen console versions of their games run or load slower to push people toward buying the new consoles. The load times in this were enough to make me become bored with waiting.If you really love the open-world sandbox type of game, you may find some nuggets of joy in this otherwise drab world. If you want something funny, though, I expect you'll be unhappy with this one. If you want wild action, again I'd say you're barking up the wrong tree. However, as a summer filler type of game, this does the trick. It all comes down to individual tastes with this one.Three Stars. Average. Not awful, not amazing.

Like most people, Watch_Dogs popped up on my radar a few E3s ago when it was basically a giant tech demo from Ubisoft. The footage kept getting more and more interesting, but most of the hype had gone away by release day. Honestly, I had always planned on picking up this title, but probably not until I saw it on a sale for 75% off or something along those lines.On the 360, Watch_Dogs doesn't look too bad - the devs over at Ubisoft did a good job toning down the textures and keeping the game looking as good as it does. It obviously doesn't hold a candle to the next-gen systems like the XBox One or PS4, but it's not ugly by any means.That's really the best thing I can say about Watch_Dogs - it doesn't look bad on the 360. Everything else was downhill for me.First off - load times. It was Skyrim all over again. Resetting a mission, failing a mission, quitting a mission - all of these actions take a 15-20 load screen. This doesn't seem half bad until you run into that one mission you can't quite pass and have to reattempt multiple times.It should also be noted that it seems like half the game content is racing based. It seems like you're spending half your time running from the police, running from bad guys, chasing bad guys, etc. Again, this probably wouldn't be quite so bad except that it's almost impossible to get away from chases without specific skills upgrades. Somehow every single cop and bad guy are able to sit on your bumper through miles of traffic and accidents.Quite a few folks have made the GTA comparison - I'm going to compare it to something else, Saints Row IV. There are several aspects of the game play that really feel like they just took SR4 and took the cartoony aspect out. There's minigames dispersed throughout the city, vehicle collecting, random chases, unlocking area towers, and so forth. However what made SR4 fun was that it never took itself seriously. It allowed you to go OP and literally become a comic book superhero. Take that away and you've got Watch_Dogs.Even the hacking aspect feels forced and quite often - useless. I had initially thought that the game was meant to be played similar to the Splinter Cell series. Stealth 90% of the time, kill only when you have no other option. There's literally no downside to going through and massacring every enemy in the game. In fact, it's often easier to head shot every guard instead of parkouring yourself into a position to hop from security camera to security camera in order to explode a fuse box.If the game was fun to play - even the killing aspect could be overlooked. It might be one of those things you bookmark for later - go through the first play-through on easy mode, killing everyone in sight, and on the second play, do everything hard, don't kill anyone. Honestly, I don't know if I'll even finish the first play.

I love sandbox games like Assassin's Creed, inFamous, and GTA. I am really enjoying, but not loving, this game. I've spent a lot of time on the side-missions, which are unique and challenging, instead of playing through the story. The story so far has been good, not great. So far, it's all about getting revenge and taking down a greater power that tried to kill the main character, but killed his niece instead.The music is great and there are a lot of radio stations to choose from.The driving is challenging. It's better than the older GTA games, but not as good as a driving sim like Project Gotham, though the controls are similar. I prefer the default which brakes with the left trigger and accelerates with the right trigger. Each car sounds and drives different. That puts them one over the Gran Turismo franchise!The shooting is like Gears of War in the use of cover, leaping over obstacles, but I can't shoot blindly over cover quite as well as in GOW. Auto-aim is available, but is not as easy to use as Modern Warfar.The free-running is like that of an athletic individual, not quite ninja-esque like Assassins.Good story. Good gameplay. Plenty of side-missions and challenges for hours of fun. You'll never exhaust the side-missions. There will always be a crime happening somewhere for you to go and thwart. Those aren't usually the most entertaining side-missions, but it always involves some level of running, driving, and hacking so I enjoy them.

Executive Summary: buy on sale and only if you have an xbox one or PS4. You’ll probably be done with this game in a weekend and probably will never play it again afterward.I don’t think this game should be played on the Xbox 360. It’s just a pain. First off, it was a horrible install that took maybe two hours. I did other stuff for a few hours and it eventually completed. Secondly, I got very tired of looking at load screens. I rarely write game reviews these days. It's too subjective and people invariably seem to feel slighted if their favorite game is critiqued. I am confident however that most people who had the misfortune of purchasing this game will agree with me. And that's it's a very messy, unpleasant game.The E3 tease turned out to be a graphically fabricated lie but putting aside that, the game itself is just so nasty. I really feel like the developers genuinely went out of their way to make a game as offensive to the player as possible. Any time you feel you're getting a some enjoyment, the mission turns into a cluster of police just suicide ramming you. You're supposed to 'hack' your environment to escape in a car but usually that results in you yourself being the victim of the attack since the method of tripping explosives usually work against you. It's actually easier just to jump into the water and swim away, which feels cheap.There are moments of goodness, which makes this affair more frustrating. The gang hideout side missions showcase what this game could and should have been; a stealthy game of chess where you're taking out bad guys at your pace using the surroundings as your ally. Sadly this is short lived and even during main missions where this mechanic is employed, the campaign inevitably ends with you moshing your way out with twenty police cars chasing you, and their associate terribly car handling, they just ram you to death. And boy will you die a lot in this game, or rather the missions will just end. Did you like the "tail without getting caught" missions in Asssassins Creed where one mistake results in an insta-fail and restart? Every single main mission is like this here. Every single one.Let's add insane load times to this mix, and unskippable phone conversations which you will hear many, many times and you have a dirty, vile little game that punishes the player for trying to enjoy it.Forget that it's graphically out of date, that it didn't deliver what it promised, that it's a new IP. It's just plain awful and not worth your time and definitely not worth your money. I do wonder how so many people who apparently worked on it (hundreds according to the credits) were able to make such a game. How not one of them asked themselves "isn't a game supposed to be, you know  fun?" Because if they had, they would not have released Watch Dogs as it is.*main campaign completed with 70% of the game done.

I feel like I've said this with every Sims 3 expansion pack to date, but Island Paradise might be my favorite (And I also ownThe Sims 3: Pets Expansion Pack,The Sims 3 Plus University,The Sims 3: Generations - PC/Mac,The Sims 3 Seasons, andThe Sims 3: Ambitions.).  I love that it adds both richness and variety to your game play so if you're finding yourself a little bored with Sims and longing for more variety and challenge it is a great choice.This expansion offers so much to love.  For starters, the new neighborhood, Isla Paradiso, is gorgeous and feels distinctive from the other neighborhoods in that it is spread across various islands vs. one solid landmass.  I also thought the scenery was very pretty and really captured that paradise vibe.  Accordingly, you also get a lot of new water-related activities.  The opportunity to discover things is especially interesting because it gives your sim's interactions a purpose and also gives you something to work toward.But probably my favorite aspect of game play is the ability to build and run your own resorts.  I've always loved the entrepreneurial and career aspects of the game so to me this was exciting.  I especially appreciate that it is much more involved than owning other businesses (i.e. the restaurant, movie theater, etc.) and really lets you take charge of the decision making.  For beginners, you have the option of taking over the town's struggling resort for free and there are also blueprints that make it easy to build your resort if you're a novice.  Reviews from guests help you guide what improvements you make to the resort to get a 5-star rating and maximize profits.  From there the sky really is the limit.  I also appreciate that you can hire staff so the resort can (mostly) run itself if you choose freeing your sim up to have another career or enjoy ample leisure time.  It also adds continual challenge if you want to maintain a 5-star resort over time as I found that my guests were increasingly picky about what they wanted.  (I could see where this might bug some gamers, but I liked that it kept the game from being too easy.)  Really my only nit about building and running resorts is that in order for the resort to be open for business you have to place a resort tower.  That in and of itself wouldn't be a big deal, but you can't seem to edit their appearance and there are only four options to choose from: Island Beach Bungalow, Beach Resort Tower, Spanish-Style Resort Cottage, and Eco-Modern Resort Tower.  This means if you have another theme in mind you'll likely have to deal with a tower on your property that doesn't match the rest of your decor.  (Though as a cheat I've heard of other players sticking their resort tower in the basement though I do believe it limits your ability to upgrade it and I haven't tried it myself.)Really the only thing I didn't enjoy about this game is that if you move your household to Isla Paradiso from another neighborhood their family tree, relationships, goals, etc. are all gone.  This was disappointing to me since I'd been building a long family tree for my Sim.  Had I thought more fully about this, I probably would have waited to have my sim divorce her husband after she moved to Isla Paradiso so she could at least maintain contact with him.  I really wish this world could be treated much more like University, but alas that is not the case.  Thankfully you can keep your job and your job rank if there is a similar career available in Isla Paradiso.  My Sim was in the medical profession and thankfully was able to continue on that track as she had invested a lot of time in schooling and growing her career.Overall this is a fantastic EP and having tried many of them would definitely be one of the first I'd recommend, especially if you love tropical environments and the entrepreneurial aspects of the game.

Another problem that burns me up to no end is Ubisoft's desire to enforce the same old checkpoint saved game bologne and in some circumstances, the game doesn't even save the checkpoint. As a Chicagoan, I was really looking forward to the release of this game.  So far, I think the game's rendering of my city is my favorite aspect.  Though they've taken creative license with the overall map and the look of individual buildings, many notable landmarks (including the building I work in) are pretty true to real life.  For me, it made it cool to move around the map taking on missions, because there is something fun about doing things in your city that you would never be able do in real life (i.e. go on high speed chases, climb buildings, etc).  From my exploration, so far the most literal interpretation of Chicago seems to happen in the loop, though I'm curious to explore other districts/neighborhoods to see how they compare to real life.Beyond my love of how this game brought Chicago to life, I also think a lot of the missions are very interesting and do seem distinctly different from games like Grand Theft Auto and Assassin's Creed.However, where this game falls down for me is in its overall cohesiveness (or in this case, lack there of).  While individual elements are good, to me the whole game experience doesn't gel as well as I've come to expect with franchises like GTA and Assassin's Creed.  My experience is also likely due in part to the fact I haven't really been loving the whole narrative/storyline of the game.  I don't want to give it away, but in my experience it seemed to detract, rather than add, to gameplay.  I found myself wanting to rush through it to get to my next mission.I will admit I am torn when it comes to what star rating this game deserves.  To me, 3.5 stars is probably the most accurate, but since Amazon doesn't offer 1/2 stars, I've rounded up to 4.  I do think for this being the first installment of what could easily be a franchise, it seems like a good first effort and does offer some fun game play.  But it does seem like further development work is needed to bring it up to par with GTA and others.  If you go in expecting this to be of the same caliber, you will likely be disappointed.

Now we see what happens when Assassin’s Creed and Grand Theft Auto hook up for a one-night stand: they give birth to a bastard child known as Watch Dogs.In Watch Dogs, from AC maker Ubisoft, you play a hacker whose sister, and her family, were murdered by some mysterious bad guy as a way of getting said hacker to back off an not interfere with their Deep and Sinister Plans ™. Left unexplained is why they didn’t just kill the hacker, but games like this aren’t generally known for their lack of plot holes (hello, entire Assassin’s Creed franchise!).The game play is smooth, and familiar to anyone who has played Assassin’s Creed or GTA. There’s some slight variation in the controls and, sadly, you don’t seem to be able to climb up every building in creation, then drop down and assassinate them, but you can’t have everything. What you do get to do instead is go around and hack into everything. And I mean everything. Soda machines, power grids, traffic lights, possibly toasters…if it has a computer chip and an internet connection, you can apparently hack it.Now this can cause some problems for you. I tried hacking traffic lights and the like while in a high-speed police chase. This did not end well for me, nor for the four or five people I ran over in the process (sorry, guys!). I’m also unclear why causing a power outage in a baseball stadium causes light figures to explode and power outlets to spark. Apparently this universe’s version of Chicago managed to develop pretty much all the same technology that we have, except, alas, for the circuit breaker.But speaking of Chicago, the whole city seems to be lovingly rendered for your amusement, and it looks just gorgeous. The whole game does, really. On my PC (which is what I’ve been using to play), the graphics are just amazing! Textures on cloth, reflections, etc, everything looks wonderful.On the other hand, the sound. I have very good speakers. I have them turned up all the way. I have the volume on my PC turned up all the way. I could barely hear any of the dialogue. I went in and adjusted the sound settings in the game, and there was no real change. So I think we might have a glitch. Hopefully this will be fixed via a patch sometime soon.That minor complaint aside, this really is an impressive game, and I look forward to logging many, many more hours.

Watch Dogs is the story of Aiden Pearce. He is a genius hacker with a dark past. He was a criminal in the past and his actions led to the tragic death of his family. Now Aiden is out for blood and aims to take down the criminals. This takes place in the future and in the city of Chicago. There is a sophisticated computer network in place that can control practically everything around the city. Aiden can hack into the network and take control and utilize them as additional resources. There are tons of opportunities to hack the system. For example if you are in a car being chased by the cops you can switch traffic signals all to green so there will be an accident. You can also raise a drawbridge so the cops are stuck on the other side. I won't ruin all the surprises but there are tons of different hacks and you can unlock many more as you progress.You can also unlock new combat moves and crafting skills. You earn skill points as you play and you can unlock the skills that are most interesting to you. You can craft new items from parts that you find or purchase at a pawn shop. For example you can craft a lure that you throw down as a distraction to get people to go to it. As you fight there are many things to consider and you really need to adjust your methods depending on the situation. Sometimes you will need to be stealthy and sneak in and out unnoticed. Other times you can go in guns blazing. It just depends on how many guys you are up against and what your goal is. There are tons of different campaign missions and side missions along the way. Every few minutes it will pop up and say that a crime is in progress and you can choose to intervene or not. There are online missions to play as well. You can also just explore the vast city and get into trouble with no real purpose at all. Just keep in mind that the citizens will love or hate you depending on your actions. If you are constantly running down innocent people with your car then they will eventually hate you and will cooperate with the police to nail you. If you are careful not to cause civilian casualties and are constantly helping the citizens of Chicago then they will love you and will be much less likely to turn you in.This game is incredibly complex and thoroughly entertaining to play. There are tons of weapons to choose from and unlock and loads of different cars to drive and unlock. In a way this game has a lot of the same characteristics as Grand Theft Auto but there many differences as well. The language in Grand Theft Auto is pretty bad and it's hard to play with my kids in the house. This game certainly has some language but it's not even remotely close to being as bad as Grand Theft Auto. I like Grand Theft Auto a lot too but I honestly enjoy playing Watch Dogs more.The city is huge and you can explore wherever and whenever you like. Whether it's on the streets, roof tops or in the water inside a boat or swimming there is always some place new to explore. The graphics in this game are very detailed and smooth. The whole experience really pulls you into the games and makes it feel like real life. This is going to be my favorite game for the foreseeable future.

Watch Dogs was so hyped up after the E3 announcement that I thought this would be the next-gen game to watch out for. Now I have finally played the heck out of it, I thought I would summarize my thoughts on it.Watch Dogs is basically a open-world fusion of GTA and Assassin's Creed with Batman Arkham City thrown in. The story surrounds the protagonist Aiden Pearce who is a vengeful hacker against the new central ctOS system in Chicago after a hack job gone wrongand his family murdered. Aiden would use his hacking skill to exercise vigilante justice. This seems like a fresh idea but in reality hacking is simplistic and becomes repetitive over time.The open world environment and tons of side missions make it fun and addictive to play. You can drive, assassinate, shoot, blow things up or in whatever way you choose to get the job done. However, there are disappointed and terrible moments as well. Driving is not exactly enjoying because the control is not fun and it's hard to see what's in front especially in a fast car. Also, sometimes things get absurd like blowing up a fence but the fence remains standing, or you get a clean escape from cops in a boat because they are too hydrophobic.The single player mission would take you many hours to complete especially if you have to do all the side missions and quests. However, this could be repetitive and diminish your desire to finish it. Multiplayer is fun but lacking at times. There is virtually no co-op game mode. Instead, you get a variety of competitive game modes to play. Two modes I like the most are Intrusion and Decryption. They offer some unique gameplay which is different from the online military shooters that I've grown to love.Watch Dogs received so much hype and also got delayed because Ubisoft Montreal said to need more time to finish it. Now the finished product is a mixed bag. While it's fun and addictive, it also has terrible moments in which I almost threw my controller at the TV. There is plenty of room for improvement. It's like a lot GTA with innovative hacking scheme, but not as polished and grand as GTA. Anyhow, I would give this game 4 stars, for its innovative hacking gameplay.

I was excited for Watch_Dogs because I love the television show Person of Interest, which has a somewhat loosely similar premise (using the internet of things to manipulate the world around us), though to notably different ends. After having played Watch_Dogs for a little bit, I will admit that the storyline seems intriguing, but that it is difficult to enjoy due to the game play. There was very little tutorial details built into the game itself, with the expectation in the first mission being that you know the mechanics of sneaking about from hiding place to hiding place. The shooting mechanics are also unusual; they feel like a first-person short model grafted on to a third person perspective, which makes things like aiming a little difficult. If you played Max Payne 3, you probably can get a sense of what I’m talking about. For comparison’s sake a better style third-person shooter would be (going again with a Remedy game) Alan Wake, or the multi-platformer Blood Stone.As you might expect from an Ubisoft game, the story is compelling, save that the protagonist is only somewhat sympathetic to the point at which I have played in the game. The storytelling is sufficiently tight that you don’t get bogged down in details, but not so tight that essential plot elements are either easily lost or omitted altogether. The side quests are interesting, though they do not add a significant amount to the main storyline, and if your primary objective is to finish the story as quickly as possible, they can be omitted without any grave threat to comprehension that I have found.If you are able to get past the game mechanics, I think there is enough here for the player to enjoy about the game, but if you (like me) tend to feel that the wrong type of game mechanics interfere with enjoyment and play-though, you might consider giving this one a pass.

Overall, I think Watch Dogs is a worthwhile title.  It takes different approach from the typical FPS shoot-em-ups that seems to dominate console games anymore, with the hacking aspect taking over for at least some of the gunplay.We already had a copy of Watch Dogs for the PC, and it was pretty clear that the PS3 graphics suffer in comparison - resolution and clarity suffer.  But since I'm comparing this game on a modern PC with an NVidia GTX graphics card vs an eight year old console, I really can't penalize the PS3 version too much.  Recommended.

What's the deal with all the open-world sandbox games with "dogs" in the title lately? Sleeping Dogs, Watch Dogs, what's gonna be next? Eating Dogs, Walking Dogs, Lap Dogs, Hot Dogs?Anyway, Watch Dogs is fun if you like sandbox games. Don't look for a lot of innovative gameplay or a radically new take on the genre. With the exception of invasive multi-player (more about that below), it's a mashup of a lot of stuff that has come before it.In video game math, we can say:Watch Dogs = Grand Theft Auto + Deus Ex + Max Payne(free roaming, multiple ways to beat missions, a super slo-mo powerup, lots of guns)Watch Dogs = Grand Theft Auto + Heavy Rain + Lizbeth Salander + Edward Snowden(gang warfare, a dark, disturbing, voyeuristic tone, hacking, conspiracies, NSA-type surveillance)Watch Dogs = Grand Theft Auto + Clockwork Orange + the Untouchables(carjacking, ultraviolence, Chicago)So if any of that turns your head, you'll probably dig Watch Dogs. Or if experiencing a deviant dystopia that is influenced by Orwell, Kafka, andGaitskillsounds cool, you'll like Watch Dogs.The feature that seems to have received the most hype is the persistent and invasive multi-player. You don't have to launch a special multi-player mode to have other, REAL people enter into your game. Unless you're involved in a mission, another player can try to hack you or tail you at any time. I've never been big into multi-player gaming so I can't say this makes or breaks Watch Dogs for me...but I do think it's an interesting way to keep the game constantly changing and challenging for everybody. The online car racing, on the other hand, is exactly like it is in other driving games. As usual, knowing the courses and their shortcuts throughly is the key to succeeding.Ubisoft could have done a few things better. First, the load times are atrocious on PlayStation3. Every time you die or fail a mission, it's a long wait for the game to reset itself. This takes you out of the game and breaks up the flow. The only game that was worse for this is Stuntman. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the same studio, Reflections, was involved in developing both games! Second, again possibly related to Reflections, driving is kind of a pain. Pretty much every vehicle is hard to control because of floaty, super squirrely, or unresponsive handling. Finally, the story and character development doesn't rise above typical videogame level. While the writing in Watch Dogs is no better or worse than in most games, Ubisoft could have taken more care with such a highly promoted, Triple-A release. None of these are showstoppers, though.Bottom line: Watch Dogs is a fun and, thanks to current events, highly topical game. It might make you paranoid as well. Four stars.

I guess you could say I’m a fan of UBI Soft games as I’ve played almost all of theAssassin’s Creedgames and just finished playingFar Cry 3.  The games I’ve played use a definite formula created by UBI Soft.  Assassin’s Creed is an open world concept where mapped areas are unlocked during game play, the map becomes visible after climbing tall structures for an eagle’s nest view, and treasure chests, feathers, and flags are hidden throughout the land to be found.  In Far Cry 3, another open world concept where mapped areas are unlocked during game play, the map becomes visible after climbing and reactivating radio towers, plus crates, relics, and lost letters are hidden throughout the land to be found.  What makes the game play interesting isn’t the formula, but the richly created worlds and the combat actions.Watch Dogs by UBI Soft, is yet another game set in a rich and interesting world.  My first impression is that Watch Dogs is similar to the GTA franchise, except far more tedious.  The protagonist uses a cell phone to hack into security systems, stop lights, other cell phones, and more for the purpose of stealing money or finding criminals to fight.  Map areas become open to information by hacking cell towers, songs can be taken from other’s cell phones, and mini games are found everywhere.  While the formula mentioned above is used, it’s somewhat difficult to recognize.  A good portion of the single player game is driving around the city at fast speeds.The premise of the single player game is interesting.  Hacking into the electronic world around us to accomplish tasks may be the future.  Seeing facts about the automated people in the game somehow makes them feel more real.  Plus money is easy to acquire through hacking ATMs and draining people’s bank accounts through their cell phones.I am finding this game to be so tedious and frustrating.  I am not good at driving at high speeds in games.  While getting from point A to point B isn’t so much of an issue, there are many timed destinations where one must be skillful or repeatedly complete the challenge until it’s met.  I can’t seem to get the weapon system down, so instead of interesting fights, I just die while struggling to figure out what I’m doing.  I guess it doesn’t help I just finished Far Cry 3 before jumping into this game and none of the controls are remotely similar.  The fact is, a few hours into this game and I hate it.Watch Dogs by UBI Soft has an interesting and creative premise.  If I could figure out the controls and actually accomplish something, the game might be fun.  However all I am is frustrated.  If you’re looking for an alternative to GTA and are good at high speed driving, perhaps this game is for you.PROS:Creative premiseInteresting hacking abilitiesCONS:Tedious and frustratingConfusing controls
