XBOX OneFirst, let me say that I'm a mid 40's Grandfather of 6 and I don't really care whatconsole gets you excited as this is just my opinion and personally, I have reasons why I like and own both of them.ENGINEERING AND DESIGNMicrosoft went with a more traditional look (This was not rushed as it was just one of 75 versions of the Xbox One)  with the Xbox One but, their choice of size favored functionality.  With the Xbox One, the power brick is separate so it has less heat in the casing and the Heat Sync is pretty large so it is able to dissipate heat much more effectively thanks to it's design.There's potential here for MS to overclock the hardware thanks to the design of the system and the ridiculous amount of Cache (Cache is very high speed memory internal to the APU) on the APU (APU=GPU+CPU all in one chip) mean less bottle necks between the CPU Cores and the GPU (Inside the APU).I would give this a 4.5 as they could have done better with the looks but, I'm very pleased the console will not over heat (Some PS4 customers are already complaining that their console strobes a redlight and has to cool down before they can use it again, I should note, my PS4 has not done this).CONTROLEverybody loves the Xbox controllers and most see the improved features as a pleasing but minor improvement.  I don't really see this as a benefit because, why improve on something most people found so close to perfect?One thing I like about the MS Controllers, they use letters!  Letters are so engrained into our lives it is much easier for me to remember those patterns where shapes have been there since we were kids but, they were never put into any chronological order so, you literally have to create a pattern in your mind to remember them by (this has always been odd for me with my PS Vita, PSP, PS2, and PS3 before my PS4 and maybe it is just me that finds this harder).Now, as for Kinect and the voice commands...  These commands can work awesome assuming nobody else is talking!  As soon as people in the room or on TV start talking (really makes it a challenge to control your TV shows and probably why Siri has not yet made an appearance on Apple TV), you can throw everything out the window and you pretty much have to wait for them to stop talking because the Xbox is easily confused at this point!  Also, MS not having some method of preventing gamers in online games from executing commands on your system so, that's another flaw...  Of course the biggest issue is that Xbox: On just never works and most have found this to be true (Somebody believes it is firmware corruption but, I've yet to confirm this be restoring my system from an offline source).What's good about the kinect is that there are multiple commands (about 50 or so) that allow input and when they work, they're awesome!  Moving around the console with them works very well and that gives me hope but, MS needs to create an Alias that we call the system to issue these commands to prevent trolling!Due to the issues with Kinect, I have to knock the otherwise great controls down to a 4 because everything else works well.***UPDATE***Kinect has improved a ton with the February update and it no longer gets crazy confused when the TV is on or others are talking.  Xbox on, is the one command that gives me trouble still.LAUNCH GAMESDead Rising 3 -Might be the best game on the system with very cool graphics (not the best on either system but, very solid), solid game play, creative ideas, and a good story to boot!  This actually might be the best game on either of the next gen systems and pretty handily beats both of Sony's exclusives with little effort, in most areas.FORZA 5 -This is a very nice racing sim that suffers from the fact that there are only 200 cars and 15 tracks.  Of course those issues are compounded by the fact that Microsoft had plenty of premium DLC for sale on launch day!  Right now, this is probably the 2nd best Next Gen Exclusive and Microsoft has both of the top two exclusives but, they got a big pass here because Sony didn't have the foresight to have GT6 ready for their PS4 (This was a pretty dumb move by Sony) otherwise, this wouldn't have been so highly rated.  Also, the fact that you have to race the entire first five races in an unmodded car, so you can build your drivatar is very annoying.RYSE -At first glance, this resembles the game play of Assassin's creed except, you're using a Roman soldier instead of some time traveling killer.  The story, while not historically accurate is actually pretty good!  The graphics in my opinion are clearly superior to anything else that launched with either console in this generation (Yes I've played Killzone: Shadow Fall).  Also, the game play has 21 very tough levels and I never found it repetitvd but, what I did find was that this was my favorite launch title.Killer Instict -If you remember the SNES days when fighting games like Street Fighter 3 were all the rage, then you no doubt remember the SNES exclusive launch title of the same name.  Back in the day, Killer Instinct had revolutionary graphics for a home console and it truly was a title worth buying the console for.  This time around, the graphics are still pretty impressive but, they're not revolutionary and with the  limited game play, it makes for a decent fighter that is shown up quickly by Injustice on the PS4.  The good news though?  This is a free to play game with big limitations.Unlike the PS4, I would give the Xbox Launch titles a 4.5 because they not only have the three best launch titles, they also have more exclusive launch titles that are fresh ideas even if they don't always deliver what was expected.XBOX LIVE GOLDUnfortunately, Microsoft charges for everything you do online with their consoles...  If you want to watch Amazon Instant Video, Netflix, or Hulu Plus, you're going to have to have an Xbox Live membership and while that's pretty lame, it isn't like most gamers don't already have the feature.Another downside to this service, you can't even setup the Xbox OneGuide without having this membership and that makes using it to control your TV even more of a pain!The upside here is that Microsoft has put together the best network out of the three game console makers and not only is the network very quick, you will almost never see the thing go down!  Also, they control the servers and the content so, refunds for bad games or in app purchases go through Microsoft instead of chasing down some random 3rd party dev with an attitude.Another plus, the network does work for every account on your system and all features work for all accounts.Sony has a lot to learn here from Microsoft and I would rate this feature a 4.5 with a hit for the XBLG One Guide requirement as you can't set it up without the service but, once it is setup, it works fine even if Live expires.INTERFACEIf you used Windows 8 then the interface for the Xbox One is very familiar to you.  While this isn't an exact copy of the Windows 8 start screen, it is very close.  Overall, it is fairly easy to use where only pinned items appear on the start screen and apps are kept in the apps folder, videos kept in the videos folder, Pictures, Movies, and the like all have their places as well.The Start screen is broken up into 3 sections.  Pins, Home, and Store.  Stuff isn't automatically added so it never really gets any larger but, there's quite a bit there and I wish it were more customizable but, only what I want pinned is actually pinned so, I'm at least happy about that.The biggest downside here is that the interface isn't complete.  There really is no way to see storage or battery life.***UPDATE***Microsoft added storage management and a battery meter (The battery meter works better than on the PS4) in the February Update!CUSTOMER SERVICETo me, Microsoft has always handled customers with kid gloves!  They know, you don't treat your customers right and they will find somebody who will treat them better.With the Xbox 360 I had numerous issues with my launch console but, Microsoft too care of everything without even the slightest bit of hesitation.  If I had an issue with a game, MS dealt with it!  If it was hardware or services, MS dealt with it!  There were no repeat calls or you'll need to contact x or y company for this issue!  Nope MS Owns all levels of customer service for their platform!Customer service at MS is always top notch so I would rate this as a 5!MISSING FEATURESAgain, both the PS4 and Xbox One are missing features but, I'm tired of hearing how the Xbox One is incomplete when comparing lists it is clear, the PS4 might be missing more things than the Xbox One (You can see these in my PS4 review).*No YouTube uploading (live drive makes uploading to other sources, via PC, possible)*No Social Media Support built in (Apps might come but, they're not there yet)*No Support for 3D Bluray*No Netflix, Hulu+, Amazon Instant Video, or Hulu+ without Xbox Live Gold membershipCONCLUSIONI keep hearing people say, the Xbox One isn't a complete product and I agreed with that assessment.  My real issue with this is that the PS4 isn't really a complete product either and singling out the one console without calling out the other is pretty lame!  Also, Microsoft has fixed every complaint that people have had with the Xbox One and Sony has yet to even Address a single issue with their console.With the Xbox, I at least have a decent browser, youtube, and upload of game DVR footage to a cloud so I can pull it up on my PC and use it with whatever sharing service I want.I also appreciate the fact that they didn't integrate social networking in the console but, I'm not sure everyone feels that way.To me, MS put unfinished features into the system and Sony omitted standard features because they weren't finished but, both equate to unfinished consoles!Now, with all that said, I find the Xbox One to be a very pleasant surprise and I'm not disappointed with the console in the least!DESIGN  = 4.5CONTROL  = 4.5LAUNCH GAMES  = 4.5XBOX LIVE  = 4.5INTERFACE = 4.5CUSTOMER SERVICE  = 5TOTAL  = 4.6I get this isn't the most powerful console on the market but, it wins in just enough of the aesthetics that it really is a more well rounded system overall and I'm just generally more impressed with their desire to deliver on every level even if they do miss the mark on some features.For me, this is the better of the two launch consoles right now but, anything can change.  There are a lot of people who want to judge these on a specs sheet but, that really doesn't mean a console will be better, it just means the hardware is a little stronger and that doesn't always mean it will be more fun!

So I like most had no intention of even giving Microsoft a chance. I got my PS4 and am happy with it. However I on a whim decided to give MS a chance. It's nice to be able to be watching tv and immediately jump into any game I have loaded in the disc slot or on the HDD. The ability to turn on my tv, cable box, and console with a simple push of my controllers button or with my voice when I come in from work is nice.The games look great also and run well. I have decided to go all digital on my Xbox One this generation and it's been fun. Every game at my fingertips. No fussing with cases etc.At the same time blu-ray playback is fine. It's bare bones but I don't really care because I just want to watch the movies.Now the downsides:Kinect voice control is 50/50 at best. I've gone out of my way to set it up properly and yet only half the time does it still recognize what I'm saying. It's just faster to use a controller most of the time. This brings me to another complaint. Microsoft for the love of god please release a media remote for this console. Sure I can use my controller but this isn't as good as having a media remote would be.The install times for games before you can even play them is a bit on the long side. With PS4 I can play a game after a couple minutes. With the Xbox One it can take 30 minutes plus before I can start a game and then I can't play some parts of it. This is one area MS needs to improve. At the same time the menus and operating system of the console takes some steps back. Everything is basically an app within the OS. This results in a very clunky experience. I click to go into friends and I get a loading screen. I click to go to messages and get a loading screen. I click to go to the store and loading screen. Seeing a trend here? Also I would like to see notifications when friends come on and go offline. This simply isn't there.  It isn't all bad though. I do like how MS allows you to pin the apps and games you want to a section right to the left of the home screen. They however need to work on a way to sort it. As it is now that is very clunky. It's like with the 360 where you move an item to the front. It's in a square grid though. I'd like to be able to sort from left to right in alphabetical order. Instead it has items up and down from right to left.The last thing is that there is absolutely no option to sign you in automatically without Kinect and no management of your storage on the console.Overall though the console is a good console and I've had a lot of fun with mine. I just hope that MS can make some improvements to their OS. I'm honestly glad I bought the console and have no problem eating crow.

Just received my new system, and so far it's pretty good.  Just some quick notes:Updates  - I have to say, this is such a weird part of modern gaming.  I remember the excitement of getting all of my previous systems, plugging them in, putting in a game, and enjoying my brand new game console.  With this console (just like my Wii U) instead of this happening, when I fired up the system, I immediately had to update the system which took about a half hour (at 6Mb/s).  When it was finally able to start, I began exploring a bit.  I decided to download all the things which make the system work.  Things like CD and DVD functions were not standard apps and had to be downloaded.  Then I decided to download the free Kinect Sports preseason.  It took several hours, so I went to bed.A few days later, I received RYSE, which I rented, and excited to play that game, popped it in.  To my dismay, the game needed a 3 GB update.  Once again, I went to bed waiting for it to download.I guess it's a double-edged sword.  It's great that they are still taking the time to perfect things, but it's kind of a drag.  I can imagine how frustrated kids must get waiting to finally use their system.Pros - That being said, I really like my new system.  It feels familiar, yet also feels very modern.  The interface with the Kinect is cool.Kinect - So many people look down on this feature, but I'm glad they made it a standard part of the system.  Although not perfect, I think it's really impressive technology.  You can scroll with gestures, use voice commands and I can only hope that some developers will get creative with it.  Playing Kinect Sports was fun.The motor is gone inside of this generation's Kinect, so you'll have to adjust it by hand.  It almost seems like a step down, but once it's in place, you won't have to move it, so it's not that big of a deal.  They've also added a heat sensor to the Kinect which can measure heart beat, and body temperature when you are doing things like exercising.  As you work out, it will show which muscles are being used.  I have to admit, it's kind of weird knowing that a camera is watching you in your living room all the time though.  It's kind of Orwellian.Home screen - It has a Windows 8 Live Tile experience.  You can move things around, pin things to specific places, etc.Internet - it's cool to have on the system for favorites, but if you want to search for something unique, the Kinect voice function won't work for in the search engine, leaving you to have to use the controller to type it in.  Since this is so tedious, it's just easier to pick up the laptop or phone and search what you are looking for.Controller -  it' similar to the old one, but it feels smoother.  I like it.  the rumble pack is subtler.Games - So far I've just played RYSE.  It had some good graphics, but I don't obsess over frame rates and polygon counts, so all I can say is it looked good to me.  I do like the fact that you can easily go back between the game and the home screen.  There are not a lot of games out right now, but I'm glad that people clamored to keep the discs.  I like buying cheap games or renting them.TV, Apps, etc. - while I was curious about all the things included, the truth is I probably won't use most of the stuff.  I already have Netflix, Spotify, etc. so I don't see myself buying a bunch of stuff through their store, which I know MS would love most people to do.  I do like the fact that I can now Skype from my TV.  The only problem, as many people have noted, is that you need to maintain your Gold membership to do all of this.The Look - I don't know...it's a little boxy, kind of forgettable and fades into the background.All-in-All - I like it.  It seems like each iteration of a system there are so many heated opinions, some even saying that the console era is dead, and there's always the casual vs. hardcore gamer arguments being made.  Personally, I like consoles because they're standard.  Yes the technology stays in place for several years, but you know the games will work on them.  I like popping in a  disc, sitting on the couch with a controller and playing a game.As far as the "casual" aspect of the system, I kind of think people are missing one big point.  There are a lot of people who would like the casual aspects of the XBOX.  Fun party games, being able to work out with the Kinect counting calories, and all the other functions are what might bring more people to like game consoles.  And the thing is, the gaming is still at the center of the system, so you can be hardcore and play.  So if you like these aspects of a game console, I'd say you won't be disappointed.

I've had Xbox consoles since the very beginning. And when the original Xbox Live service became available, I subscribed as well. Since then, I've seen these consoles evolve (in both good and bad ways.) After all the rumors circulated before this console launched, I was a cautious. After buying it, I don't regret it, but it's very far from a perfect machine.The good:-Games look great-Ability to route Cable TV through the console is cool-When Kinect works, it's cool-The controllers are very nice-Apps (although seems like everything is loaded with apps nowadays)-Console isn't too bad to navigate-Quiet (relatively)-Microsoft Development Team seems to actually pay somewhat attention to what people don't like (they changed the "always on connection, changed party chat functions around, changed the friend panel, etc.) Some could say these things shouldn't be broken to begin with (I agree), but at least feedback is making changes.-Easy hookup-Watching Netflix, Hulu, or TV while playing games is amazingThe Bad:-Expensive, especially against the PS4-Lack of game variety (hope you like first person shooters)-Server problems have been annoying.-Buggy (party chat errors, game crashes, random things activate Kinect, etc)-Mine attracts dust like a magnet. It's literally always dirty-Headsets and Headset adapters :-Headsets hookup via a wireless adapter to the controller. The controller projects the sound to the headset. This is a very buggy and annoying way of doing things. When using a headset, my controller / headset will glitch out and require pulling the battery pack out to correct.-Xbox Live is no where near as smooth or polished as the 360.Other thoughts:Anyone considering the jump to the latest console should look closely at the game library available. The Xbox in particular is top dollar and has a select few games to play. If you're a die-hard adventure game player or RPG player, there isn't much for you (yet). Also, anyone buying this console expecting perfection is going to be very disappointed. I've had this console since week one, and there seems like every day there's some new hiccup that crops up. The upside to this is these problems are far fewer than launch week. With every patch, this system gets better. And the Xbox Fitness (going to be additional yearly fee after 2015) has the potential to be amazing (if you're into that sort of thing)Anyone on the fence should look objectively at whats available, what they want the console to do, and whether or not they can wait. At $500, it's hard to recommend this console to casual gamers (especially if they don't have cable, Netflix, Hulu, etc). I think anyone who waits will be rewarded handsomely with a less buggy, larger library of games, and hopefully cheaper system.

I'm writing this a couple months after the Xbox One launched, and you only buy a game console for one purpose right now --> ambition & the likelihood it will reach those ambitions.  You rarely need to buy a game console for the games this early on (they take a while to get a good selection) and even the revolutionary NUI & media features could probably wait for a price drop.The point is ambition....vision.....what they are building, and the Xbox One slays all competitors in this area.  The Xbox Team has released a system here that is designed for the next decade, with a full fledged NUI (voice, gesture, etc) and cloud processing built into the cost of the system/service.The only competitors close to this are Sony, with the PS4, who are playing catch up with the Xbox 360 (providing solid peer-to-peer gaming, for a price) and building in 'me-too' NUI features as a (rarely purchased/supported) add on.  Valve's Steam box also deserves a mention, and could very well rewrite all the rules 2 or 3 years down the road.  The Steam box will benefit from not relying on a traditional game console life cycle, but will also take longer to reach maturity.So, the Xbox One stands alone....but what does it do that's so special?1.  Next generation graphics.  While this is typically used as the key metric of every new game console, it is probably the least exciting part of what will come out in this round of the video game consoles.  You had near photo-realism in the last generation, and it's just diminishing returns from there on out.  The important thing is that the Xbox One is designed for and has all the power needed for modern TV's -- 1080p resolution.  It will be stressed for 4k resolutions, but those aren't going to be a meaningful part of the market till well into the lifecycle.2.  NUI (Natural User Inteface).  When the IPhone came out I said (along with many others) that I'd never use a phone without a physical keyboard.  Times change, and gesture/multitouch/voice recognition technology will only improve as the machines & software on them learn to react to us better.  The voice control on Xbox One isn't perfect, but it's more than good enough and is guaranteed to get better.  It will feel odd using it, at first, and soon it will feel odd that any device doesn't make voice commands available.In a quasi-gaming sense, the only way I've used the Kinect features is for Xbox Fitness and this is a far better system than anything in the past.  It reads your pulse on sight and the movement detection is clearly a solid generation ahead of the first Kinect.  Developers still haven't nailed the formula for gaming right, but it took 30 years to get game controllers to the level they've reached, so it will probably take a few more years to find a killer app for the Kinect features in gaming.3.  Hyper-V, Media and Apps too.  Switch from Skyrim to Netflix in the Xbox 360 and it means shutting down the game and turning on Netflix (and a lag between each).  Want to switch between gaming and TV?  Find the right remote then.  The problem is that this isn't how life works, and the Xbox One manages to be a powerful & fast multitasking media hub.  It relies on something called Hyper-V in the background which solves the first problem (game to media app) -- so that transition happens in seconds and the transition back to the game you were playing happens just as fast.  Want to do two things at the same time?  Maybe not, because the apps aren't there yet to make this worthwhile -- but it doesn't take a great deal of vision to see how useful snapping apps/other media to the side will be.Here again, the Xbox One is pushing the edge.  No other system can match these features, and while the commands & implementation are not perfect, they are more than good enough at the moment & guaranteed to improve.4.  The Cloud.  The cloud is nebulous, because unlike other modern technological innovations, like the IPhone or tablet computers -- you never really see it.  Still, it's something that has slowly been invading our world -- we rely on it for email (gmail, Hotmail, etc), storing pictures and even playing games (WoW, etc).  Over the next decade more and more people will move to Fiber connections and the economies of scale doing processing in the cloud will explode, but even now that power can be harnessed for games.The Xbox One is the first and only console designed to take advantage of the cloud, and I think this is going to revolutionize gaming more than any other element over the next decade.  Microsoft, unlike other competitors in gaming hardware, has a completely unfair advantage in this area because of their investment in building Azure.  This is a network of billion dollar facilities around the world with more processing power than you can imagine.  How will it revolutionize gaming?  It will do this simply because it will make things possible that were never possible before.  Here are some examples:-- Project Spark.  Is a very high level visual programming tool for games that is built in the cloud, which will allow anybody to create every game they can imagine - and play it anywhere.-- TitanFall (and, likely, many imitators to follow).  Moves the Call of Duty formula to the next level, utilizing cloud based AI to make every person in a multiplayer game feel like the hero.-- Minecraft for the Xbox One.  Creates persistent worlds, where many people can login at any time, together or alone, and modify a shared world of their creation.This is the leading edge of a revolution in gaming, and the things listed above are not fully possible on any other platform.TL;DR / Summary:  The best reason to buy a console early on is for its ambition and likelihood of meeting those goals.  The Xbox One is by far the most ambitious console and Microsoft is better placed than anyone to meet those goals.  This system will do revolutionary things in its lifetime that no other system can match anytime soon, and it moves the standard/out-of-box technology of gaming systems ahead farther than any system in the last 30 years.

As with anything, there are good, bad, and really bad things about this device. Before you immediately dismiss this as 'he's a fanboy', understand that my FIRST (owned) console was a PS2, last generation, I owned both, two of them even, as the first was ripped off, and put a LOT more miles on the 360 than I ever did the tired old PS3. Just couldn't enjoy the PS3 as much.That said, on to the One review. While I understand that some of this may be just the same with the PS4, that's not the product I'm reviewing here. I may (if I purchase the PS4) write a review for it, but at this time I'm not doing so.Firstly, I do  understand that this is a new product. That said, things will inevitably change, and hopefully for the better..The good:The system is a 'next gen' system, making gaming a completely different experience. For example, no longer am I stuck waiting for a 'save point' to exit the game. With this device, it's simply possible (as long as I'm in a safe spot) to go to the home menu, turn it off, and I'm right back where I want to be when I log back in.Speaking of logging in, Kinect recognition in is a good thing, when it works. Being an early adapter of the Kinect (v1), I was impressed with how well it worked, and how they actually got it to work well enough on the 360. I'm still on the fence about how well the 'update' works, however, so I'll keep that for a later time.Being a next gen system, the graphics and audio on this thing are just great, better than, honestly. They are miles above the previous generation.One central location for most of your TV and media:Having finally gotten around to hooking TiVo into the One, and exploring the BRD app, I have to say, this is a pretty decent feature. Frees up an HDMI slot from the stereo/TV (not that it'll control the stereo), and makes it a good bit easier to watch TV/Movies. Not badThe bad:Forced installs and 'motion control' are two reasons that I left the PS3 in the dust. Guess what's back on the One? Forced installs, and at least a semblance of motion control. I cannot STAND that garbage, but it's there.The UI appears to need some work (read: a good deal of it), but they're aware of that and they know it needs to be updatedThere's not a ton of AAA titles out right now for it, but, again, that's what I get for being an early adopter. Not complaining, just saying it's a bad thing (as well for the PS4).In order for the Kinect to function properly, apparently, you have to sit right in front of it. Not off to the side, etc. This was noticed when playing Dead Rising 3, and the whole controller motion thing came into play. Assuming, of course that relies on the Kinect. Sitting to the side, doesn't work so much. Standing right in front of it? Yup, that did it.No BR-3D , but I knew that. Not a complaint, just a 'bad' thing . They're rumored to be working on it.The ugly:Probably the UGLIEST part of this system (and with the PS4) right now is the forced install, and updates. Seriously, 40+ gig for Ryse, 20+ for Dead Rising. With just 4 games installed (2 downloadable), I'm at 20% space used. I don't know WHAT'S going to happen if I actually get the collection as high as my 360 collection is (100+ games), because that's going to just be a disaster.Sure, some of that's on the devs, but forcing a game install is just a bad, bad thing.No external storage (yet) makes this even worse. We don't know what they're planning on doing about it, but eventually fans are going to get extremely upset when enough AAAs come out that their drive is just massively filled up. Bad Microsoft! At least Sony is allowing drive upgrades (as with the PS3), though, that's going to be a problem there as well, since you can only upgrade so far ;)Overall? A decent system. I enjoy it, but it's a good bit of a letdown as well. Here's hoping that they'll fix what needs to be fixing in an efficient time frame.

The scale of FIFA 14 is immense.  There are a whopping 631 teams in the game, including 47 "International" teams which you can use to recreate World Cup play (USA, Brazil, England, etc.).  There's a roster of 272 "Free Agents," and an in-depth Create-A-Player you can use to fill in the gaps.  If you were like me, watching the 2014 World Cup group play and thinking about2006 FIFA World Cup - PCor a past FIFA experience, FIFA 14 is a must-have at its current $18-20 price tag.There are two ways to go about getting FIFA 14.  You either get the online game code from Amazon, or from Origin, EA's gaming client.  I bought the digital deluxe version of FIFA 14 from Origin directly, and the cost was $24.99.  The download included 1,575 FIFA Points (FP), which are used ONLY for FIFA 14's featured game mode, FIFA Ultimate Team (FUT).  You don't need FP to play FUT, but it sure helps.From what I've read and experienced, FUT is nothing but a money sink, but I wanted to try it out anyway (hence the purchase of the deluxe edition).  It's fun, but at the end of the day you need to keep your players going by obtaining contracts every 13 games, per player, for a 23-man roster.  The frustration adds up.  Everything else about the mode is fun, and there are over 200,000 live transfers available from the online community right now, but needing to obtain player contracts is tedious busy work.  I would only play FUT if you are willing to spend an inordinate amount of time doing things other than playing games.  It's a beautiful single-player experience (or entirely online experience if you want it) enhanced by an online community, but that also means you need Internet connectivity at all times to make the mode work.Anyway, and thankfully, while FUT feels like a Facebook game on steroids at times (I can't tell you how many hours I clocked into the Madden card game on Facebook), you don't need to play FUT to have fun.  Navigating the menu might take some time, as well as the controls (I still dread penalty kicks and the like as I have no idea how to operate the goalie), the UI will grow on you over time.  I use an XBOX controller for PC and it works great.  It even has the ability to skip songs via the "Back" button.  On that note, be sure to Google how to change what tracks play, as it's confusing at first, and half the songs are skippable.  I'm in the process of finding out how to replace a lot of them, or add my own, which seems like an easy enough fix.

Before I criticize them too much, the story is decent and like I said it is pretty much everything Indiana Jones didn't do (as far as myths and legends)Story:- Can't tell if it's the same Quartermain from League of Extraordinary Gentlemen or somewhere random (seems rather cliched for an adventurer's last name). Basically you and some branch of the government of USA are searching for the Heart of Atlantis. The heart is scattered in pieces and you have to get them before the Germans do. (Takes place around WW1/WW2)Pros:- The story is somewhat original and a fresh take on an old legend.- The atmosphere and level design is very realistic and well done. (The game uses Unreal Graphics engine)- Enhanced the flashlight part of gameplay from Alan Wake (still feel as though they ripped it off, but it's a little bit better to control)- The actual length of the game is rather the perfect amount, not too short and not neverending.- When you first start out the controls suck, but you then realize that you actually gradually get better based off of treasure you find in the levels. (A more realistic approach to a first-person shooter, as no one is ever good at anything in the beginning)- The collectibles actually pertain to the game (helps you enhance your character)Cons:- While the story is decent, the dialogue is the most cliched dialogue for any adventure story ever.- I feel they ripped off a lot of controls and concepts from more successful games.- For a game that has a puzzle difficulty option, the difficulty doesn't effect the puzzles (which aren't that hard on the hardest difficulty), but rather the clues the game gives you.- For a game the is linear progression there is a lot of empty space.- Things that you can use in the environment aren't obvious.- Not much of a tutorial.- The multiplayer is pretty much Call of Duty: Black Ops, except no one is online either (which like half the achievements revolve around online play). Or it is like Call of Duty Zombies mode.Other:- I got 550G on one playthrough on the hardest difficulty (wasn't hard at all).- Like I said no one is ever playing online so it's sort of pointless.It's up to you to decide whether you want it or not. You could almost call this an imitation FPS version of Uncharted, right down to the hero that's rough around the edges, girl that's book smart, and old man team.  Same kind of environments, same kind of enemies (plus mummies), same kind of puzzles, same kind of notebook, etc.  The compass is a good touch but it slows you down more than it helps you.  The treasures are pretty easy to find without it anyway.  My biggest problem with it has got to be the controls and overall movement.  The controls aren't very fluid, even with the sensitivity cranked up, and your player is kind of sluggish.  Being able to jump is just a joke because you can only jump about an inch (not much of an exaggeration) from the ground and it's never really even required.  It's more of an annoyance because half of the time that you are trying to select an item, you end up jumping instead.  That's mainly because the A button is used for both actions and you have to be decently spot-on to select an item.  There's somewhat of a variety of weapons, at least their names are different, but most of the assault rifles look and perform much the same.  The sniper rifles have varied zoom aspects and the handguns vary mainly by clip size.  At this point, the game is selling for less than $20 so it's not too bad of a purchase if you're trying to squeeze the last few drops out of your Xbox 360 before you bite the bullet and get an Xbox One.  If you've got plenty of games to play already, you may want to pass this one up.

It doesn't bring me any joy to write a semi-bad review on a part of a series I have enjoyed a lot over the years; 'Tides of War' still remains one of my all time favorite FPS's, and 'Wolfenstein' was a nice surprise.  I suppose my main complaint w/this one(besides the terribly wimpy gun sounds...)is the lack of tension, a sense of real purpose, and a huge feeling of just going the motions at times; There is a considerable lack of fear in wondering what is around every corner here, and the many of the objectives of 'find the switch and pull it' grow tiresome; I generally found the characters not very engaging, and it was hard to care about what happened to who. This was one of those games that I finished by telling myself every night 'maybe it will get better...' until it was over; On a good note, it does pick up a lot near the last part of the game, and the fact that I still played thru it should show my faith in the series, even if it was just for a great last quarter of the game.That being said, everything graphically/technically is amazing and smooth; some of the best moments come from the cut scenes, and the creative storyline had so much potential; and while there are a few bright spots here and there, I would have to say it was very average to me; I am open to changes in a franchise, but this one seemed to still belong in castles...lol. Sure, throw in the robots too(another impressive element of 'the New Order''), but the futuristic 60's didn't do it for me personally. And the music of the last few games was so much more menacing than here; it sounds nice and very professional, but seems more like a movie score and doesn't really always help the game out. To me, this is a game that had all the tools it needed from A-Z to make a spectacular game, but just got lazy on everything but the drive and intensity of the game; you never have a firefight w/more than 12 soldiers it seems like, and there are no surprises of soldiers stampeding out of nowhere for some shoot-outs, and the hardest things to kill are the robots, which often just seems like something too familiar and semi-poorly done intensity rise(it seems more like a chore than something fun...). I personally thought games like 'Rainbow 6: Vegas', 'Bioshock 1 & 2', and 'BLACK'(even though they are all older games)were much more complete and effective in creating a more menacing and unpredictable experience; I know they are all semi-different games, but they all had a purpose in mind, and some pulled it off much more successfully than others...Again, this isn't a horrible game, but just not what I had hoped I guess. I can't fault the thought and technical efforts that went into this project in any way; I was just hoping for more of a well rounded, involving experience that didn't always feel like an exercise in video game mechanics or sound/graphical presentation. You could do a lot worse, but i still put my $ on 'Tides of War'...

Let's cut to the chase: the game play is mediocre at best.  Here is where The New Order really let's gamers down.  The guns do not sound realistic or special.  Handling weaponry is awkward and unsatisfying most of the time.  To add insult to injury, they give you the opportunity to dual-wield weapons that are already inaccurate.  Bullet contact sounds pathetic.  It is surprising that in this day and age, after games like COD have gotten it right, The New Order fails here!There are a lot of unexpected obstacles in each map that prevent fluid movement, climbing, etc.  Also, the AI is pretty stupid.  Sometimes stealth works because Nazi's do not ever turn.  Sometimes stealth cannot work because enemies see you no matter what you do.  This makes game play uneven and disheartening, so you often just charge into a fray blazing.While most of the game is way too dark, a lot of its environments and character models and robots are very well-done.  The game is a lot of fun to look at, so you assume the game play is going to rock.  Nope.  It falls flat often.When the best part of the game is the series of cut-scenes, you have to ask yourself if you just wasted a lot of money.Well, overall, The New Order is a DECENT shooter with nice graphics and a good soundtrack.  Combat is lackluster much of the time.  If this had been released 7 years ago, I'd say it was amazing.  But a lot of great games have been made since then.  The game-makers should have paid attention.Better, more realistic shooters/gun combat games to check out: Hitman: Absolution, COD series, Fallout, Assassin's Creed series,  The Witcher series, or even Dishonored.

Wolfenstein was the first FPS game that I played way back in the DOS days. For this new one, the good news: The graphic is awesome. The system requirements are not that high, I was able to nearly max out with no lag throughout the game. The weapons are very well design, you can tell it's from an ID game. All the weapons look cool when shooting. The weapon sounds are okay, but not close to being as good as BF4. There is a story that is not so bad, but far from great. While I really enjoyed this game, there is nothing beyond the simple campaign. It is basically a run and gun type of game with some aspect of stealth. There are slow, boring moments in the game, and you can feel it, but that is what you get when mixing an old type of gameplay with a story-driven one. While you can carry as many weapons as you want, the ammunition is so limited that you can't just use any weapon you want. The gameplay would work great with Doom and maybe Quake, but for a WWII type of game, it is mediocre. You won't find anything revolutionary in this game. The welding gun is nothing special. You can upgrade it to shoot multi-beams, but then you only get to shoot it once, then look for a refill station. Also, why isn't there auto-pickup? Nothing is more annoying than looking down and tapping e to pickup every little thing that drops all over the place, mean while 10 guys are chasing and shooting you. This will keep me from replaying the game. The worst part about this game is the difficulty spike, I was doing well on medium, then suddenly half-way into the game I could barely pass a section even after dying 10 times. I had to switch down to easy-mode to beat the game. Unfortunately unlike the old games, you can't just save anywhere you want, therefore the dumb checkpoint system. I'm guessing the difficulty spike is either a problem with the gameplay mechanics, or the developers are just trying to prolong a short-game by preventing you from beating it. The game is not at all worth the full $60, but at less than half that price, I think it is worth playing through at least once. Compared to FPS like HL2, which introduced physics, has gravity gun, HDR lighting, MODS, personal servers, etc., this new Wolfenstein game offers nothing but a VERY BASIC FPS game. It's ashamed, because the actual run-and-gun aspect in this game is really fun. A few MODs here and there, or multiplayer coop shootouts can turn this game into something that is worth $60. Too bad game companies today are all into that DLC greediness, and DLC are far less exciting than MODs. I'm just saying because $60 is ridiculously high.

Being only 19 years old, I have not been around long enough to be able to participate in the nostalgia that this game could bring to older gamers. I have never played the older Wolfenstein games, so they will not bias my opinion of this game. Let's jump to it!If you have read any of my other reviews, you can probably tell that I'm not hard to please when it comes to games. Sure I have some standards, but for the most part I'll give everything a chance and not completely rule anything out until I've played it. This game does not disappoint by any means.Story: I'm sure you are all familiar with the story at this point, so I'll just give my take on it. It was actually a really engrossing story, and I really enjoyed it. I kept wanting to play the game because I wanted to know what happened next. It had all of the parts that make a good story: action, romance, tough choices, emotion, and best of all, killing nazis. The voice acting was great, and it had great pacing. I completed it in 12.4 hours on the middle difficulty, and I'm going to play through again on the hardest to see how the story is different. There is one point towards the beginning where you have to make a choice, and depending on the choice it will affect your game, so I'm going to play through again on the alternate storyline to see how it differs.Gameplay: Plays like a first person shooter, pretty standard. One thing that I don't like is that most games (to me at least) are easier to play on PC, but this one was a bit more difficult. Running and sliding isn't a major part to this game, but it is required to level up some perks (which I'll explain later), and it's really hard to hold shift to run, W to move forward, and C to slide, all at the same time. I imagine that had I used a controller it would have been easier, so take that into account. I also saw a lot of people complaining that you had to manually pick up ammo, and maybe because it's because I just came from playing Metro 2033 (where you also have to manually pick up ammo), but I say so what? Everyone complains that they want more realistic games, so this one makes it a bit more realistic by having you manually pick up ammunition, and everyone complains at that! There is no pleasing gamers! Lolol.One other quick thing that I also liked was their health system. Your maximum health limit is 100, so if you find a health pack that would put you over that 100, say to 150, your health would go up to 150 on what they called "overcharge", and then slowly deteriorate back down to 100. So you can still pick up health packs that you find along your way, but you can't get completely overpowered and get like 500 health. Your health would only regenerate to the nearest 20 I think, so if you lost health to 54, it would go back up to 60. If you hit 17, it would go back up to 20. (I don't know if it's the nearest 10 or 20, I didn't pay attention that much hahaha.) I also really liked that you really could take either level as stealth, or all out guns blazing. The stealth system was really well done.I keep remembering gameplay aspects I need to add xD Another big complain I heard was about the enemy AI, and how they were basically really dumb. I had probably 2 or 3 spots throughout the entire game where I encountered them acting really weirdly, but for the most part they functioned as they should, taking cover, shooting, trying to flank me, etc.Sound: As I stated before, voice acting was great. I really enjoyed the music in this game, you got into some pretty cool fights and when you did it would start blasting some heavy metal in the background to get you pumped up. I'm not an expert on how guns are supposed to sound, but all of the gun sounds were great. One thing about the voicing that really really really pleased me was that when you went up against most of the enemies, they spoke german. Not a british accent, not english with a german accent, but full on, fluent german. I loved that, because it really helped immerse you in the game. One thing that I actually thought was really funny was that with the subtitles in the game, you can set them to on, off, or just when someone is speaking a foreign language (which is what I had it set to). There's this guy in the beginning that's on your team that speaks English with a Scottish accent. He is in no way not understandable, I could understand him fine, but it still put up subtitles for when he talked. I just thought it was funny that it put up subtitles, even though he was speaking english xDLevel up system: The perks system in this game is quite different than most games, but I actually really enjoyed it. There are 4 skill trees, and instead of having to level up Perk A to get to Perk B, and then Perk B to get to Perk C, each perk had a requirement that you had to complete to unlock it. To get so many kills with a certain weapon, or get a certain amount of stealth takedowns. That way you could work on whatever skill tree you wanted, and whatever perks you wanted to unlock. (If that doesn't make sense, let me know in the comments and I can try and clear it up a little bit hahaha.)Graphics: There was one thing that really bothered me about the graphics. They look great, from far away. But as soon as you get up close to the walls, just as an example, you could see how awful the textures looked. They were 2D, grainy, and just plain gross. I know it's just nitpicking, but hey, that's what reviews are for lol. The game also had cinematic prerendered cutscenes, which only ran in 30 fps, but looked better than the ingame. I don't imagine this game is too terribly taxing, I have a 770 and could max the game out, AA and all. There were some framerate stutters occasionally, but for the most part is was a fluid 60 fps.Dislikes: I had very few dislikes about the game, but one of my big ones I thought was kind of a stretch with the main character. Not giving away any plotpoints, but there was a point where you get stabbed in the stomach, and then after you take the guy down you basically get up and act like it's no big deal, and at one point help boost a guy up to like a ledge. It's like really? If you really got shanked through the stomach with a bowie knife you wouldn't be doing that. One other thing that I didn't care for was the main character. I didn't hate him by any means, but to me he didn't have any believability, or emotion. He was actually really great, until about a fourth of the way through a game, and after that he just kind of clammed up and didn't have any personality. Maybe he's supposed to be that way, I don't know, but it was something I didn't care for.Overall, I was extremely pleased with this game. I had heard great things about it, and I was not disappointed. I got it for $30 on a steam sale, and would have easily paid up to $45 for it. It has a ton of replayability, an awesome story, decent graphics, awesome soundtrack, and as stated previously, best of all? You get to blow apart nazis. :D

The levels get a bit larger and less linear.  And the locations change up quite a bit and become surprising and inspired.More importantly,  I am having 200% more fun with this game than Bioshock Infinite. which was very shiny and pretty, but man was the shooting dull.  With Wolfenstein, you can run and gun or use stealth or at any time use a combo of those. It is an old school FPS, yes, but it has more in common with an FPS like HalfLife, rather than the frenetic shooters where enemies are coming at you all of the time.Easily an 8.5 out of 10 as long as you know this is more a look backward at FPS shooters than anything miraculously new and different.

It's not going to reinvent FPS as we know it like the original, but it is a fun shooter just to sit back and get engrossed in for a while. It plays great on my Asus Republic Of Gamers laptop, at around 60fps with the GTX Nvidia 660m. And even some lesser cards could handle it on Medium to Low settings. I had it on High and it looked great. I wouldn't say graphically it's super intense, but the textures are very very smooth and nice to look at. Bethesda really did their homework and the developers got it right when it game to a really smooth look game. No texture popping, no framerate drops (yet), and the movements are very precise and quick. I was actually very very surprised at this fact.I really only give 3 stars because it just reminds me of a revamped, polished version of Wolfenstein from 2009. Only without the Occult overtones, and a more futuristic almost (Timeshift) type of vibe. Of course with more experiments, gore, and other nasty values Nazi's have been known for. So yes it's much more "vulgar" in a lot of ways. Also it does give you that "Killzone 2" out on the battlefield feel as well. Only with a lot more going on. Picking up armor (helmets), health packs, and ammo all harken back to the FPS's of old, which doesn't really bother me. It's very quick, and responds the instant you go over top of it. The game in general just moves very fast, which is good. Except when you want to cruise, sneak up on people, or just do a little bit of sight seeing, or exploration. Plenty of things to find all around, if you look close enough.Even with the mouse the controls are slick and spot on, and you can get headshots with great ease. The double up guns are pretty cool as well, gives you the old west of the future feel. And by holding down BOTH mouse buttons you can gun down the Nazis like mowing a German lawn. Lots of fun. Other than that, well story wise it's decent, nothing we haven't seen before, except maybe actual things that went on during the holocaust. Which some may find offensive. But I wouldn't say anything is really "over the top", also having giant robots doing unthinkable deeds isn't nearly as bad as humans. For some odd reason. So it's a good game for all consoles, as I've seen and heard. PC is where it all started for FPS so I thought yeah I'll get it for this and reminisce. So a 3.5 would be a bit more fair. I've heard it's a short game, and I think I'm about halfway through, I just know rumors. But if you collects "everything" I'm sure it's a bit longer, than just flying straight through. Move slowly, enjoy your 60 bucks. I think there is enough to do here for some replay value. We'll see.

So New Super Mario Bros. U rekindled my faith in the New Super Mario branch of the franchise with its strong level design and fresh-enough content for a sequel that the 3DS entry wishes it had. This particular installment in the lineup was made for this purpose - To highlight the 20th Anniversary of Luigi. And with that in mind, you'd think Nintendo would make this one even fresher, providing some all-new worlds and environments ideal for Luigi and his abilities helping it give off a unique and interesting experienceOooor it could just be a merely smaller clone/rehash of New Super Mario Bros. U............Unfortunately, we're given the latter. Everything you've seen in NSMBU is present and accounted for, including the worlds, bosses, etc. You even get the same cutscenes and sequences on the maps! NOTHING was changed....except for the level design...and Luigi's usual characteristics (higher jumping, slightly floatier) have been implemented.For whatever reason, the levels are all made much shorter ON PURPOSE. The maximum time limit is always 100 seconds, so you're always pressured to breeze through the pint-sized levels, not being able to take the time to establish any actual fondness or appreciation of the levels themselves. Even then, the levels are not quite as up to snuff as in other NSMB games, with the exception of maybe NSMB2. When playing as Nabbit, you can collect power-ups as extra lives, and not take damage from ANY enemy, including bosses. When one hears of this monolith of the gaming industry one thinks of the work it has accomplished as a simulator of racing. However I shall describe how from the height of it's prosperity in the Playstation 2 era it came to be a tired monolith. Yes a monolith with little else besides. The racing that was not without its flaws in Gran Turismo 4 has not advanced in this game - nay perhaps has retrograded. Just for one small example, the status of tires was easily understood in Gran Turismo 4. Not so in this game and let's not forget that just after a race when you may have won, the game sometimes glitches and you lose it. If compared with its polished predecessors it does not seem much of an accomplishment.Where do we start? Is it the lack of consistency throughout? Is it the bizarre lack of response after upgrading certain cars? Is it the use of some tracks too regularly, (especially when there are some really good new tracks they could have included more)? Is it the lack of feel in many of the cars? Is it the unrealistic power induced understeer in rear wheel drive cars that should go straight to oversteer? Well, it's all of these things and more. The whole feel of the game is of a lie, of a lack of integrity of inconsistent responses, and that is the worst thing.Then there's the stupid choice of cars to include - all sorts of pointless little hatches and buzz boxes wasting space when there could be so many amazing cars that weren't included. What happened to the famous 230SL? Why not a Maserati Ghibli?  Has nobody heard of Monteverdi? This could have been a collection of all the best cars throughout motoring history, but as it is it's just a mixed up collection with no theme.GrandTourismo 6 trades on its predecessors, but why should people keep handing over money to those putting out a clearly unprofessional and unimaginative product? Essentially they want money for nothing. Kazunori Yamauchi of this once shining organization should clear the decks and get in some new direction.Five was really bad and this corrects some of its faults but it's still a major disappointment with only occasional moments of pleasure.Boring, man. Never again.

The game is known for fantastic graphics, amazing vehicle physics, and great tracks. The game also has a superb multiplayer mode that will keep users coming back. The user interface is improved over the previous installment, and the game still continues to have a roster of cars that is second to none. The interior of the cars (for most cars, that is) are fantastic, mimicking the real world versions of the car. In particular, the Viper looked exactly as it would in a dealership. Offering many different types of racing types, this is a one stop shop for most racing enthusiasts.This game, however, is not a must-have installment for the franchise. The graphics are not improved over Gran Turismo 5, if they have I did not notice. The frame rate drops from 60 fps. The load times are initially long but appear to decrease as data installs from disc onto the drive (it installs the game in pieces as opposed to one large install, just as it did in GT5). The music is good, but rather odd - if feels as if I am more at a rave or dance club rather than playing a racing game.The biggest problem lies in the single player campaign's lack of intelligent AI. The artificial intelligence is pathetic. The game also has no balance: you can upgrade your car to beat the competition with little to no skill required. Drive off the track, its okay. Collide full speed with the car, that's fine - you'll get cosmetic damage and both of you or however many cars that were involved in the pile up will be on their way. No qualification either. That is the problem: real-time changing weather and time is fine and great, amazing, but what is a race without consequence for poor performance? Where is that sense of accomplishment when talent gets you to win the race, not a car that outpaces the competition (not even performance limitations, which I am glad they introduced from GT4, make races feel competitive). There are modes, such as Rally, Kart Racing, and a few others where the cars are close enough together in performance to create competition, but they are exceptions. Online multiplayer remedies these problems by making these actual options, but unfortunately the single player has no such options. Maybe cutting that 1,000 plus library of vehicles in half would allow for developers to focus on re-tooling the AI that feels no different than Gran Turismo on the PlayStation (yes, I am referring to the first installment).This is a good, solid game but the game still has problems with damage and AI in single player.

233 reviews but Amazon asks for mine... so here goes...I had read about all the issues with this release so I waited a month for the price to come down.  Thank heavens I did that, because it's the one thing that makes me think it was worth it.  Because it took me less than a month to get to 99% career completion, and I'm already feeling like the fun is over and the game isn't going to be updated fast enough to keep me waiting for the problems to get fixed.  That's two months, and lots of things are still glaringly messed up.As everyone has noted over and over, GT6 is a LOT like GT5 with some very small improvements (handling, graphics, menu arrangement), some things that haven't changed at all (weak sound, car quality, camera views, interiors, did I mention rubbish sound?), and some things that have got worse (handling, graphics, gameplay depth).  Yes, you will have to start over, which I don't think is a bad thing but some longtime fans of the series have said they don't want to do for the 6th time.  I started racing without ABS about 2 years ago, so this is the first GT title I've done entirely with no driver aids of any kind (not even the standard caveat of GT5 of "only ABS 1").  Problem is, one of the things that was broken for a long time and is still not really right, is how cars behave when you turn off ABS.  Some immediately lock wheels no matter how gently you touch the pedal, no matter what brake bias you set, no matter how fast you are going.  Another problem is the cars still float way too much (something wrong with how gravity is rendered) and now they roll over if you just take a little too much kerb... cars in general feel way too light and stay airborn way too long over crests and such.  And they get going way too fast for the amount of aero they have dialed in, so there's still something wrong with the effects of drag and downforce.  Then there's the problems that happen once you're not the only one on track.The AI from GT5 is still present in GT6, meaning every race is a chase-the-rabbit where you start last (or near the back) in a rolling start where the leader is 20 seconds up the road already.  They still brake way too much in corners and let you go by, if you haven't already attached yourself to their rear bumper and lost all your momentum.  The AI only know their racing line, they have little concept for racing side-by-side so they will often collide with you even if your car placement is totally pro, and when they do act like a backmarker being lapped they still cross the track width (sticking to the racing line) while braking, in such a way that you often have nowhere to go.  The grid starts seem like an afterthought - mostly they are in the SuperGT races, but it's still a rolling start where the rows are spread far apart and the leader is - you guessed it - 20 seconds ahead.Race events are extremely thin compared to previous GT titles.  Remember when you used to have to do all the Formula GT races to their full distance (e.g. 78 laps of Monaco) or the full 24 hour races at Le Mans and Nurburgring?  Then GT5 decided to cut the Formula GT races to 20 laps and only 5 tracks but still retained the endurance races?  Well GT6 dropped the Formula GT races entirely, and now you get to do the 24 *minutes* of Le Mans.  Yes, I said MINUTES.  And all the other career races are short, no more than 5 events of 5 laps each, some a lot less than that.  Even the license tests consist of only 5 challenges per level.  And SRF is still forced on for a lot of the experience, which makes no sense in events that allow you to compete with your online friends (license tests are like the GT Academy in that way now, but unlike the Academy in that the training wheels are bolted on).Ultimately I try to get past all that stuff and just enjoy the replay value in practicing my favorite cars and tracks (GT6' Nordschleife is still the best I've tried so far, and they now have the awesome Mt. Panorama - yes Bathurst), but with the enduring frustration of incorrect camera angles and engine sounds on my fav cars, and physics problems that make me throw something at the (...er, well it's not my tv's fault or the PS3 so hold on there), and still no good Seasonal *races* (only time trials) for the fun of trying different cars while racking up credits to get more cars...  It's kind of a letdown.  It makes me want to play something else.Bottom line - if this is your first racing game then you might enjoy it... but for longtime racing game fans especially those who have gained some skills and experience, it might give you buyer's remorse.  2.5 stars - but I'd give it only 2 if it still cost $60.

I am just going to post a review that I have saved before. I will be listing pros and cons from major aspects of the game (gameplay, graphics, fun and replayability or the ability to restart the game and it still be fun).gameplay: The basic gameplay is that what it always has been, you get a licence and then you do the races that the license allows starting with your basics, then B, A national, B international, A international, S international, and Rally International and each one gets harder than the last to obtain including the difficulty of the races that you can do with it. This career seems a bit repetitive but SCEA has always found a way to keep the game fresh, which they did this time as well. Although there are interior views on the car, there are no textures on the view on the standard cars which make up about 82% of the dealership but with 1200 vehicles (i cant say cars because there are a lot of trucks and vans on the game) there are a lot of vehicles that have very beautiful interior views (premium vehicles). You can customize your vehicles with performance upgrades and there have been slight improvements to the visual upgrades (slightly more selection but mostly for aerodynamics because its a sim and not for making your cars like street racing). Another big difference is the loading times which has been drastically reduced for the last game, Gran Turismo 5. There is so much to say about this game but this is just the biggest improvements. There was one thing I was a bit worried about and that was Micro Transactions and low payouts  but now, since the update, where you can double the payouts just by logging in each day; there is really no reason for micro transactions. I logged in every day for five days but didn't play to get the maximum payout and then did about 11-13 races and earned 200,000 cr.Graphics- This game has far better graphics than any other PS3 game. Since the PS4 has been out, people have been saying that they never pushed the PS3 to its limits and it still had a lot of room to grow (even me). This game was meant to push the PS3 with everything it has but there has been problems with the Fat classic PS3 and the Slim model running it. The only PS3 that I have heard that has been able to run it properly is the Super Slim model (which was released around December 2012) probably because that model had greatly improved hardware. Everything, the suspension (which actually moves up and down now), Rendering, textures, and physics have been drastically improved to a mind boggling level.Fun- Hours on end of addicting entertainmentReplay Ability- Well considering that the game is pretty much limitless, you probably shouldn't reset it but if you did you will always find something new to do.OVERALL SCORES:Gameplay: 10/10Graphics: 9/10Fun: 10/10Replay Ability: 8/10NOTE: Standard cars and premiums cars aren't Identified by those names anymore but you can tell if you are looking at a premium car in the store if the option "view gallery" is not blacked out.

I love the GT series and this one continues to impress with excellent graphics, physics, and game play.A few notes:The main user interface has been drastically changed (again) and feels like a step backward at first, but after you get used to navigating around it's fine.It appears you no longer have the "preowned car lot" to choose bargain priced cars from.Unless my memory is faulty (haven't played GT5 in a year now), it starts out with a lot more things locked than with the old model. The new design forces your initial progress more by only unlocking a few things at a time. It's not long before a lot of things are unlocked and you have more freedom in how you proceed, but it was a little annoying the first couple of sessions. Maybe I don't want to start with a Honda Fit at the Sunday Cup!Thankfully, it has not lost any of its gameplay and an hour slips away in what seems like minutes when I sit down to play. There's always one more thing you want to do or complete... which is good.As before, the network-based seasonal events are the best way to make big, fast money, but they only let you win once. I haven't yet found the race, as there was in GT5, where I could easily win in 10 minutes and make a quick quarter-million as often as I want to. It's also a lot stingier with awarding you cars than before.I don't know if it was a bug, or just misleading, but one frustration I had was when I tried to enter a race that was for "GT 15th Anniversary Edition" cars only, one being the Ford Focus ST. I spent a bundle maxing out an ST only to find my car didn't qualify... it wasn't specifically labeled "15th anniversary" but it was the only Ford ST available, unless there's a hidden prize car. Anyway, that was a frustrating waste of 100K.The other thing that annoyed the heck out of me was that I pre-ordered this game and played it shortly after it was released... and already it required about 1.5 GB(!) of updates before I could play it. This is a very frustrating trend. Sony should give free (or very cheap) updated replacement discs when they do this. I recently bought a 12GB PS3 as a secondary unit, installed the original GT5 on it only to find it needed SEVERAL gigabytes of updates... using up a huge portion of the limited storage.Other nit-pick: GT6 has started embracing the in-game purchases, where you can spend real money at the Playstation Store to buy additional credits or cars. I got both of these upgrades as part of a full-price pre-order deal, and it was fun (and a bit frustrating to figure out) to get these hot cars up front, but overall, I dislike this trend and if it ever starts taking away the enjoyment of playing the straight version of the game, they will lose me as a customer.Anyway... awesome game/simulator...Enjoy!

The Metal Gear Solid franchise has been and will always be the greatest video game franchise of all time. There are no other video game franchises  I can think of that can deliver great stories, innovative gameplay, expert voice acting and relevant as well as post-modern writing all in one package. Time and time again, each entry of the series has changed the climate of video games. The creator Hideo Kojima is a visionary, and a genius in my book, but he has also single handedly proved that video games can be more than just a mere form of entertainment people can play, but rather an experience as well as a great expression of art. I own all the main entries of the Metal Gear franchise, but in order to play them I have to bust out the old PS2 and PSP just to play them. With this convenient collection I can now play all the games in one great bundle on one system.This collection contains all the main games in the Metal Gear Solid series directed by Hideo Kojima including:- Metal Gear- Metal Gear 2: Solid Snake- Metal Gear Solid (via download from voucher code included)- Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty- Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater- Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots- Metal Gear Solid: Peace WalkerMGS2 and 3 also include some of the bonus features included in their re-releases, Substance and Subsistence respectively. This collection also includes Metal Gear Solid VR Missions (a compilation of side missions played with the MGS1 mechanics) once again like MGS1, has to be downloaded via voucher code included in the box. Also included are 2 graphic novels which can be viewed as 2 full length movies based on the Metal Gear Solid 1 & 2. I have played and completed all of these games in the past except for VR Missions, but I appreciate the HD transfer for all games and even the trophy system which are nice. The only gripe I have with this collection is the omission of "Metal Gear Solid: Portable Ops" which in my opinion is an important canonical story in the series; however the reasoning behind this was because Hideo Kojima did not direct the game himself and only served as an executive producer. Portable Ops contained some origin stories for important characters such as Roy Camball, Gray Fox and subtle hints of the creation of the Patriots. Despite that, this is the definitive collection for the Metal Gear Solid series thus far with easily over 100 hours of gameplay. If you have never played any of the Metal Gear Solid games before and are interested, this would be perfect for you: and for the MGS purists such as myself who simply wants all of the games in one convenient package than this is a great deal.

If you've never played these classics, you owe it to yourself to run out and pick up a copy this instant. If you've played them before, this is a budget-priced return to some of the most influential video games ever made. Either way, Metal Gear Solid HD Collection is money you won't regret spending.

This game is very, very fun, but as others have pointed out, make SURE you have room for the patches the game requires before playing.Now that that's out of the way, Need for Speed Rivals is made by Ghost games, a new game developer who is watched over heavily by Criterion (the makers of Hot Pursuit and the Burnout series). The game combines Most Wanted's open world with the addictive Cops Vs. Racer mindset of Hot Pursuit. After a short tutorial (which really isn't that bad, it's only 20 minutes of your time), you pick one of these two sides and hit the road. The game (almost always) gives you the option of choosing from 3 lists of challenges (jump X distance, win Y races, etc.) for both sides, your reward is a new car, rinse and repeat. This repetitiveness is why I knocked off the star. The handling is also very similar to the previous games in the franchise, going with the arcady, pick up and play mechanics (Gran Turismo/Forza, this is not). If going around hairpin turn at 200 MPH in a new McLaren isn't your thing, stick to Gran Turismo. The graphics are amazing, taking from Battlefield's Frostbite engine.The few complaints I have is the repetitive gameplay if you play it for too long, and that while playing as a racer the game sometimes spams your game world with WAY too many cops. I get that Ghost wants challenge in the game, but not being able to drive for 2 minutes without "PURSUIT STARTED" gets a little annoying. Also, car customization on the cops side is much more limited than the racers side of the game.Overall, this is a great first game by Ghosts, and I look forward to their later works.

I was hoping the release of Rivals would be far better than 2010-released Hot Pursuit. While the latest EA Need for Speed series is better, fans will soon realize it needs improvement on several fronts. The widely mentioned disconnection during a gameplay is a true story that I have experienced quiet a few times. When you pursue a racer (or are running a way from the law if you're a racer), the session has been known to disconnect while it "migrates host." During the process, a player could lose points newly acquired. I play this game using the cop career more, so this review is not covering much of the racing side. The police cars are of course newer and better (because they are faster) but I was very disappointed to see they didn't add the new Ford Interceptor (it was featured in Hot Pursuit as one of the future cars -- along with the now defunct Carbon Motors-owned E7). There are also no Chevy Impalas or Caprices either. On the other hand, they have the more muscled seventh generation Dodge Chargers in there. I know that one will have a hard time catching racers with an Interceptor, an Impala or even a Charger but it would have been nice to have more car choices that we know are on our streets for those, like me, who free roam a lot. Talking about free roaming, this game doesn't have that feature in the real sense of the term. That's not necessarily a bad thing, actually. You can free roam. But based on your settings, you could actually be playing online at the same time with other people. If you don't realize it right away, you could eventually the hard way. A random player could ram into your car unexpectedly, trying to destroy it. And if you're a cop that just got T-boned, that would trigger a pursuit and it will be up to you to take the racer down or ignore them. You can opt to play in single mode, without being bothered by the online community. Choosing that option effectively converts the game to free roam drive mode unless you're playing the various missions. The missions themselves are kind of basic. Your job as a police officer is to shut down illegal racers in Redview County. Several methods are used, such as Rapid Response or Interceptor missions. Or simply patrol the roads or park your car somewhere and wait for a law breaker to drive by. In any case, every mission goals will be displayed on the right of the tv screen. I like the police dispatch communication in the game. The 911 lady appears to be busy with calls in this game. It is definitely better compared to Hot Pursuit. What I don't like are the police sirens or lights. In Hot Pursuit, the sirens sound better and more realistic. I don't like the fact that I can't switch between a wail and yelp sound, for example. Unfortunately, the LED lights in Hot Pursuit are absent in this game. Rivals is an OK game. Certainly slightly better than Hot Pursuit. I wish they had included all those things mentioned above. Hopefully, a future release of the series (where you can play as a cop) will be more promising.

I'm not a tennis expert by any means, but when I was younger I played casually quite a bit and I have a (very) basic grasp of fundamental strategy.I got this a week or so ago as the FAOTD and so far I'm very pleased. I don't have the patience to master something where I can't feel the buttons.My only gripe with the game is that the game sometimes confuses a shot command with a movement command.  To position your player you simply touch where you'd like him to go.  The instructions tell you that the quicker you give your shot command after the other player hits the ball, the more power you'll have.  Well, if you, say, reposition your player to the center of the court, and then give a shot command while he's in motion, the game will often read that second input as another movement command, so your player will run to another part of the court.  This happens more than I would like.  I've tried to be very deliberate with my finger swipes, but it still happens.Overall, this is a great game, especially for a FAOTD.  Fun and challenging, and worth the time I've spent with it.

Frankly,  my experience with digital tennis has been limited to the table arcade games back in the mid-80s, and VIRTUA TENNIS CHALLENGE reminded me how much my serves sucked then as they still do now.
