I remember as a kid playing my fathers games with him. From Doom to Metal Gear Solid, I played all sorts of games all across the board ever since I was a kid. Going into this game, I honestly had low expectations. All of the trailers and videos I had seen did not impress me for some reason. Don't get me wrong, the game looks fun and looked nice mostly, but nothing about the news of the game were really all that inspiring for me to make me play it. That was until I gave the game a shot, and let me tell you that it was one of my better decisions I have made.The story is the main reason why I love the game so much. At first, it seems pretty straight forward and simplistic, but also boring and by the numbers (nothing that COD or anything haven't already worked with or towards in some fashion already). But this changed right after the first mission; the story is still straight forward and easy to follow. However, the story becomes stronger, more grounded, more emotional and connectable all because of the character development, the arcs of the story, and the interactions of the characters. Without spoiling anything, I will avoid talking about the story and further or the characters themselves, but know that the story and the path the story takes is fantastic, as well as refreshing in an era full of bland and passable story modes in games; this game is single player only, and is the better for it.The mechanics are also tight and solid. The cover mechanics operate quite a bit like Killzone; you hug to whatever cover is near you with the left trigger (L2), and you move around the cover piece with the move stick. This allows for the ability to pear over cover, peak around, or peak under cover pieces in whatever manner you wish. The reason why I love this cover mechanic so much is because you never feel stuck on cover, but instead you move around any piece of cover at will, and yet can easily run on the move again too without having the Velcro feel (it makes sense for that in 3rd person shooter games, but 1st person shooters should avoid it in my opinion). All of the guns feel solid, nice, and react the way I would expect them to if they were real. I love that the guns are never fully kept at all times, but instead picked up in each mission; gives more weight to the storyline and what happens in it. Overall, the shooting, cover, movement, and so on all feel fantastic and smooth.On to the other aspects of the game. For one, the sound is great. All the guns sound great, the voice acting and and dialogue is awesome and actually avoids the game feeling too campy or corny. Also, the machines and so on also all sound great. The level designs are all interesting and awesome; they are cool set-pieces that actually have a cool direction that the level ends up revealing. Also, for a first person shooter of this sort to actually have old school hidden areas, it is a godsend to a gamer like me. Plus, I love the fact that there are health and armor upgrades to be found, as well as the collectibles actually being really cool and builds the story even further. Spin off the health and armor system, I love the fact that they reintroduced the old school health systems of old with the new school; the health works by points, with armor being able to be picked up to help reduce damage to the health meter a little, but the game also has a regeneration system that will only restore up to the next nearest even 10th number (so if your health falls to 70 points, then it will regenerate to 80).All of the above are my loves and positives in this game, but really I only have one gripe, and really it is small (yet noticeable enough to deduct a point obviously). This game being a next gen title, I expected it to look better than it does. Now, the character models and most of the areas look great; the game shines when in the sunlight and when outdoors. However, the game does a much weaker job in detail and beauty when it comes to the indoors and the normal, bland grey areas (like the subway or the first mission). The details in the areas of the game could have been better, as well as some of the enemies at times, but really like most of my articles graphics are never the biggest deal so long as they are not horrible (by the way, 8-bit games looks great to me if the aesthetics is kick ass; aesthetics is not graphics). My one other gripe is the amount of activity to earn from the game. I only complain on this topic mostly because I am use to my shooter titles having an extra mode somewhere (most times it is MP related, but a Horde like mode or something would have been cool to do, or Spec Ops or something). Both of these points are small and do not take away much from the game at all, but instead leave just a tad bit to be desired in some areas.This game is fun, exciting, interesting, and should be played and tried by anybody who might be remotely interested in a more story propelled shooter title, focused on an alternative WWII timeline. In any case, have fun gamers, enjoy the review, and let me know if I can help with anything!

I love the action, story, weapons and overall concept.  This is a fun shooter that also incorporates elements of stealth.  Graphics are decent but more PS3 than "next-gen" looking.  In general, it's a fun game and I don't regret the purchase one bit.  It is also the only game in my PS4 library (which is over a half dozen games at this point) that I've played not once, not twice, but three times already.  So, replay value is very high.  All in all, it is probably the most fun game I've purchased so far.However....This game can be hard, and not in a good way.  It is way too difficult at times and that difficulty starts almost immediately.  A combination of occasionally poor camera angles, terrible (as in practically non-existent) ammo monitoring/alert system, auto-aiming that does more harm than good, and sometimes whacky controls can induce a controller smashing rage in no time at all.  Throw in ruthlessly distant checkpoints and you'll find yourself like I have numerous times: ready to hurl the PS4 controller through the 60-inch screen after wasting ten minutes slaughtering two dozen enemy soldiers and a handful of heavily armored and armed robots, only to have some little cowardly guard or commander dart out and finish you off with one shot because you have like 5% health left after the battle.  Sometimes the game will get really cruel and just send an entire new wave after a particularly hard battle with not nearly enough food and ammo for you in comparison top the enemy.Now, it wouldn't be too bad if the checkpoints weren't so ridiculously spaced and the game so unrelentingly cheap at times.  Like, did I mention that the enemies seem to know your every move and always seem to time a full out assault perfectly as soon you run out of ammo or get critically low on health?  If you try to take cover and fight with some type of strategy, then they'll usually just lob grenades at you until you die or finally give up and come out into the open armed with 19 bullets against twenty foes.  As I mentioned earlier, it doesn't help matters that the game does an absolutely terrible job of alerting you when you are out of ammo.  Another extremely irritating quirk is the strict rail system. This is gaming by numbers where familiarity and memorization win. The enemies will attack in the same manner, same pattern always.  Once in a blue moon, an action that YOU take will alter their attack, but if you confront them the same way, they will attack the same way. My last gripe is the programming.  There are some serious bugs in this game.  The most loathed issue, at least by me, is the terrible navigation and environmental detection AI. I've lost count of how many times my character had to just sit there completely exposed because he couldn't jump up a two foot embankment to take cover. I think this may be a nasty byproduct of the play by numbers rail system because this anomaly usually happens when I try to backtrack to scoop up items I attempt to preserve during one of the many one against 500 men, ten virtually indestructible robots, cyborg dogs and even regular foot soldiers who seem to withstand an increasingly startling amount of damage before falling.  I lobbed three grenades and pumped 5 shotgun rounds into one so-called regular soldier, not even one of the hulking iron-clad monstrosities that are supposed to stake tons of damage.  He STILL did not fall.  In fact, one of the so-called boss soldiers was ten times easier and quicker to kill than the regular soldier.  Did the damage detection AI get screwed up or something?  A couple other quirks are the ammo wheel (make sure you look at the arrow, not the highlight. Can't tell you how many times I've chosen the wrong weapon in the heat of battle because the weapon being highlighted is independent of the arrow pointing to the weapon.Now, with all that said, the game is still extremely fun and highly addictive. I simply can't stop playing.  Do I think you should buy it?  Sure.  Just invest in some of those Wii strap thingies and maybe a soothing cup of relaxing tea before playing.  Unless you're a Wolfenstein master or just one of those lucky people with nothing but endless hours of free time per day to devote to mastering FPS, this game WILL tick you off several times eventually due to cheapness.  May not hurt to take a blood pressure pill or two before playing as well...  Excellent game, all out fun but definitely infuriatingly frustrating at times.  It has greatly increased my vocabulary of things I can call a game out of anger.  It's a great game but it could have been a class if it were more -evenly balanced and some of these glitches were patched.  Seriously, unable to jump up a two foot embankment to get to cover, so BJ has to stand there getting blasted because he's surrounded on every side and that two-foot embankment is the only clear area????  Lame...*July 12 update*Now, the more you play, the better you become at overcoming these little obstacles.  That is also what helps make the replay value so high.  Now that I have a good feel for the mechanics and the game engine, this elite glitches have become less bothersome.  However, they were infuriating on the first play through.  I waffled on my original rating, giving it a three-star because I was so mad at the initial shortcomings.  However, After playing the game several times, I still want to play it when I need a quick adrenaline fix.  No other game in my library has that kind of attraction.One last note regarding a choice you will be forced to make at the beginning of the game.  I won't spoil it with specifics but you will need to nod to either your left or your right.  If you are a newbie like me, I strongly suggest you nod to the right.  The basic differences of the choices are as follows:Nodding to the right will give you health upgrades which are permanent once unlocked.  Your health capacity will stay the same for the entire game.  It also gives you the ability to hot wire items.Nodding to the left will give you armor upgrades which increase the amount of armor you acquire by 10% with each upgrade.  For instance, after the first upgrade, if you pick up what was previously a 10+ upgrade, it will become an 11+ upgrade.  The problem is, unlike the health upgrades, it neither increases the total amount of armor you can wear at once (it always stays at 100%) nor is it permanent.  In fact, sometimes, I lost armor between chapters whereas when I played with the health upgrade, I never lost health.The story stays basically the same with a few necessary minor changes based on your choice but they are very minor.

Absolutely great game, living up to its full potential.  This is how you bring back an "IP".  It still has sections of flat out crazy shooter violence, but it's smart enough to make the majority of the game built on stealth and exploration while leaving most of it optional, focusing on player freedom.It's completely built around its story with excellent characters, cutscenes, and voice acting.  And that, combined with the variety of gameplay, makes it very reminiscent of Half-Life 2 (which I don't throw around often, it truly does feel that way here).It also has a bunch of throwback references to the original Wolfenstein and remembers its past games, even allowing you to play in an updated version of the original game at one point.I usually choose to play games on Easy, but I must say, it treats its hardest difficulty very well and is actually playable (which is good since it gives a trophy/achievement for it).  Also gives lots of other things to help the player like a ton of health/armor pickups, and saving progress of your in-game achievements even after death (e.g., "kill 20 guys" will still count the ones you just killed before dying, making those way easier to get).One of its best features is that it forces you to make a choice early on in the game and it ends up changing almost all the cutscenes after that point as well as a few collectibles/secret areas.  This makes a second playthrough (which btw, keeps all your progress so it's basically a New Game+ mode) completely worth it, which is good so you can go back and find collectibles you missed (you actually HAVE to do both to find everything, but it's not an issue as it gives you a level select option if you just want to jump to a specific one).With amazing graphics/beautiful levels, varied gameplay, humor, emotion, great characters, and still managing to keep its cool/violent fun and tongue-in-cheek arcade feel, this game totally surprised me and shattered my expectations.  Great, great job devs (MachineGames, this being their first release).P.S.  I have to acknowledge their excellent and refreshing decision to NOT include multiplayer in the game.  Games don't need it pointlessly tacked on and I have to applaud the devs for knowing what they wanted, and their publisher Bethesda for not forcing them.

Let's face it - WWII first person shooters are a dime a dozen. While the FPS genre has taken a decided futuristic bent and avoided historical shooters for quite some time, there was a time when the market was hit by an absolute deluge. MachineGames take on the venerable Wolfenstein series is really an excellent game. While certainly not revolutionizing the genre, it gives us an intriguing story and plenty of replay value - a surprise for a single player only game.While it starts in a world with the Nazis close to victory, it jumps forward to the early 1960s, showing us a sci-fi world as the Nazis would have imagined it. While many people will talk about the lunar bases and hulking robots, The New Order does a fantastic job of showing the dark side - the concentration camps, the summary executions, the brutality and cruelty of history's most notorious and evil regime. In the massive concrete super cities and scientific breakthroughs of The New Order, we are never allowed to forget the basic inhumanity that underpins it all. It's a wonderful story that should be experienced, not related in a review.As for game play, it does a perfect job. The game transitions smoothly from stealth play to open combat, allowing players to proceed as they wish, the traditional shooter nature of the game well punctuated by bosses that can require a creative approach to the outright guilty pleasure of manning a machine gun turret. Those of us who recall the original Wolfenstein will smile as we dine on dog food and uncover hidden passages.I had a lot of hesitation when I preordered Wolfenstein and admittedly, I was on the fence, considering cancelling right up until I got the notice it shipped. Once I got to play it though, my fears were dispelled. It was worth my money and it'll be worth yours as well.

Wolfenstein: The New Order is the first game developed by MachineGames, a new game development studio comprised of industry veterans who worked on such titles as The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay and The Darkness. After leaving Starbreeze, these talents started MachineGames to continue their passion of making great games, and if Wolfenstein: The New Order is any indication, this studio has a bright future ahead of them.First and foremost, Wolfenstein: The New Order is a single player game. Is that a negative? Not one bit. There are enough multiplayer games out there if that's what you're into, and only a few of them actually succeed, so it's best to leave multiplayer to the games that have people who want that and not waste resources on it when they could be better spent making a meatier and more satisfying single player game, and that's exactly what MachineGames did with Wolfenstein: The New Order. Depending on your style of play, you can get 20 hours out of this game on one playthrough, which is very long for a first-person shooter. In addition, both running & gunning and stealth are viable options since the level design allows for exploration and planning which is important if you're playing stealthily. This also adds replay since there are two different ways you can play the game. As for the shooting, it's so buttery smooth and packs a punch. I haven't played a shooter in a very long time that felt this good. As for stealth, it's pretty basic but satisfying. It's fun throwing knives at the enemy or using a silenced pistol. :)Onto the graphics, this game is available on Xbox One, PS4, PC, Xbox 360 and PS3, so it's a cross-generational release, which means it won't be the most graphically impressive game you've ever seen. Sometimes it looks outstanding, sometimes it looks okay, and other times you'll notice that some textures aren't as detailed as they could be. With that said, Wolfenstein: The New Order is a rarity on consoles like Xbox One and PS4 since it outputs native 1080p resolution and 60 frames-per-second on both.Now the big surprise for me is the story. Wolfenstein was never known for story, but The New Order changes that. Likable protagonists, despised antagonists, all wonderfully voiced and acted. In addition, the soundtrack is tops.Wolfenstein: The New Order surprised me by how good it is. Probably my favorite FPS since Half-Life 2.

Most underrated game of the year for me so far. Holy cow this game is so much fun.Of course I have to get this off my chest after seeing all these pathetic one star reviews boohooing about no multiplayer added onto a single player game. Go play COD, Battlefield, Destiny and other multiplayer heavy games and leave our wonderful single player games alone. Some of us still relish in awe at a well done single player game. This is one of those games.Pros:*No this game is not Uncharted 4 gorgeous, but it does look next gen nevertheless and it runs like a dream without me ever encountering a single glitch or slowdown. Great environment destruction too. At no point did I think to myself this game could look better.*Stealth that actually works. This is one of the elite few game that knows how to provide working stealth mechanics. I have gone through most of the levels on full stealth using my throwing knives, takedowns, and silenced pistol. When stealth breaks down because of a mistake you made then it is time to bring the pain. Dual wielding weapons to annihilate and even dismember your enemies that foolishly try to stop you. The AI are no fools though, they will try to take cover and even flank you or come after you when you try run away because you realize that sometimes when you run out of ammo you're not a god, you do bleed and there is no auto recovery to save your sorry be-hind so you will have to find health and armor packs the good old fashioned way. Oh, and I should mention this is not one of those auto aim games. You actually have to aim at the enemies.*Easter eggs... Make sure you go to sleep and have a nightmare. What more need be said.*Level diversity is something I was not expecting with this game and was pleasantly surprised when I got to kill Nazis on the moon. Some cool underwater parts as well.*Man what a great story and a great cast of characters. I would rank the story and characters up there with Bioshock Infinite, Uncharted1-3, The Last of Us (okay maybe not last of us good but it's still really good). Not many FPS have a good story.*These are the best Nazis I have ever killed in a game and the Nazi bosses I had to fight were huge, mean, and tough. They required a little strategy on my part as well.*There are some side missions and while they aren't anything spectacular they add to the story and are nice to have.*Bewbs... There is some sexual behavior going on in this game (two scenes in particular) and yes it fits into the story. Yes we are all grown ups here. At least you should be since this is a rated M game.*The inclusion of perks is nice because in order to get them, some are a bit of a challenge and they all have a reward.*This game has a great length to it taking me about 14 hours to complete it on normal while doing a little exploring and collecting some extras. I am about to do a new game plus to try and get the rest of my perks and any collectables I missed along with making a different choice than the last time (it is just one choice that has kind of a big impact on the rest of the game). So yes there is replayability to this game.Cons:*WHAT!? NO MULTIPLAYER!?!? THAT IS SO STUPTHBTHBTHBTHPPPPPPTHHFRT!Noooo, there are no cons to this game. Unless your a Zelda or Naughty Dog game no game can be perfect.Overall if you are bored with the lack of games currently plaguing the PS4 until later this year or even if you are on another system, this is one of the best story driven FPS I have played in a while. Easily the best one so far for the PS4 and who doesn't like to kill some Nazis.

Story: 9/10  The new Wolfenstein is a must have for PS4. This isn't like COD, with it's 4 hour campaign where every level is exactly the same. This is Wolfenstein. It's a good, long game with an interesting and fresh sci-fi story, where you fight the unstoppable Nazi army with guerrilla warfare, as you hunt down the creator of all their robot tech.Gameplay: 12/10  This is a much needed return to the old-school type of FPS we used to love. No health regeneration, difficult enemies, boss fights, a good plot, and multiple weapons. It's very replayable; it may be a bit linear at times, but how you tackle the enemy is up to you. Go in with a shotgun in each hand, or slip up behind each soldier and knife them quietly. The robot enemies are very challenging, especially when they fight alongside the soldiers, who actually have decent AI. Like in an old-school FPS, you are not immune to bullets, and your enemies are not total pushovers either.Graphics: 10/10  The graphics are of course beautiful on the PS4. Blood and gore is realistic and quite satisfying, the physics of the game are quite good too.The verdict: 10/10.  It's more than you can expect from any other FPS game on the market right now.

Unlike most of the people who review this game, I haven't played the old school Wolfenstein's and this was my first foray into the series.Story:  I haven't finished the game and don't plan to but so far it's full of cliches but has a little more heart in it than most action games.Gameplay:  Oh my god this feels like a rejected call of duty, the character movements are too tight all the guns shoot like garbage and there is no impact for up close kills.  The enemies are all 3 different types:  Nazi generic guard, Nazi generic dog/robot, and my favorite the same bald guy plays every single "commander".  Also you have open areas and cookie cutter corridors to go through, nothing special here.Graphics:  mediocre, welcome to next gen.  Where everything is mediocre, honestly at some points I wasn't sure if i was playing a ps4 game or a ps3 game.  The environments are bland and it's corridor after corridor.  Textures are sometimes good, sometimes low res.Sound: Solid, nothing to write home about, nothing bad either.Overall if this game wasn't called Wolfenstein most people would not even bother with it.  It's a generic shooter that has awful shooting mechanics.  If you, like me, haven't played the old games don't bother with this one.

Wolfenstein was the original...without it there wouldn't be Doom or Halo or Call of Duty. Those series owe a lot to what the original Wolfenstein created on PC all those years ago. Now a new one hits and while I have lost a lot of interest in the series (it tried to be what it wasn't and tried too hard to be Halo and COD) I decided to give this one a shot and have been blown away. This is old school first person shooter at the core. There not much in the way of "innovation" or standard FPS features like regenerating health or the ability to just collect things by walking over it...but this is very much a welcome return. Make for a more intense gun fight. The graphics are some of the best I've seen for a next gen system and the story is hands down better than most recent FPS. Its also nice to see a FPS spend more time fleshing out a single player campaign as not everything needs to be multiplayer focused. This game is extremely graphic so its definitely not for younger kids but if you are looking for a great single player experience you definitely can't go wrong with Wolfenstein The New Order.

I was really surprised how much I ended up liking this game.  I was hesitant at first, because I still remember how bad the last Wolfenstein game was.  But this one feels fresh, and renewed.The New Order doesn't have the best Next Gen graphics, but they're still good.  For me, if everything is look clear, then the graphics are good.The story is really good too.  The game is pretty long with 16 challenging levels.  I started off with the second highest difficulty, but it was insanely hard after the fifth level.  As you make your way through the game your weapon choice will keep getting better.  There are some really cool guns in this game.As the gameplay goes, it's your standard FPS linear game, but ammo is a scarce resource and stealth is a big part of your missions too.  If you like FPS with a linear storyline then this is the game for you.  A linear game isn't always good, but this one is.

I have played so many FPS games and was expecting yet another tired addition to a repetitive genre. My expectations were low. I was happy to be wrong . . .This is a great game. Amazing graphics, outstanding FPS mechanics, and a decent story with great voice acting. Just before I started this game, I had just finished reading The Man in The High Castle, which is a science fiction classic set in an alternate history version of the 1960's where the Nazis rule the world. This game is set in the same alternate time period, a 1960's where the allies lost and Nazis rule the world. The little touches really sell the story and the immersion, like the public service announcements you hear extolling the virtues of the master race while encouraging you to inform on your neighbors and loved ones. The mood here is more somber than prior games in this franchise. It is not as satirical as Borderlands, yet not quite as somber as the Bioshock franchise. It strikes a nice balance in between.The levels are huge - and incredibly well done. After I have finished shooting Nazis in the face, I often marvel at the beauty and polish of the levels and graphics. Clearly a lot of effort was put into the game, and it shows. On the Xbox One, it really shines.Anyway, if you enjoy a good shooter, you will enjoy this game. It may appear as just yet another shooter, but the production values help to elevate it to something much more.

When I got the XBOX One I was disappointed that there were not many games available.  This game regained my faith in the new system.  This is a FPS in the truest sense of the phrase.  It does not have a multiplayer but the game itself makes up for that.  It is a mature game so there are parts which make the getting coffee scenes in GTA look like a Disney movie so please don't buy it for your child because you will have some explaining to do about the human reproductive system. It is also quite violent. I like that its not just a shoot em up; you must formulate a strategy in some parts.  You also get to search for enigma codes and gold.  The game is kind of short for most seasoned players with 15 to 20 hours of gameplay.  There is also a hidden easter egg where you will play the original 3D game which started it all.All in all its a fun game to play before games like Destiny and Batman come out in the upcoming months.

I would like to give you guys a quick round up of the game cutting out any spoilers ofcourse1) I am a huge FPS shooter fan, but i am also looking for the story line in the game and boy oh boy does this game cuts in the best FPS shooter i have played in a long time, ranging from emotional to dramatic to mind blowing and devastating action making you feel helpless at time's to leave your controller alone.2) I usually am not a huge fan of graphics over gameplay, but in this game.. both are a met, you guys will not be dissapointed.3) For action's such as melee and knife throwing , this game will make you crave for more.4) Last but not the least. i got the XB1 edition , and it took me 3 days to try and install due to some kind of issue regarding the update , so guys if you do have the option to go , go for the PS4 edition..

This game is a lot of fun with an in depth story that you can control which I love. The guns and the action are top notch and the graphics are ridiculously good. The facial expressions and shadows are the best Ive seen other than Ryse Son of Rome. It has a high replay value and is worth your money!

One of the best games out for the XB1 so far. No multiplayer, but a compelling and fun story. Boss fights can be more annoying and frustrating than legitimately challenging, so that hurts replayability for me - knowing how terrible the boss fights were constructed. That said, really solid game otherwise.

Every gamer should know this is the game series that created the FPS genre so it should be no surprise that this sequel/reboot still has lifeblood to continue all these years later. I'm actually shocked that the storyline, dialogue, voice actors, and setpieces are all movie quality. BJ is actually a fully fleshed out character in this and so are the creepy nazi villains. The graphics are solid with some much needed polish courtesy of next gen...er this gen now lol.I recommend any fan of gory shooters to go and add this to their cart. I had a blast (pun very much intended) blowing away nazi heads to pieces.

Good game to play through. Has an old school wolfenstein feel to it.  They even bring you back to the real old school wolfenstein for a level.  Overall as a wolfenstein fan I was happy.  Not worth $60 though.

For the first few hours of this game, I was stunned by the visuals.  Some of the character models look a bit wonky but the environments leverage the megatextures of ID Tech 5 engine and it looks pretty stunning. The shooting and sounds also feel great.At its best, the game brings back the feeling of the best story driver shooters, Half Life 2 comes to mind often. At other times though, the level design and AI don't quite work, especial y later in the game. For example, there is a mission that takes place on a bridge and before this level, I never had any issues with ammo. But starting with this level, I needed to stop and re-charge my weapon between every encounter. Thought it played a lot like HL2, it was much more frustrating for the games pace to suddenly slow down when, prior to this level, you never really needed to worry about ammo.The other problem that pops up quite a bit is that because the enemy AI is mostly just "aggressively advance", Wolfenstein  will bring out the classic method of just spawning a lot of enemies in a group to add challenge instead of advanced enemy AI.But other than these odd level design choices and classic missteps, I enjoyed the action quite a bit. Mostly its well-paced and lets you play a bit of stealth followed by action etc.  I really like the "perk" system here as well. The game basically presents a number of challenges to the player. As you complete these challenges, you get extra abilities.I really like how the game rewards you for trying out different styles of play.  I would have liked an upgrade system where you manage the upgrades but the game asks you to make sure you search around the level to find the upgrades. Most of these seem to be along the main path bot to get all the upgrades you will also have to make sure you look around the whole level.  This adds a bit of adventure to the game. I think I would have been annoyed by this if the levels did not look so great. There are other collectibles (gold etc.) but they don't seem to have much impact on the game.This game includes many elements from other great FPS and puts them all together in a very fun package. If you are a fan of old, story driver shooters, you may find a lot of fun here.

Great game. Only complaint is picking up stuff. I wasn't really a fan of always looking on the ground to pick something up. Other than that great game. If you haven't got this game yet, wait till it's about $40 or something. Really no point in buying a $60 single player game.

This game has a decent story about what if the Nazis had won the war... But the game falls short because it's too different from Call Of Duty. The gameplay is not fast paced and smooth like in the COD games. I honestly think if the gameplay mechanics were just like COD this game would be a 10/10.

If you're a fan of the over the top gore and dark humor, this game is for you.  It's not a brainteaser, it's a stress reliever and you'll get some laughs.  Gameplay isn't overly simple and there are some nice boss battles.
I was hoping for a fun game and it is insane!  I love the fact you have these robot dogs chasing you all the time.  You think your through the stage and all of a sudden your dead.  LOVE IT!

I love this game for what it is,...a great single player game. The graphics look amazing, the sound is phenomenal (especially with surround sound) and the game play is VERY smooth. Plenty of weapons to go around and upgrades to achieve. Lots of secrets to find as well so plenty of exploring is at hand. You're not rushed so take your time to explore and enjoy the game in its entirety. In my opinion, if you liked Half-Life you'll enjoy this game just as much. My only problem with this game is that it does not have multiplayer.Which is sad because I'm sure it would be amazing and maybe give call of duty a run for it's money. I took away one star just for that reason but this is still a MUST HAVE.

It's really neat how seriously this game takes its premise.  You play as a solider who has essentially been in a frozen state from 1944 until 1960 and when you come to in 1960, you find that Germany has won WW2.  What a truly fascinating concept to really explore and explore, they do.  There isn't a ton of story in this game unfortunately, but the story they do tell is pretty interesting.  In between these bits of story are fun, worthwhile FPS levels where you can go about it with stealth or just mow everyone down and either way, it's really satisfying.  If I was to criticize this game, I would say that I don't think anything about the actual gameplay feels very new and the enemy AI isn't terribly interesting nor challenging.  I'm also just not a very big fan of games that seem to expect you and the enemies to get shot numerous times before dying.  There are also a few really odd uses of poor quality textures (a coiled hose on the ground as a flat texture? wha?!).  However, it's really a good amount of fun to play if you like single player FPS experiences.  If you don't already know, the game has two separate timelines, so the game requires two play-throughs to fully experience.

As someone who got hooked on the genre with Wolfenstein 3D back in the early 90's, I have always enjoyed these games.  I'm happy to say that The New Order more than lives up to the name and the expectations that come with it.  The New Order is first and foremost, a very fun shooter.  The gameplay is fun the and the mechanics are solid.  The story is better than the last few since it has more options when dealing with an alternate timeline.  The graphics are simply amazing and even better than looking at the gorgeous screenshots is seeing it in motion since it runs at a silky smooth 60fps.  Not once did I see any frames drop or screen tear.  ID (John Carmack) really know how to make great game engines.Without spending all day going on and on about how awesome this game is, I'll just say "pick it up, you won't regret buying this game".

The graphics are quite cheap in most of the cutscenes. The storyline is so pieced together with the RANDOMEST ideas that overall when you're playing the game it's a very undeveloped / not too fun of a storyline. I just feel like I'm playing a pointless shooting game with endless Nazi's coming at me... Pretty disappointed from Machine Games on this one. Sorry I'm being 100% honest, but this was a HUGE letdown. 2/5 at best.

Fun and interesting first person gameplay...CHECK!Great Storyline...CHECK!Interesting Characters...CHECK!AWESOME WEAPONS!!!...CHECK!This game has a classic FPS feel with all of the modern shooters bells and whistles...If you like collectibles this game will easily keep you busy for a good 15-20 hours at least.  MUST BUY!!
A ton of fun if you enjoy single player shooters, the game is very well made, and the story is great.

Bethesda makes some of my favorite games and the reason why is the fact that they always exceed my expectations. I expected a corridor shooter with a over the top story but I got much more. The game starts out exactly as you would think, in the middle of action trying to survive and what this game does well is use the situations to slowly teach the player how to play the game. So it starts out as a corridor shooter and slowly expands into more of a sandbox teaching game mechanics as you go. Wolfenstein is full of secrets and gives players plenty of reason to replay levels and the entire game in order to get the full experience. This version of Wolfenstein seems to have been influenced by Dishonored which I liked because I enjoy stealth but guns blazing is always an option for those with a more aggressive play style. There are ways to enhance your play style too by completing objectives to unlock perks. There are also armor and health upgrades that can be found depending on a choice you must make early in the game which splits the game into one of two timelines. Wolfenstein gives the player choices of how to play and where to go to accomplish the missions. I really thought that this would be a nice filler game to keep me busy until Watchdogs released but I'm realizing that this game has a lot to offer and will now be competition for my Watchdogs play time. I highly recommend fans of FPS games and Stealth fans alike to pick this up, one of the best games I've played in a while.

Great all around game. Bought it used from Amazon still had the Doom 3 beta too. Probably one of the best campaigns I have played story wise. Its like reading a good novel based on am g alternate universe where Nazi Germany won the war and is the supreme world power.

If you liked the previous versions, you will love this one. Plenty of Nazis to blast and treasures to find. What else do you need? The game play is smooth and the graphics are very good too. This is one of the best games I've played on the Xbox One. Buy it, you'll love it.

I love open world games like Skyrim , Dragon Age and any other large RPG that can consume literally hundreds of hours of your life , but sometimes like right now I just want a simple go this way , pull this lever and shoot that kind of game and Wolfenstine : the new order fits the bill very nicely.Graphics : honestly they are not the best I've ever seen but they are very pleasing to the eyes. It's not what I would call the next gen graphics that you really want to see on your shiny new Xbox One , but they are better than the 360 and ps3 , so at least  we are getting better graphics than what we would have gotten on our last Gen machines :) but all we need is a little patience and time and the next gen graphics we want will be here soon enough.Story : the story is interesting enough that it keeps me in my seat and wanting to play more and more . I literally had to make myself put the controller down and get some much needed stuff done around the house , all the while thinking about my new wolfenstine game and wanting nothing more than to just sit back down and play a bit more , but alas we must be responsible and do what is needed . So my Wolfenstine thirst will not be quenched until later tonight when the wife and kids are tucked in the bed asleep , haha then it's game on baby !!!!game play : its what you would expect from most FPS games , the controls are smooth and precise , the button layout is the same as Call Of Duty except you cannot go prone. The major difference in this game and most of the others is we get to play in an alternate reality ( during WW2 ) where the Nazis have won and we are the repressed that are fighting for our freedom. On top of that we of course get our supernatural and far advanced enemies to deal with but this is par for the course and it wouldn't be Wolfenstine without it. To me this breaks up the monotony of the every day shooter we get time and again. Call Of Duty and battlefield are great and I will play them all but they are still just all about the same. Wolfenstine gives us something fresh and new and in my opinion its something that was sorely needed.if you are thinking of getting this game , just do it if you can , it's fresh , exciting and certainly very entertaining. I don't regret my purchase one bit and I'm certain you will feel the same.. Cheers and happy gaming :)Solid 5 out of 5Edit : the farther I get into the game the better it looks , also I have seen the 360 version on my neighbors console and I have to say there is a noticeable difference in graphics between the 360 and the Xbox One . The X1 version is far more superior to the 360 version. The X1 version is really , really ,really crisp ,clear and detailed. I'm not down playing the 360 version if that is all you can get at the moment because it looks good as well , but the X1 version is the one to have if you can get it..
Call me crazy but going gun crazy in a game that doesnt slow down really makes my day...  Great entry to the new platform.

This might have been great if it had been rolled out 5 years ago, but looking at it as a $60 main stage launch it is a dismal failure compared to any other shooter that has come out since the launch the new platforms.The graphics don't match COD, and shouldn't even be allowed to be compared to BF4 on the xbone.Maneuvering through the set pieces is a simple exercise of button mashing, no challenge at all.You are ammo starved through the play regardless of how many guns you stumble across.The controller has ample buttons that could be used to handle your inventory but you can only use two items at a time, after that you have to stop and load whatever other item you want to use.The one good thing I can say about it is the player movement, it is quick, smooth, and responsive.I was on the bubble as to whether or not I was going to pick this up launch day, and what decided it was the Doom beta access, but hind sight being what it is I wish I had just said no thanks.

I haven't come anywhere near finishing this game, I just wanted to set the record straight with my confirmed purchase, compared to some of the dimwitted reviews I've read. I'd say the graphics are about a 7, compared to other current next gen titles. Story and mechanics are also a 7 or an 8. The lean/cover system is impressive, other shooters should take this into consideration, when in Call Of Duty you can't lean unless you are facing a wall, here you may lean any direction whenever you desire.  Wolfenstein doesn't attempt to be something that it is not, I wouldn't call it linear, there are multiple paths in which have nothing to do with reaching your goal. There are a lot of fine details that I appreciate, facial animations, collectibles are detailed and written well. Hit detection is outstanding, while headshots and enemy death animations are entertaining to say the least. Highly recommended to those that are entertained by fantasy violence, and guns.

this is a superb game which i had waited for 40 years for, since the very first one on the commodore 16.graphics sounds gameplay light sabre effects were the bestonly thing is, graphics are downgraded on the xbone to standard definition, sound became stereowhat happened? inferior hardware.everybody knows that.

I've had bad luck with not liking the last couple of games for which I popped $59, so I waited for the price to drop and got it for $39. It turned out to be a good enough game for $39, especially considering that Sniper Elite V3 is $49 and even Sniper Elite V2 is still $34 after more than 2 years. OTOH, this may say something about the continuing popularity of SE V2 versus Wolfenstein ("WS").While I generally liked the play of SE better (mainly because it does not bog down with unnecessary talking and standing around which cannot be skipped), I liked the environments of WS better. (It's hard to beat going to the moon, even if far from believable.) I also liked being able to set mines and traps in SE, which you can't do in WS.I thought that the gun battles in WS were very repetitive. Also, if an enemy in SE sees a body you've killed and left lying around, he alerts everyone, but in WS, the enemy seems to just ignore them. (A nice feature in SE is that you can pick up a body and hide it.)Complaints aside, there's enough good & interesting about WS that I can give it 4 stars.

I was a little hesitant to buy this at first because I wasn't sure if I wanted to pay $60 for a linear single player only shooter. I found this on sale at Costco for $34, so I had to pick it up at that price (if you caught this review in time then run to Costco! It's a nationwide deal). It's definitely worth the $34 and after playing it I have to say it's even worth it at full price.Though I have played through classics like the original Doom, original Half Life, Quake, etc, this is my first Wolfenstein game. What a blast! The game mechanics are very simple but it has a surprising amount of depth. You can tackle many situations using different strategies. In many cases you can either go guns-a-blazing, or clear an area using stealth. It's surprisingly fun going the stealth route.One simple but cool feature is the perks system which has a few dozen mini challenges that if completed will give you passive perks. For example if you get enough grenade kills then you'll get an additional grenade slot, or if you shoot enough people while being stealthy your gun will do more damage. The challenges are actually fun and well integrated so they don't feel tedious.One feature you should take advantage of if you have Kinect is the voice commands. Most actions are easier to execute using a controller (such as throwing grenades or reloading), but being able to switch weapons by just saying "knife", "assault", etc is very helpful. Otherwise you have to use a somewhat clumsy radial menu which does not pause the game when active. I hope more games integrate Kinect like this, even though it's very basic it is also very helpful. The voice commands are not enabled by default but are easy to turn on in the settings menu.As far as graphics are concerned they are a bit hit and miss. They are a little bit of a miss because character models look a bit odd and textures are a little sloppy (especially up close), but they are also a hit because the actual environments are amazing! One thing I love is how varied the environments are. never did I feel like things were becoming repetitive. I also like how this game uses pretty much the full color spectrum and doesn't limit itself to dull grays, greens, etc like many modern gritty FPS games. A lot of care went into level design. Also, this game runs at a full 60 frames per second and I never saw it dip once no matter how much action was on the screen. This translates to extremely smooth gameplay and controls that feel great.I'm happy they went with just a simple finely tuned single player experience and didn't add any fluff. The campaign is lengthy for a shooter (15-20 hours) and everything just feels right.If you are looking for an old school shooter then don't pass this one up!

I pre ordered this game after burning out of the other games available for the Xbox One. Since Bethesda was involved in it, I was secretly hoping for a Fallout 3 + Nazi's sort of scenario. Sadly, this is not the case. Wolfenstein is built around linear levels.After beating the game I don't know how to feel about it. I felt like it's a bit short to charge $60 for, but then again it seems like every game generation the games get shorter and shorter. The graphics are beautiful, the voice acting is well done, and the best part is the characters. Each of the characters is really well done.It's a first person shooter, and for the most part it's pretty well done. The perk system is unique and added small challenges to help mix up game play. I wish they would have done more with this system because I enjoyed it. I enjoyed the stealth aspect, but I felt like it was sort of an after thought. The dual wielding is pretty much useless most of the time.The graphic content and such for this game is pretty intense. Definitely not a game for kids at all. This game deals with all sorts of grisly details (concentration camps, torture, maiming, etc) and is definitely not for the squeamish.In the end, I wish it were longer. At $60, I can't recommend it. If you get an opportunity to rent it, borrow it, or pick it up used for $<40, I'd say go for it.

I purchased this game along with my new Xbox One. I wanted to pick a game that really showcased the power of next gen consoles and based (at least initially) on the reviews of the game, it seemed like a good choice. Additionally, I had been a fan of the Wolfenstein franchise from the early 90s.Unfortunately, the game has come up short on several fronts. Let me itemize the good and the bad:The Good- Graphics are very well done. The textures and cut scenes look very good although not quite as 'advanced' looking as I would have expected on a next gen console. But nonetheless, still quite impressive.- The weapon play and controls are done well and the menu options are intuitive and easy to comprehendThe Bad- The story drags terribly. As an FPS with a single player campaign, I understand the need for brief interludes here and there. But this game utilized them too frequently, basically stalling forward movement and creating a fragmented storyline that had too many instances of minimal action and extended areas of un-necessary dialog. Better editing would have helped tremendously here.- The game is EXTREMELY buggy. This was, hands down, the biggest frustration point. It all began when attempting to install the game, which is a requirement for play. The installation procedure failed numerous times at the offset. I had to repeatedly restart the install in order to get to the point where I could play the game. Unfortunately, that is where I ran into the second problem: the game started to repeatedly freeze during gameplay. The good thing is on next gen consoles, you can stop the game like a mobile app without having to reboot the console. But the freezes were happening at virtually the same point in the game. After searching online for answers, I found numerous users were experiencing similar problems. After reading some tech notes, most recommended deleting the game and re-installing it while the console was not connected to the internet. I did that, although I ran into problems with the install yet again. Once the second install was complete, I could move forward into the campaign only to encounter ANOTHER point where the game would arbitrarily freeze at certain points. Despite restarting the game, the freezes would not allow me to continue. I now proceeded to delete and reinstall the game for a THIRD time. Once again, I could proceed in the campaign only to encounter the game freezes further on! At this point, I finally reached my breaking point and stopped playing.It is very obvious that Bethesda did NOT do an adequate job of proper QA on this game, as I have read numerous stories online of users encountering similar issues. I emailed Bethesda tech support asking for assistance and received no reply.Ultimately, the game itself could have been a good showcase for next gen consoles, but these quality issues really put a damper on the playability of the game as a whole. I hope Bethesda is taking time to deal with these issues so other gamers have a more fluid gaming experience.

It's really easy to make Nazis the bad guys in a game--but after all the Call of Dutys and Medal of Honors, what's hard is making a game that centers around Nazis and can still make the bad guys seem original and new.  I'm someone who's played every incarnation of the "Castle Wolfenstein" games, even a very strange kiosk that you could pay-to-play the older 486 PC version using a joystick and a VR headset.  Having recently re-played the "Return to Castle Wolfenstein", it was a real experience to pick up this newest entry in the series."Wolfenstein: the New Order" is a great update to this classic series.  First-Person Shooters have changed a lot in the many years this series has been around, and the updates here really give a classic concept the feel of the latest & greatest that FPS games have to offer.  There is a good storyline, complete with top-drawer voice talent and the return of our hero B. J. Blascowicz.  We have weapon choices that include dual-wield, fast action with many a melee opportunity, and the same feel of collecting medkits and armor and occasionally overcharging your health for an upcoming rampage that made all of The New Order's predecessors so much fun.  Probably the best nod to the more recent games is the fact that there's more than one way to complete a level:  this isn't just a matter of being able to navigate the map through different paths, it's also that you can make choices that let you vary between stealth and run-and-gun.  FPS games don't often have the ability to view the map these days, so that makes for a nice bonus that is carried over from the earliest days of the Wolfenstein series.What makes the story fresh is that we are playing to an alternate history:  after an opening mission in 1946, our hero is out of commission until 1960, and it's a world where the Nazis won the war, all has been lost, and now B.J. is left to try to pick up the pieces entirely on his own.  Each level is a movie-quality step towards saving the world, and each level has a purpose that advances the main story.  The alternate 1960 is a mix of technologies that has a fairly believable look and feel, and some of the 'newer' technology mirrors the strangeness we saw in the depths of 'Return to Castle Wolfenstein' and the occult-driven more recent entry that was just called 'Wolfenstein'.As much fun as the game is, there are a few drawbacks.  I've had times where climbing a ladder is still the bane of Our Hero's existence and I spend time bobbling around looking for the grip point.  Switching weapons isn't a fast way to keep the firepower flowing when the bullets are low--sometimes it's just a trip to a quick death.  Changing ammo with the radial wheel can be clumsy.  I have a real problem with grenades:  sometimes I bump the shoulder button to throw (hold down means you want to select weapons) and nothing happens.  I won't spoil the story for you, but there is one particular mission that sounds like a great squad-based opportunity but by the time you reach the end you find yourself wondering what the point was.Still, "Wolfenstein:  the New Order" is a great title, and I think with time I'll come to love it as much as its predecessors, some of which I still play today.

What's so wrong with having an offline VS mode against the computer? Nothing, that's what. And that's just the beginning of a long list of things wrong with this game. The next big issue is the limited character roster and not being able to transform (go super saiyan) during battle. This is one of many things that makes DBZ Battle of Z become a hole in the franchise.Pros:Online Co-op and Battle modesLots of charactersHuge BattlefieldsCard SystemIn-Game Currency and pricesLoading times aren't that longCons:No offline multiplayerExtremely dumb Partner AIRuthless CPU enemy AI (in most missions)Inability to control difficultyThat intro cutscene is the only one throughout the entire gameConstant on Lag (sometimes tolerable)Battle MechanicsIf you think you can beat every single mission in this game offline, you dead wrong, pal. The AI in missions like the Cell Games, and Broly, the enemy AI hands you your @ss on a silver platter and asks if you want fries with it. You need to have a PSN and a headset (to coordinate attacks with you friends, unless you want to stand still in the middle of battle and type stuff) if you plan on surviving the Missions. And you also need to work as the best team you have possibly been in, because if you won't everyone will go around punching one thing, when the smart choice is to punch the other thing. There are 4 classes: melee, ki blast, supporter, and interfere. Melee focus on close combat, Ki Blast focuses on long-range combat, supporter class focuses on healing, and interfere focuses on distracting the enemy. You'll need one of each class for maximum team power. Every time you clear a mission, you get cards. These cards can boost stats, help gain extras, and some of which act as items. You need to use these cards with heavy thinking and understanding, or else you will screw up you character, but that is pretty hard to do. There is more to this game than what I am saying, but You'll have to look at Metacritic or IGN for more info. I would only buy this game if you a Hardcore Gamer or a Hardcore DBZ fan.

After hearing several times that the Bioshock series was atmospheric and a must-play, I couldn't pass up the opportunity to get the all three for a great deal on Amazon. I had very limited previous knowledge/experience with the series.  I'll briefly touch on each game individually and then my overall consensus of the series.The original Bioshock's story is pretty memorable and the voice acting is great. There are some interesting twists in the plot and some of the final quotes are unforgettable (e.g., "A man chooses..., a slave obeys"). The maps are less linear than some shooters but there is a map and waypoint system to find your way around, usually. Some of the characters and ideas were extremely novel and creative. However, the first two games use the same graphics engine, which is pretty old now. I'm sure they would have been quite the experience back when they first came out but the graphics have not aged particularly well. The combat is clunky and I constantly ran out of ammo and I felt like I spent more time scrounging for money and trying to get more ammo than I would have liked. That being said, I felt like the strengths of the first game slightly outweighed the weaknesses and overall I would give the first game a 3.5/5.The second Bioshock looked identical to the first and was set in the same underwater world. This game was the most disappointing in the series because it contained all of the flaws of the first game (clunky combat, poor controls, fetch quests) but with a far less memorable storyline and they took a killer idea (playing as a Big Daddy) and having the melee weapon rely on ammo (gasoline). Essentially, I only finished the game in case there were important story elements for the third game, but it felt very much like a chore to do so: 2/5Bioshock Infinite is a gorgeous game, visually. The brightness was such a huge contrast to the other games' dark, gritty atmospheres and was a very welcome change.  I really felt like I was exploring a new world world that had a cheerful facade covering some deep, dark secrets. The story was pretty interesting despite its flaws and the plot twists were in the spirit of the first game. The characters were also more memorable.  Even though I did a lot of scrounging for money in this game too, the sound effects of gathering money were like music to my ears (ka-ching) and money was hidden a little better, so it felt less tedious than the first game. I liked being able to use the hook-thing to jump on aerial tracks to get around to different parts of the map but this was only available in certain areas and was really limited so it felt more like a tease rather than a sweet method of transportation for an open world game.  For the most part, I liked the weapons better in Infinite than the other games, but I hate that you can only carry 2 at a time. And again, the controls are still so loose compared to other FPS like Borderlands or Battlefield. Being able to use Elizabeth's powers seemed like a good idea, in theory, but it was poorly executed and often distracting. Overall, it seems like the game was torn between an action-adventure and a FPS and didn't really excel in either: 3.5/5I play a lot of first-person shooters such as Battlefield 3 and Counter-Strike so the combat and "loose" controls of Bioshock throughout the entire series was very disappointing to me. I couldn't ever really find a mouse setting that worked well because the sensitivity was different for the X and Y axes, such that looking up and down would be great but then turning in a circle would take too long. I also felt like the power ups in the game were disappointing. I love spells when they are fun, useful, and don't require a great deal of attention to refill mana (or in this case, epo). But in the Bioshock series, without a ton of upgrades (which aren't usually until the end of the game), you can only use the powers a few times before you have to "reload" them, which requires ammo! I ended up just sticking to a few of them that seemed more useful than others and mostly relied on weapons.

If you have played Season one of The Walking Dead, there is probably nothing to stop you from getting into this immediate follow-up episode, but just for the sake of record, reviewing seems to be in order, and here I will do it to build on the previous review.Obviously, if you have not played Season one, you absolutely should play it for the amazing storytelling and tense emotional undulations, you will not regret it and it will be the best thirty dollars you can spend on a good narrative-driven video game right now.400 days, quite simply touted as the companion episode to Season one and the prequel of sorts for Season two, isn't going to be that all-encompassing experience just like the first series of episodes, but more an attempt to bring the serial storytelling dynamic to a new place. Clementine, the main protagonist of the first season, isn't going to be here, and neither would any of the story arcs from previous episodes be featured here in any shape or form. This is a brand new story, and a fresh smorgasbord of characters appear in a story compressed like a single comic issue.The analogy of a single comic issue applied here seems apparent when you first dig into the episode, with it featuring five different groups of characters who have no seeming relation to each other. Telltale has said it's going to feed into the main bulk of Season two, and while you wonder how that will pan out, a little testament to the efforts to create a polished serial story, that point isn't going to matter much once you work your way through these nuggets of gameplay.They all have a story to tell, and of the heart-tugging variety too. It no doubt follows on the same dilemmas of living in a post-apocalyptic Zombie-infested world. To save someone means to sacrifice another, and to do something that looks right to you may have consequences on another front, but the gameplay looks improved here, like Telltale has learned many lessons from making adventure games thus far and applied them.The improved gameplay would do well to satisfy the hunger anyone waiting for Season two may have. Lots of gunplay, lots of exploration yearns to show just what to expect from further episodes, you will cling onto these stories like a person clinging onto the vignettes in a themed short story collection. Curiosity will kill the cat, and you begin to feel invested in these people's lives.Not all of them are put-together individuals but are fractured in their own vices and struggles, and Telltale is brilliant for creating a link between them, a clever ending and way of pointing towards the cloudy future. The episode is clever, although short, and if you want more Adventure game goodness from Telltale this is a no-brainer.For those who haven't played the first season, what are you waiting for?

This is probably the game I most anticipated this year. I was nervous, though. I didn't want to spend money on it when it seemed so many people were experiencing problems, so I waited for an opportune moment. I figured the February ten dollar reduction and the availability of free DLC was as good as any reason to buy it. I have waited to review this game for a few days to get a better appreciation of the game, but I can honestly say Battlefield 4 is an impressive game.I've experienced relatively few problems with the multiplayer, and I have played the game every day since I received it (nearly a week now). The most grievous problems I am experiencing includes a loss of sound. This happens whenever I join a new match. However, this seems isolated to team death match. I did not have this problem with any of the other game modes. This has happened about two or three times. I have not experienced this in all of the matches I've played; thankfully, most of the team death matches I have played have been relatively bug-free. The frame rate also drops every once in a while. This happens for maybe a negligible five seconds, though. The only other grievous problem I I've had was the single-player not saving the game. I was on the second level when I decided to switch over to multiplayer. I returned and had to start the single-player from the beginning. I didn't really mind, though. These levels are easy enough to beat, and the multiplayer is far more exciting.The sheer power of having thirty-two other teammates is nothing short of awesome. I've had a pretty good time getting into large matches. I understand there aren't very many full servers yet, but it has been three months since the game was released. The bad press Battlefield Four has been getting has also impacted the prospects of a larger base of players. Building a larger community will take more time. However, you can find large matches if you do some digging through the server browser. Be sure to favorite the ones that seem to have the most players.I decided to go premium. I love the re-imagined Frostbite Three, Battlefield Three maps! They are far more dynamic than they ever were in battlefield 3. The look and feel of the game on PS4 is a true improvement over the previous gen consoles. PC is arguably the best way to go in terms of versatility, but I highly recommend people give the next gen version of this game a try. Overall, Battlefield Four is truly an amazing development for FPS gaming.*Update* 3/02/14I'm continuing to experience a loss of sound for team death match. If you enjoy close-combat, infantry-only styled FPS, you may not enjoy the game very much for this reason. However, the domination mode (conquest without vehicles) works just fine for me. Again, if you enjoy infantry only-styled warfare and you're interested in BF4, wait a while longer. Hopefully a patch will fix this soon.*Update* 5/20/14In the two months since my previous update, I'd say the game, while still great and fast-paced, is definitely getting on my nerves. Ever since the Naval Strike DLC has come out, I've begun experiencing problems that were relatively uncommon for me.One of the most annoying and infuriating is a drop in frame rate. It is not a frequent problem, but it is an intermittent and unpredictable problem. I might be simply laying down an ammo crate or sneaking around a corner, when the frame rate will bottom-out.Another problem I've been experiencing at a much greater rate is rubber-banding. It was actually a minor annoyance before the Naval Strike DLC was released, but it has become far more common. I have no idea why this is happening, but it certainly seems linked to the latest DLC.I considered myself among the lucky few not experiencing problems, but it seems my luck has run out. Granted, the new maps are creative and a lot of fun when the game is running at its full capacity, but I sincerely hope the newest patches will eventually kick-in. Until then, my rating for this game will be four stars.*Update* 6/22/14Update opening statement: THANK YOU DICE!!! ...!!! The netcode updates have been out for a couple of weeks, and the online game-play is so much better. The problems I've been experiencing lately are far fewer. I'm no longer rubber-banding across the map for entire matches, and the frame rate does not drop unreasonably during heavy game-play. The announcement of the future expansions makes me nervous, though, especially in light of the bug increase, but I'm hoping the netcode fix will reduce the potential for game-debilitating bugs when I get the last two expansion packs. My impression of Battlefield Four remains positive. I feel like it deserves a five star rating, despite all the problems surrounding it.

I've played all the COD games, and I played Battlefield 3.  I didn't really get into battlefield 3 for some reason; I think graphically, on the last-ten consoles, it just was too pixelated and low-res for me to enjoy.  On the other hand, the latest entry to Call of Duty (Ghosts) was a total failure.  The campaign (at least in the digital version) was an optional download!  That's how little they cared about the single player mode.  Someone at Infinity Ward was quoted as saying "only 10% of players play the single player campaign".  Either they're wrong or I'm in the 10%, but I like a good story and single player campaign, so I'm either in that 10% or there's a lot more people who like single player FPS games (take a look at how well a lot of single player FPSs have sold, and they have sold very well, so this is not something to skip over as they did with COD Ghosts-such a failure).So, hearing really good things about this game, I bought it (digital download).  The definitive edition is definitely the PS4 version, with the superior hardware, higher framerate, and running at 1080P!  And Kudos to these guys for picking up where the older COD games left off (COD Black Ops 2 was quite a thrilling single-player campaign; what a story!).  This game feels more like COD Black Ops 2 in terms of plot/campaign.  It's long, very immersive, you get to do a lot of really cool things.  Jumping out of airplanes, just for one.  Then, all the vehicles!  There are so many ways to accomplish missions, it borderlines on a sneak game like Deus Ex: Human Revolution (and there are definitely sections where you excplicitly have to sneak and use stealth).  There are a ton of ways to conquer each mission; it's all up to you.They did a good job, too, with encouraging exploration.  There are collectables, and the maps are absolutely enormous.Gameplay-wise, it's perfect, the familiar controls are there and you have both your twitch shooting, as well as mounted weapon sections, sniping, everything!  There are also some really neat innovations; using the cyber binoculars to pinpoint enemies, and ordering your squad to attack.  There are a lot of things to manage, and it's really addicting.  There is a *lot* to do.I also give massive credit to the AI in this game.  This is the first game where I've really felt like the enemy combatants were doing what another real-life player would do.  It makes the game harder, but more realistic.  In COD you had guys running in to walls and stuff; none of that here; they will do their best to outsmart you, so it's your job to come up with a way to outsmart them.  Really cool concept; I hope more of this AI is used in the future.And I know I already said it once, but the PS4 version of this REALLY is a next-gen game; when you read the credits there is a whole section devoted to the next-gen team.  I haven't gotten into multiplayer yet, but I'm sure that's where a ton of the action lies; using vehicles and teamwork, and only the next-gen PS4 version allows for 64 players at a time!  Incredible.My last note is, GameTrailers said, to paraphrase, "Microsoft wouldn't let us show any footage of their version, so we're showing the PS4 version, and we're happy to report that the graphics are indistinguishable from the PC version set to the highest graphics settings, including in multiplayer".After the tragedy and lies that made up COD Ghosts, being such a huge letdown (a crappy 4 hour campaign and nothing new in multiplayer), it looks like Battlefield has stepped up to the plate and is now the king of mainstream warfare FPS games.  A campaign that took at least 20 times longer to finish than the Ghosts campaign, much more interesting technology, better graphics with a brand new Frostbite engine (especially on the PS4 version running at 1080P,), etc!  Good job, Battlefield Team!  This is the pinnacle of shooters right now.UPDATE:Since getting into multiplayer, I have to say, it is the most complex, insane, deepest multiplayer experience I've ever experienced.  I've only scratched the surface.  But 64 players at 1080P is just incredible.  Players are set up into squads, and there are multiple classes with many unlocks.  I've been playing Killzone: Shadow Fall every day for a while, which is top-notch, and has a 3-class system.  This, on the other hand, is totally different.  Ground vehicles, airplanes, helicopters, squads, and even a quick chat button reminiscent of Tribes 2 (e.g., "Need a Medic!").  Time will tell whether I keep with this, as there is a steep learning curve, but I believe that with enough patience there is a great reward to be had here, possibly over every other multiplier FPS out right now (oh, how I miss Tribes 2...  Teamwork is so important!).  My only qualms with this is that it's its difficult to distinguish friendlies from enemies; even with the recon's scope; everyone appears red.  Not like the binoculars in the campaign.  You die a lot and often don't know how that person possibly killed you from that position.  Hopefully it's not hacking, but supposedly the PC version has it.  Time will tell.  Multiplayer on this is definitely a steep, steep learning curve, though.  Still, I'd take it over COD anyway.  Killzone 3 and 4, I think are a bit more streamlined.  Set up turrets, call in air support, etc.  BF4 is almost TOO much, but I'm going to give it time.

Like many of you, I was hesitant to purchase Battlefield 4 after the horror stories that had plagues its launch. I recently bought my PS4, and needed some games to play with friends. I probably wouldn't have bought it if not for my friend from work constantly pestering me to buy it so I could play with him. I am very glad he did. I never got big into Battlefield 3, but Battlefield 4 is so intense words can't even describe it. Playing through headphones, you feel like you are really in the battle. Bullets whiz by your ears, explosions blinding you. It is by far the most intense shooter I've ever played. I can't speak for the campaign, as I haven't played it yet, but multiplayer is immensely enjoyable.The environmental destruction and the Levolution are amazing. It's really scary when you're hiding behind a wall, reloading your RPG to shoot at a tank, and then all of a sudden the wall isn't there, being blown away in a blast of shrapnel and flames. The maps are big, but the matches are 32 v 32, so there are more than enough people to fill them. There are lulls here and there, but for the most part the matches aren't without a moment's rest, just go go go, action all the time. I don't know how long I will play religiously, but for the week or so that I've had it it's been an incredible experience.The only issues I have with the game are two main ones: One, there is still the occasional lag. I don't know if this is my internet, or Battlefield itself, but I will be running across a field and I'll see my guy stutter while he's running. It's an annoyance, but not enough to detract me from playing the game. The other issue I have is that sometimes when a match loads, it will take almost a full minute for all of the textures to render. Again, not a dealbreaker, but an annoyance :PAll in all, the game is tons of fun. I didn't play it at launch, so I can't compare, but as of April 22, it's a really fun game to play. It's really fast paced, really intense, and it looks great. If you're hesitant, don't be! I got it and haven't looked back, it is by far the most fun FPS i've played. (Aside from fantasy FPS games like Borderlands, those are in a different league ;) )**Update**I've completed the campaign, and I don't understand all the hate for it. Sure it's not groundbreaking, but what FPS army shooter's campaign is? It was good. Some of the dialogue was a little cheesy, but for the most part it was pretty solid. I liked it :) And playing on hard had just enough challenge to attempt a few missions a couple times without making you so frustrated you don't even want to try.

It's all a giant team deathmatch and with so many players in a match you are basically just one of the crowd unless you are one of the hardcore players who is fully dedicated to the game. The fact that the two are considered rivals makes me certain that I do not want to play COD at all.I would've given this one star, but I found it to be more fun than Killzone Shadow Fall so I had to give it some credit.
