It's nice if parents DO want to join in or control the playlist, as the game has different menus and playlist options that are tailored specifically for them to use or that can be adapted for their children's use. This game doesn't do anything that the regular Just Dance can't; it runs on the same engine as the standard Just Dance game, and probably receives less attention than its parent game (just an observation based on the money spent on licensing music, etc.). But it is nice that they attempted to secure some tracks from very popular kids shows. Just Dance is still the best series of dancing games for standard home consoles, and this kids version is, as with their previous kid versions, a thoughtful and welcome addition to their pantheon of releases.

I've never used a gaming headset before, although I've been getting slightly more interested in them after seeing some of the more respectable top fighting game players using them. As an added bonus, you can even listen to music on your phone or mp3 player with it with the right jack.It may seem gimmicky to include a port for your phone, and I can safely assume that most people won't be using this feature. However, it's still nice to have in case you're waiting for an important call, or have a job position where people are calling you frequently. Both the mic that flips out of the headset, and the one that hangs from the cord are great and worked without any problems.If I had something to compare this to, I'd give a more detailed review. Since it's my first item like this, it'll serve as the standard if I get another one. I haven't used it a whole lot for games since I don't play many multiplayer ones, given my work schedule, but for anyone who's looking for a quality headset that isn't going to break the bank, this would be an optimal choice.

Up until trying the RIG, I was the one odd duck in my XBox Live group that used a traditional plain Jane, official voice-operated switch (VOX) headset that had trouble capturing my voice and sending it consistently over party chat.  Everyone else had Turtle Beaches like all the cool kids while I ate at the loner table with my $20 headset and ate PB&J; sandwiches.Thank GOD I had the opportunity to try out the new Plantronics RIG system as I've been using nothing since.  It's more comfortable  than any other gaming headset I've used, the VOX is virtually seamless, easy to connect, universal, and everyone keeps telling me to turn the volume down as they can hear my game.  I was originally going to get one of these for my brother but, after playing with it for over a month, he can get his own!Now, I have not really used a Turtle Beach except at demonstrations at gaming or electronics stores and I felt like they were designed more for teenage heads, and by that, I mean smaller than my gargantuan sized head.  They weren't really all that comfortable and, like Alienware computers, grossly overpriced.  With all that in mind, I was very excited to try out the RIG system.When my headset arrived it didn't take long for me to connect it to my XBox 360.  Come to think of it, it took all of twenty seconds to figure out where the USB cord goes, connect audio jack here, this there, and viola!  I started up a party chat and did some sound tests by myself to see if the mic icon would flash indicating that my voice was being recognized by the VOX and transmitting.  It was, so I then invited a few people in to see if they noticed a difference WITHOUT telling them I acquired a new headset.The first friend came in and noticed a difference almost immediately and commented on it.  He said there was no real delay in my speech so he heard everything I said and told me to turn down the VOX volume as he could also hear my XBox and my phone when a text message arrived (It's Joker from Mass Effect saying, "Message coming in... patching it through!").  The next guy comes in and notices a similar change within five minutes, then the last person noticed immediately.  We then went on to play Borderlands 2 for a few hours and they kept commenting on how I should NEVER go back to my old headset and gave some pointers on how to dispose of it from burning it to shooting it.  Either way, I wasn't the only satisfied with the RIG with it's comfort and ease of use, my friends on Live were also satisfied that I didn't have to repeat myself several times over my old headset during the heat of fighting a raid boss.So, it worked well on XBox Live, now onto something a little more MMO-ish.  My older brother has been playing Final Fantasy XIV (14) on his PC for quite some time and had been trying to recruit me to play it.  After much refusing given my reservations on MMO games, he got me a copy for my PS3 (I'm an egalitarian console owner) and a 1-month free trial.  After realizing that the PS3 chat and PC chats are not compatible (that we know of it) we tried another method of chatting via TeamSpeak on my laptop.  After merely switching the AUX and USB cables over to my laptop, I was able to begin almost immediately and we played for hours on end.  Turns out, MMO games aren't that bad but not quite my cup of tea.  After switching Free Companies (guilds) within FFXIV we had to switch software over to something called Mumble and, again, a seamless transition.Now after a month of prolonged use and countless hours online, I have come to really like the RIG and will be using it as my primary until it breaks and that doesn't seem like anytime soon.  My only beef is that, sometimes, the AUX input doesn't seem to line up right and I have to adjust it while making a long noise with my mouth and wait for the others on chat to go, "That's it!"  On occasion, something hits the mute button and I won't notice until someone points out that I stopped talking.  Not much a fault to the RIG and more my dirty man cave.All in all, the RIG is a very nice choice for the price over other brands like Turtle Beach.  It's easy to install even for us n00bs, comfortable to wear even after prolonged use, and your friends will notice a difference if you are leaving the traditional $20 plain Jane headsets.

First things first....Plantronics makes great headsets and this one is no different.  It has excellent sound quality and a myriad of connections options to keep you in the game while connected with a mobile device for calls and music.Basically the device connects to your game console with the included cables...in our case we used the 2.5mm connector to our XBox 360 and simultaneously a 3.5mm connector to an iPhone 5.  Both devices are connected to the headset with the included circular puck that is essentially the mixer...allowing you to get sound from both the game console and your phone....  The puck like device has the controls that you need to adjust volume levels and or switch between devices…  The larger portion of the dial controls the main volume for listening while two levers on the face control the volume/mix of the game audio or cell phone audio. There is also a button that switches instantly between game and phone so you can switch to an important call and mute the game audio…vice versa if you want only game audio and no cell, you can do that.The puck also is the mixer for the system.  There are 2 cables that run out of the back of the puck allowing you to connect your devices.  One long cable that ends as a usb plug and a 3.5mm audio plug to connect your computer or game console (yes it works with computers as well as gaming consoles).  It has a short cable with a 3.5mm plug only so you can connect to your smartphone, ipod, etc…  The other end of the puck has a 3.5mm port to connect the headset.  There is also a 2.5mm port so  a user can connect an Xbox 360 controllers microphone port directly to the mixer.The sound quality is great...as was expected.The cons are simple....this is quite expensive for what it does, it does not offer surround sound, and if used by younger members of your family you can expect a spaghetti tangle of wires very quickly.....  I simply fear that this will last for a long time due to the number of wires involved and thus I removed 1 star from the review.  It is a great product which leaves something to be desired...  Personally wireless may be the way to go for us.

We've had our PS4 since launch day (Knack, Killzone and Assassin's ordered separately, a bunch of downloads added as they appeared on the Plus) and we are very happy so far. As soon as we got it out of the box (pretty), we connected to our Wi-Fi, did a rather thorough tour of the system and took note of its capabilities (good stuff but some disappointments), checked out the new menu system (impressive), ran the mandatory update and did a quick round of Knack (fun). Many more rounds of Knack followed, especially by our 10 yr. old with occasional co-op help from me or one of her older brothers - yes, you can easily drop into a game and help out if you feel like it.Given the DualShock 4's rather short life on a charge, getting a bundle with a second controller makes a lot of sense. Or just order one separately because, even if you are a lone player you will almost certainly miss a standby, charge controller if you don't have one.So, without regurgitating published specs... let's talk about what we're getting.THE AWESOME AND THE GOODHere they are, first briefly, then discussed below. Still under 'first impressions' so I may add or remove some as we keep playing, learning and exploring.- Awesome, flawless graphics. Day one games are just that, probably not taking full advantage of the system but Knack hints at what's possible.- Near-revolutionary new DualShock 4 controller.- 10x the processing power of a PS3 and it shows.- 32x more RAM- Games on physical disks can be borrowed, traded- Digital content made available at whatever PS4 you log into- HDD still upgradeable without voiding warranty - our 1TB 7200 RPM upgrade should arrive later today.- No power brick- Game and chat audio can be sent to a headset through DS4's 3.5mm port- All or most media apps (Netflix, Amazon, etc.) currently on PS3 are available on PS4 as well.- Online access is 100% optional. Yes, you can do it all, including system patches without ever connecting your PS4 to the Internet.- PS Plus subscription only required for (most) multiplayer games, not for media services- Remote play (tested it on a Vita with Killzone and it works)- Plenty of sharing, social features- DualShock 3 chargers can be used with DualShock 4 controllers- Move is supported with the new cameraI will rate the system's graphics capabilities as approaching the level of 'awesome. They are good enough to make me a little concerned that some of my current favorite PS3 games may lose some of their appeal. The graphics improvement is not as radical as in PS2 vs. PS3 but, believe me, it's significant and you just can't miss it and if you got used to frame rate drops and 720p or less resolution well... be prepared to get yourself unused to them because they're not going to happen much on the PS4.The DualShock 4 controller, while looking familiar from a distance, is a major redesign and everything that changed or was added was for the better. The touchpad (clickable, multi-touch, etc.) is the most visible addition or... actually the light bar is more visible and games may or may not take advantage of these two but they are not the only changes. The better designed (concave tops) analog joysticks, the trigger-like R1/L1s, the in-controller little speaker, the audio jack, the more precise Sixaxis motion detection, the new hand-filling form factor make of a significantly better controller. Sony calls the DS4 'evolutionary' and clearly it's not a full redesign but it improves over the DS3 in a big way.Sony claims that the PS4 has 10 times as much processing power than its predecessor. I don't know how this is measured but the PS4 is clearly and without a doubt much more powerful than the PS3. Everything appears to be smoother, more responsive and after one hour or so with Knack's sometimes super-busy environments, it seems that frame rate drops and low-res games are going to be very much things of the past, even when hundreds/thousands of little particles are moving independently on the screen as things break, explode or in the case of Knack re-form.Then there is the memory. It's not something that we 'see' but, when compared to the PS3, there is 32 times as much system RAM (8GB of GDDR5) and, without going into technical details, it's a lot faster and a lot easier for a game to use than PS3's memory. I tend to play 'huge worlds' RPGs and I expect to see some awesome ones for the PS4 in the near future and the extra memory should help a lot.As Sony's PR guys keep reminding us every time they get a chance, physical discs are not tied to individual accounts so you can still sell them, swap them with a friend's game or give them away. It should be great for as long as the publishers don't do 'online passes' and they won't if enough of us refuse to buy the titles that have them. Speaking for myself, that encouraged me to order three 'big' games at launch time knowing that I may be able to swap or sell one or all if I didn't feel like keeping them after trying them out.The PS4 should allow us to  access our digital content on someone else's PS4. It's something that I may try over the weekend because we are going to be at a friends' house that got their PS4 at about the same time we received ours. I will update my review if it doesn't work.A few PS3 digital downloads are already available for the PS4 and are 'free' if already purchased for the PS3. We should ask that the list is greatly expanded.The HDD is still upgradeable. Yes, it's something that we had on the PS3 and I am happy to see that Sony kept this option alive. My original 60GB PS3 was upgraded twice to the point where it became a 500GB PS3 and everything would have become very very frustrating if upgrading it wasn't an option.Online is completely optional if you are willing to jump through hoops. Patches can be downloaded on a PC and ran off a USB drive if you really, really want to avoid ever going online.We already have a PS Plus subscription and we are happy with what get out of it but not everyone wants quick access to indie games or online multiplayer. Yes, it's not as good a deal as PS3's always free online but it's still 'good' when compared with other platforms.And, of course, there's a bunch of things I didn't try yet such as sharing stuff with everybody and some things that were promised but not implemented yet such as the ability to drop into someone else's game and help them out. I will update my review once I experience them.THE  UGLY AND THE BADAnd... yeah, not everything is awesome and here it is what needs to be fixed or get better so that we all become a happy gaming family. This may seem to be a long list but I am confident that quite a few of the items below are going to be addressed sooner rather than later and nearly all of them before the end of 2014.- No MP3 support (how dumb is that?)- No Media Server/DLNA support (see above)- No support for audio CDs (no big deal to most but still dumb)- No support for Bluetooth headsets (I bet they'll fix this soon)- No support for mice of any kind (Bluetooth or USB)- No support for an external, USB-connected HDD (it's probably coming with a future update)- DS4's lightbar can't be turned off, camera or no camera- Doesn't play PS3 games (inevitable but worth noting it because it's a fact)- Not too many games at launch (see above, but it's getting better already)I can't believe that Sony decided not to support MP3 and DLNA and they MUST fix this ASAP. These were good features on the PS3 and taking them away to force us into Sony's paid Music Unlimited service is not going to work and it's not going to win Sony any friends. And while at it, where's Pandora? Most of the shortcomings above are fixable and, if Sony wants us to be a bunch of happy gamers they better address them all as soon as possible.[NOTE: I just read a couple of news stories stating that Sony will in fact add MP3, audio CD and DLNA support very, very soon. They better. They also claim that the PS4 lacking them at launch has had nothing to do with Sony promoting their Music Unlimited service.]WHY GET ONE TODAY?Unlike the original PS3, this one won't play most previous generation games except for those you can get at the PS store. There's a couple dozen launch titles and big promises for some really big games to be released soon, some of them big exclusives but I predict that my PS3 and the PS4 are going to sit next to each other for at least a couple more years in my living room unless Sony makes playing PS3 games possible on the PS4 and they just might do that soon through some 'off the cloud' service.These being said, now that I have one, I am happy that I placed my preorder back in June. Anyone buying their first console should probably go with the PS4. Yes, there are great PS3 games out there but Sony will stop developing anything major after Gran Turismo 6 and lots of great games are coming to the new generation. As for those like me who already have a PS3, I know that we'll all end up with a PS4 or Xbox One or maybe both at some time in the future. Speaking for myself, PS4 or not, I'm still going to get my Dark Souls 2 on the PS3 and play it all throughout 2014 and beyond unless they announce a PS4 version but I'm looking forward to play at least half a dozen announced and soon to be released PS4 titles.WHY FIVE STARSThe big MP3/DLNA/CD disappointment notwithstanding - and this WILL be fixed - the PS4 has the potential of becoming a great gaming platform. Seven (in the case of Xbox actually eight) years between consoles generations is a lot of time and gaming changed a lot over all these years. The technology improved and there was a lot of innovation, some of which is going to play a lot better on the new gen platforms.I love the PS4 for all the technical improvements over the last gen and for being a new and improved gateway to great and greater games, for the greatly improved but still familiar DS4 controller to the not so familiar but easy to navigate new menus and for all of its raw power. I also appreciate it being a lot more affordable at launch then the PS3 was 7 years ago and for keeping tradeable disc-based games and offline playing still viable. Not everybody has access to the Internet all the time and some of us want to be able to play offline every now and then, Internet access or not. It's possible that my rating will change after another day or another week or month of using the PS4 and it will definitely change if most of the issues I noted above don't get fixed but, as of right now, it's a five star rating for the great experience so far and for the promise of it actually getting better in time._____________________________________________UPDATE:Just upgraded the HDD to aHGST Travelstar 2.5-Inch 1TB 7200 RPM SATA III 32MB Cache HDD(awesome). It was all done in minutes and we now have some 820 GB free space vs about 320 GB before the upgrade. And game loads appear to be faster too. As for the original 500 GB HDD, it's not going to waste. It's now inside an inexpensiveSabrent Ultra Slim 2.5-Inch SATA to USB 2.0 External Aluminum Hard Drive Enclosureand attached to our Wi-Fi router as shared storage for our media files that, hopefully, the PS4 will soon be able to access.-->> Brush your teeth, it's the law! <<

After years of wait and speculation the PlayStation 4 finally arrived. I was lucky enough to have pre-ordered it and receive it upon launch. This was the first console I ever pre-ordered or received at launch and I finally realized what it means to be an early adopter. While it feels great to have a fantastic piece of hardware, I feel like at the moment it is mostly going to waste as most of my time thus far has been spent watching movies and television shows.While their has been a reasonable number of launch titles, most of them were not exclusively made for the PS4 and many of them are smaller studio indie titles. One game I played in particular that really started to show the potential of the system was Killzone Shadow Fall. The graphics were very noticeably crisp and smooth, unlike I have experienced before.There are a few facts about the PS4 that can not be denied. First off the PlayStation 4 has the ability to run games at 60 frames per second. Any higher a frame rate will really go unnoticed without the proper equipment and frankly most players would likely not be able to tell the difference. Unlike it's rival, the Xbox One, the PlayStation 4 natively runs games in 1080p without the need to upscale. Like the PlayStation 3 the PS4 also can play DVDs and Blu-Rays, however, the step back thus far has been that there is currently no support for an external drive or mp4 video files as well as mp3 audio files. Another familiar feature of the PS4 is it's ability to run video apps such as Netflix, Amazon, Redbox and many more. The PlayStation 4 moves further into the future with it's PlayStation camera (formerly known as the PlayStation Eye) used for it's motion sensing technology. The interface is a clean and refreshing change from the mostly criticized XrossMediaBar (XMB).It's design is simple and understated, a sure nod to the PlayStation 2's launch design. The console is quite easy to set up and integrates flawlessly with High Definition set ups. I have my PlayStation 4 hooked up to my 60" LED TV and my HD Sony 7.1 receiver and truthfully it looks and sounds like a dream. At this point the trick will just be finding the right games to show it all off.One of the most impressive features of the PlayStation 4 has been it's controller. While the differences between the PS2 and PS3 controllers were minimal (aside from the wireless function) the differences between the PS3 and PS4 controllers were significant. This is the first time I have ever held a PlayStation controller in my hands and felt truly comfortable. The other controllers have always been a little too small here or there, not form fitted, but the PS4 controllers ergonomic design fits like a glove. I love the implementation of both the controller speaker and the touchpad, of which I think the Sony studios will find many creative things to do.All in all the PlayStation 4's future is blindingly bright, as we've been told Greatness Awaits.

I've been a gamer since I was a kid with Atari 2600, so I've been waiting over 30 years for a console to come out with mind blowing graphics and great games. I've watched games/graphics progress since then with Nintendo, SNES, PS, N64, PS2, Gamecube etc etc. I use to be an Xbox fan (still own my 360 for old games) but made the obvious switch to the PS4 with much trial and error. Walmart is a great place to get your taste of something, then take it back if you don't like it. That's how I made the comparisons with this and Xbox One (wink). So this is my second unit, one I bought back in about December or so, but the lack of content made me just wait a few more months. Back then I had no interest in the Xbox One and I still really don't after "trying one".As I said I went ahead and gave the Xbox One a shot, even though I was leary (hearing and seeing/reading all the bad Xbone press and reviews) because being a computer engineer (and building gaming rigs) I know all about power, gpu's, memory, and just how to make an overall good gaming system. Well Sony has succeeded in doing that this time around. The PS3 was a very good system but more of a media hub then a hardcore gaming unit. I really only liked it a lot because of it's great exclusives. And Sony still has the best, but waiting on them is a little bit disconcerting. So after trying out the Xbox One I really couldn't believe the difference in overall quality, graphics, and just the overall feel that Microsoft were trying way to hard to make a gaming machine, mixed with a super multimedia living room (all in one system). And after playing it for about a day games like (Forza 5, Tomb Raider DE, Thief, (and a few downloadable demos) I just found it to be way behind. The controller felt like a generic aftermarket 10$ brand. The graphics were dull and ugly, with very little to hardly any textures, that or they looked very "cartoonish". Even with a game like Forza 5, the cockpit looked great, but everything else looked like it was an Xbox 360 game, or worse! No I'm not kidding.So I said well that clenches it, back to the PS4. Now I'm very content, and after playing the same games, and also getting AC4 (9.99 upgrade), Outlast (for free), and Second Son all I can say is this is the definite way to go. The graphics are all in 1080p, with "maybe" a few in 900p, none of which I've played. And controller feels tight and well made. The interface is just plain simple (like it should be). Updates are on the way this month to add more apps, and a few other things. So waiting and being patient is just part of the process. I'm not sure why Microsoft went with such a weak GPU (50% weaker to be exact), when they could have had one of the best on the market, had they not been so cheap. There GPU is basically  a graphics card in the range of a 99$ to 159$  you would put in a Desktop PC. And there is a new card for around 159$ (Nividia 750 GTX) that runs a game like Titanfall fall "better" than the Xbone, which is just pathetic for a system that's 499$ or 450$ (Walmart and Sam's Club). It should cost no more than 350$ tops. This isn't to sound like a fanboy, especially since I'm 38 and not 16, these are just facts. Pros and Cons of both.PS4 ProsGreat graphics, full 1080p (very few that aren't)Great tight, comfortable controller (doesn't feel cheap)Simple interface, much like it's predecessor.Very quiet, under heavy load it runs hot, but nothing alarming (note) Remember how hot the back of the PS3 was? And it never once would shut down.The best Blu Ray player-which it should be since Sony invented the technology.Boots up super fast.Uses the newest DDR5 memory that enhancing everything the system has to offer. (Which will only get better)Disc load/install times are less then or around a minute tops.No lame gimmicks to make sales, or get peoples attention (Touch pad is odd, but innovative)CheaperEasy to upload 15 minutes of gameplay to Facebook, then download from your PC and upload to Youtube. Only 720p footage but still great.ConsOccasionally the PS Store will just vanish and leave you with a blue screen. Restarting solves it, very minor, and doesn't happen that often. I have great a 50mb connection, so it may just have something to do with that. Fickle.Downloads are usually between 3 to 5 mps. Occasionally boosts up to 7. (Not really a CON, but not a consistent speed) Fluctuates a bit to much. Also this depends on online traffic as well.It does have weaker wireless than the Xbox One, and Wii U, but this is something minor. They both use the newer 802.11ac wireless adapters with higher ghz. Not sure why Sony chose not to go that route.Online gameplay can be "fickle" as I say, but pretty steady for the most part. Occasionally getting knocked out of a game once and a while.Selection of games is still slim, but games like Destiny, Wolfenstein (with DOOM Beta), Alien Isolation. Watchdogs, The Evil Within, and some promising indie games are just around the corner. Patience. :)Xbox One ProsThe Kinect isn't actually that badI'm use to windows 8, so the interface is decent, I just don't prefer it.The online gameplay is more stable than PS4I think the system being large has a slight advantage when it come to staying cool. Time will tell.Voice controls can be fun, but get old after about a day. IMOA few more games than PS4-None which are out of this world.ConsPoor textures, sub HD resolution, no excuse for not running most if not all games at full 1080p. This is 2014!!Framerates are either worse of better than PS4, but only by lowering resolution and cutting corners. Which just looks horrible.Uses a weaker GPU, slower DDR 3 RAM, and has 32 mb of ESRAM which will do nothing but "upscale games". Which won't make a difference at all. Sony doesn't have this issue because they did it right the "first" time. No going back to free anything up, or software updates to improve anything (power wise or graphically). Except some minor glitches here and there.So that's it in a nutshell, PS4 got things right this time around buy using a better GPU, faster RAM, and giving people a better overall gaming experience. While (most already know) what Xbox One did, no use kicking a dead horse (system). I may get an Xbone one day in about 2 years when it's about 350$ used or something, for a few exclusives, but as of now, PS4 wins in all categories. Period. I don't want a system that's going to be playing catch up and always making excuses, and apologizing for it's mistakes. I would rather get a Wii U as a "secondary" system just for it's 1st party games for fun. At least Nintendo admits there mistakes, and doesn't keep making empty promises to it's fan. Being a 38 year old man I still love gaming (not hardcore) but I know enough to know what the best is. And right now this is it. PC gaming is great, but can get old quickly. So this is the closest thing you can get, so go out and buy one. They are everywhere now.Thanks.BTW:Keep one of your old systems for those old classic titles. They have at least another 2 years left in them, if not more.

It looks like a mouse batman would use lol-  you can customize the length of the mouseHere are the negatives- My computer doesn't always detect the mouse in wireless mode for some reason so I have to plug it in to detect the mouse again- The buttons on the side require too much pressure to use which isn't good for on the fly commands- It's not seamless at all when changing between programs like my g602 is. Pros: FINALLY, a gaming mouse for those of us with big hands. i mean FINALLY. i can't understand how both Logitech and Razer both went on so long without developing a decent gaming grade mouse that fits people with bigger hands. the Ouroboros comes with adjustable sliding palm rest that slides out and angles. it also comes with thumb and pinky rest which was what i was really looking for. also finally there's a place to rest your ring finger, unlike the Mamba/Death adder.CONS: lack of adjustable arch. the mouse is flatter in overall height than most, and the height is none adjustable, making palm grip almost NOT REALLY a palm grip. read more below. also the clutch button doesn't seem to be constructed with the same level of detail as the rest of the mouse. (see more below).Additional info: so here's a prime example of mass amount of R&D; and technology went into place but ultimate come up short on some of the obvious features. Razer if you're listening. this mouse needs a adjustable arch. i mean come'on, adjustable sliding palm rest with adjustable angle but no adjustable arch for height? this mouse is so flat, flatter than most gaming mouse that you can't really do a true palm grip and still use the side button at the same time. this mouse is more for people with hybrid palm grip (finger with back palm), and people with claw grip. if you were to really rest your entire palm on the mouse, like a true palm grip would, it's just not ergonomically feasible to use the side buttons.also the clutch button, although not as difficult to use as some in previous reviews made out to be, has a major problem. the clutch button itself clicks just fine, but it doesn't register when it clicks, you have to push it "pass the click" for the clutch to register. it's almost like the button itself and the sensor isn't well constructed. reminds me of some cheapo keyboard that you get for $10 that some keys although do stroke, doesn't actually register unless you hold it down pass the stroke really hard. that's exactly what the clutch button on this mouse is like.also i think if you were to make a mouse that's so specific for gaming, you should make one that's truly ergonomic for right hand grip or left hand grip. making it for both right and left just isn't as ergonomic and comfortable as one that's tailored for one or the other. i still prefer the comfort level of the G400 and MX518. Logitech, if you're listening, you'd be smart if you come out with an adjustable slideing palm variant of the G400 line that has raiseable height, angle, and pinky/thumb flaps.i never could really get used to the death adder/Mamba. although they're quite comfortable, they lacked the space to rest your ring finger. as a result, i was putting tremendous amount of pressure and over stretching my ring finger using the death adder to a point that my wrist started to feel the pain. the Ouroboro fixed that, whether intentional or unintentionally, by having a slight extra space next to the right button that allows you to rest your ring finger, same as logitech's G400/MX518. what this mouse shines is the pinky/thumb flaps that allows your pinky and thumb to rest. and slidable palm rest for people with bigger hands like me. although the mouse is fairly flat in height, you can't really achieve a true palm grip with this mouse without being uncomfortable using the side buttons. you can only do a half palm grip where your fingers touch the buttons, and the back of your palm touches the mouse.notice i did not mention about the wireless feature. i solely bought this mouse due to the advantages mentioned above, not for it's wireless capability. i could certainly do without wireless.this mouse is NOT worthy of the current retail price. and honestly i could do without the fancy jewel case and pass the savings onto the consumers. i only paid half the retail after using two of my gift cards. it's overall a good gaming mouse, but ultimately came up short on a few things. i WOULD recommend this mouse if you can get it for half price or little more than half. but there're a lot more sensible choices for you if you were looking to buy this mouse at full retail.EDIT: tried the wireless mode. the wireless mode sucks!. everytime you switch over from wired to wireless, it takes at least 2~3 minutes, i am not kidding, for the mouse DPI to react to what you have it set in the software panel. not only that, everytime you reboot, boom!... it takes 3~4 minutes "after you boot into windows" for the software to recognize the DPI setting that you have set it to. guess what happens before that 3~4 minutes? the mouse runs at like 8000DPI!!!! i can't even click on a window because moving a inch basically swipes the whole screen. so there, you have to sit there and WAIT.... WAIT... WAIT.... and WAIT..... THEN... you're ready to use the mouse. do yourself a favor, don't even bother with the wireless mode. it's too bad because the wireless mode actually tracks well, and responsive. i am taking another star off the review for this reason.if you're looking to get a responsive razer wireless mouse. stick to the Mamba. i cannot with a clear consciousness recommend this mouse to someone as solely a wireless mouse. at least not until they come up with a fix. the Mamba is just as responsive, tracks just as well, and doesn't have any bugs in wireless mode i know of. i had the mamba in my living room HTPC doing occasional gaming, it worked perfectly if it weren't for the ergonomic design flaw i mentioned above that causes your ring finger to stress out.all latest driver and firmware updates btwEDIT: 1/14/2014. Wireless function has completely stopped working. it just died. tried to pair up the mouse again by following the instruction, and can't even get the mouse to enter pairing mode anymore. wired mode still works. tried different USB ports and makes no difference. i am sending this POS back for a full refund. back to my old true and tried G400s. revising the review to 1 star.

When I first bought the mouse and installed the software, I was happy with it. However, the sensor seemed fidgety (even after setting up the mouse-pad material configuration). After they were installed, the mouse lit up and the DPI was changable (through the 4 different profile buttons), but the sensor was unresponsive. The mouse didn't move my cursor. This was a great way for me to share my hobby with my children. The content is entirely child-appropriate, but also fun to navigate.Overall, the graphics are great. Even with my old graphics card (8800GTS), the game ran fluidly and beautifully.The sound quality was also quite nice. Mickey sounds like Mickey and all of the sound effects were in place.But the greatest part of the game is the fantastic gameplay. It plays like the old Sega Genesis version, but then introduces all sorts of fun twists. Being chased by a giant apple or timing a jump on a floating marshmallow swimming around a cup of hot chocolate were just simply challenging, rewarding and fun.The game is not super-easy, but it's not very difficult either. Castle of Illusion is a really fun platform game. It's all out running, jumping, stomping your enemies, swinging, swimming, the usual. You collect diamonds along the way to unlock the subsequent levels. You don't need anywhere near the 800 possible diamonds to proceed, however. More diamonds, chili peppers, statues, and playing cards unlock costumes and really bland concept art as paintings in the castle.The story is a traditional Disney fairy tale. Mickey and Minnie are in love. The witch captures Minnie. Mickey goes to save the day. The narration reads like it's from a child's storybook. It's nothing that will blow your mind, but if you love Disney, you'll enjoy the story. Mickey and the other characters sound great, exactly like you'd expect them to, though their dialogue is limited.The graphics update for this game is phenomenal. It's gorgeous artwork in the traditional Disney style.Level design is exceptional, reminding me of the charm of games on the original Nintendo and Genesis systems. Each level has a theme and all the obstacles fit well within the theme.At times the game makes you move quickly as platformers traditionally do and you need to make quick reactions as the floors fall out from under you. It does feel like a bit of a memorize and repeat formula at times and can be a bit frustrating if the checkpoint is a bit further back.Boss battles are unique each time, as the various monsters have different themed attack patterns. The forest tree boss rolls like a log, the toy world boss is a jack in the box that jumps around and tosses a spring-loaded boxing glove your way, etc.The controls are very simple and worked perfectly on the XBOX controller for Windows. I would have liked an option to pan the camera to look around the immediate area for hidden collectables (as that is a significant part of the game), but it's not that big of a deal. Sometimes I would just make a jump to see what I could find. A few times it paid off. Other times, I fell into the abyss. Once I couldn't see what was on a platform I needed to jump to and a bookworm bit me. I think that was just a random glitch though because that area didn't have the same problem again. I never had any other technical concerns about the game. It's a rock-solid game.Sometimes, the game switches to more of a 3D perspective instead of side-scrolling. It's rarely used. You can play an entire level with one camera style and suddenly the boss is in 3D mode, so that can be a bit counter-intuitive. It's slightly challenging to judge the depth of your jumps in this mode, but it's not that big of a deal.I would recommend this game, but not at the $15 price point. It only takes about 2 hours to complete the story. Then you can repeat the levels of your choosing any time you want as time trials. Combined with a small system of collectibles, the game does present some replay value, though the collectible rewards aren't really that exciting.
Great case for the Nintendo 2DS. Love the feel of it, plus it has space to hold some game. Just enough added protection when I wanna throw my 2DS in a bag a go.

While I have no doubt this officially-licensed case will protect the Nintendo 2DS I bought to wrap itself around, the strange texture of the case leaves me reminiscing about grade-school art class, and my first experience with sand-paper. Also, this exact product is cheaper elsewhere, and I would not recommend purchasing this product for over 10$.

I recently picked up a red 2ds bundle that came with this case and two games.I plan on picking up a better case asap because this one doesn't really offer much protection it is a cheap and flimsy case that doesn't even have much padding the only purpose I see this serving is keeping your 2ds screen scratch free if kept somewhere safe,other than that I don't think its worth picking up unless you're able to get it for a low price.
This is the exact carrying case for the new Nintendo 2DS.  The 2DS will not fit in any other case because it is slightly larger than the other DS's.

like every nintendo product an excellent quality materials and technology the resolution of the screen is very good and the games have good graphics in spite of being a portable console, but the most negative feature is the display of this as it is very difficult playing some kind of game it seems that is designed to run some games better than others.

After Christmas, I got a 2DS.  I have wanted one for a while.  After I got it, I knew I needed a case.  I saw this one at ebgames.  I got it and it is great!  The system fits in it nicely.  It does not have much room to move around once in the case.  It even has a little part on the top back that can hold games.  Three if I am not mistaken.  I am 100% happy with my purchase of this.  I would recommend it to anyone who wants something to put their 2DS in.

As I said in another review for the red case, It's a solid cheap starter case but you will eventually wanna buy something bigger and better. It carries the 2DS well along with 3 games. Protection is alright but like every case, It's not gonna be perfect. If you have a lot of 3DS/DS games though, You will want to buy a separate case for your games. Also a bit disappointed that it doesn't hold the charger.Overall, For a cheap case it's not bad but you are better off spending more on a bulk case that can carry everything instead of one so limited, Such as this case.
This is the exact case you need for the new Nintendo 2DS.  It is slightly larger than the other DS's.  It also has a little storage space inside for 3 - DS games.
Only great case for the 2DS for now. Inside you have card slots for games. Materials feels really nice. I like the blue very much.

I was using this as a PC controller. After about 2 months, the "A" button lost all of its spring. About a month after that, the d-pad cracked into 4 pieces while I was playing a game. The controller was, admittedly, seeing moderate to heavy use, but I was not abusing it. it would get unplugged and put away when not needed, and I'm never rough with my controllers. The thing is just cheaply made. I would not buy anything else from this company.

This is an awesome looking controller. This doesn't just light up, it lights up bright! I have this hooked up to our xBox 360 and it works well. While wireless controllers are nice, it's handy to have ones that's wired like this one since there's no batteries to go dead on it while you're playing. With as bright as it is, if it was made wirelessly with batteries, I'm guessing it would go dead quickly. So it makes sense that a controller like this is made to be powered through the cable.The cable is plenty long. I can sit as far back from the TV and use it the same as I would if it was wireless. All the buttons work well and are responsive to pressing on them. It feels just like a standard xBox controller, so there's nothing especially different one would need to get use to. It looks cool and works great. I have it in the blue and now I'm wanting to pick one up in the green and red as well!

I have two Xbox 360s and love them but I'm a wireless user and don't see myself going back to wired controllers. I got this mainly to use with my laptop for Steam PC games. The great news is that my Windows 7 laptop immediately recognized the controller via USB and downloaded the drivers.This isn't to say your laptop just became a Steambox automatically. Some games still don't work well with the controller. So check your game first. But if your game does work with a controller then this controller will work for you.The only thing I don't like is that it glows blue. It's not my thing and looking at it in the dark can be blinding. I really do like seeing through the controller though. It's very neat to see how everything works. Fortunately there is a way to shut off the glow (or change it to pulse - just don't.) There is a small black button on the bottom back.

This Afterglow controller comes pretty close to being a clone of the official Xbox 360 controller.  This is a wired controller, with 10 feet of cable. The controller is the same size and shape as the official controller.BUTTON QUALITY: The buttons, analog sticks, triggers, and d-pad are quite good. They have the same look and feel as the official controller. The analog sticks have the same feel, grip, movement, and smoothness. There are a few differences. The XBOX button is smooth and barely recessed, but it works fine. The BACK and START button placement is different, but it's also fine. It requires a bit more movement of the thumbs from the analog sticks to reach them. On the official controller, you barely need to move your thumbs from the analog sticks.  The one issue I had was the shoulder buttons. They are weaker, not as reinforced, and feel slightly flimsy. They are still responsive but don't provide that heft when pressing them that the official controller does.LED: There are 7 LEDs placed asymmetrically. They are bright when looking at the controller, but not blinding since the LEDs are laid flat, parallel to the circuit board. But if you look at the controller at an angle and directly into the LEDs, then they are blindingly bright.  There are three modes. OFF, Flash during vibration, and Always On. The button is located on the back near the bottom. Press once to have the LEDs flash during any vibration in the game. This works really well and does a great job of matching up with the vibrations. Press a second time for the LEDs to be always ON.BUILD: Made of durable, clear, hard plastic. The surface is super smooth. In comparison, the official controller's surface is smooth but slightly textured. Because of the clear plastic, you can see the internal circuitry.  Even when the rumble/vibration is working, you can see the components moving.If they improve the shoulder buttons, this controller makes a great replacement.  I've been using it for a month now and nothing has worn out or seem weakened yet. I'll update if it does.  Overall, this is a pretty good controller, and since you are not required to have the LED's on at all, this is a good wired controller replacement.

My son decided this is his controller now.  He likes the lights and says it works just as well as the official controllers.  Of course, it's a plugin model so that is somewhat limiting.  It does have a quick disconnect plug which prevents someone from pulling the xbox out and that is good but it has made for some untimely disconnects.  The quality seems good and the buttons all react and feel like I would expect.  For me, I like the wireless remotes but this is a decent alternative if you need another controller but don't want to spend a lot.

My biggest problem with the after market controllers is the lack of longevity in the product.  This particular company seems to have made a decent controller that has some lasting power. A month in so far and seems to be holding up well. I will keep my fingers crossed & hope it keeps on working. Other than that...cool design with option to turn lights on or off.
It was in great condition. and was a great gift for my son for Christmas. So sorry it took me long to write a review on it.

My son loves this controller, but my husband isn't quite so jazzed about it. Why the difference? Let's first look at what they agree on:1.) Wired is nice. Weird, right? But they both agree that it is actually nice not to have to worry if they put the controller on the charger just right the night before. So they at least have one controller always ready to go.2.) Feel like an Xbox controller. I thought "Duh"...but apparently...this isn't as much of a no brainer as I thought. Especially with the clear controllers they can sometimes be too slick feeling. This one feels like you are using a standard Xbox controller. (I guess that could be good or bad.)3.) Controls like an Xbox controller. Not too sensitive, but no a "dead stick" either. They say you can move between this and an Xbox controller without having to get re-adjusted to how it handles.What do they disagree on?The light! My son loves it and thinks it is nice. My husband thinks it is too bright. Ah well, I guess you can't please everyone.Overall: 4 stars. If you are looking for a wired, lit, and very standard controller, you got it right here!

One of the reasons I got this controller is you can hook it up to your computer and use it to play Steam games.  The driver takes a bit to download and get working but this thing is a beast once you get it up and running.  Thankfully you can turn off the lights which I do because it is pretty irritating.  Regardless thing thing works like a champ.Hooking it up to the xbox is pretty anticlimactic.  You hook it up, it plays fine.  That being said there isnt much of a reason to use a wired controller with the xbox as the wireless controllers are somewhat the same price now.  The main reason for this thing personally is being able to use it for Steam.  This is where this controller rules.I have used it on an Alien, a Dell and an XPS and they all work great.  You hook it up to a standard USB port and after you download the drivers you can play your games.This is a solid controller.  It feels good and works well.  The buttons are a little off but you get used to them pretty quick.  I was up and running pretty fast and the controller feel became second nature after a few minutes.  The price on this thing is pretty fair and I just like it.Finding a Wired Xbox controller is getting more and more difficult.  I do not know if they even make them anymore.  With the advent of the xbox one I am thinking they are going to get even more difficult to find.  Give this a shot, you wont be disappointed.  I have played a few games on steam and this controller has done well with Bioshock, DayZ, Boarderlands, Riptide and a few other cheaper games.
They work great and I like the flowing aspect of the controller. They might feel slightly different than an official controller but they would just as well.

Bright, bold and blue! It took only one weekend for my youngest son to tell me that wireless controllers aren't all they are cracked up to be. He happily switched over to theAfterglow Wired Controllerand hasn't looked back.Funny thing about wireless controllers, players don't often stray beyond the comfortable distance covered by a cord - nearly 10 feet.My 9-year old son says the controller size and plastic texture feels comfortable. He was happy to upgrade as his wireless controller was showing significant signs of wear.Overall, I'm happy with the price and the fact that a corded controller eliminates the need and hassle for batteries, rechargeable or otherwise. My only regret is that the Afterglow Wired Controller wasn't available when we first purchased the Xbox 360.Rating: Five stars

If you plan on sitting reasonably close to your xbox while playing, this controller will be sufficient. The pros and cons of a wired controller versus a wireless controller are fairly obvious. Wired controllers eliminate the need for constantly replacing batteries, but you are limited by the length of the cord as to how far you can go from the xbox. It is also messier looking when you store the controller and a tripping hazard if you are playing around kids and the less coordinated. I am not impressed by the lights on this controller, but it is simple to turn them off with a small button on the back of the controller. The controller feels good in my hands and the cord is plenty long enough for where I sit. I measured the length of the cord and it was about 9 ft 9 inches, pulled pretty tight. If you are sitting close to that distance or farther then you will either need a cord extension or find a different controller. If you are sitting closer then I would recommend this controller.

I gave this to my kids to try out and they love it. My youngest son said that it works much better than his previous afterglow controller which had a sticky directional pad. Otherwise the controller is very responsive, the kids like the bright led lights and it makes for a good extra controller for when they are having friends over. I will update this review later if there are any problems with the controller after they've used it for a while.

Great Feeling and Comfortable in my small hands.  Feels warm after holding this for awhile, most likely due to the lights.  I don't mind it because my hands are usually cold anyway, however, my kids complain that its warm.  I like wired controllers because they are a lighter weight. The color is bright & bold!

So far, I've used the Afterglow Wired Controller for the XBOX 360 (Blue) more for playing PC games via Steam, but I've put it through its paces on the XBOX 360 and I'm glad to report that I've experienced no problems. In fact, this is a pretty darned good controller in just about any way that matters.Controls are responsive and both the D-Pad and analog sticks feel good. Playing a platformer like Guacamelee! calls for some pretty exact controls in places, and I was able to pull off some of the more complex combinations on this one with no more difficulty than I would have had with the stock X360 controller. The buttons are a little on the "clicky" side, but they're responsive and well-placed. The breakaway cable (which has been a staple of wired XBOX controllers from the get-go) is present and is welcome, as-always (I have small children...it's already proven its worth).Set-up is a breeze on either platform. On my PC (Windows 7), all I had to do is plug it into an available USB port. After a minute or so, drivers were installed automatically and I was able to play directly using Steam Big Picture. The XBOX 360 was obviously even easier as it was ready-to-go as soon as it was plugged-in.The controller is obviously plastic, so I was halfway expecting it to feel cheap and chintzy, but it actually feels pretty solid and well-made. There were no cracks at all in my controller (something I looked for as soon as I received it, since some other reviews mentioned them).As for the lights, this is a take it or leave it "feature" for me. They're kind of cool, and playing in a well-lit room, you'll probably not even notice them. They're probably a bit too bright for playing in a dark room, at least if you're playing anything a bit more ambient or atmospheric (might be a bonus for a game like Space Giraffe though). Fortunately, you can turn the lights off completely, so it becomes a non-issue. I've found that once I turned them off, I've rarely felt the need to turn them back on.If you're looking for a solid wired controller and aren't afraid of going for a 3rd-party controller, then the Afterglow is a great option. The price is good (and likely to get better in the coming months) and you shouldn't have any complaints as far as the functionality goes.

This Xbox 360 controller is a perfect clone of the real thing.  It's sturdy, solid, the buttons operate perfectly without being too loose or stiff, and it illuminates as it should.  I have to admit, it's pretty fun playing with this thing as the lights flash blue.  There are no lags with the response time when I push the buttons, and it's very responsive in general.My only gripe is it's wired.  Xbox controllers are all wireless, so the idea that a flashy replica is wired lowers the value a bit.  The cord is 10 feet long which is a good length, but I have a 60-inch tv and sit about 12 feet away, so make sure this cord length will suit your needs.  Because of the size of my TV and the distance I sit from it, I won't be using this controller at all.So yeah, this is a cool looking controller that works perfectly, but the fun is tempered by being wired.

My son and his friends (7 years old) really thought this was the coolest thing. Having the lights down low and playing some Minecraft with a glowing controller apparently is way cool. Also awesome, the vibrations that make you "feel" the rumbling on the game. GO MOM!Super easy to use, plug in and play and the cord is extra long!

First of all the response on the controller is great.  I noticed a lag with navigating through menus with my wireless controller but this one (because it hooks up to the console) is very quick in accessing game content.Having a wired controller isn't bad but the 10 foot cord comes up shy when playing on a larger TV. It is just too short for my purposes.The actual controller is light and has a cheap feel when comparing it to a standard xbox controller.The light does have three modes, off, on all the time, and flashing when it rumbles. The light is very bright especially in a darker room and the mode where it lights up when it rumbles is distracting and tends to get annoying and bothersome to the eyes.When the light was on the all the time mode, it was nice in a dark room because it acted like a night light.Overall the controller worked well, the cord needs to be longer and the light was decent when in all time mode but still gimmicky overall. There are definitely better ones out there.

Since each of my three kids already had their own controller for our Xbox 360, I joking referred to this controller as "Daddy's Controller" when it arrived in the mail. Actually, I was looking for a "guest controller" that could be available for use when one of the kids has a friend over and the other two also want to join in on the fun.While sporting a corded (USB) power source, this controller functions in the same way as the standard controller. It has all of the same buttons and analog stick and rumble features. The biggest difference is the clear plastic case and cool blue LED lights that light up as soon as the Xbox is turned on. The only benefit the standard controllers have over this one is added mobility. This controller will require you to stand/sit fairly close to the TV in the room or to the Xbox (whichever is closer to you). Also, it will automatically sync and take on the role of controller one (primary), so you need to recognize that the most bossy person/control freak in the room will probably insist on using this controller.This is a nice product. I look forward to using it over the course of this new year and I will post follow-up remarks at the end of that period of time - positive or negative.

This light-up wired controller works pretty good with our Xbox 360.  It feels comfortable in your hands and the buttons and controls are easy to use, although they seem a little bit stiffer than the regular Xbox controller but that could be perhaps because this is fairly new and hasn't been used much yet. There were a few times where we had been playing for a while and some of the controls would simply stop working and we would have to unplug and re-plug the controller in to get it working again.  Not sure what the issue is there but it has only happened a few times.  My husband was excited to find that it works on his Microsoft Surface tablet but was quickly disappointed when he found out that it just doesn't work well - he had to keep unplugging and re-plugging and got very frustrated with it but considering it's not made to be used with the tablet I don't think it's that big of a deal.  It looks pretty cool when lit up, it's very bright but if you're playing in the dark the brightness of the controller can be a bit of a strain on your eyes after a while.  Overall it's an ok controller, a bit of a novelty item if that's what you're looking for but our preference is for the wireless controllers.

This controller functions just like regular Xbox controllers with the added feature of the lights.  If you'd like to add something different to your gameplay the afterglow controller provides a nice light show. For times when you find the afterglow lights distracting, you can disable the light mode. And here we find one of the glitches. On my controller even with the light mode disabled, the lights will randomly flash from time to time.The controller feels like any other Xbox controller when it's in your hands. I feel that the start and back buttons are too high up and small though. I also find the joystick a little too loose for my taste.Even with the small criticisms I still feel it's a good controller and worthy of a four star rating.

The LED lights in this are easy to turn off fortunately because they are bright in a dark gaming environment.  The extra long cord is nice and it feels like a slightly compacted version of the official XBOX controller with a better D-bad.  The clear shell looks great and feels good in the hand.  The RB and LB buttons seem like they need a light touch and might break over extended use.  Good controller to have on hand as a multi/back up or when you want the room illuminated during night gaming.

The Afterglow wired controller for the Xbox 360 works and feels very much like the official version. The smooth clear polycarbonate body of the controller is well made and shows off the inner workings and bright LED lights. The look overall is very techy cool, but I do find the bright LED lights rather distracting for my vision and would like the option to dim or shut them off altogether. My 10 year old thinks this controller is very cool and has adopted it as his own.The differences between the Afterglow and the official Xbox360 controller are minimal. The biggest difference I see is that the two mini side buttons on by the central X button are are slanted ovals rather than circles. The buttons and thumb sticks operate smoothly and are responsive, just like the Xbox version. Once I get involved in a game, I don't even notice the difference between the two controllers.I've plugged the Afterglow in both my Xbox360s, on my desktop PC with Windows 7, and my Windows 8.1 laptop. No problems whatsoever. All my devices recognized the Afterglow controller as an Xbox360 controller. No drivers to download, it was instant recognition. I used it to play Darksiders II on Steam, Halo 4 and Gears of War on my Xbox360's and Spartan Assault on my laptop.The biggest annoyance is the super bright LED lights. They don't shut off when my Xbox was shut down, so it's necessary to pull the wired controller out if you want the LED lights off.Overall, I like the Afterglow controller. It looks good, feels good, it's responsive, works with my Xbox360s and my computers, and has worked well with the variety of games I've played with it. Because it's wired, I don't have to worry about low battery issues.

This is a wired USB controller that works on both the Xbox and the PC. It is clear plastic that lights up and allows you to see the inner workings of the controller. It is very solid and feels great in your hands. The buttons and the sticks all feel good and move well. You might want a wired controller for finer analog control of some games. I also saves on batteries.Notes:- The cord is 10 feet long but is USB so you could extend it yourself.- The lights are cool but can be turned off.- Feels and works great.- Well built.
This works as it should and the glow in the dark feature makes it much more fun to play with.

This is such an awesome controller!  When the lights aren't on you can see all the parts inside, making you want to take it apart and learn how it works, much like Gretchen's brain and her big hair full of secrets. The buttons offer no resistance and are easy to press, and the analog sticks move fluidly and make your hands smell like peppermint.  I also play with this controller on my computer and have had no problems, except with getting my pink shirt back.I know a lot of people like cordless controllers, but irregardless, I prefer wired.  I like that I don't have to worry about buying batteries for it or having them fail while in the middle of a game.  It's made of good quality materials, and Glenn Coco and I would recommend it!  You go, Glenn Coco!

There are 2 keys factors to consider when deciding whether to purchase this product:#1 = It's a wired controller, not wireless.  That said, the wire is 10 feet long which is ample for most tv/couch distances but if this is a concern you might want to take measurements before making the purchase.  For me, having a wired controller on my 360 was a nice change of pace in not having to deal with batteries but it really depends if you prefer the convenience of wireless.#2 = The light and the looks:  Personally I really liked the clear plastic casing of this controller.  It will definitely grab the attention of your friends when they see it for the first time and when it lights up the reactions are amplified further.  However, if you are using this controller lit up in a darkened room it may be too bright and distracting at times.  Fortunately the controller has 3 modes - on, off, and on only when the controller rumbles.  Personally I prefer the 3rd option as having the lights flashing in tandem with the rumble jolt is always fun and surprising.If the above 2 factors are not of concern then this is a great 3rd party controller.  It looks great, feels comfortable in the hands and is cheaper than the standard Microsoft wireless controller.

This controller works exactly like it should. It's really easy to get started, just plug it in and it works. I prefer wireless controllers, but the cord on this is plenty long. I love that it's see through; it's really neat seeing all of the components inside. And the blue lights are really pretty.

If you are looking for a new 360 controller and don't mind it being wired, look no further. Well, if you mind it being translucent, keep moving, but other than that, this is a great controller.Let's get this out of the way - the translucent case is cool, the lights, not so much. The nice thing is, you can turn the lights off or set them to pulse only when the controller vibrates. If you couldn't turn this off, it would be a definite skip as in darker rooms the flashing or pulsing is really distracting.The cable from the controller is 3m or about 10 ft long. You should be able to sit comfortably on the couch with this when plugged in. Another reason I like the controller is the quick release. So if your dog runs through the living, your cat, your children or you wife/husband and they trip on the cord, it should quick release and not pull your controller, or more importantly, your Xbox 360, across the room.The analog sticks are smooth and work well. The cross pad works OK for fighting games, but isn't perfect.Overall, a great controller at a good price compared to the first party controller, and this is also fully Microsoft licensed.Highly recommended if you don't mind translucent and the possibility of flashing.

This is a lovely controller. The colored lighting is very pretty, and can be turned off or set to vibrate only if you desire (although why you would deliberately buy a lighted controller and then turn off the lights is beyond me). If like me you like to play late at night with all the lights out this combined with a light-up headset is just the ticket.In terms of overall performance, this unit is VERY close to a normal Xbox 360 Wired/Wireless controller. It is slightly more stiff in all buttons and controls, and the amount of play in the analog sticks is slightly different. If you are crazy sensitive about that sort of thing it may throw you off (fighting games, etc). The controller itself likewise feels very hard/solid. I had a slight discomfort playing racing games due to the way the controller rubbed/pressed against my hand while holding down the analog triggers. Nothing casual players can't adjust to.One thing I really appreciate is the controller is fully compatible with Windows gaming PCs and was instantly recognized by my PC and auto-configured. I was able to start playing PC games with it immediately.I already have two wireless controllers I use for my 360, and another official Xbox 360 wired controller. With this setup I can play two-player games on my PC with the two wired controllers, or play four player on my 360. This makes me very happy. For people who want an extra controller for guests and like/don't mind the pretty lights and slightly different feel, this one is a winner. For the hardcore or those with sensitive hands, they may want to pass, especially if they don't like the lights/color/style of this controller. It's the same price as the official Microsoft wired controller.

This controller doesn't get a tremendous amount of use in our household so I can't comment on it's durability . It was fun for awhile due to the novelty of colorfulness and bright lights but even with it's long cord it just can't compete with the convenience of the wireless controllers. Still it is nice to have for the times that the kids forget to charge their other controllers and it does look pretty!

This was taken for many test runs by an 11-year-old and 9-year-old boys.The cable is the only drawback that we can list. Of course the other controllers are wired, but in our living room this wasn’t a problem since the cable is ample long to reach to the couch.The boys REALLY liked that is lights up (they’ll turn off the lights in the room) but they also like the fact that they can turn off the light when they choose to. That was a surprising high point of their experience.There is no noticeable difference in performance. They gravitate to using this over the stock remotes, partially for the cool factor, and partially for the ease of always being able to find it since it’s plugged into the machine.We enjoy it a lot – It’s very sturdy (it’s already been dropped at least half a dozen times) and they all seem to really like the light-up color.Would definitely buy another one of these if we end up expanding our unit anymore.

I owned the first iteration of this controller a couple of years ago and my two main complaints were brightness and stick 'throw'.The brightness issue, if you can call it that, is still prevalent in so much as the LEDs used here are super bright. Given that the LEDs are the main selling point I would have liked to have a brightness selection option to maybe tone them down just a little and it was something I wished for on my older one. Of course if it was too dim then I'd be complaining about that as well. You do have the option to switch off the lights or only have them on when the device rumbles so really it's down to personal preference.My only other gripe was the movement of the thumb sticks; there was a small delay in moving the sticks before it acknowledged that you had moved them. I don't mean lag, just a point at the center where no movement was being registered. In the older model I just got used to it, but I'm happy to report that the throw seems to have been reduced or indeed removed making this the best wired controller I own.And wired controllers are the way to go for the hardcore gamer. Any wireless controller would have some minuscule lag it's just the nature of the beast and if you want near 100% reactions to your actions then you need to be jacked in.The location of the buttons and the triggers are all similar to MS' stock stick although the smooth feel of the plastic here is silky and feels so good.A great controller priced right with insanely bright lighting. Awesome stuff.

I didn't realize how worn out my old controllers were until i received this one. With my old controllers the joystick was so worn out that when i tried to make my characters stand still they would wander on their own. Now that i have this new joystick that doesn't happen anymore. The joystick is very responsive, along with the rest of the buttons, and no more wandering! I also like the blue glow. I wish they could make this in a wireless, but understand the lights would use the battey too quickly. Overall a great replacement joystick. Will probably get another one in the near future.
My son is a huge Luigi fan! This case made his 30th Luigi edition Nintendo 3DS XL just that more special for Christmas!

This pouch is very cute. I love the retro Luigi theme and the zipper pull is a coin which adds to the cuteness factor. It fits my 3DS XL well and provides excellent protection for it no matter what bag I'm carrying it in (purse, backpack, etc.). Why only four stars instead of five? This pouch only has slots to carry 6 extra games. I have another pouch that is slightly smaller than this one and it holds 8. A minor criticism but this has become the pouch to my secondary 3DS XL and I carry the pouch that holds 8 with me everywhere.

This case is way too soft for my liking. I was hoping for a harder case, but I guess that's my fault with the moniker of "hard POUCH". Either way, I feel if this was dropped with a 3DS in it, the 3DS wouldn't survive unscathed. That is the most important part of a case to me. Aesthetically, this case is perfect in every way. Shame I had to wait almost 2 months for this thing to get in stock and ship to me.
Luigi has always been my favorite Bro.

I love this case. It is really great quality. The image of Luigi is very nice but make sure you don't scratch it. The zipper are in shape of coins which i thought was really nice touch. The inside feels really smooth and your 3DSXL will be safe inside.

Here is what I have to say, I love the system. It is great. I will go over some common complaints, since I disagree.Complaint one, it doesn't fold. I've had folding systems, I'm a heavy user of the systems, I've had broken hinges from over use, I'm glad this doesn't fold, it isn't as aesthetically appealing, but I don't really care if it looks slick or child like, I really don't mind that it looks designed by Fisher Price.Complaint two, it isn't built for large hands.
